These sets of distinguishing characteristics， when present in constellation， permit pseudolymphomas with lymphoid follicles to be discriminated from follicu-lar lymphomas in most instances.

【73】Similarities between pseudolymphoma and lymphoma exist clinically. Both the inflammatory and neoplastic processes are characterized clinicallv by painless papules， plaques， nodules， or tumors that vary in size and in color from red to violaceous. Both occur commonly on the head and neck. The presence of tumors of gigantic proportions favors a diagnosis of lym-phoma. As is true of malignant neoplasms in general， lymphomas continue to grow relentlessly； pseudolymphomas stop growing or even regress.

【74】Immunoperoxidase techniques may clarify the nature of an infiltrate of lymphocytes with associated follicles. The same principles that govern dif-ferentiation ofpseudolymphoma from lymphoma in sections stained by hematoxylin and eosin obtain equally for sections stained by immunoperox-idase techniques， to wit， a mixedpopulation favors pseudolymphoma， and a monomorphous population of llymphocytes favors lymphoma. Follicular lymphomas， being B-cell lymphomas， stain with B-cell markers in both lymphoid follicles and the interfollicular dermis and subcutaneous fat. Pseudolymphomnas tend to reproduce the normal architecture of a lymph node， i.e.， B-cells predominate in germinal centers， and T-cells predominate in the dermis between lymphoid follicles.

【75】Another difference between pseudolymphoma and lymphoma is re-vealed when immunoperoxidase techniques are used to detect expression of surface immunoglobulins. Lymphocytes of a pseudolymphoma express a mixture of lambda and kappa light chains. Lymphomas， on the contrary， express only one light chain or neither of them.

【122】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【123】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【124】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【125】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【126】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【127】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【128】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【129】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【130】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【131】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【132】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【133】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【134】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

【122】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【123】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【124】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【125】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【126】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【127】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【128】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【129】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【130】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【131】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【132】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【133】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【134】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

【122】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【123】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【124】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【125】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【126】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【127】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【128】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【129】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【130】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【131】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【132】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【133】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【134】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

【122】**INTRODUCTION TO COMPLAINT**

【123】Tinnitus is not a condition itself-it is a symptom of an underlying condition， such as age-related hearing loss， ear injury， or a circulatory system disorder. Causes are：

【124】· Presbycusis： occurs with aging

【125】· Acoustic trauma：long exposure to loud noise

【126】**· Ear infections： bacterial or viral infections**

【127】·Earwax blockage： causes hearing loss or irritation of the eardrum， which can lead to tinnitus

【128】·Bony structure changes： otosclerosis

【129】· Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders： TMJ impairment

【130】· Head injuries or neck injuries： head or neck trauma， hearing nerves， or brain function linked to hearing

【131】· Acoustic neuroma： This noncancerous (benign) tumor develops on the cranial nerve that runs from the brain to the inner ear and controls balance and hearing； condition generally causes tinnitus in only one ear

【132】Ototoxicity： a side effect of certain medications or alcohol

【133】·Ménière’s disease： inner ear disorder that may be caused by abnormal inner ear fluid pressure

【134】·Pulsatile tinnitus： head and neck tumors， atherosclerosis， high blood pressure (BP)， turbulent blood flow， and malformation of capillaries

【3】**Age at Onset**

【4】**Infancy/Childhood Onset**

【5】Sydenham chorea may present acutely in childhood following streptococcal group A infection 删除2:<u>(Chapter 17)</u>. However， a more insidious onset， particularly in the setting of other neurological abnormalities， favors a diagnosis of AR inheri-tance of a metabolic disorder 删除2:<u>(Chapters 8， 13)</u>. There are a number of disorders in which a variety of movement disorders may be present. These are typically part of a constellation of neurological abnormalities which may vary with the age at pre-sentation. Dystonia appears to be more common than chorea for the disorders with early onset， possibly due to the coexistence of rigidity or spasticity due to pyrami-dal tract involvement. AR inheritance of mutations of critical enzymes is the etiol-ogy. The diagnosis is made by assaying blood and urine for organic and amino acids， by enzyme assays in lymphocytes， or by genetic testing， as indicated.

【6】Another common etiology of movement disorders in the pediatric population is cerebral palsy. Spastic di- or quadriplegia， due to pre- or perinatal ischemia or periventricular hemorrhage， may evolve to a hyperkinetic disorder in later years. The history of the disorder should be diagnostic. While dystonia is more com-monly seen， chorea can also occur and in some cases can be quite violent. This can be precipitated in particular by metabolic stress such as infection and may require general anesthesia or neurosurgical intervention.

【7】**Adult Onset**

【8】Onset of neurological disease during adulthood is typical for the AD disorders. The age at onset of the trinucleotide repeat disorders varies inversely with the size of the trinucleotide repeat expansion. Most cases present in adulthood， often after the reproductive years； however， young-onset forms are not uncommon， particu-larly with paternal inheritance.

【9】It is being increasingly recognized that AR disorders can present during adult-hood， usually in atypical forms， for example， when the causative mutations result in only partial enzyme deficiency， such as with PKAN 删除2:<u>(Chapter 8)</u> and AT 删除1:<u>(Verha-gen et al.，2009)</u>. In other AR disorders， the cause of the late presentation is not so well understood， for example， in chorea-acanthocytosis (ChAc) 删除2:<u>(Chapter 6)</u>， although it is suspected that initial， subtle psychiatric signs of basal ganglia dys-function may be present during adolescence. Aceruloplasminemia 删除2:<u>(Chapter 10)</u> also presents later in life， most likely as symptoms emerge once a critical amount of iron has accumulated in the target organs.

【10】McLeod syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 7)</u> is an X-linked disorder which characteristically presents in middle-aged men 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Danek et al.， 2001； Jung et al.，2001)</u></u>， although it may be detected at a younger age if blood typing is performed or serological tests demonstrate elevated levels of creatine kinase or liver enzymes. Occasionally， carrier females have been symptomatic， presumably due to X-chromosome inactivation 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Hardie et al.， 1991； Jung et al.， 2001； Ueyama et al.， 2000)</u></u>.

【11】**Late Adult Onset**

【12】Elderly patients who develop chorea should be thoroughly evaluated for a neoplas-tic syndrome or for an autoimmune disorder， especially if female 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>. In the absence of these， HD should be considered a possible diagnosis. Late onset is often associated with CAG repeats in the borderline range， where penetrance is reduced； but instability and expansion with vertical transmission are likely， raising genetic counseling issues. If HD has been excluded， other genetic etiologies may be consid-ered， including HDL2， which can present at later ages with lower pathological repeat sizes 删除1:<u>(Rodrigues et al.， 2008)</u>. The entity of“senile chorea"is obsolete as these cases are now recognized as most probably being due to late onset of genetic disorders.

【13】**Disease Progression**

【14】**Acute Onset**

【15】As with all neurological disorders， details of disease progression are strongly suggestive of the nature of the diagnosis. Sudden onset of chorea which does not progress indicates a vascular event， either ischemic or hemorrhagic 删除2:<u>(Chapter 16)</u>.

【16】Sudden onset of chorea related to medical illness suggests a causal relationship such as a metabolic 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， postinfectious， or autoimmune 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>

删除5:<u>**I. INTRODUCTION**</u>|删除换行|etiology. However， the pediatric inherited metabolic disorders may be unmasked by stresses such as fever， illness， and trauma 删除2:<u>(Chapter 13)</u>， confounding the diagnosis.

【18】A common type of sudden-onset chorea in childhood is Sydenham chorea， seen following a streptococcal throat infection 删除2:<u>(Chapter 17)</u>. Cases usually resolve after a few weeks， but symptoms may be debilitating.

【19】**Subacute Onset**

【20】Development of chorea over days to weeks may suggest a metabolic process删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， such as nonketotic hyperglycemia in a non-insulin-dependent dia-betic patient， although these patients can present quite acutely. Other metabolic disorders which present with this time frame include a range of electrolyte distur-bances such as hyper- 删除1:<u>(Sparacio et al.， 1976)</u> and hyponatremia 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Piccolo et al.，2003； Tang et al.， 1981)</u></u>， hyper-删除1:<u>(Matsis et al.， 1989)</u> and hypocalcemia 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Howdle et al.， 1979； Topakian et al.， 2006)</u></u>， or hypomagnesemia.

【21】Endocrine abnormalities related to thyroid or parathyroid disease may cause chorea 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， specifically hyperthyroidism 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Fidler et al.， 1971； Fischbeck and Layzer， 1979； Lucantoni et al.， 1994)</u></u>. Hypo- and hyperparathyroidism have also been associated with chorea， which may be paroxysmal，likely due to distur-bances of calcium 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Hattori and Yorifuji， 2000； Soffer et al.， 1977)</u></u>.

【22】参考段删除-1:<u>A subacute presentation may be seen with prion diseases， specifically new vari-ant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease， related to bovine spongiform encephalopathy删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Bowen et al.， 2000； McKee and Talbot， 2003)</u></u> 删除2:<u>(Chapter 11)</u>， or with slowly grow-ing mass lesions 删除2:<u>(Chapter 16)</u>.</u>

【23】A similar time course can be seen with paraneoplastic syndromes 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Albin et al.，1988； Batchelor et al.， 1998； Dorban et al.， 2004； Kujawa et al.， 2001； Tani et al.，2000； Vernino et al.， 2002)</u></u> 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u> and has been reported with a variety of tumors， including renal， small cell lung， breast， and Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lym-phoma. The causative autoantibodies include anti-CRMP-5/CV2 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Muehlschlegel et al.， 2005； Vernino et al.， 2002)</u></u>， anti-Hu 删除1:<u>(Dorban et al.， 2004)</u>， anti-Yo 删除1:<u>(Krolak-Salmon et al.， 2006)</u>， anti-NMDA receptor， and others.

【24】**Chronic Progressive Course**

【25】A slow disease course， progressing over a number of years， particularly when accompanied by cognitive or psychiatric findings， is likely to indicate a neurode-generative process， for example， due to HD 删除2:<u>(Chapter 3)</u>， the AD inherited ataxias删除2:<u>(Chapter 12)</u>， a neuroacanthocytosis syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapters 6，7)</u>， or a neurodegen-eration with iron accumulation syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapters 8-10)</u>.

【26】**Chronic Stable Chorea**

Choreiform movements which develop gradually but do not progress can some-times be attributed to use of a medication. either as a direct side effect or as a tardive syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 14)</u>. Benign hereditary chorea 删除2:<u>(Chapter 4)</u> should also|删除0换行|be considered， particularly if there is childhood onset and an AD family history. This condition is due to mutations of thyroid transcription factor 1 (TITF-1)删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Breedveld et al.， 2002； Devos et al.， 2006； Mahajnah et al.， 2007； Willemsen et al.， 2005)</u></u>， also known as NKX2.1， although it may be genetically heterogeneous删除1:<u>(Bauer et al.， 2006)</u>. The chorea may respond to L-dopa 删除1:<u>(Asmus et al.，2005)</u>.

【28】参考段删除-1:<u>A similar， relatively stable， temporal presentation may also be due to auto-immune processes， as in lupus 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Font et al.， 1998； Watanabe and Onda， 2004)</u></u>， Sjogren syndrome 删除1:<u>(Venegas et al.， 2005)</u>， and antiphospholipid antibody syn-drome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>.</u>

【29】**Episodic Chorea**

【30】The paroxysmal hyperkinetic disorders are more typically dystonic in nature， and thus， they have been classified with the genetic dystonias， although chorea can be a component 删除2:<u>(Chapter 19)</u>. The diagnosis of these disorders was previously based upon their phenomenology and precipitating factors， but this is being replaced by molecular identification. Many appear to be due to mutations of ion channels and to respond to anticonvulsants. More rarely， episodic chorea may be psychogenic in etiology 删除2:<u>(Chapter 21)</u>.

【31】Paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia (paroxysmal dystonic choreoathetosis， DYT8) is due to a mutation of the myofibrillogenesis regulator gene located at2q33 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Friedman et al.， 2008； Rainier et al.， 2004)</u></u>， which may be involved in detoxifying alcohol and caffeine 删除1:<u>(Lee et al.， 2004)</u>. Episodes of dystonia and/or chorea typically occur at rest and may be precipitated by alcohol， caffeine， stress， extremes of temperature， fatigue， or fasting. Episodes are much less frequent than those of paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia， and only a few may occur in a month； but they tend to be more long-lasting and severe.

【32】参考段删除-1:<u>Paroxysmal choreoathetosis with spasticity (DYT9) has been localized to1p.21-p13.3 删除1:<u>(Auburger et al.， 1996)</u>. Episodes in these patients were precipitated by exercise， stress， alcohol consumption， and sleep deprivation and consisted of dystonia， choreoatherosis， and dysarthria. Spasticity also occurs and can persist between attacks.</u>

【33】Paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia (PKD； paroxysmal kinesigenic dystonia， DYT10) of childhood onset may be familial or sporadic and is characterized by very frequent， brief episodes of limb dystonia following movement. Episodes often resolve with age. Treatment with anticonvulsants is usually beneficial删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Chatterjee et al.， 2002； Huang et al.， 2005； Picard et al.， 1998； Tsao， 2004)</u></u>， sug-gesting a channelopathy. Other cases are associated with features such as seizures删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Cuenca-Leon et al.， 2002； Thiriaux et al.， 2002)</u></u> and have been termed“benign infantile convulsions and paroxysmal choreoathetosis”删除1:<u>(Szepetowski et al.， 1997)</u>.

【34】Paroxysmal exertional dyskinesia (DYT18) is an intermediate form with invol-untary movements developing following more prolonged exertion than PKD， which can last from minutes to hours. This syndrome is one of several neurological

【38】**Medical History**

【39】The medical history may be informative in the patient with chorea. In pediatric cases nonneurological features can be very helpful in indicating a specific inher-ited metabolic disorder 删除2:<u>(Chapter 13)</u>.

【40】Patients with endocrine disorders， especially diabetic patients with nonketotic hyperglycemia 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， and autoimmune disorders 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u> may develop chorea， in some cases as the presenting symptom. Patients with aceruloplasmin-emia typically have diabetes mellitus due to deposition of iron in the pancreas删除2:<u>(Chapter 10)</u>. One-third of patients with Friedreich ataxia also develop diabetes， which is thought to be due to mitochondrial dysfunction 删除2:<u>(Chapter 12)</u>.

【41】Women of childbearing age should be evaluated for pregnancy (chorea gravi-darum) or may develop chorea related to estrogen-/progesterone-containing med-ications 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Caviness and Muenter， 1991； Miranda et al.， 2004； Nausieda et al.，1979； Suchowersky and Muthipeedika， 2005)</u></u>. Hormone replacement therapy may similarly be responsible， possibly due to sensitization of dopamine receptors by estrogens. However， contradictorily， suppression of estrogen with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone may also result in chorea 删除1:<u>(Gironell et al.， 2008)</u>.

【42】The gene identified as causing benign hereditary chorea has been reported as part of a multisystem disorder due to a mutation of the gene TITF-I 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Breedveld et al.， 2002； Devos et al.， 2006； Mahajnah et al.， 2007； Willemsen et al.， 2005)</u></u>， which causes congenital hypothyroidism， hypotonia， and pulmonary problems删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Doyle et al.， 2004； Ferrara et al.， 2008； Glik et al.， 2008； Krude et al.， 2002)</u></u>删除2:<u>(Chapter 4)</u>. 【47】Cardiac disease， specifically cardiomyopathy， is frequently found in Friedreich ataxia 删除2:<u>(Chapter 12)</u>. Similar findings， along with arrhythmias， are seen in McLeod syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 7)</u>.

【48】In children with acute onset of chorea， evaluation for a recent upper respiratory tract infection by streptococcus group A， in consideration of Sydenham chorea删除2:<u>(Chapter 17)</u>， is essential. These are typically part of a constellation of neurological abnormalities which may vary with the age at pre-sentation. Dystonia appears to be more common than chorea for the disorders with early onset， possibly due to the coexistence of rigidity or spasticity due to pyrami-dal tract involvement. AR inheritance of mutations of critical enzymes is the etiol-ogy. The diagnosis is made by assaying blood and urine for organic and amino acids， by enzyme assays in lymphocytes， or by genetic testing， as indicated.

【6】Another common etiology of movement disorders in the pediatric population is cerebral palsy. Spastic di- or quadriplegia， due to pre- or perinatal ischemia or periventricular hemorrhage， may evolve to a hyperkinetic disorder in later years. The history of the disorder should be diagnostic. While dystonia is more com-monly seen， chorea can also occur and in some cases can be quite violent. This can be precipitated in particular by metabolic stress such as infection and may require general anesthesia or neurosurgical intervention.

【7】**Adult Onset**

【8】Onset of neurological disease during adulthood is typical for the AD disorders. The age at onset of the trinucleotide repeat disorders varies inversely with the size of the trinucleotide repeat expansion. Most cases present in adulthood， often after the reproductive years； however， young-onset forms are not uncommon， particu-larly with paternal inheritance.

【9】It is being increasingly recognized that AR disorders can present during adult-hood， usually in atypical forms， for example， when the causative mutations result in only partial enzyme deficiency， such as with PKAN 删除2:<u>(Chapter 8)</u> and AT 删除1:<u>(Verha-gen et al.，2009)</u>. In other AR disorders， the cause of the late presentation is not so well understood， for example， in chorea-acanthocytosis (ChAc) 删除2:<u>(Chapter 6)</u>， although it is suspected that initial， subtle psychiatric signs of basal ganglia dys-function may be present during adolescence. Aceruloplasminemia 删除2:<u>(Chapter 10)</u> also presents later in life， most likely as symptoms emerge once a critical amount of iron has accumulated in the target organs.

【10】McLeod syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 7)</u> is an X-linked disorder which characteristically presents in middle-aged men 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Danek et al.， 2001； Jung et al.，2001)</u></u>， although it may be detected at a younger age if blood typing is performed or serological tests demonstrate elevated levels of creatine kinase or liver enzymes. Occasionally， carrier females have been symptomatic， presumably due to X-chromosome inactivation 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Hardie et al.， 1991； Jung et al.， 2001； Ueyama et al.， 2000)</u></u>.

【11】**Late Adult Onset**

【12】Elderly patients who develop chorea should be thoroughly evaluated for a neoplas-tic syndrome or for an autoimmune disorder， especially if female 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>. In the absence of these， HD should be considered a possible diagnosis. Late onset is often associated with CAG repeats in the borderline range， where penetrance is reduced； but instability and expansion with vertical transmission are likely， raising genetic counseling issues. If HD has been excluded， other genetic etiologies may be consid-ered， including HDL2， which can present at later ages with lower pathological repeat sizes 删除1:<u>(Rodrigues et al.， 2008)</u>. The entity of“senile chorea"is obsolete as these cases are now recognized as most probably being due to late onset of genetic disorders.

【13】**Disease Progression**

【14】**Acute Onset**

【15】As with all neurological disorders， details of disease progression are strongly suggestive of the nature of the diagnosis. Sudden onset of chorea which does not progress indicates a vascular event， either ischemic or hemorrhagic 删除2:<u>(Chapter 16)</u>.

【16】Sudden onset of chorea related to medical illness suggests a causal relationship such as a metabolic 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， postinfectious， or autoimmune 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>

【18】A common type of sudden-onset chorea in childhood is Sydenham chorea， seen following a streptococcal throat infection 删除2:<u>(Chapter 17)</u>. Cases usually resolve after a few weeks， but symptoms may be debilitating.

【19】**Subacute Onset**

【20】Development of chorea over days to weeks may suggest a metabolic process删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， such as nonketotic hyperglycemia in a non-insulin-dependent dia-betic patient， although these patients can present quite acutely. Other metabolic disorders which present with this time frame include a range of electrolyte distur-bances such as hyper- 删除1:<u>(Sparacio et al.， 1976)</u> and hyponatremia 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Piccolo et al.，2003； Tang et al.， 1981)</u></u>， hyper-删除1:<u>(Matsis et al.， 1989)</u> and hypocalcemia 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Howdle et al.， 1979； Topakian et al.， 2006)</u></u>， or hypomagnesemia.

【21】Endocrine abnormalities related to thyroid or parathyroid disease may cause chorea 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， specifically hyperthyroidism 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Fidler et al.， 1971； Fischbeck and Layzer， 1979； Lucantoni et al.， 1994)</u></u>. Hypo- and hyperparathyroidism have also been associated with chorea， which may be paroxysmal，likely due to distur-bances of calcium 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Hattori and Yorifuji， 2000； Soffer et al.， 1977)</u></u>.

【22】参考段删除-1:<u>A subacute presentation may be seen with prion diseases， specifically new vari-ant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease， related to bovine spongiform encephalopathy删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Bowen et al.， 2000； McKee and Talbot， 2003)</u></u> 删除2:<u>(Chapter 11)</u>， or with slowly grow-ing mass lesions 删除2:<u>(Chapter 16)</u>.</u>

【23】A similar time course can be seen with paraneoplastic syndromes 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Albin et al.，1988； Batchelor et al.， 1998； Dorban et al.， 2004； Kujawa et al.， 2001； Tani et al.，2000； Vernino et al.， 2002)</u></u> 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u> and has been reported with a variety of tumors， including renal， small cell lung， breast， and Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lym-phoma. The causative autoantibodies include anti-CRMP-5/CV2 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Muehlschlegel et al.， 2005； Vernino et al.， 2002)</u></u>， anti-Hu 删除1:<u>(Dorban et al.， 2004)</u>， anti-Yo 删除1:<u>(Krolak-Salmon et al.， 2006)</u>， anti-NMDA receptor， and others.

【24】**Chronic Progressive Course**

【25】A slow disease course， progressing over a number of years， particularly when accompanied by cognitive or psychiatric findings， is likely to indicate a neurode-generative process， for example， due to HD 删除2:<u>(Chapter 3)</u>， the AD inherited ataxias删除2:<u>(Chapter 12)</u>， a neuroacanthocytosis syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapters 6，7)</u>， or a neurodegen-eration with iron accumulation syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapters 8-10)</u>.

【26】**Chronic Stable Chorea**

Choreiform movements which develop gradually but do not progress can some-times be attributed to use of a medication. either as a direct side effect or as a tardive syndrome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 14)</u>. Benign hereditary chorea 删除2:<u>(Chapter 4)</u> should also|删除0换行|be considered， particularly if there is childhood onset and an AD family history. This condition is due to mutations of thyroid transcription factor 1 (TITF-1)删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Breedveld et al.， 2002； Devos et al.， 2006； Mahajnah et al.， 2007； Willemsen et al.， 2005)</u></u>， also known as NKX2.1， although it may be genetically heterogeneous删除1:<u>(Bauer et al.， 2006)</u>. The chorea may respond to L-dopa 删除1:<u>(Asmus et al.，2005)</u>.

【28】参考段删除-1:<u>A similar， relatively stable， temporal presentation may also be due to auto-immune processes， as in lupus 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Font et al.， 1998； Watanabe and Onda， 2004)</u></u>， Sjogren syndrome 删除1:<u>(Venegas et al.， 2005)</u>， and antiphospholipid antibody syn-drome 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u>.</u>

【29】**Episodic Chorea**

【30】The paroxysmal hyperkinetic disorders are more typically dystonic in nature， and thus， they have been classified with the genetic dystonias， although chorea can be a component 删除2:<u>(Chapter 19)</u>. The diagnosis of these disorders was previously based upon their phenomenology and precipitating factors， but this is being replaced by molecular identification. Many appear to be due to mutations of ion channels and to respond to anticonvulsants. More rarely， episodic chorea may be psychogenic in etiology 删除2:<u>(Chapter 21)</u>.

【31】Paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia (paroxysmal dystonic choreoathetosis， DYT8) is due to a mutation of the myofibrillogenesis regulator gene located at2q33 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Friedman et al.， 2008； Rainier et al.， 2004)</u></u>， which may be involved in detoxifying alcohol and caffeine 删除1:<u>(Lee et al.， 2004)</u>. 【39】The medical history may be informative in the patient with chorea. In pediatric cases nonneurological features can be very helpful in indicating a specific inher-ited metabolic disorder 删除2:<u>(Chapter 13)</u>.

【40】Patients with endocrine disorders， especially diabetic patients with nonketotic hyperglycemia 删除2:<u>(Chapter 15)</u>， and autoimmune disorders 删除2:<u>(Chapter 18)</u> may develop chorea， in some cases as the presenting symptom. Patients with aceruloplasmin-emia typically have diabetes mellitus due to deposition of iron in the pancreas删除2:<u>(Chapter 10)</u>. One-third of patients with Friedreich ataxia also develop diabetes， which is thought to be due to mitochondrial dysfunction 删除2:<u>(Chapter 12)</u>.

【41】Women of childbearing age should be evaluated for pregnancy (chorea gravi-darum) or may develop chorea related to estrogen-/progesterone-containing med-ications 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Caviness and Muenter， 1991； Miranda et al.， 2004； Nausieda et al.，1979； Suchowersky and Muthipeedika， 2005)</u></u>. 【10】Management of AD is complex involving not just the patient but also the caregiver. Early diagnosis and a cor-rect diagnosis are important for future planning regard-ing living environment， supervision and care， and estate planning. The caregiver now has access to centers and groups offering training， support， and counseling. The AD patient cannot be cured； however， the process may be slowed or the cognitive and behavioral problems may be managed medically. For the cognitive impairment asso-ciated with AD the primary medications are cholinesterase inhibitors such as tacrine (Cognex) and donepaxil(Aricept). These drugs inhibit degradation of acetyl-choline at the synaptic cleft. Cholinesterase inhibitors appear to provide modest benefit on neuropsychiatric and functional outcomes for mild to moderate Alzheimer's dis-ease.1 A newly approved drug， memantine， is an uncom-petitive NMDA-receptor antagonist (angi-glutamatergic) and has been shown to be effective in reducing clinical de-terioration in moderate-to-severe Alzheimer’s disease.

【11】Disease-altering strategies include the use of ginkgo biloba extract， vitamin E， monounsaturated fatty acids， NSAIDs， and estrogen 52.53 A recent， randomized， double-blind， placebo-controlled study54 did not demon-strate any effect of slowing AD in women who took es-trogen replacement therapy (ERT) for l year. It appears that ERT may not slow the progression， yet more re-search is needed to determine if it has a protective effect if started early enough. Novel approaches are being de-veloped for the treatment ofAD. One approach is based on the observation that mice minus one third of the cells needed for cognitive function were able to regain cogni-tive function when their brains were infused with nerve growth factor (NGF)Apparently， this research implies that function of the remaining cells can be enhanced enough to make up for the loss of other cells.

【12】DepressionAlthough when compared with younger patients， older patients are affected less often (7% to 10%of community dwellers) by obvious depression， atypical presentations are more common in the elderly.56 Most specifically is the misdiagmosis ofdementia (i.e.，memory loss) when， in fact， depression is the cause (i.e.， pseudo-dementia). Also， older patients may suffer from the de-pression associated with chronic disease， cancer， and prescribed medications. Some drugs that can cause de-pressive symptoms include antibiotics， anticonvulsants， antihypertensives， antineoplastic agents， antiparkinson-ian agents， corticosteroids， digitalis， and hormones. Depression is covered more extensively in Chapter 20； however， for the older patient two screening tools may be useful： the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). These question-naires can identify alinost 90% of patients with depres-sion. The longer version ofthe GDS takes approximately10 to 15 minutes to fill out， whereas the shorter 15-item version (GDS15) takcs only a few minutes and is recom-mended by some groups as the screening tool of choice.58 The BDI is short and takes only 5to 10 mninutes to completc； it is considered reliable and valid for screening.

【13】DrugsThe elderly account for about 30% of pre-scription drug purchases and 40% of nonprescription drug purchases. Over a 5-year period， 90% ofthe elderly are taking at least one medication with the average non-institutionalized patient often taking three to four medications. The risks from drug usage increase expo-nentially with each additional drug. Forty percent of the elderly must take one drug each day to perform ADLs.60In addition to the high percentage of the elderly taking medication， the issues of polypharmacy and age-related changes affecting dosage are of particular concern. FallsAlthough falls are considered an almost natural result of growing older， the impact is far greater than of-ten assumed. With the exclusion of nontraumatic causes of death， falls are the leading cause of death due to trauma， primarily from head injury and complications associated with hip fracture.61 A fall may be the decision point for nursing care or extended care residency. In addition to the obvious pain， the associated loss of mobility leads to de-pendence and often results in depression and other sec-ondary consequences. The increased risks of injury from falling arise from poorer reaction time， osteoporosis，and， if the head is involved， more intracranial space， which al-|删除0换行|lows more shear to the dura and blood vessels. As many as one third of patients over the age of 65 report one or more falls per year. This rate dramatically increases over the age of 85. Women fall more often than men with es-timates as high as twice the rate of men. The major causes of falling include (in order)： accidents， gait disturbance， dizziness/vertigo， drop attacks (no loss of consciousness)， confusion，postural hypotension， visual disturbance，and syncope.62 The reasons for these causes include prima-rily age-related changes in posture and proprioception and the effects of medication(s).63 In the elderly， postural changes exhibit an extrapyrarnidal pattern of more flex-ion， a gait that involves shorter stride length and slower walking with increased muscle tone (stiffness). Increased sway is commonly the first sign of gait imbalance in the senior. Decreases in proprioception may be the result of normal aging； however， they are accelerated or auginented by dysfunction in the upper cervical spine and the result of diseases such as diabetes. Balance is coordinated through vestibular， visual， and proprioceptive interaction. Loss of one of these functions is more easily compensated for than loss or decrease of two. With poorer vision and/or prioprioceptive loss or decrease， the patient is at sub-stantial risk of loss of balance.

The most common causes considered would be medications (e.g.， antihypertensives) or the autonomic reflex blunting effect of diabetes. Interestingly， the management strategies of men differ from those of women.67 Men are more likely to limit flu-ids and traveling and， in fact， are more likely to see a physi-cian about incontinence. Stress incontinence (due to ure-thral hypermobility in women) is uncommon in men， although radical prostatectomy may increase stress on the external urethral sphincter. 【6】页码段删除-1:<u>#### Case vignette 1</u>

【7】A 63-year-old male with past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and atherosclerosis presented to the emergency room after he suddenly fell to the floor and was unable to get up. He found that his right arm and leg were paralyzed and he found it excessively difficult to speak or swallow.

【8】Neurologic examination showed that he had paralysis of his right side with increased, exaggerated deep tendon reflexes. Motor examination of the face was normal, however upon protrusion his tongue pointed toward his left side; the left side of his tongue was atrophic.

【9】The sensory exam indicated that pain and temperature were bilaterally normal from the body and face but there was loss of joint position sense (proprioception) from the right lower extremity. Examination of other cranial nerves was normal.

【10】页码间删除-1:<u>##### Discussion</u>

【11】Spastic paralysis of the right arm and leg indicates injury to the corticospinal tract somewhere along its length. The additional tongue signs place the corticospinal lesion above the cord, in the medulla, on the left side. The tongue usually points to the side of a lesion of the nucleus or fibers of CN XII. Atrophy of its muscles confirms a lower motor neuron lesion of the fibers of CN XII on the left side.

【12】Loss of proprioception from the right lower extremity is consistent with injury to the ventral-most fibers of the medial lemniscus on the left side. Absence of other sensory findings limits the area of involvement to the distribution of the penetrating branches of the vertebral or anterior spinal artery, which include the pyramids, exiting fibers of CN XII, and the medial lemniscus. The diagnosis for this patient is medial medullary syndrome.

【23】##### Discussion

【24】The patient's complaint of weakness of the left arm and leg and the confirmation of spastic paresis, most marked in the upper extremity, indicates involvement of the corticospinal tract, either at high cervical levels of the cord on the left or somewhere above the cord on the right. The finding of cranial nerve signs involving the right medial rectus and loss of papillary light reponse places the lesion above the cord and into the brainstem. More specifically, the right side of the midbrain, where the third cranial nerve nuclei and fascicles are located.

【25】The major cranial nerve sign involves the fibers of the right oculomotor nerve. The cause of the patient's complaint of diplopia is explained by the neurologic exam wherein the right medial rectus muscle is paralyzed upon attempted lateral gaze to the left and in convergence. Vision in optic nerves was normal but there was failure of the right pupil to constrict to light or upon convergence. This indicates injury to the parasympathetic component of the third nerve in addition to fibers supplying the extrinsic muscles of the eye and the eyelid (levator palpebrae). This places the lesion in the midbrain. The sensory examination was normal indicating that the tegmentum of the midbrain was spared. Except for a minor facial weakness cranial nerve motor functions were unaltered.

【26】These symptoms place the lesion in the crus cerebri, probably more medially since the arm was more severely affected than the leg, where oculomotor fibers exit into the interpeduncular fossa. 【7】A 63-year-old male with past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and atherosclerosis presented to the emergency room after he suddenly fell to the floor and was unable to get up. 【10】页码间删除-1:<u>##### Discussion</u>

【11】Spastic paralysis of the right arm and leg indicates injury to the corticospinal tract somewhere along its length. The additional tongue signs place the corticospinal lesion above the cord, in the medulla, on the left side. The tongue usually points to the side of a lesion of the nucleus or fibers of CN XII. Atrophy of its muscles confirms a lower motor neuron lesion of the fibers of CN XII on the left side.

【12】Loss of proprioception from the right lower extremity is consistent with injury to the ventral-most fibers of the medial lemniscus on the left side. Absence of other sensory findings limits the area of involvement to the distribution of the penetrating branches of the vertebral or anterior spinal artery, which include the pyramids, exiting fibers of CN XII, and the medial lemniscus. The diagnosis for this patient is medial medullary syndrome.

【23】##### Discussion

【24】The patient's complaint of weakness of the left arm and leg and the confirmation of spastic paresis, most marked in the upper extremity, indicates involvement of the corticospinal tract, either at high cervical levels of the cord on the left or somewhere above the cord on the right. The finding of cranial nerve signs involving the right medial rectus and loss of papillary light reponse places the lesion above the cord and into the brainstem. More specifically, the right side of the midbrain, where the third cranial nerve nuclei and fascicles are located.

【25】The major cranial nerve sign involves the fibers of the right oculomotor nerve. The cause of the patient's complaint of diplopia is explained by the neurologic exam wherein the right medial rectus muscle is paralyzed upon attempted lateral gaze to the left and in convergence. Vision in optic nerves was normal but there was failure of the right pupil to constrict to light or upon convergence. This indicates injury to the parasympathetic component of the third nerve in addition to fibers supplying the extrinsic muscles of the eye and the eyelid (levator palpebrae). This places the lesion in the midbrain. The sensory examination was normal indicating that the tegmentum of the midbrain was spared. Except for a minor facial weakness cranial nerve motor functions were unaltered.

【26】These symptoms place the lesion in the crus cerebri, probably more medially since the arm was more severely affected than the leg, where oculomotor fibers exit into the interpeduncular fossa. The sudden onset after coronary bypass surgery suggests a vascular infarct. The vessels supplying this area are the short penetrating paramedian branches of the basilar and posterior cerebral arteries. The diagnosis for this patient is Weber's syndrome.

【23】##### Discussion

【24】The patient's complaint of weakness of the left arm and leg and the confirmation of spastic paresis, most marked in the upper extremity, indicates involvement of the corticospinal tract, either at high cervical levels of the cord on the left or somewhere above the cord on the right. The finding of cranial nerve signs involving the right medial rectus and loss of papillary light reponse places the lesion above the cord and into the brainstem. More specifically, the right side of the midbrain, where the third cranial nerve nuclei and fascicles are located.

【25】The major cranial nerve sign involves the fibers of the right oculomotor nerve. The cause of the patient's complaint of diplopia is explained by the neurologic exam wherein the right medial rectus muscle is paralyzed upon attempted lateral gaze to the left and in convergence. Vision in optic nerves was normal but there was failure of the right pupil to constrict to light or upon convergence. This indicates injury to the parasympathetic component of the third nerve in addition to fibers supplying the extrinsic muscles of the eye and the eyelid (levator palpebrae). This places the lesion in the midbrain. The sensory examination was normal indicating that the tegmentum of the midbrain was spared. Except for a minor facial weakness cranial nerve motor functions were unaltered.

【26】These symptoms place the lesion in the crus cerebri, probably more medially since the arm was more severely affected than the leg, where oculomotor fibers exit into the interpeduncular fossa. The sudden onset after coronary bypass surgery suggests a vascular infarct. The vessels supplying this area are the short penetrating paramedian branches of the basilar and posterior cerebral arteries. The diagnosis for this patient is Weber's syndrome.

【7】A 63-year-old male with past medical history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and atherosclerosis presented to the emergency room after he suddenly fell to the floor and was unable to get up. He found that his right arm and leg were paralyzed and he found it excessively difficult to speak or swallow.

【8】Neurologic examination showed that he had paralysis of his right side with increased, exaggerated deep tendon reflexes. Motor examination of the face was normal, however upon protrusion his tongue pointed toward his left side; the left side of his tongue was atrophic.

【9】The sensory exam indicated that pain and temperature were bilaterally normal from the body and face but there was loss of joint position sense (proprioception) from the right lower extremity. Examination of other cranial nerves was normal.

<mark>【10】页码间删除-1:##### Discussion</mark>ion</u>

【11】Spastic paralysis of the right arm and leg indicates injury to the corticospinal tract somewhere along its length. The additional tongue signs place the corticospinal lesion above the cord, in the medulla, on the left side. The tongue usually points to the side of a lesion of the nucleus or fibers of CN XII. Atrophy of its muscles confirms a lower motor neuron lesion of the fibers of CN XII on the left side.

【12】Loss of proprioception from the right lower extremity is consistent with injury to the ventral-most fibers of the medial lemniscus on the left side. Absence of other sensory findings limits the area of involvement to the distribution of the penetrating branches of the vertebral or anterior spinal artery, which include the pyramids, exiting fibers of CN XII, and the medial lemniscus. The diagnosis for this patient is medial medullary syndrome.

【14】A 68-year-old female had coronary bypass surgery 2 weeks before she suddenly started to experience diplopia. She also felt a weakness in her left arm and leg. She was noted to have a ptosis of the right eye lid.

【15】At the hospital she was alert, awake, and fully oriented. Her general physical condition was good. Her speech was articulate and the content was good. Her visual fields were normal but when asked to open her eyes the right eyelid did not open fully. When asked to look straight ahead the right eye was deviated to the right. On attempted lateral gaze to the left only the left eye responded. When asked to look at the tip of her nose, only the left eye was adducted and only the left eye showed pupillary constriction. Furthermore, only the left eye was reactive to light.

【16】Upon smiling there was a minor weakness on the left. Her palate elevated symmetrically, gag reflex was normal, and corneal and jaw jerk responses were normal. The tongue protruded midline.

【17】Motor strength was normal in the extremities on the right but was reduced on the left, especially in the arm where there was an increased biceps reflex and resistance to passive stretch.

【18】Sensory examination was normal to all modalities for the face and the extremities.

<mark>【10】页码间删除-1:##### Discussion</mark>ion</u>

【11】Spastic paralysis of the right arm and leg indicates injury to the corticospinal tract somewhere along its length. The additional tongue signs place the corticospinal lesion above the cord, in the medulla, on the left side. The tongue usually points to the side of a lesion of the nucleus or fibers of CN XII. Absence of other sensory findings limits the area of involvement to the distribution of the penetrating branches of the vertebral or anterior spinal artery, which include the pyramids, exiting fibers of CN XII, and the medial lemniscus. The diagnosis for this patient is medial medullary syndrome.

【23】##### Discussion

【24】The patient's complaint of weakness of the left arm and leg and the confirmation of spastic paresis, most marked in the upper extremity, indicates involvement of the corticospinal tract, either at high cervical levels of the cord on the left or somewhere above the cord on the right. The finding of cranial nerve signs involving the right medial rectus and loss of papillary light reponse places the lesion above the cord and into the brainstem. More specifically, the right side of the midbrain, where the third cranial nerve nuclei and fascicles are located.

【25】The major cranial nerve sign involves the fibers of the right oculomotor nerve. The cause of the patient's complaint of diplopia is explained by the neurologic exam wherein the right medial rectus muscle is paralyzed upon attempted lateral gaze to the left and in convergence. Vision in optic nerves was normal but there was failure of the right pupil to constrict to light or upon convergence. This indicates injury to the parasympathetic component of the third nerve in addition to fibers supplying the extrinsic muscles of the eye and the eyelid (levator palpebrae). This places the lesion in the midbrain. The sensory examination was normal indicating that the tegmentum of the midbrain was spared. Except for a minor facial weakness cranial nerve motor functions were unaltered.

【26】These symptoms place the lesion in the crus cerebri, probably more medially since the arm was more severely affected than the leg, where oculomotor fibers exit into the interpeduncular fossa. The sudden onset after coronary bypass surgery suggests a vascular infarct. The vessels supplying this area are the short penetrating paramedian branches of the basilar and posterior cerebral arteries. The diagnosis for this patient is Weber's syndrome.

【13】**3.4.4 Treatment of Lewy body disease (and Parkinson’s disease with dementia)**

【14】**AIrecentsystematic review by Morrin， Fang， Servant， Aarsland， and Rajkumar ((2018) on the efficacy of nonpharmacological interventions in LBD revealed that there are only a few studies regarding nonpharmacologi-cal interventions in LBD. Further none of these studies had an evidence-based medicine level higher than three， which means that there are no con-trolled studies on this topic at all. The majority of these studies used brain stimulation (deep brain stimulation， transcranial direct current stimulation， etc.). Only one study focused on cognitive impairment and followed a single case design， therefore offering limited evidence. The results of this study dis-played a positive result for the cognitive intervention. However， on the back-ground of this review， it is impossible to argue whether a nonpharmacological treatment of LBD is possible or not.**

【15】**There are no definite guidelines for a pharmacological treatment of LBD. The tendency to develop visual hallucinations restricts the possibility of a dopaminergic treatment. On the other hand， LBD patients are hypersensitive to neuroleptic drugs， which might be helpful to reduce the hallucinations. The acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors may be beneficial in dampening the tendency to hallucinate， however， this is not always the case. The German guideline for dementia argues that memantine may reduce the neuropsychiat-ric symptoms in LBD patients. It should also be noted that the efficacy of acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors was shown for demented PD patients but not for patients with the clinical diagnosis of LBD. Thus the usage of these drugs in LBD might not routinely covered by the healthSsystem reimbursement.**

【23】**3.4.6 Summary**

【24】**Patients with LBD suffer from attentional deficits including short- and long-term attentional fluctuations. If LBD is suspected， relatives and the patient should be examined for such deficits (e.g.， by using the Mayo Fluctuation Scale) and through alertness and vigilance tests (as long as the patients tolerate such investigations). Cognitive fluctuations and visuoper-ceptive disorders are predictors for the existence of visual hallucination， which is a prominent sign of LBD. The screening test of the VOSP， the incomplete letters test of the VOSP， and the number location test of the VOSP can be used to explore the existence of visuoperceptive impair-ments. The screening test of the VOSP assesses the tendency to detect par-eidolias due to a local attention bias， the incomplete letters test concerns the ventral visual pathway and the numbers location test the dorsal visual pathway. If the patient is able to， a more strenuous copying task should be included as part of the assessment as opposed to the items of visuocon-struction of the CERAD-NAB. The exploration for visual hallucination should also include enquiries regarding REM sleep behavioral disorder and concerning dream-like states during the night and illusion of movement or objects in darkened room or in the evening. If visual hallucinations are present， one should exclude low-level visual deficits (retinopathy)， which may also lead to visual hallucination unrelated to the diagnosis of LBD.**

**There is a risk that patients with LBD might decompensate in response to being treated with neuroleptics. Thus acetylcholinesterase inhibitors might be implemented first to suppress visual hallucinations， and only afterwards low|删除0换行|dose neuroleptics. Up to now， it is unclear whether or not functional cogni-tive treatments have any effect.

【26】**3.5 Multisystem atrophy**

【27】**3.5.1 Clinical symptoms and neuropathological findings**

【28】**Contrary to PD， in MSA the alphasynuclein protein displays abnormal depositions mainly in astrocytes (not so much in neurons) and is concen-trated in areas of the autonomic nervous system (peripheral and central). Within a few years， patients develop rapidly progressing balance， speech， and coordination abnormalities 删除1:<u>(Palma et al.， 2018)</u>. The clinical diagnosis of MSAisnot very predictive of the postmortem-validated diagnosis删除1:<u>(Stankovic et al.， 2019)</u>. A recent study comparing MSA with the results of postmortem neuropathological examinations found that only 62% of the patients suffered from MSA and more than one-third from another disease删除1:<u>(Stankovic et al.， 2019)</u>. The misdiagnosed patients suffered from LBD， PSP， and PD. An incorrect diagnosis of MSA frequently occurs during the first visit (~40%). However， the likelihood of a correct diagnosis increases with the number of visits—up to 92% for patients with a probable MSA and 63%for patients with a possible MSA.**

【0】 visual deficits.**

【1】**Extraction and identification of shapes can be assessed by several neuro-psychological tests and specifically the VOSP 删除1:<u>(Warrington & James， 1991)</u> and the BORB 删除1:<u>(Humphreys & Riddoch， 1993)</u> has been used to study the relationship between test-related performance and visual hallucinations in PD and LBD patients. Fig. 3.16 shows one item of the incomplete letters test of the VOSP. If the participants are oriented to local and small areas of the spatial outlay， participants will report that they see an “C” 删除2:<u>(left upper margin of the figure)</u>； however， if they are oriented to the whole picture they should be able to perceive the letter“K”， which is the correct answer. Please note that the test contains two practice items to instruct the patients to look for the global shape of the figure.**

【2】**VOSP Incomplete Letters - requires the subject to identify sets of 20 objects degraded by removal of some edge information.**

通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 3.16** **Item from the incomplete letters task of the visual object and space perception** battery. From Gabrovska， v.s.， Laws， k.r.， Sinclair， j.， McKenna， p.j.， (2003). Visual object pro-cessing in schizophrenia： evidence for an associative agnosic deficit， Schizophrenia Research，59(2-3)，277-286.</u>|删除换行|patients during such tests and during working memory tasks. The study revealed that LBD patients are severely impaired in the incomplete letters， the object decision task of the VOSP and also in the digit span task， whereas AD patients did not differ in these tests from of healthy controls.**

【4】Mori et al. (2000) utilized tests from the BORB on size discrimination， form discrimination， visual counting， and overlapping figures. Compared to AD patients， LBD patients displayed impaired performances in visuopercep-tive tasks. Mori et al. (2000) also compared patients with LBD that suffered from visual hallucinations with those not suffering from visual hallucina-tions. Patients suffering from visual hallucinations presented more difficul-ties discriminating between overlapping figures than those without visual hallucination.

【5】These findings were the starting point of a series of studies from the group of Mori et al. regarding the possibility of distinguishing patients with LBD from patients with AD by provoking visual illusions and analyzing the relation to visuoperceptive deficits. Uchiyama et al. (2012)， for example， published a paper on pareidolias， that is， visual illusionary conjunctions pro-voked by real world photographed pictures. Fig. 3.17 shows pictures from their task， whereby the yellow arrowspoint to the segments where pareido-lias can be detected.

【6】通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 3.17 Example from the pareidolias task of the Uchiyama et al. (2012) study. Examples of illusory responses. Patients with dementia with Lewy bodies often misidentified objects or patterns in the picture as real faces (yellow triangle) or as figures of people and ani- _mals (white triangle)._**</u>

【7】**Healthy controls did not respond to the existence of the pareidolias spontaneously. Further patients with AD performed almost as well as healthy controls. Patients with LBD， however， demonstrated a significantly increased tendency to name the pareidolias. The study of Uchiyama et al.(2012) also replicated the former finding that LBD patients differed signif-icantly in shape detection， position discrimination， object decision and face recognition from patients with AD and from healthy controls. In another study including PD patients and healthy controls， Uchiyama et al.(2012) showed that PD patients also display an increased level of misiden-tifications compared to healthy controls； however， the rate of misidentifi-cations was less than one-fourth of the misidentifications of the LBD patients in the former study. The comparison of the PD patients in visuo-perceptive tests with healthy controls revealed a similar result. PD patients also expressed problems with the incomplete letters test， object decision， and the recurring figures test. Thus PD patients and LBD patients share similar qualitative problems in visuoperception but differ on a quantitative level.**

【8】**In another more recent study Yokoi et al. (2014) refined the pareidolias test by presenting black/white patterns， some of which included a small con-crete object， some of which did not .**

【9】**Again， patients with AD and healthy controls never responded to an item without an object with a false positive； however， patients with LBD pro-duced quite a number of false positive responses. In this investigation， Yokoi et al. (2014) distinguished between LBD patients with and without visual hallucinations. Both groups produced significantly more false positives than AD patients and healthy controls. LBD patients with visual hallucinations wrongly confirmed the presence of objects even more than those without visual hallucination. Furthermore this difference was more pronounced for faces than for animals 删除2:<u>(LBD patients reported seeing a face more often although the item did not entail any face-like structure)</u>. In a postmortem**

(2011) documented that the presence of visual halluci-nations correlates with the presence of Lewy bodies in the brain. The conver-gent findings of these studies are a strong argument that the presence of visual hallucination makes the diagnosis of an alphasynucleinopathy proba-ble. From a clinical standpoint， however， it should be added that there is one age-related ophthalmic syndrome defined by experiencing formed visual hal-lucinations： the Charles-Bonnet syndrome. The Charles-Bonnet syndrome is caused by a retinopathy most likely due to the loss of bottom-up innerva-tion. Patients suffering from Charles-Bonnet syndrome experience well-formed and fluid visual hallucinations. Therefore in clinical practice this dif-ferential diagnosis always should be taken into account (e.g.， by looking for severe impairments in visual acuity or asking for an ophthalmological assessment).**

【11】**Visual hallucinations are defined by seeing something that is not present. Closely related to the pathology of visual hallucinations， there is another neu-ropsychiatric syndrome which is more often present in LBD and PDD than in AD. This syndrome is called delusional misidentification and is usually restricted to relatives of patients with Capgras syndrome 删除1:<u>(Thiel， Studte， Hildebrandt， Huster， & Weerda， 2014)</u>. Patients with Capgras syndrome recog-nize the faces of relatives but do not believe that the subject with this face aligns with what their relatives really look like. In addition， for cognitive neuropsychological purposes， patients with the Capgras syndrome show almost no impairment in face recognition (i.e.， no prosopagnosia). However， patients with LBD suffer from face recognition problems， whereby these problems also correlate with their tendency to detect pareidolias 删除1:<u>(Uchiyama et al.， 2012)</u>.**

【12】**misidentification； however， Perini et al. (2016) stated that most of VaD patients had a diagnosis of mixed dementia. Therefore this high number may reflect a combined vascular and LBD.**

【13】**3.4.4 Treatment of Lewy body disease (and Parkinson’s disease with dementia)**

【14】**AIrecentsystematic review by Morrin， Fang， Servant， Aarsland， and Rajkumar ((2018) on the efficacy of nonpharmacological interventions in LBD revealed that there are only a few studies regarding nonpharmacologi-cal interventions in LBD. Further none of these studies had an evidence-based medicine level higher than three， which means that there are no con-trolled studies on this topic at all. The majority of these studies used brain stimulation (deep brain stimulation， transcranial direct current stimulation， etc.). Only one study focused on cognitive impairment and followed a single case design， therefore offering limited evidence. The results of this study dis-played a positive result for the cognitive intervention. However， on the back-ground of this review， it is impossible to argue whether a nonpharmacological treatment of LBD is possible or not.**

【15】**There are no definite guidelines for a pharmacological treatment of LBD. The tendency to develop visual hallucinations restricts the possibility of a dopaminergic treatment. On the other hand， LBD patients are hypersensitive to neuroleptic drugs， which might be helpful to reduce the hallucinations. The acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors may be beneficial in dampening the tendency to hallucinate， however， this is not always the case. The German guideline for dementia argues that memantine may reduce the neuropsychiat-ric symptoms in LBD patients. It should also be noted that the efficacy of acetylcholine- esterase inhibitors was shown for demented PD patients but not for patients with the clinical diagnosis of LBD. Thus the usage of these drugs in LBD might not routinely covered by the healthSsystem reimbursement.**

【16】**3.4.5 A case example**

【17】**A 72-year-old female patient reported severe dizziness while walking. She sees people that other people do not see and who seem to be not there. Sometimes her left hand does things without her intention， however， she was unable to provide an example for this.**

【18】The visual field showed no deficits， eye movements were unimpaired and there was no sign for a vertical gaze paresis or restriction of vertical sac-cades. Additionally the performance in the VOSP subtest “incomplete let-ters” and “number location” was impaired.

**She performed the Lurija bimanual coordination task without problems. The applause sign was unimpaired， however， the fist-edge-palm test revealed|删除0换行|problems in copying hand positions. Rey's complex understanding was too difficult and therefore its execution was discontinued. The results of the MMSE showed a score of 15， which corresponds to a moderate dementia. The patient expressed a friendly mood. The patient could not be assessed with Beck’s Depression Index (BDI) due to the severity of the cognitive impair-ments. The results of the CERAD-NAB are listed in Table 3.3， whereby a severe impairment in all assessed cognitive functions can be seen.

【23】**3.4.6 Summary**

【24】**Patients with LBD suffer from attentional deficits including short- and long-term attentional fluctuations. If LBD is suspected， relatives and the patient should be examined for such deficits (e.g.， by using the Mayo Fluctuation Scale) and through alertness and vigilance tests (as long as the patients tolerate such investigations). Cognitive fluctuations and visuoper-ceptive disorders are predictors for the existence of visual hallucination， which is a prominent sign of LBD. The screening test of the VOSP， the incomplete letters test of the VOSP， and the number location test of the VOSP can be used to explore the existence of visuoperceptive impair-ments. The screening test of the VOSP assesses the tendency to detect par-eidolias due to a local attention bias， the incomplete letters test concerns the ventral visual pathway and the numbers location test the dorsal visual pathway. If the patient is able to， a more strenuous copying task should be included as part of the assessment as opposed to the items of visuocon-struction of the CERAD-NAB. The exploration for visual hallucination should also include enquiries regarding REM sleep behavioral disorder and concerning dream-like states during the night and illusion of movement or objects in darkened room or in the evening. If visual hallucinations are present， one should exclude low-level visual deficits (retinopathy)， which may also lead to visual hallucination unrelated to the diagnosis of LBD.**

**There is a risk that patients with LBD might decompensate in response to being treated with neuroleptics. Thus acetylcholinesterase inhibitors might be implemented first to suppress visual hallucinations， and only afterwards low|删除0换行|dose neuroleptics. Up to now， it is unclear whether or not functional cogni-tive treatments have any effect.

【27】**3.5.1 Clinical symptoms and neuropathological findings**

Within a few years， patients develop rapidly progressing balance， speech， and coordination abnormalities 删除1:<u>(Palma et al.， 2018)</u>. 【0】rologic functions； i.e.， if a patient's arm is paralyzed or paretic， then fine motor coordination is difficult to assess； likewise， it would be unfair to label a patient as having severely impaired memory if the patient is aphasic.

【1】The Mental Status Examination

【2】A good mental status examination leaves no doubt about the patient's level of arousal for the next examiner. Terms like "sleepy，" "lethargic，""stuporous"may mean slightly different things to different examiners. The best mental status exam simply states what the patient can or cannot do. For example。 "The pa tienf was awake， watching television， and speaking normally，" or “The patient was asleep， arousable to tactile stimulation， but would fall back to sleep if un-stimulated."

【3】Remember to check basic and objective information. Is the patient oriented to person， place， and time? Assess the patient's attention. This is most easily done by having the patient repeat a series of random numbers， starting withL three numbers in 3 seconds and working up until the patient is no longer able to correctly repeat them (normal is five to seven numbers in as many seconds). This is known as the digit span. If a patient's attention is impaired， as demonstrated by a digit span of less than 5， then more complicated mental status testing may be difficult to interpret. For instance， a patient with a digit span of 3 is not likely to be able to remember three objects in 5 minutes， but this does not necessarily imply a primary memory problem and may just represent poor attention to the examiner. Impaired attention may mean simply that the patient is preoccupied or anxious or may signily an acute confusional state or encephalopathy.

【4】Speech is important to assess for both fluency (language output) and com-prehension (language input). An impairment of smooth and fluent output sug gests dysfunction of the dominant (usually left) frontal lobe (Broca's area)， while fluent output with an inabilily to understand spoken language indicates damage to the dominant parietar-temporal area (Wernicke's area). Difficully with both flu-ency and comprehension is usually the result of a more extensive dominant hemi-sphere lesion \[such as a middle cerebral artery infarct).

【5】Cranial Nerve Examination

Objeclive assessment of many of the cranial nerves (CNs) is possible， and thus brainstem function may be assessed even in comatose or otherwise uncooperative|删除0换行|patients. Abnormalities in the cranial nerve exam usually suggest underlying brainstem pathology.

【7】CN I： Sense of smell usually is not tested， but may be by asking the patient to identify a characteristic aroma with eyes closed (e.g.， coffee， flowers).

【8】CN II： Check visual fields to confrontation 删除2:<u>{Can patient see movement in all fields? Can patient count fingers in all fields?)</u> and look for consensual pupillary _reactivily._

【9】CN ⅢII， Ⅳ， VI： Have the patient follow the movement of light in all directions.

【10】Doll's eye maneuver (oculocephalic)-This is most useful in patients whose consciousness is impaired. A normal or positive response occurs when vigorousiy rotating the patient's head to one side， and the eyes deviate to the opposite side. An abnormal or negative response is when the eyes do not move in the orbits regardless of head position-the doll's eyes are absent. A fully conscious patient may be able to voluntarily override this reflex， resulting in a "false" nega-tive result.

【11】Cold calorics (oculovestibular)-ear canals are inspected for a clear view of the eardrums， the patient's head is hyperextended about 30°， and ice-cold water is irrigated into one ear canal A normal or positive response in an awake patient is deviation of the eyes toward the irrigated ear and nystagmus beating away from the irrigated ear. (Since awake patients can voluntarily move their eyes， and since cold calorics can be quite nauseating， calorics are seldom indi-cated in awake patients.) A normal or positive response in a comatose patient is deviation of the eyes toward the irrigated ear， with no nystagmus. An abnormal or negative response shows no eye deviation. After 5 minutes， repeat the test with the opposite ear.

【12】CN V： Ask the patient to close his/her eyes， touch (or use a pin to prick) the patient's face on the forehead， cheek， and chin on either side， and have the pa-tient identify specifically or point to the place touched.

【13】CN VII： Ask the patient to close his/her eyes tightly and look for the ability to "bury the eyelashes" symmetrically. Look for a symmetric smile. Ask the patient to "puff out his/her cheeks" and try to gently push the air out of the cheeks with your fingers. Ask the patient to clench his/her teeth together and look for sym-metric contraction of the platysma muscle \[stretches from the chin/ jaw to the clavicles).

【14】CN V/VII： Corneal test-A light wisp of colton or tissue is brushed gently against the cornea， approaching from the side (not from the front). A positive re-aPPI sponse is eye closure/blinking. This should be done on one eye， then the other. Corneals may be absent in patients with a history of contact lens use. This test is not routinely performed in awake patients.

【15】CN VIII： Whisper numbers (or lelters) into the patient's ear from a distance of about 1 foot and note if the patient can repeat the numbers.

CN IX/X： Gag test-Using a Qtip or tongue depressor， touch the back of the oropharynx on one side， then the other， and look for a gag with symmetric palate elevation. If the patient is intubated， a Qtip can still be used. Pulling on the endotracheal tube is not recommended as a method for testing the gag reflex. A decreased or absent gag sometimes can be found in otherwise|删除0换行|normal patients， but an asymmetric gag usually is indicative of brainstem pathology.

【17】CN XI： Against resistance， have the patient shrug his/her shoulders up(trapezius) and turn his/her head to one side \[sternocleidomastoid). Remember， difficully turning the head to the right indicates a weak left sternocleidomastoid， and vice versa.

【18】CN XII： Ask the patient to stick out his/her tongue. The tongue will deviate toward the weak side.

【19】**Motor Examination**

【20】Although the motor examination as typically discussed relies significantly on patient cooperation， there is a lot of objective information that can be elicited by a skilled examiner.

【21】Muscle bulk is very objective， and focal atrophy or fasciculations are a sign of chronic lower motor neuron disease (ALS， neuropathy， radiculopathy， some-times myopathy).

【22】Muscle tone can be assessed by passively moving a joint through its full range of motion. Flaccid tone offers little or no resistance， and the movement will seem limp. This demonstrates either an acute upper motor neuron lesion or a lower motor neuron lesion. Spastic tone offers more resistance the faster the movement. Spasticity is seen with subacute or chronic upper motor neuron injury{spinal cord injury， cerebral infarct， brain tumor， multiple sclerosis， ALS). Rigidily shows equal resistance throughout the entire range， regardless of the velocity of the movement. Occasionally rigidity has a ratchely quality， which is referred to as cogwheeling \[Parkinsonism， other basal ganglia disease). Experience aids greatly in the accurate evaluation of muscle tone.

【23】Pronator drift is an excellent method of testing for subtle corticospinal weakness. The patient is asked to hold both arms fully extended in front of him/herself with the palms up. The palms should be level and not touching each other. The patient must then maintain this position with the eyes closed. A _P_ positive drift (and hence， evidence of corticospinal weakness) is characterized by not only a downward movement of the affected side， but also pronation of that extremity.

【24】Subtle lower extremily weakness is suggested by external rotation of the hip at rest.

【25】Direct strength testing of individual muscles is graded on the following scale：

【26】No movement

【27】Twitch or faint movement
