【12】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【13】 Parathyroid hyperplasia: This is an unlikely diagnosis because only a single abnormality is present. Multiple foci of tracer activity would be expected with parathyroid hyperplasia.

【14】 Thyroid cancer: The absence of a palpable mass on physical examination, an elevated serum calcium level, and normal images obtained 10 minutes after radio-pharmaceutical administration make this diagnosis unlikely.

【15】 Thyroid adenoma: The history of hypercalcemia makes this diagnosis less likely. Furthermore, the abnormality on the MR image is located posterior to the thyroid gland.

【16】 Metastatic disease to a supraclavicular node: The lack of a history of a primary malignancy and absence of other abnormalities on the MRI study make this diagnosis unlikely, although it is not excluded.

【17】 Parathyroid adenoma: The presence of a single, focal abnormality on the Tc-99m sestamibi image in a patient with hypercalcemia makes parathyroid adenoma the most likely diagnosis.

【18】DIAGNOSIS

【19】Parathyroid adenoma

【20】KEY FACTS

【21】Clinical

【22】 Hyperparathyroidism is the result of increased para-thormone production. Two types of hyperparathyroid-ism are recognized—primary and secondary.

【23】 Primary hyperparathyroidism is due to endogenous hypersecretion of parathormone, which is caused by an adenoma (usually a solitary lesion) in 80% of cases, hyperplasia (usually of all four glands) in 10% to 15% of cases, and parathyroid carcinoma in about 5% of cases.

【24】 Secondary hyperparathyroidism results from hypocal-cemia causing stimulation of the parathyroid glands and increased parathormone production. It is usually secondary to renal failure but can be seen in malab-sorption and renal tubular disorders.

【25】 Tertiary hyperparathyroidism occurs when one or more glands hypertrophy due to secondary hyperpara-thyroidism and then function(s) autonomously.

【26】 Symptomatic patients with hyperparathyroidism and a radiologic or metabolic abnormality should be treated by surgery.

【27】 Persistent hypercalcemia after surgery for hyperpara-thyroidism occurs in 3% to 10% of cases and results from failure to remove all hyperfunctioning glands.

【28】 The combination of radionuclide imaging and new parathormone assays that can be performed very quickly (<15 minutes) and, hence, intraoperatively, permit decreased operative time and help in identifying all hyperfunctioning tissue, thereby facilitating total resection of all hyperfunctioning glands.

【29】Radiologic

【30】 The double-phase Tc-99m sestamibi study consists of early (10 to 20 minutes after radiopharmaceutical administration) and delayed (2 to 3 hours) imaging. It is very accurate for the localization of hyperfunctioning parathyroid tissue.

【31】 The double-phase technique is based on the more rapid tracer clearance from normal thyroid than from abnormal parathyroid tissue.

【32】 Tc-99m sestamibi is more accurate in localizing abnormal parathyroid tissue than other radionuclide techniques, such as sonography, CT, and MRI, which are also used for this purpose.

【33】 The detection rate of abnormal parathyroid tissue depends on the gland size. Adenomas are generally larger than hyperplastic glands (frequently <500mg) and, thus, more accurately detected.

【34】 Tc-99m sestamibi is very accurate in detecting ectopic parathyroid glands that cause hyperparathyroidism, but the abnormality must be within the field of view. Parallel-hole, high-resolution collimation is used to ensure that the neck and upper chest are included in the field of view.

【35】 Thyroid adenomas, thyroid carcinomas, and lymph nodes involved with sarcoidosis have been reported to cause false-positive results on Tc-99m sestamibi imaging studies for parathyroid adenoma evaluation.

【51】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【52】 High-grade urinary obstruction: This diagnosis is unlikely because the baseline study does not show a rising baseline renogram, as would be expected with high-grade obstruction.

【53】 Acute tubular necrosis: This diagnosis is very unlikely because there is no history of an appropriate precipitating event (e.g. an episode of hypotension) and because acute tubular necrosis would be expected to affect both kidneys in a symmetric fashion.

【54】 Unilateral renal artery stenosis: This is not the appropriate diagnosis because the function of both kidneys (rather than one kidney) worsened after administration of an angiotension-converting enzyme inhibitor.

【55】 Bilateral renal artery stenoses: This is the best diagnosis because the function of both kidneys decreased following enalaprilat administration. The findings in the left kidney are characteristic for severe renal artery stenosis—there is a change from an ascending/ descending pattern on the baseline cortical renogram to an ascending pattern after enalaprilat administration. The pattern in the right kidney, however, is also abnormal, with a prolonged cortical phase, significant residual tubular radiotracer activity relative to peak, and a 13% increase from the baseline study (which exceeds 10% from baseline, thereby meeting criteria for renal artery stenosis).

【56】 Chronic renal disease not causing hypertension: This diagnosis is unlikely because of the abnormal response to the angiotension converting enzyme inhibitor.

【57】DIAGNOSIS

【58】Bilateral renal artery stenoses (75% right kidney and 99% left kidney)

【59】KEY FACTS

【60】Clinical

【61】 Renal artery stenosis is a common cause of secondary hypertension and is present in 1% to 4% of hypertensive patients. It predominantly occurs in whites.

【62】 Renovascular hypertension is produced by excessive renin release, which itself results from a decrease in renal perfusion.

【63】 In 70% of cases, renovascular hypertension results from atherosclerotic stenosis.

【64】 Fibromuscular hyperplasia is the etiology in 30% of patients who have renovascular hypertension (being more common in women) and is the predominant cause of renovascular hypertension in adults <40 years of age.

【65】 The following clinical features increase the likelihood that hypertension is secondary to renal artery stenosis:

【66】>  Onset at age <20 and >50 years

【67】>  Abdominal bruit

【68】>  Atherosclerotic disease at other sites

【69】>  Abrupt deterioration of renal function after the administration of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors

【70】 Some patients may be managed medically if renal function does not deteriorate.

【71】 The use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors has improved the success rate of medical therapy.

【72】 However, patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis may develop marked hypotension and deterioration of renal function after administration of these agents.

【73】 Surgical treatment is generally successful, but percutaneous transluminal angioplasty is now the preferred approach for fibromuscular hyperplasia and discrete atherosclerotic lesions.

【74】Radiologic

【75】 Angiography is the gold standard diagnostic procedure for determining renal artery stenosis but has a number of drawbacks: (1) it is an invasive procedure, and (2) it provides an anatomic definition of the arterial luminal diameter but not the physiologic significance of a stenosis—that is, that hypertension is on a renovascular basis. Renal vein renin determination is also an invasive procedure and has not proved to be accurate in the diagnosis.

【76】 CT angiography (CTA) and MR angiography (MRA) is primarily used to evaluate for renal artery stenosis. These techniques have the advantage of: (1) being noninvasive, (2) having the ability to depict not only the lumen of the artery but also the wall and the surrounding soft tissue, and (3) having the ability to evaluate other abdominal organs such as the adrenal glands. Disadvantages of CTA and MRA include: (1) the requirement for intravenous contrast agents that may be con-traindicated if the patients have renal insufficiency, especially when the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is <30 mL/min, (2) the fact that MRA cannot visualize calcifications, and (3) the fact that CTA uses ionizing radiation. A limited MRA can be performed without intravenous contrast material using a white blood technique but the efficacy is lower.

【77】 Urography and conventional radionuclide scintigraphy have an unacceptably high rate of false-negative and false-positive results in the diagnosis of renovascular hypertension. Doppler ultrasonography also has variable sensitivity and specificity in the diagnosis of reno-vascular hypertension, particularly in larger patients.

【78】 Response of hypertension to renal artery angioplasty cannot be predicted from the degree of arterial stenosis alone but must be combined with provocative tests such as scintigraphy following the administration of angio-tensin-converting enzyme. Some patients with mild stenosis but positive angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor scintigraphy have substantial reduction in hypertensin following angioplasty, whereas patients with severe stenoses but negative scintigraphic studies do not generally respond to revascularization.

【91】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【92】 Myocardial infarction: Myocardial infarction would not be expected to have normal homogeneous radiotracer uptake on the resting Tl-201 study, making this diagnosis incorrect.

【93】 Myocardial ischemia: The development of a stress-induced perfusion defect that is not present on the resting perfusion image is the typical finding in myocardial ischemia. The findings in this case are most consistent with this diagnosis.

【94】 Attenuation artifact: Most often a problem in obese women, this artifact should be seen on both the rest and stress images. It usually involves the lower anterior wall and the anteroapex regions. The defect seen in the case presented is larger than that typically seen due to attenuation artifact. Furthermore, attenuation artifact would not be expected to involve the septum, as in the present case.

【95】 Artifact from a left bundle branch block: This elec-trocardiographic abnormality can create a reversible perfusion defect, but it most often involves primarily the interventricular septum and is not as extensive as the defect presented in this case.

【96】 Artifact from patient motion on the stress image: Motion artifact can create apparent perfusion defects that usually, though not exclusively, occur in the apex. This diagnosis is incorrect because the defect seen in the case presented is much more extensive than that expected from patient motion. In general, review of the raw data in a cine mode can often identify patient motion of a degree sufficient to create apparent perfu-sion defects.

【97】DIAGNOSIS

【98】Stress-induced myocardial ischemia in the vascular territory of the left anterior descending coronary artery

【99】KEY FACTS

【100】Clinical

【101】 The symptoms, pain location, and radiation patterns, as well as the precipitating factors of angina pectoris due to myocardial ischemia can be variable. If the clinical index of suspicion is sufficiently high—that is, a >10% probability that the patient has significant coronary artery disease—further evaluation is indicated.

【102】 The episode of unexplained syncope in this patient is worrisome because it may have been related to transient myocardial ischemia and a potentially fatal arrhythmia.

【103】 Based on this patient’s presentation and perfusion images, the diagnosis is significant coronary artery disease, which was documented at cardiac catheteriza-tion.

【104】 Prevention of myocardial infarction and left ventricular damage is a primary objective in the treatment of this patient.

【105】Radiologic

【106】 The scintigraphic findings in the case presented are the typical pattern seen with stress-induced myo-cardial ischemia. A perfusion defect following stress testing that is not seen on the resting image indicates segmental myocardial ischemia. The perfusion defect is secondary to altered blood flow during coronary artery dilatation that occurs in response to physical (e.g. exercise) or pharmacologic (e.g. dipyridamole or dobutamine) stress testing.

【107】 A fixed defect at rest and stress can be caused by either myocardial infarction or artifact due to attenuation of photons by surrounding soft tissue or noncardiac structures.

【108】 Myocardial perfusion imaging can be performed with Tl-201 alone, Tc-99m sestamibi alone, or as above, with a combination of the two agents. The dual isotope technique combines the advantage of Tl-201 (the preferred single-photon radiopharmaceutical for identifying viable myocardium) and the advantage of Tc-99m sestamibi (superior image quality following stress). The dual isotope technique also decreases overall imaging time.

【39】**OME years ago， a volume coauthored by me enti- _tled Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology 删除1:<u>(Lea 8 Febiger， Philadel-_ phia， 1982)</u> came to fruition. The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. 【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. 【156】UTIATE psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【39】**OME years ago， a volume coauthored by me enti- _tled Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology 删除1:<u>(Lea 8 Febiger， Philadel-_ phia， 1982)</u> came to fruition. The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical pres-entation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations although we did not deliberately and completely disre-gard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45 sections because the data presented here are our own.

During the 9 years in which this book was evolving， I was fortunate to collaborate with five fellows in dermatopathology at New York University. ClifWhite ran the first lap and handed the baton to Don King， who passed it|删除0换行|flawlessly to Jim Troy， who ran an extra lap before placing it securely in the hand of Les Rosen， who ran the anchor lap and crossed what we thought was the finish line. One additional lap had to be run by Suthep Jerasutus， who re-shot every photomicrograph in order to achieve extraordinary qual-ity that will delight the reader’s eye， mind， and mind’s eye. The ability， energy， aanndd assiduity of my fellows made “working” on this book a joy for me.**

【45】A special word of thanks is due Drs. Helmut Kerl， Alfred Kopf， Matthew Harris， Daniel Roses， Robert Hurwitz， Edward Wilson Jones， and Nopadon Noppakun for permitting us to use some of their clinical photographs； Wil-liam Atkinson for performing color corrections on all of the clinical photo-graphs； William Slue and Meryll Krolick for taking some of the clinical pic-tures； and Sherry Hutchison for painstakingly typing and retypingthe manuscript. I also appreciate the efforts of Tom Colaiezzi and Ken Bussy of Lea Febiger， who shepherded the work from manuscript to bound book a book painstakingly and lovingly designed by the incomparable Howard King.

【46】As has been true of virtually all of my writings during the past 13 years， Dr. Morris Leider kindly， carefully， and critically edited the manuscript from Preface to Glossary. Between the time that the manuscript was sub-mitted to the publisher and the time that the book was isin galleys， Morris magnitude of his loss for me， personally and professionally， is immeasurable.

【47】We hope that this book will be a useful adjunct to Sherlockian solving of histologic puzzles in dermatopathology， and will enable differential diagno-sis to become specific diagnosis.

【156】UTIATE psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【39】**OME years ago， a volume coauthored by me enti- _tled Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology 删除1:<u>(Lea 8 Febiger， Philadel-_ phia， 1982)</u> came to fruition. The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical pres-entation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations although we did not deliberately and completely disre-gard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45 sections because the data presented here are our own.

During the 9 years in which this book was evolving， I was fortunate to collaborate with five fellows in dermatopathology at New York University. ClifWhite ran the first lap and handed the baton to Don King， who passed it|删除0换行|flawlessly to Jim Troy， who ran an extra lap before placing it securely in the hand of Les Rosen， who ran the anchor lap and crossed what we thought was the finish line. One additional lap had to be run by Suthep Jerasutus， who re-shot every photomicrograph in order to achieve extraordinary qual-ity that will delight the reader’s eye， mind， and mind’s eye. The ability， energy， aanndd assiduity of my fellows made “working” on this book a joy for me.**

【156】UTIATE psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical pres-entation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations although we did not deliberately and completely disre-gard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45 sections because the data presented here are our own.

【156】UTIATE psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【156】UTIATE psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【39】**OME years ago， a volume coauthored by me enti- _tled Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology 删除1:<u>(Lea 8 Febiger， Philadel-_ phia， 1982)</u> came to fruition. The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical pres-entation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations although we did not deliberately and completely disre-gard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45 sections because the data presented here are our own.

During the 9 years in which this book was evolving， I was fortunate to collaborate with five fellows in dermatopathology at New York University. ClifWhite ran the first lap and handed the baton to Don King， who passed it|删除0换行|flawlessly to Jim Troy， who ran an extra lap before placing it securely in the hand of Les Rosen， who ran the anchor lap and crossed what we thought was the finish line. One additional lap had to be run by Suthep Jerasutus， who re-shot every photomicrograph in order to achieve extraordinary qual-ity that will delight the reader’s eye， mind， and mind’s eye. The ability， energy， aanndd assiduity of my fellows made “working” on this book a joy for me.**

【155】零碎段删除-1:<u>**G**<<mark>【154】人名段删除-1:Guttate Psoriasis Seborrheic Dermatitis</mark> have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【39】**OME years ago， a volume coauthored by me enti- _tled Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology 删除1:<u>(Lea 8 Febiger， Philadel-_ phia， 1982)</u> came to fruition. The text was concerned with 45 sets of skin diseases that cause difficulties in differential diagnosis because they have so many histologic features in common. During the preparation of that work， and in the intervening years， it became apparent to me that many more sets of diseases of the skin could be contrasted in like manner and with equal profit to colleagues who are faced， as I amn daily， with problems of differen-tial diagnosis. It was for this reason that 45 more paired sets of cutaneous diseases were selected for a second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Der- _matopalholog._**

【40】**_Theepurpose of this second volume is identical to that of the first as_ lescribedin its Preface in these words：**

【41】**In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a manner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphic statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted discases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are repro-duced in low and high magnification. Clinicalphotographspermit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【42】**The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted diseases have in com-mon， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appear-ances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical pres-entation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【43】We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and sometimes hun-dreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations although we did not deliberately and completely disre-gard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45 sections because the data presented here are our own.

During the 9 years in which this book was evolving， I was fortunate to collaborate with five fellows in dermatopathology at New York University. The ability， energy， aanndd assiduity of my fellows made “working” on this book a joy for me.**

【155】零碎段删除-1:<u>**G**<<mark>【154】人名段删除-1:Guttate Psoriasis Seborrheic Dermatitis</mark> have several histologic changes in common， among them mounds of para-keratosis containing neutrophils， slight focal thinning of the granular layer， slight epidermal hyperplasia， dilated vessels， and a sparse superficial peri-vascular predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate. Consistent major histologic differences between them enable these two inflammatory processes to be separated. In guttate psoriasis， there are an increased number of' mitotic figures in the epidermis， marked edema of the papillary dermis， and promi-nent tortuosity of blood vessels in the dermal papillae. In seborrheic dermatitis， there are abundant plasma in the mounds of parakeratosis， scale-crusts often situated at the lips of spongiotie follicular infundibula， follicular plugging by cornified cells， and solar clastosis.

【157】Guttate (i.e.， drop-sized) lesions of psoriasis are pink， slightly scaly papules that may presage progression to widespread， thick plaques with micaceous scales typical of psoriasis vulgaris， or these small lesions may be the only manifestation of psoriasis. A synonym for guttate psoriasis is erup-tive psoriasis， because often these lesions occur suddenly and are wide-spread. The cause of psoriasis is unknown， but a genetic predisposition and high familial incidence have been demonstrated in several studies. Interest-C1IrS ingly， one clinical setting in which guttate psoriasis occurs suddenly after streptococcal pharyngitis has been associated with HLA-A 13. These pa-tients often have “spontaneous”remission of their cutaneous lesions， and if they develop psoriasis it is usually slight.

【158】As eruptive or guttate psoriasis evolves with time into thick plaques of psoriasis， some histologic features of eruptive psoriasis continue while new ones develop. Dilated and tortuous vessels in the papillary dermis that al-most touch the undersurface of the epidermis are present at each stage. The mounds of parakeratosis are surmounted by neutrophils， which with time become more numerous. In addition， there is more thinning of the suprapapillary plates and thinning of the granular layer， with marked lengthening of the epidermal rete ridges， which are often thinned but of remarkably even lengths. Edema of the papillary dermis is prominent， espe-cially in fully developed plaques， but there is usually less epidermal spongio-sis than is seen in earlier lesions.

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common， scaly inflammatory disease that may occur at any age and that tends to be chronic. It is， in most instances， readily recognized clinically and， therefore， biopsy is seldom performed. When a lesion is biopsied， the pre-operative clinical diagnosis is usually lupus erythematosus. Seborrheic dermatitis begins as erythematous mac-|删除0换行|ules that become confluent to form patches， but the macules are not the discrete guttate lesions that are noted in psoriasis. There is a gradual pro-gression to slightly raised， profusely scaly lesions. The scale-crusts often appear shiny and feel crumbly because of plasma within them. The ana-tomic areas most commonly affected， referred to as the seborrheic areas， are the scalp， sideburns， eycbrows， cyelashes， malar areas of the cheeks and nasolabial folds， and the presternal， interscapular， and axillary regions. The scalp and groin are especially and commonly involved in infants.

【160】Seborrheic dermatitis is a common condition， much more common than is psoriasis. In infants， this disease oftcn appears as so-called cradle cap， which responds readily to local treatment with "keratolytic”shampoos and topical corticosteroids. Rarely， both infants and adults may develop widespread seborrheic dermatitis sufficient to result in erythroderma. One very unusual syndrome is Leiner’s disease， originally called erythrodermia desquamativa， in which infants develop a widespread， scaly， seborrheic der-matitis-like eruption with confluent redness of the entire face that is associ-ated with severe diarrhea， failure to thrive， and a functional defect in one component of complement， C5a. The eruption in Leiner’s disease is not true seborrheic dermatitis， any more than is the seborrheic-like dermatitis of Letterer-Siwe disease authentic seborrheic dermatitis. Clincially and histo-logically the latter disease is histiocytosis X.

【161】Occasionally， a pink， scaly eruption in "seborrheic" areas may re __ semblepsoriasis. The term inverse psoriasis is used for it when there are other more clearly diagnostic areas involved with psoriasis. When no such clues exist to enable precise diagnosis， the terms sebo-psoriasis or seborrhiasis have been employed. These terms are misleading because they imply that the condi-tion is a combination of both seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis， when， in fact， it is almost always one or the other. SeborTheic dermatitis usually has a straightforward clinical appearance. Psoriasis， in contrast， has numerous clinical manifestations， including pustules， nail pits with onycholysis， geo-graphic tongue， and tinea amiantacea (localized psoriasis in the form of very thick， asbestos-like plaques on the scalp).

【24】_6\._ Inflammation of the pericardium may be secondary to an infection， usually viral， but bacterial， mycobacterial， and other etiologies are possible. Inflam-mation also may occur as a result of direct injury to the pericardium， such as post-cardiac surgery， or from chest trauma. Adiacent inflammation of the lung， as occurs with pulmonary embolism， or the heart， as occurs with acute my-ocardial infarction， also can cause pericarditis. Myocardial infarction may cause an acute pericardial effusion or a later， autoimmune phenomenon called Dressler's syndrome. Dressler’s syndrome also can occur after cardiac surgery. Other collagenvascular diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or systemic lupus erythematosus commonly cause pericardial disease. Pericarditis is also one of the cardiac manifestations of rheumatic fever. Systemic illnesses such as uremia and hypothyroidism can cause pericardial inflammation and effusion. Finally， certain drugs may cause pericardial disease and/or effusion including hy-dralazine， procainamide， and minoxidil.

【39】ENDOCRINOLOGY

【40】General Considerations

【41】Endocrine disorders present in myriad ways and are a category in the MEDI-CINE DOC mnemonic. Critical to the understanding of these disorders is the con-cept of a stimulatory signal ("trophic" hormone) from a remote source and a target gland that produces the "effector" hormone. Feedback from the target organ or from a metabolic product further downstream is often responsible for the subsequent inhibition of the trophic hormone. Because of this regulatory system， endocrine disorders may result from dysfunction of the stimulatory or the effector organs. When considering endocrine disease， think about the consequences of hyper- and hypo-function of each effector gland and its stimulatory gland.

【42】Note that standard endocrinologic testing is best done in an out patient setting when the patient is in a stable state of health. Acute illnesses in hospitalized patients can unpredictably alter hormona testing and make test interpretation unreliable.

【43】Pituitary/Hypothalamus

【44】The pituitary is the master， or "TOP GLAND，"  because it produces six major hormones (TSH， prolactin， growth hormone， the gonadotropins LH and FSH， and ACTH)， and stores two others (ADH and oxytocin). The pituitary-hypo-thalamic axis is a tripartite system consisting of the anterior pituitary ("TOP GLA")， the posterior pituitary or neurohypophysis ("N") and the hypothalamus ("D"). The posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of an area of the hypothalamus. The optic chiasm lies anterior and superior to the pituitary gland and is compressed by anterior pituitary neoplasms causing visual field defects. Visual symptoms may be the first sign of a pituitary tumor. The anterior pituitary is a major producer of en-dogenous opiates， including endorphins， enkephalins， and dynorphins.

There is considerable variability in hair growth in normal men and women； thus abnormal hair growth is difficult to define.

【124】2\. The clinical scenario dictates the diagnostic evaluation of hirsutism.Poly cystic ovary disease ("PCOD") is one of the most common causes of pathologic hirsutism and is subacute in onset. Rapid onset and frank virilization are charac-teristic of malignancies and mandate complete evaluation.

【125】3\. The history should focus on drug ingestion， family history， and menstrual his-tory. 【130】8\. Patients with Cushing's syndrome may not always have hirsutism. Glucocorticoids suppress adrenal androgen production. ACTH stimulates androgen production.

【146】1\. Primary adrenocortical deliciency is rare， but secondary (due to steroid ther-apy) is relatively common. Adrenal insufficiency may be unmasked by stress due to， for example， systemic illness or infection.

【147】2\. Causes of adrenal insufficiency include anatomic destruction of the adren-als(autoimmune destruction， surgical removal， infection， hemorrhage， or metastatic invasion)， metabolic failure (congenital adrenal hyperplasia or enzyme inhibitors such as metapyrone or ketoconazole)， ACTH-blocking anti-bodies， suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis due to steroid therapy， and hypopituitarism secondary to hypothalamic-pituitary disease.

【148】3\. Primary adrenal insufficiency may be part of a polyglandular autoimmune syndrome. Associated conditions include lymphocytic thyroiditis， premature ovar-ian failure， diabetes， and hyperthyroidism. Additional disorders include perni-cious anemia， vitiligo， alopecia， sprue， and myasthenia gravis.

【149】4\. Laboratory diagnosis of adrenal insufficiency requires ACTH stimulation lesting to assess adrenal reserve capacity for steroid production. Serum and uri-nary steroid levels may be in the normal range in mild adrenal insufficiency， and therefore are not reliable for diagnosis. Basal levels of cortisol and aldosterone may be subnormal， but definitive diagnosis is obtained when they fail to in-crease after ACTH stimulation.

【150】5\. Consider adrenal insufficiency in any patient on steroid therapy， since dura-tion of therapy cannot reliably predict which patients will have suppression of the adrenal axis. Patients on steroid therapy who have significant intercurrent ill-ness should be given stress-dose steroids empirically while acutely ill.

【151】6\. Solumedrol and prednisone interfere with the ACTH stimulation test. Hydrocortisone therapy makes interpretation of the test difficult， as well. In a pa tient with suspected adrenal insufficiency， dexamethasone may be given acutely， as it will not interfere with the ACTH stimulation test. Both solumedrol and pred-nisone are ultimately converted to prednisolone， which directly interferes with the cortisol assay. Hydrocortisone also directly interferes with the cortisol assay. Dexamethasone does not interfere， but if it is given over several days it can sup-press the adrenal axis. Dexamethasone also has very little mineralocorticoid effect and may not improve hypotension as dramatically as hydrocortisone.

Adiacent inflammation of the lung， as occurs with pulmonary embolism， or the heart， as occurs with acute my-ocardial infarction， also can cause pericarditis. 【40】General Considerations

【41】Endocrine disorders present in myriad ways and are a category in the MEDI-CINE DOC mnemonic. Critical to the understanding of these disorders is the con-cept of a stimulatory signal ("trophic" hormone) from a remote source and a target gland that produces the "effector" hormone. Feedback from the target organ or from a metabolic product further downstream is often responsible for the subsequent inhibition of the trophic hormone. Because of this regulatory system， endocrine disorders may result from dysfunction of the stimulatory or the effector organs. When considering endocrine disease， think about the consequences of hyper- and hypo-function of each effector gland and its stimulatory gland.

【42】Note that standard endocrinologic testing is best done in an out patient setting when the patient is in a stable state of health. Acute illnesses in hospitalized patients can unpredictably alter hormona testing and make test interpretation unreliable.

【43】Pituitary/Hypothalamus

【44】The pituitary is the master， or "TOP GLAND，"  because it produces six major hormones (TSH， prolactin， growth hormone， the gonadotropins LH and FSH， and ACTH)， and stores two others (ADH and oxytocin). The pituitary-hypo-thalamic axis is a tripartite system consisting of the anterior pituitary ("TOP GLA")， the posterior pituitary or neurohypophysis ("N") and the hypothalamus ("D"). The posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of an area of the hypothalamus. The optic chiasm lies anterior and superior to the pituitary gland and is compressed by anterior pituitary neoplasms causing visual field defects. Visual symptoms may be the first sign of a pituitary tumor. The anterior pituitary is a major producer of en-dogenous opiates， including endorphins， enkephalins， and dynorphins.

【40】General Considerations

【41】Endocrine disorders present in myriad ways and are a category in the MEDI-CINE DOC mnemonic. Critical to the understanding of these disorders is the con-cept of a stimulatory signal ("trophic" hormone) from a remote source and a target gland that produces the "effector" hormone. Feedback from the target organ or from a metabolic product further downstream is often responsible for the subsequent inhibition of the trophic hormone. Because of this regulatory system， endocrine disorders may result from dysfunction of the stimulatory or the effector organs. When considering endocrine disease， think about the consequences of hyper- and hypo-function of each effector gland and its stimulatory gland.

【42】Note that standard endocrinologic testing is best done in an out patient setting when the patient is in a stable state of health. Acute illnesses in hospitalized patients can unpredictably alter hormona testing and make test interpretation unreliable.

【43】Pituitary/Hypothalamus

【44】The pituitary is the master， or "TOP GLAND，"  because it produces six major hormones (TSH， prolactin， growth hormone， the gonadotropins LH and FSH， and ACTH)， and stores two others (ADH and oxytocin). The pituitary-hypo-thalamic axis is a tripartite system consisting of the anterior pituitary ("TOP GLA")， the posterior pituitary or neurohypophysis ("N") and the hypothalamus ("D"). The posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of an area of the hypothalamus. The optic chiasm lies anterior and superior to the pituitary gland and is compressed by anterior pituitary neoplasms causing visual field defects. Visual symptoms may be the first sign of a pituitary tumor. The anterior pituitary is a major producer of en-dogenous opiates， including endorphins， enkephalins， and dynorphins.

【3】5.Here is a mnemonic for the differential diagnosis of pericarditis：

【24】_6\._ Inflammation of the pericardium may be secondary to an infection， usually viral， but bacterial， mycobacterial， and other etiologies are possible. Inflam-mation also may occur as a result of direct injury to the pericardium， such as post-cardiac surgery， or from chest trauma. Adiacent inflammation of the lung， as occurs with pulmonary embolism， or the heart， as occurs with acute my-ocardial infarction， also can cause pericarditis. Myocardial infarction may cause an acute pericardial effusion or a later， autoimmune phenomenon called Dressler's syndrome. Dressler’s syndrome also can occur after cardiac surgery. Other collagenvascular diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or systemic lupus erythematosus commonly cause pericardial disease. Pericarditis is also one of the cardiac manifestations of rheumatic fever. Systemic illnesses such as uremia and hypothyroidism can cause pericardial inflammation and effusion. Finally， certain drugs may cause pericardial disease and/or effusion including hy-dralazine， procainamide， and minoxidil.

【39】ENDOCRINOLOGY

【40】General Considerations

【41】Endocrine disorders present in myriad ways and are a category in the MEDI-CINE DOC mnemonic. Critical to the understanding of these disorders is the con-cept of a stimulatory signal ("trophic" hormone) from a remote source and a target gland that produces the "effector" hormone. Feedback from the target organ or from a metabolic product further downstream is often responsible for the subsequent inhibition of the trophic hormone. Because of this regulatory system， endocrine disorders may result from dysfunction of the stimulatory or the effector organs. When considering endocrine disease， think about the consequences of hyper- and hypo-function of each effector gland and its stimulatory gland.

【42】Note that standard endocrinologic testing is best done in an out patient setting when the patient is in a stable state of health. Acute illnesses in hospitalized patients can unpredictably alter hormona testing and make test interpretation unreliable.

【43】Pituitary/Hypothalamus

【44】The pituitary is the master， or "TOP GLAND，"  because it produces six major hormones (TSH， prolactin， growth hormone， the gonadotropins LH and FSH， and ACTH)， and stores two others (ADH and oxytocin). The pituitary-hypo-thalamic axis is a tripartite system consisting of the anterior pituitary ("TOP GLA")， the posterior pituitary or neurohypophysis ("N") and the hypothalamus ("D"). The posterior pituitary is essentially an extension of an area of the hypothalamus. The optic chiasm lies anterior and superior to the pituitary gland and is compressed by anterior pituitary neoplasms causing visual field defects. Visual symptoms may be the first sign of a pituitary tumor. The anterior pituitary is a major producer of en-dogenous opiates， including endorphins， enkephalins， and dynorphins.
