【7】CASE 28

【8】GLEN A. TOOMAYAN

【9】HISTORY

【10】A 27-year-old woman with 2-year history of enlarging nontender left lower leg mass.

【11】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-28A Axial fat-suppressed T2-weighted image through the lower leg demonstrates a large, well-defined, rounded mass arising within the posterior soft tissues of the calf. The mass is hyperintense with areas of hypointensity centrally.</u>

【12】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-28B Axial T1-weighted Image at the same location as in (A) demonstrates the mass to be homogeneously hypoin-tense. The mass arises in an intermuscular location between the soleus and gastrocnemius musculature.</u>

【13】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-28C Axial T1-weighted image after the intravenous administration of gadolinium demonstrates heterogeneous enhancement of this mass with areas of relative hypoenhancement centrally.</u>

【14】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-28D Sagittal fat-suppressed T2-weighted image demonstrates the fusiform shape of this mass. A peripheral nerve is seen leading into the superior aspect of the mass and away from the inferior aspect of the mass.</u>

【15】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【16】 Peripheral nerve sheath tumor: The mass is well defined and demonstrates hyperintensity on T2-weighted images with heterogeneous hypointensity centrally, referred to as the “target sign.” The mass is fusiform in shape and is located between muscle layers. A peripheral nerve is seen leading into and away from this mass. These are all features that are typical of benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors.

【17】 Hematoma: While hematomas can mimic other soft tissue masses, the relatively diffuse enhancement as well as the shape and location of this mass exclude this possibility. In this particular case, the history would also exclude this diagnosis.

【18】 Soft tissue sarcoma: While this diagnosis cannot be entirely excluded, it is unlikely in this case given the constellation of imaging findings described above that are characteristic of a nerve sheath tumor. There are many cases of enhancing soft tissue masses that cannot be reliably characterized as benign lesions. In these cases, soft tissue sarcomas would need to be included in the differential diagnosis. This patient was referred to an orthopaedic oncologic surgeon who performed a core needle biopsy to confirm the diagnosis of a benign schwannoma.

【19】DIAGNOSIS

【20】Peripheral nerve sheath tumor, in this case a schwannoma

【21】KEY FACTS

【22】Clinical

【23】 Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors are characterized as schwannomas and neurofibromas, both of which arise from the Schwann cell within peripheral nerves.

【24】 Schwannomas are distinguished from neurofibromas histologically by alternating Antoni A and B regions and the presence of large quantities of S-100 protein by immunohistochemical analysis.

【25】 Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors usually present as painless, slow growing masses.

【26】 Neurofibromas most frequently affect patients between the ages of 20 and 30.

【27】 Most neurofibromas are solitary. Only 10% of neurofibromas occur in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1). Multiple neurofibromas can be seen in patients with NF-1.

【28】 Peripheral neurofibromas typically arise from small peripheral nerves in the skin and subcutaneous tissues although they can also arise from deeper peripheral nerves.

【29】 Neurofibromas may be localized, diffuse, or plexiform. Plexiform neurofibromas involve a long nerve segment and its branches and are pathognomonic for NF-1.

【30】 Schwannomas are slightly less common than neurofi-bromas and occur most frequently in patients between 20 and 50 years of age.

【31】 Most schwannomas are solitary and are not associated with NF-1.

【32】 Schwannomas most commonly occur in the head and neck and along major nerve trunks.

【33】 Treatment of benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors is usually surgical resection. Schwannomas are generally separable from the nerve after incising the epineurium, allowing nerve function to be spared. Neurofibro-mas are usually inseparable from the nerve, meaning tumors arising from deep nerves are often partially resected or debulked to preserve nerve function.

【34】 Malignant nerve sheath tumors account for 5% to 10% of all soft tissue sarcomas. While 25% to 75% of malignant tumors arise in patients with NF-1, only 5% to 13% of patients with NF-1 develop malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.

【35】 Malignant tumors usually present as rapidly enlarging, painful masses.

【36】Radiologic

【37】 Schwannomas and neurofibromas are indistinguishable by imaging.

【38】 Deep peripheral nerve sheath tumors grow in fusiform fashion along the long axis of the nerve. The fusiform shape is the most reliable indicator of a peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

【39】 These masses classically taper at either end and the nerve from which the tumor arises may be seen to enter and exit the mass.

【40】 Nerve sheath tumors demonstrate nonspecific hypoin-tense signal intensity on T1-weighted images and hyperintense signal intensity on T2-weighted images, and usually demonstrate heterogeneous enhancement after the intravenous administration of gadolinium.

【41】 The mass may demonstrate a central region of lower signal intensity on T2-weighted images known as the “target sign.” This results from greater fluid content within myxoid tissue at the periphery of the mass. The central hypointense component corresponds to collag-enous or fibrous tissue.

【42】 The “fascicular sign” may be seen on T2-weighted imaging as multiple small circular structures within the mass with surrounding hyperintensity. This is attributed to nerve fascicles within the mass.

【43】 The “split fat sign” is a rim of hyperintense tissue on T1-weighted images surrounding the tumor. This is seen when a nerve sheath tumor arises in an intermuscular location and is surrounded by intermuscular fat.

【44】 Muscle atrophy is a variable finding that may be seen in a muscle supplied by the affected nerve.

【45】 Schwannomas are more likely to be located eccentrically along the course of a nerve while neurofibromas are more likely to be situated centrally.

【46】 Schwannomas are more likely to demonstrate cystic components than neurofibromas.

【47】 Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors may appear similar to benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors by imaging. Imaging findings that may suggest malignancy include large size (>5 cm) and poorly defined margins with infiltration of surrounding structures.

【53】CASE 29

【54】人名段删除-1:<u>DAVID K. KRUG</u>

【55】HISTORY

【56】A 16-year-old female who injured her knee while playing softball.

【57】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-29A Sagittal fat suppressed FSE T2-weighted MRI of the knee. High signal intensity in the lateral femoral condyle consistent with bone contusion.</u>

【58】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-29B Sagittal fat suppressed FSE T2-weighted MRI of the knee. High signal intensity in the inferomedial patella consistent with bone contusion. Joint effusion with fluid-fluid level consistent with hemarthrosis. Osteochondral fragment is seen in the anterior intercondylar notch.</u>

【59】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURE 5-29C Axial fat suppressed FSE T2-weighted MRI of the knee. High signal intensity in the inferomedial patella and anterolat-eral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle consistent with “kissing” bone contusions. There is associated chondral injury of the medial patellar facet.</u>

【60】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【61】 Transient patellar dislocation (TPD): This diagnosis is favored given the constellation of findings including bone contusions of the anterolateral lateral femoral condyle and inferomedial patella, medial patellar chon-dral injury, loose body and hemarthrosis.

【62】 Acute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Contusions in the lateral femoral condyle are often seen with acute ACL tears. The classic pivot shift contusion in acute ACL injury involves the lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral tibial plateau. Contusion of the medial patella is not associated with this injury.

【63】 Direct trauma: Direct blow to the lateral knee, such as seen in clipping injury in football players, can result in bone contusions about the knee most commonly in the lateral femoral condyle. This diagnosis would not account for the patellar contusion or osteochondral defect, and is therefore not the best diagnosis.

【64】DIAGNOSIS

【65】Transient patellar dislocation

【66】KEY FACTS

【67】Clinical

【68】 Classic mechanism of TPD is internal rotation of the femur on a fixed tibia while the knee is flexed. Contraction of the quadriceps results in net lateral force on the patella and dislocation. Direct blow to the medial knee may also result in lateral patellar dislocation.

【69】 Comprises 9% to 16% of all acute knee trauma in young athletes with hemarthrosis. Dislocation is usually transient with spontaneous relocation, and most patients do not realize this type of injury has occurred.

【70】 It is estimated that 50% to 75% of all patellar dislocations are incorrectly diagnosed at initial clinical evaluation. MRI can accurately diagnose suspected or occult patellar dislocation, and is useful for evaluation of the extent of associated soft tissue injuries and intra-articular abnormalities.

【71】 Surgical management may be indicated for significant osteochondral defects, loose bodies, or associated meniscal or ligamentous injuries.

【72】Radiologic

【73】 Mechanism of injury results in a characteristic pattern of bone marrow contusions involving the lateral femoral condyle, which is seen in up to 100% of patients on MRI, and the inferomedial patella.

【74】 Injury to the medial retinacular complex is invariably present, and is commonly seen on MRI.

【75】 Joint effusion or hemarthrosis is almost always present in the acute setting, and is often large.

【76】 Close evaluation of the cartilage is extremely important, as chondral injuries of the patellofemoral joint and of the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle are common in these patients, and in some cases indicate surgical management. Osteochondral loose bodies are seen in up to one third of patients.

【77】 Other MRI findings may include lateral patellar tilt or subluxation, injury to Hoffa’s infrapatellar fat pad, and shallow femoral trochlea.

【85】CASE 30

【86】人名段删除-1:<u>KAVITA M. PATEL</u>

【87】HISTORY

【88】A 19-year-old female college student with 4 months of wrist pain.

【89】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURES 5-30A and 5-30B AP (A) and lateral (B) radiographs demonstrate a large, somewhat expansile lucent lesion centered in the distal radial epiphysis, with a narrow zone of transition, which extends to the distal radius subchondral bone. The lesion does not have a sclerotic margin and there is no evidence of internal matrix.</u>

【90】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURES 5-30C and 5-30D Coronal Tl-weighted (C) and axial fat-suppressed FSE T2-weighted (D) images demonstrate a solid lesion of decreased signal intensity on the Tl-weighted image and increased signal intensity on the T2-weighted image, which is a nonspecific appearance. The axial image demonstrates the expansile nature of the mass along the volar aspect of the radius.</u>

【91】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【92】 Giant cell tumor (GCT) of bone: This is the best diagnosis given the location of the lytic lesion in the meta-epiphysis of a long bone, extending into the subchondral bone. The lesion meets the criteria for a GCT of a long bone, given lack of sclerotic margin, lack of internal matrix, and occurring in a patient with closed physes.

【93】 Aneurysmal Bone Cyst (ABC): This is a possible diagnosis as ABCs can occur in the epiphysis of long bones (though they do not have to), and the lesion in this case is mildly expansile and occurring in a patient <30 years old, which are features typical of ABCs. However, ABCs usually have fluid-fluid levels demonstrated on MR imaging, which is not seen in this case.

【94】 Intra-osseous ganglion or large subchondral cyst: On plain x-ray, intra-osseous ganglion is a well-circumscribed lucent lesion with a sclerotic rim, most frequently seen in the medial malleolus of the tibia, carpal bones, femoral head or acetabulum. It is thought to be due to osseous penetration of a soft tissue ganglion or perhaps proliferation of synovial rests. These lesions are usually not painful, unless associated with inflammatory or degenerative arthritis, which is not evident in this case. Also, these lesions are usually cystic, rather than solid, on MRI.

【95】 Chondroblastoma: Chondroblastoma is an epiphyseal lytic lesion with a narrow zone of transition usually seen in skeletally immature individuals. Chondroblastoma typically demonstrates a peripheral rim of sclerosis and can contain chondroid matrix. Chondroblastoma often elicits thick metaphyseal periostitis, remote from the epiphyseal location of the lesion, which is not seen in this case.

【96】 Metastasis/Myeloma: Metastatic or myelomatous lesions are the most common cause for a lytic lesion in individuals over 50, and these lesions can occur in the epiphysis. The patient’s young age in this case makes this a very unlikely diagnosis.

【97】DIAGNOSIS

【98】Giant cell tumor (GCT) of bone

【99】KEY FACTS

【100】Clinical

【101】 GCT of bone is a relatively common benign bone neoplasm which almost always occurs in skeletally mature patients, most commonly presenting in the third or fourth decade. Patients usually present with pain. Sometimes localized swelling, decreased range of motion or a pathologic fracture is present.

【102】 Women are affected slightly more commonly than men, although malignant GCT is more common in men (3:1).

【103】 Approximately 10% of GCTs are “malignant.” Determination of malignancy is made either by histology or by the presence of pulmonary metastases, as even benign GCTs may demonstrate “aggressive” features (such as cortical disruption and soft tissue mass) at imaging. A rare subtype, “benign metastasizing GCT,” presents with pulmonary metastases that are histologically identical to benign GCT. The majority of malignant GCTs are due to irradiation of a previously documented GCT.

【104】 Multifocal GCTs of bone are rare. There is a rare, possibly familial, association of multiple GCTs with Paget’s disease.

【105】 Definitive treatment consists of intralesional surgical resection. Marginal resections are associated with a higher recurrence rate (40% to 60%) than newer techniques utilizing extended surgical margins and bone grafting or methylmethacrylate packing of the defect (<25% recurrence rate).

【106】Radiologic

【107】 The characteristic radiographic appearance of GCT of bone is an eccentric lytic lesion in the meta-epiphysis of a long bone, although large lesions often appear more central. The lesion extends into the subchondral bone, causing the appearance of extension to the articular surface. There is usually a narrow zone of transition, and surrounding sclerosis is extremely rare. As these tumors occur in skeletally mature patients, the physes are closed. CT improves detection of cortical penetration, which is seen in up to one half of cases, and subtle pathologic fractures. MRI improves detection and delineation of any associated soft tissue mass.

【108】 The most common sites for these tumors are the long tubular bones about the knee (50% to 65%), distal radius (10%), sacrum, and proximal humerus. GCTs occurring in flat bones (such as the pelvis), the calca-neus, apophyses, and other growth centers, such as the patella, do not always follow the same rules as those in long bones do; that is, the classic imaging findings of long bone metaepiphyseal GCTs are not always present.

【109】 MRI of GCT demonstrates a well-defined solid lesion, often with cystic components, with a variably present low-intensity peripheral pseudo-capsule. Solid components are typically low to intermediate intensity on T1 and T2-weighted images. MRI best demonstrates soft tissue extension and solid elements, with secondary aneurysmal components manifested by fluid-fluid levels. Secondary ABC components occur in approximately 14% of these lesions.

【110】 Biopsy of suspected GCT should be directed toward the solid components and away from the cystic components. Contrast enhanced MRI aids in differentiation of solid from cystic components, with solid components enhancing diffusely and cystic components demonstrating a thin peripheral rim of enhancement.

【111】 Patients undergo routine clinical and radiographic surveillance following resection of GCT due to the risk of recurrence. Bony recurrence presents radiographically as increasing areas of osteolysis about the surgical site. Soft tissue recurrence presents as increasing/new soft tissue calcifications or an enlarging soft tissue mass with a shell of peripheral calcification.

【21】KEY FACTS

【22】Clinical

【23】 Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors are characterized as schwannomas and neurofibromas, both of which arise from the Schwann cell within peripheral nerves.

【24】 Schwannomas are distinguished from neurofibromas histologically by alternating Antoni A and B regions and the presence of large quantities of S-100 protein by immunohistochemical analysis.

【25】 Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors usually present as painless, slow growing masses.

【26】 Neurofibromas most frequently affect patients between the ages of 20 and 30.

【27】 Most neurofibromas are solitary. Only 10% of neurofibromas occur in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1). Multiple neurofibromas can be seen in patients with NF-1.

【28】 Peripheral neurofibromas typically arise from small peripheral nerves in the skin and subcutaneous tissues although they can also arise from deeper peripheral nerves.

【29】 Neurofibromas may be localized, diffuse, or plexiform. Plexiform neurofibromas involve a long nerve segment and its branches and are pathognomonic for NF-1.

【30】 Schwannomas are slightly less common than neurofi-bromas and occur most frequently in patients between 20 and 50 years of age.

【31】 Most schwannomas are solitary and are not associated with NF-1.

【32】 Schwannomas most commonly occur in the head and neck and along major nerve trunks.

【33】 Treatment of benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors is usually surgical resection. Schwannomas are generally separable from the nerve after incising the epineurium, allowing nerve function to be spared. Neurofibro-mas are usually inseparable from the nerve, meaning tumors arising from deep nerves are often partially resected or debulked to preserve nerve function.

【34】 Malignant nerve sheath tumors account for 5% to 10% of all soft tissue sarcomas. While 25% to 75% of malignant tumors arise in patients with NF-1, only 5% to 13% of patients with NF-1 develop malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.

【35】 Malignant tumors usually present as rapidly enlarging, painful masses.

【36】Radiologic

【37】 Schwannomas and neurofibromas are indistinguishable by imaging.

【38】 Deep peripheral nerve sheath tumors grow in fusiform fashion along the long axis of the nerve. The fusiform shape is the most reliable indicator of a peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

【39】 These masses classically taper at either end and the nerve from which the tumor arises may be seen to enter and exit the mass.

【40】 Nerve sheath tumors demonstrate nonspecific hypoin-tense signal intensity on T1-weighted images and hyperintense signal intensity on T2-weighted images, and usually demonstrate heterogeneous enhancement after the intravenous administration of gadolinium.

【41】 The mass may demonstrate a central region of lower signal intensity on T2-weighted images known as the “target sign.” This results from greater fluid content within myxoid tissue at the periphery of the mass. The central hypointense component corresponds to collag-enous or fibrous tissue.

【42】 The “fascicular sign” may be seen on T2-weighted imaging as multiple small circular structures within the mass with surrounding hyperintensity. This is attributed to nerve fascicles within the mass.

【43】 The “split fat sign” is a rim of hyperintense tissue on T1-weighted images surrounding the tumor. This is seen when a nerve sheath tumor arises in an intermuscular location and is surrounded by intermuscular fat.

【44】 Muscle atrophy is a variable finding that may be seen in a muscle supplied by the affected nerve.

【45】 Schwannomas are more likely to be located eccentrically along the course of a nerve while neurofibromas are more likely to be situated centrally.

【46】 Schwannomas are more likely to demonstrate cystic components than neurofibromas.

【47】 Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors may appear similar to benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors by imaging. Imaging findings that may suggest malignancy include large size (>5 cm) and poorly defined margins with infiltration of surrounding structures.

【54】人名段删除-1:<u>DAVID K. KRUG</u>

【55】HISTORY

【56】A 16-year-old female who injured her knee while playing softball.

【60】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【61】 Transient patellar dislocation (TPD): This diagnosis is favored given the constellation of findings including bone contusions of the anterolateral lateral femoral condyle and inferomedial patella, medial patellar chon-dral injury, loose body and hemarthrosis.

【62】 Acute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Contusions in the lateral femoral condyle are often seen with acute ACL tears. The classic pivot shift contusion in acute ACL injury involves the lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral tibial plateau. Contusion of the medial patella is not associated with this injury.

【63】 Direct trauma: Direct blow to the lateral knee, such as seen in clipping injury in football players, can result in bone contusions about the knee most commonly in the lateral femoral condyle. This diagnosis would not account for the patellar contusion or osteochondral defect, and is therefore not the best diagnosis.

【64】DIAGNOSIS

【65】Transient patellar dislocation

【66】KEY FACTS

【67】Clinical

【68】 Classic mechanism of TPD is internal rotation of the femur on a fixed tibia while the knee is flexed. Contraction of the quadriceps results in net lateral force on the patella and dislocation. Direct blow to the medial knee may also result in lateral patellar dislocation.

【69】 Comprises 9% to 16% of all acute knee trauma in young athletes with hemarthrosis. Dislocation is usually transient with spontaneous relocation, and most patients do not realize this type of injury has occurred.

【70】 It is estimated that 50% to 75% of all patellar dislocations are incorrectly diagnosed at initial clinical evaluation. MRI can accurately diagnose suspected or occult patellar dislocation, and is useful for evaluation of the extent of associated soft tissue injuries and intra-articular abnormalities.

【71】 Surgical management may be indicated for significant osteochondral defects, loose bodies, or associated meniscal or ligamentous injuries.

【72】Radiologic

【73】 Mechanism of injury results in a characteristic pattern of bone marrow contusions involving the lateral femoral condyle, which is seen in up to 100% of patients on MRI, and the inferomedial patella.

【74】 Injury to the medial retinacular complex is invariably present, and is commonly seen on MRI.

【75】 Joint effusion or hemarthrosis is almost always present in the acute setting, and is often large.

【76】 Close evaluation of the cartilage is extremely important, as chondral injuries of the patellofemoral joint and of the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle are common in these patients, and in some cases indicate surgical management. Osteochondral loose bodies are seen in up to one third of patients.

【77】 Other MRI findings may include lateral patellar tilt or subluxation, injury to Hoffa’s infrapatellar fat pad, and shallow femoral trochlea.

【86】人名段删除-1:<u>KAVITA M. PATEL</u>

【87】HISTORY

【88】A 19-year-old female college student with 4 months of wrist pain.

【89】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURES 5-30A and 5-30B AP (A) and lateral (B) radiographs demonstrate a large, somewhat expansile lucent lesion centered in the distal radial epiphysis, with a narrow zone of transition, which extends to the distal radius subchondral bone. The lesion does not have a sclerotic margin and there is no evidence of internal matrix.</u>

【90】通用删除16(英):<u> FIGURES 5-30C and 5-30D Coronal Tl-weighted (C) and axial fat-suppressed FSE T2-weighted (D) images demonstrate a solid lesion of decreased signal intensity on the Tl-weighted image and increased signal intensity on the T2-weighted image, which is a nonspecific appearance. The axial image demonstrates the expansile nature of the mass along the volar aspect of the radius.</u>

【91】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【92】 Giant cell tumor (GCT) of bone: This is the best diagnosis given the location of the lytic lesion in the meta-epiphysis of a long bone, extending into the subchondral bone. The lesion meets the criteria for a GCT of a long bone, given lack of sclerotic margin, lack of internal matrix, and occurring in a patient with closed physes.

【93】 Aneurysmal Bone Cyst (ABC): This is a possible diagnosis as ABCs can occur in the epiphysis of long bones (though they do not have to), and the lesion in this case is mildly expansile and occurring in a patient <30 years old, which are features typical of ABCs. However, ABCs usually have fluid-fluid levels demonstrated on MR imaging, which is not seen in this case.

【94】 Intra-osseous ganglion or large subchondral cyst: On plain x-ray, intra-osseous ganglion is a well-circumscribed lucent lesion with a sclerotic rim, most frequently seen in the medial malleolus of the tibia, carpal bones, femoral head or acetabulum. It is thought to be due to osseous penetration of a soft tissue ganglion or perhaps proliferation of synovial rests. These lesions are usually not painful, unless associated with inflammatory or degenerative arthritis, which is not evident in this case. Also, these lesions are usually cystic, rather than solid, on MRI.

【95】 Chondroblastoma: Chondroblastoma is an epiphyseal lytic lesion with a narrow zone of transition usually seen in skeletally immature individuals. Chondroblastoma typically demonstrates a peripheral rim of sclerosis and can contain chondroid matrix. Chondroblastoma often elicits thick metaphyseal periostitis, remote from the epiphyseal location of the lesion, which is not seen in this case.

【96】 Metastasis/Myeloma: Metastatic or myelomatous lesions are the most common cause for a lytic lesion in individuals over 50, and these lesions can occur in the epiphysis. The patient’s young age in this case makes this a very unlikely diagnosis.

【97】DIAGNOSIS

【98】Giant cell tumor (GCT) of bone

【99】KEY FACTS

【100】Clinical

【101】 GCT of bone is a relatively common benign bone neoplasm which almost always occurs in skeletally mature patients, most commonly presenting in the third or fourth decade. Patients usually present with pain. Sometimes localized swelling, decreased range of motion or a pathologic fracture is present.

【102】 Women are affected slightly more commonly than men, although malignant GCT is more common in men (3:1).

【103】 Approximately 10% of GCTs are “malignant.” Determination of malignancy is made either by histology or by the presence of pulmonary metastases, as even benign GCTs may demonstrate “aggressive” features (such as cortical disruption and soft tissue mass) at imaging. A rare subtype, “benign metastasizing GCT,” presents with pulmonary metastases that are histologically identical to benign GCT. The majority of malignant GCTs are due to irradiation of a previously documented GCT.

【104】 Multifocal GCTs of bone are rare. There is a rare, possibly familial, association of multiple GCTs with Paget’s disease.

【105】 Definitive treatment consists of intralesional surgical resection. Marginal resections are associated with a higher recurrence rate (40% to 60%) than newer techniques utilizing extended surgical margins and bone grafting or methylmethacrylate packing of the defect (<25% recurrence rate).

【106】Radiologic

【107】 The characteristic radiographic appearance of GCT of bone is an eccentric lytic lesion in the meta-epiphysis of a long bone, although large lesions often appear more central. The lesion extends into the subchondral bone, causing the appearance of extension to the articular surface. There is usually a narrow zone of transition, and surrounding sclerosis is extremely rare. As these tumors occur in skeletally mature patients, the physes are closed. CT improves detection of cortical penetration, which is seen in up to one half of cases, and subtle pathologic fractures. MRI improves detection and delineation of any associated soft tissue mass.

【108】 The most common sites for these tumors are the long tubular bones about the knee (50% to 65%), distal radius (10%), sacrum, and proximal humerus. GCTs occurring in flat bones (such as the pelvis), the calca-neus, apophyses, and other growth centers, such as the patella, do not always follow the same rules as those in long bones do; that is, the classic imaging findings of long bone metaepiphyseal GCTs are not always present.

【109】 MRI of GCT demonstrates a well-defined solid lesion, often with cystic components, with a variably present low-intensity peripheral pseudo-capsule. Solid components are typically low to intermediate intensity on T1 and T2-weighted images. MRI best demonstrates soft tissue extension and solid elements, with secondary aneurysmal components manifested by fluid-fluid levels. Secondary ABC components occur in approximately 14% of these lesions.

【110】 Biopsy of suspected GCT should be directed toward the solid components and away from the cystic components. Contrast enhanced MRI aids in differentiation of solid from cystic components, with solid components enhancing diffusely and cystic components demonstrating a thin peripheral rim of enhancement.

【111】 Patients undergo routine clinical and radiographic surveillance following resection of GCT due to the risk of recurrence. Bony recurrence presents radiographically as increasing areas of osteolysis about the surgical site. Soft tissue recurrence presents as increasing/new soft tissue calcifications or an enlarging soft tissue mass with a shell of peripheral calcification.

【100】Widely used criteria for classification of vasculitis are those of the American College of Rheumatology and the Chapel Hill Consensus Conference on the Nomenclature of Systemic Vasculitis

【100】Widely used criteria for classification of vasculitis are those of the American College of Rheumatology and the Chapel Hill Consensus Conference on the Nomenclature of Systemic Vasculitis

【101】Classification criteria were developed for use in clinical trials and epidemiologic studies； they were not intended for use as diagnostic criteria

【102】**Useful information for the classification of vasculitis includes**

【103】\- Size of predominant vessels involved

【104】__ Large vessels include the aorta and its major branches

【105】**Medium vessels include muscular arteries and small arteries that can be observed with the naked eye or visualized by arteriography**

【106】**Small vessels include small arteries， arterioles， capillaries， and postcapillary venules， vessels that are typically 500 um or less**

【107】Overlap in the size of involved vessels is often observed， but predominant vessels involved usually produce the typical clinical

【108】 Demographic profile， particularly age group and ethnicity

【109】**\- Organ tropism**

【34】Tumors are found in the parietal and visceral pericardium (epicardium) as coalescent nodules that obliterate the pericardial space and may diffusely encase the heart and great vessels

【35】**Pericardial mesothelioma**

【36】Solitary or localized mesothelioma is rare

【37】\- Usually invades the heart only superficially

【38】**Pericardial angiosarcoma**

【39】_—_ Invades the myocardium， and in one fourth of cases， intracavitary extension is seen

【41】**Pericardial mesothelioma**

【42】Epithelioid， sarcomatoid， and mixed types have all been reported

【43】Histology similar to mesothelioma of pleura and peritoneum

【44】**Pericardial angiosarcoma**

【45】Anastomosing vascular channels lined by atypical endothelial cells with abundant mitotic activity and areas of necrosis

【46】Solid areas of epithelioid anaplastic cells or spindle cells are often present

【48】Reticulin stain highlights a vascular pattern in angiosarcoma

【49】CK5/6， calretinin， WT-1， HBME-1， thrombomodulin， mesothelin， podoplanin， D2-40， and h-caldesmon are considered positive markers in mesothelioma

【50】CD31， CD34， and von Willebrand factor are positive in angiosarcoma

【52】**Pericardial mesothelioma**

【53】\- Electron microscopy： numerous long， slender， smooth microvilli on cellular surface and intracellular and intercellular lumens with length-to-diameter ratio greater than 10 in epithelioid mesothelioma； epithelial differentiation of sarcomatoid mesotheliomas includes presence of intercellular junctions， surface microvilli， tonofilaments， and basal lamina formation

【59】Epithelioid angiosarcoma versus mesothelioma Epithelioid angiosarcoma shows strong and diffuse reactivity for vimentin and absent to weak staining with cytokeratin

【60】Mesotheliomas will have more intense staining with cytokeratin and less intense vimentin staining

【61】Additional immunohistochemical stains  can establish the diagnosis in most instances

【63】No definite association has been found between asbestos exposure and pericardial mesothelioma

【64】Pericardial mesothelioma may spread to adjacent pleura， mediastinum， diaphragm， and lymph nodes but rarely presents with distant metastases

【99】**The Vasculitides**

【100】Widely used criteria for classification of vasculitis are those of the American College of Rheumatology and the Chapel Hill Consensus Conference on the Nomenclature of Systemic Vasculitis

【101】Classification criteria were developed for use in clinical trials and epidemiologic studies； they were not intended for use as diagnostic criteria

【102】**Useful information for the classification of vasculitis includes**

【103】\- Size of predominant vessels involved

【104】__ Large vessels include the aorta and its major branches

【105】**Medium vessels include muscular arteries and small arteries that can be observed with the naked eye or visualized by arteriography**

【106】**Small vessels include small arteries， arterioles， capillaries， and postcapillary venules， vessels that are typically 500 um or less**

【107】Overlap in the size of involved vessels is often observed， but predominant vessels involved usually produce the typical clinical

【108】 Demographic profile， particularly age group and ethnicity

【109】**\- Organ tropism**

【110】\- Immune complex deposition

【111】**\- Presence of antineutrophil cytoplasmic and anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies in serum**

【112】Pathologic evaluation alone is usually insufficient and may not always be required to make a clinical diagnosis

【113】**Large-Vessel Vasculitis**

【114】**Clinical Features**

【115】**Giant cell arteritis**

【116】Frequently involves the aorta and its major branches

【117】More commonly found in older females； rare in blacks and Asians

【118】Patients present with a variety of symptoms， including fatigue， headaches， jaw claudication， diplopia， and vision loss； common cause of fever of unknown origin in elderly patients

【119】Often associated with polymyalgia rheumatica

【120】Aortic involvement results in aneurysms， less often leads to stenosis， and is clinically manifest in only a minority of patients

【121】End-organ ischemia may result from luminal stenosis or occlusion of extracranial branches of the external and internal carotid arteries， most commonly involving the temporal artery； may involve vertebral or ophthalmic arteries

【122】**Takayasu arteritis**

【123】Typically occurs in patients younger than 40 years with female predominance； worldwide distribution， but higher frequency in Japan， Southeast Asia， and India

【124】Involvement of the aorta and its major branches， with frequent involvement of the subclavian and carotid arteries； may also involve coronary， pulmonary， mesenteric， and renal arteries

【125】Patients often present with fever， malaise， arthralgia， myalgia， and weight loss

【126】Causes ischemic symptoms (pulselessness， claudication， and blindness)， loss or asymmetry of pulses and blood pressure， bruits， renovascular hypertension， and sometimes aortic aneurysms

【127】Gross Pathology

【128】Aortic aneurysms will show wrinkled intima with a tree-bark appearance， indistinct medial layer， and variably thickened adventitia

【129】Stenotic lesions show fibrous thickening of the vessel wall with reduction in the lumen caliber of the aorta and major arteries； thrombosis may occur

【132】**Characterized by focal granulomatous inflammation of large and medium-sized arteries**

【133】In the aorta， areas of laminar medial necrosis surrounded by granulomatous intlammation is common

【162】Because of the frequent involvement of temporal arteries in giant cell arteritis， “temporal arteritis"has often been used interchangeably with “giant cell arteritis" in the literature； however， giant cell arteritis is the preferred term because not all patients with giant cell arteritis have temporal arteritis， and not all cases of temporal arteritis are caused by giant cell arteritis

【185】__ Idiopathic systemic disease characterized by vasculitis involving medium-sized and small muscular arteries

【186】Most patients are in the fourth to sixth decades； male-to-female ratio is 2：1

【187】Patients usually have nonspecific systemic symptoms of weight loss and fever with focal symptoms in the specific organ involved (peripheral neuropathy， testicular pain， livedo reticularis， myalgias， and gastrointestinal infarction)

【188】Associated with deposition of circulating immune complexes in hepatitis B infection

【189】May become manifest in the course of hairy cell leukemia，rheumatoid arthritis， and Sjogren syndrome

【190】Arteriography detects aneurysms or occlusions of visceral arteries； commonly involved vessels are renal， coronary， hepatic， and mesenteric arteries； lung involvement (bronchial arteries) in up to 30% of patients

【191】**Kawasaki disease (mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome， infantile PAN)**

【192】Acute self-limited disease typically affects infants and children (range， 6 months to 15 years； peaks at 13 to24 months)

【193】Increased incidence in Japan and Korea

【194】**In the United States， children of American Asian and Pacific Island origin have higher incidence compared with African American and white children**

Ricker， PhD， ABPP (CN， RP)， is the Director of Neuropsy-chology and Rehabilitation Psychology and an Associate Professor in the Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation at the University of Pittsburgh. Dr. Ricker’s overall program of research is in the exami-nation of neurobiological correlates and predictors of cognitive impair-ment， recovery， and rehabilitation following human brain trauma. Current research projects include the examination of altered cerebral blood flow and metabolic correlates of impaired episodic and working memory after brain injury (through the use of fMRI， PET， and near infrared spectroscopy)， as well as the application of telerehabilitation technologies with individuals who have sustained brain trauma. Dr. Ricker has a history of federal and private grant funding in these areas. He is the author of over 48 peer-reviewed scientific publications， 15 book chapters and other professional publications， and numerous published abstracts. He is very active in national and international neuropsycho-logical and rehabilitation organizations， and has made over 70 national and international presentations. He is a member of the editorial boards of several journals in the areas of brain injury， neuropsychology and _rehabilitation， including the Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation， the_ _Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology， Rehabilitation Psychology，_ and The Clinical Neuropsychologist. He has also served as a grant reviewer for several private and federal agencies， including the Department of Defense， the Department of Veterans Affairs， and the National Institutes of Health. Dr. Ricker holds dual board certifications from the American Board of Professional Psychology in the areas of Clinical Neuropsychology and Rehabilitation Psychology. He is a member of the Board of Directors of both specialty boards， and has served as the Secretary for each board. Dr. Ricker has also been the recipient of several national awards in psychology， including two separate early career awards from the American Psychological Association， the first in Clinical Neuropsychology， and another in Rehabilitation Psychology.**</u>

【72】**Introduction**

【73】**Clinical neuropsychological assessment is widely practiced， but many of its tenets and assumptions have been based on a created consiruct of“brain damage."Of course， the use of the word “created，” the quotation marks， and italics are certainly not meant to state or imply that there is no such thing as brain damage， but rather that "brain damage” is not in any sense auniform entity， nor should it be treated as such. Nonetheless， clinicians may fall prey to the well-practiced--and even at times well-marketed-belief systemn that dictates that individual humans are either "normal” or “brain damaged，"irrespective of factors known to influence most， if not all， neuropsychological tests (e.g.， premorbid intellectual and cognitive abilities， age， education， prior experience with tests， sociocultural factors). To further compound the issue， this entity of "brain damagemay then be reflexively attributed to some sin-gular and presuined proximal cause.**

【74】**Although many readers will immediately assume that I am referring primarily to forensic situations， the fallacy of the construct of brain damage may occur in any context in which clinical neuropsychologists might practice. Many studies in neuropsychology use mixed samples of various neurologic and psychiatric patients (e.g. acquired head trauma， brain tumor， stroke， multiple sclerosis， schizophrenia， all in one group and mistreated statistically as if comparable and randomly assigned to group membership). Although such an approach can， at times， be justi-fied if one's purpose is to evaluate gross discriminative properties of a test (i.e.， sensitivity to some statistical deviation from “normal")， such a group can never be used to establish the specificity of a test or battery， and certainly cannot be used in an individual clinical case，**

【75】**Fortunately， contemporary clinical neuropsychology has begun to address these issues. This is particularly critical during this new period of enhanced training and credentialing in neuropsychology. Students must be taught that all neuropsychological tests have the potential to be affected by a multitude of variables， only one of which might be acquired brain dysfunction. Students must be made aware of the various**

【76】**Introduction**

【77】**interactions among variables. This will require much effort on the part of professors and supervisors at all levels of training. It definitely requires abandoning much of clinical lore in favor of an empirical approach to assessment. Many contemporary neuropsychologists were trained in the model of assessment sensitivity (i.e.， can a test or battery of tests effectively discriminate between “normal" versus a neuropsychi-atric condition?) or localization (i.e.， where is the “lesion"?). Given advances in both psychometric assessment and neuroimaging， however， such approaches are now outdated and simply do not help individuals with neurologic illness or injury. To be clinically useful and incremen-tally valid， neuropsychological assessment must go beyond the simple search for (or simple confirmation of) the construct of brain damage. This is particularly critical if the intent is to provide treatment or reha-bilitation beyond a simple diagnosis.**

【78】**The first three chapters of this book discuss general issues that affect any neuropsychological construct： demographics， personality， and sociocultural factors. Because this text is not designed to be either a compendium of tests or a treatment of every known neurologic entity， only a small number of neurobehavioral disorders have been selected. Adult neurobehavioral syndromes were chosen， however， based on the existence of a sufficient empirical literature that is applicable to neuro-psychological assessment. Thus， additional chapters are included that deal with dementia， HIV-related syndromes， adult seizure disorders， toxic exposure， mild head injury， moderate and severe traumatic brain injury， adult learning disabilities， and chronic fatigue syndrome.**

【81】**Psychosocial Factors in Differential Diagnosis**

【82】人名段删除-1:<u>**_Jeffery B. Allen_**</u>

【83】**Neuropsychological diagnosis， assessment， and treatment are predicat-ed on obtaining accurate information regarding the patient's optimal level of cognitive performance. First， psychological and social factors can reduce motivation， attention， or stamina， thus compromising per-formance. When this compromise occurs， various additional factors can complicate the differential diagnostic process， as the direct impact of neuropathology can become entangled with the influence of depression， anxiety， or personality changes on test performance. Some neurological or medical conditions can produce psychiatric symptoms as the first indication of the illness. Finally， understanding the etiology and nature of psychosocial and emotional sequelae of neurological conditions is critical in the long-term management and treatment of neurobehavioral conditions. For example， the psychological and psy-chosocial aspects of head injury are often the most critical in predict ing which individuals will successfully return to various social roles such as work.**

【84】**This chapter initially focuses on the specific psychosocial and emo-tional factors that are most relevant to the differential diagnostic process in neuropsychology. Next there is a discussion of how psychoso-cial and neurological variables can overlap in a way that renders the dif ferential diagnostic process more complex. The focus then turns to adapting the evaluation process in an attempt to better assess critical psychosocial factors. The chapter concludes with a discussion concern-ing the importance of integrating psychosocial information for the pur-poses of diagnosis and intervention， along with a case example.**

【85】**The word “psychosocial" is used widely， vaguely， and loosely. It is used to encompass feelings， symptoms， and functional changes in the injured patient， family members， and others. A concept as vague and loosely defined as this has little utility in understanding the nature and remediation of problems subsequent to neurological insult 删除1:<u>(Brooks，1992)</u>. One task of the current chapter is to attempt to provide some basic parameters for the term“psychosocial，"at least as it relates to dif-ferential diagnosis in neuropsychological assessment.**

【86】**A definition of psychosocial functioning appears to share some simis larity with Freud's definition of psychological health： “the capacity to work and love." In many cases， these domains are the focus of com-plaints voiced by family members and significant others concerning the post-injury changes they have witnessed in their loved ones. The con-cept can most broadly be defined as the individual's ability and satisfac-tion with his or her ability to perform activities within the community or society. This definition should include the individual's capacity to nego-tiate the immediate environments of home or work， the ability to form or maintain meaningful relationships with others， and the quality of life that is maintained throughout such involvement.**

【87】**McLean， Dikmen， Temkin， Wyler， and Gele (1984) have argued that activities associated with physical functioning such as mobility or self-care are relatively less affected than is more global social performance related to work and familial relationships. Brooks 删除1:<u>(1991，1992)</u> identi-fies three main categories of psychosocial domains that are often com-promised following neurologic insult： recreational， social and family lite， and occupational life.**

【88】**Psychosocial variables are obviously important in the differential diagnostic process， as they often partially or fully account for deficits in formal neuropsychological performance as well as more functional dif-ficulties reported by the patient. Clearly， they are also important as out-come variables due to their impact on interpersonal relationships， vocational success， and other important arenas. Thus， predicting long term psychosocial outcome can be useful.**

**A study by Malia， Powell， and Torode (1995a) examined the relation-ship between psychosocial functioning and coping style in a group of neurological patients of different etiologies. Along with completion of a psychosocial rating scale (Headley Court Psychosocial Rating Scale)， both patients and relatives completed the Ways of Coping checklist. An analysis of the Ways of Coping checklist revealed that neurological patients used one of four methods of coping： (1) problem focused， (2) emotion focused， (3) avoidance， or (4) wishful thinking. Use of avoidance，|删除0换行|emotion-focused strategies， or wishful thinking was correlated with poorer levels of psychosocial functioning. This is similar to conclusions con-cerning the relationship between coping and poorer psychosocial capacity in noi-neurologic medical populations.**

【90】**An investigation by Colantonio， Kasl， Ostfeld， and Berkman (1993) examined the influence of pre-morbid psychosocial factors on physical function and institutionalization following stroke in a group of elderly patients. Overall， the findings suggest that specific psychosocial factors have prognostic importance that extends beyond features that charac-terize the severity， nature， or comorbidity of the stroke. Interestingly， pre-stroke depression did not predict post-stroke status.**

【91】**PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS AFFECTING TEST PERFORMANCE**

【92】**A number of psychological disorders， states， or factors can affect neu-ropsychological performance. However， certain variables are more fre-quently encountered in patients with suspected neurological conditions and pose more difficulty when attempting to interpret a potentially con-fusing constellation of cognitive test scores. This may translate into a de-emphasis of critical psychological and personality factors that emerge during an evaluation.**

【93】**There is a dearth of empirical work examining the role that psycho-logical factors play in neuropsychological test performance. While some authors de-emphasize the impact that psychological distress has on the neuropsychological performance examination 删除1:<u>(Reitan & Wolfson，1985)</u>， most neuropsychologists continue to struggie with the possible influences of functional disturbance (e.g.， depression， anxiety) in the interpretation of neuropsychological data. Indeed， a number of authors have complained of the absence of comprehensive examinations con-cerning the relationship between depression severity and neuropsycho-logical test performance 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Caine， 1986； Finlayson & Bird，1991)</u></u>. A number of specific psychological and psychosocial factors commonly arise fol-lowing a perceived threat to the individual's medical or neurological status and should be thoroughly explored.**

【94】**Affective Disturbance**

**Depression is frequently one of the first reported symptoms preceding a variety of general medical conditions 删除1:<u>(Hall， 1980)</u>. Clearly， it is critical|删除0换行|to discern what degree of cognitive deficit is related to affective distur-bance rather than the neurologic condition alone. Historically， it was believed that unipolar depression tended to produce specific deficits largely in the domain of learning and memory 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(King. Caine， & Cox，1993； Speedie， Rabins， & Pearlson， 1990)</u></u>， and psychomotor speed删除1:<u>(Cassens， Wolfe， & Zola， 1990)</u>. Both of these domains require effortful processing to some degree， arguing that this activation component may be responsible for some of the performance impairment noted in depressives. This possibility is supported by the finding of better memo-ry performance on recognition trials， which eliminate the need for more effortful recall strategies. Typically， these deficits are often associ-ated with more severe levels of depression that are accompanied by inpatient treatment for the disorder. Fischer， Sweet， and Pfaelzer-Smith(1986) found depressed patients were impaired on 10 of 14 measures， suggesting global rather than focal deficits. These authors go on to sug gest that clinicians may need to adjust their impairment criteria when working with depressed patients in order to prevent diagnostic misclas-sification. Even less is available concerning the cognitive impact of bipo-lar disorder. Ricker， PhD， ABPP (CN， RP)， is the Director of Neuropsy-chology and Rehabilitation Psychology and an Associate Professor in the Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation at the University of Pittsburgh. Dr. Ricker’s overall program of research is in the exami-nation of neurobiological correlates and predictors of cognitive impair-ment， recovery， and rehabilitation following human brain trauma. Current research projects include the examination of altered cerebral blood flow and metabolic correlates of impaired episodic and working memory after brain injury (through the use of fMRI， PET， and near infrared spectroscopy)， as well as the application of telerehabilitation technologies with individuals who have sustained brain trauma. Dr. Ricker has a history of federal and private grant funding in these areas. He is the author of over 48 peer-reviewed scientific publications， 15 book chapters and other professional publications， and numerous published abstracts. He is very active in national and international neuropsycho-logical and rehabilitation organizations， and has made over 70 national and international presentations. He is a member of the editorial boards of several journals in the areas of brain injury， neuropsychology and _rehabilitation， including the Journal of Head Trauma Rehabilitation， the_ _Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology， Rehabilitation Psychology，_ and The Clinical Neuropsychologist. He has also served as a grant reviewer for several private and federal agencies， including the Department of Defense， the Department of Veterans Affairs， and the National Institutes of Health. Dr. Ricker holds dual board certifications from the American Board of Professional Psychology in the areas of Clinical Neuropsychology and Rehabilitation Psychology. He is a member of the Board of Directors of both specialty boards， and has served as the Secretary for each board. Dr. Ricker has also been the recipient of several national awards in psychology， including two separate early career awards from the American Psychological Association， the first in Clinical Neuropsychology， and another in Rehabilitation Psychology.**</u>

One task of the current chapter is to attempt to provide some basic parameters for the term“psychosocial，"at least as it relates to dif-ferential diagnosis in neuropsychological assessment.**

【86】**A definition of psychosocial functioning appears to share some simis larity with Freud's definition of psychological health： “the capacity to work and love." In many cases， these domains are the focus of com-plaints voiced by family members and significant others concerning the post-injury changes they have witnessed in their loved ones. The con-cept can most broadly be defined as the individual's ability and satisfac-tion with his or her ability to perform activities within the community or society. This definition should include the individual's capacity to nego-tiate the immediate environments of home or work， the ability to form or maintain meaningful relationships with others， and the quality of life that is maintained throughout such involvement.**

【87】**McLean， Dikmen， Temkin， Wyler， and Gele (1984) have argued that activities associated with physical functioning such as mobility or self-care are relatively less affected than is more global social performance related to work and familial relationships. Brooks 删除1:<u>(1991，1992)</u> identi-fies three main categories of psychosocial domains that are often com-promised following neurologic insult： recreational， social and family lite， and occupational life.**

【88】**Psychosocial variables are obviously important in the differential diagnostic process， as they often partially or fully account for deficits in formal neuropsychological performance as well as more functional dif-ficulties reported by the patient. Clearly， they are also important as out-come variables due to their impact on interpersonal relationships， vocational success， and other important arenas. Thus， predicting long term psychosocial outcome can be useful.**

**A study by Malia， Powell， and Torode (1995a) examined the relation-ship between psychosocial functioning and coping style in a group of neurological patients of different etiologies. Along with completion of a psychosocial rating scale (Headley Court Psychosocial Rating Scale)， both patients and relatives completed the Ways of Coping checklist. An analysis of the Ways of Coping checklist revealed that neurological patients used one of four methods of coping： (1) problem focused， (2) emotion focused， (3) avoidance， or (4) wishful thinking. Use of avoidance，|删除0换行|emotion-focused strategies， or wishful thinking was correlated with poorer levels of psychosocial functioning. This is similar to conclusions con-cerning the relationship between coping and poorer psychosocial capacity in noi-neurologic medical populations.**

【90】**An investigation by Colantonio， Kasl， Ostfeld， and Berkman (1993) examined the influence of pre-morbid psychosocial factors on physical function and institutionalization following stroke in a group of elderly patients. Overall， the findings suggest that specific psychosocial factors have prognostic importance that extends beyond features that charac-terize the severity， nature， or comorbidity of the stroke. Interestingly， pre-stroke depression did not predict post-stroke status.**

【91】**PSYCHOLOGICAL FACTORS AFFECTING TEST PERFORMANCE**

【92】**A number of psychological disorders， states， or factors can affect neu-ropsychological performance. However， certain variables are more fre-quently encountered in patients with suspected neurological conditions and pose more difficulty when attempting to interpret a potentially con-fusing constellation of cognitive test scores. This may translate into a de-emphasis of critical psychological and personality factors that emerge during an evaluation.**

【93】**There is a dearth of empirical work examining the role that psycho-logical factors play in neuropsychological test performance. While some authors de-emphasize the impact that psychological distress has on the neuropsychological performance examination 删除1:<u>(Reitan & Wolfson，1985)</u>， most neuropsychologists continue to struggie with the possible influences of functional disturbance (e.g.， depression， anxiety) in the interpretation of neuropsychological data. Indeed， a number of authors have complained of the absence of comprehensive examinations con-cerning the relationship between depression severity and neuropsycho-logical test performance 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Caine， 1986； Finlayson & Bird，1991)</u></u>. A number of specific psychological and psychosocial factors commonly arise fol-lowing a perceived threat to the individual's medical or neurological status and should be thoroughly explored.**

【94】**Affective Disturbance**

**Depression is frequently one of the first reported symptoms preceding a variety of general medical conditions 删除1:<u>(Hall， 1980)</u>. Clearly， it is critical|删除0换行|to discern what degree of cognitive deficit is related to affective distur-bance rather than the neurologic condition alone. Historically， it was believed that unipolar depression tended to produce specific deficits largely in the domain of learning and memory 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(King. Caine， & Cox，1993； Speedie， Rabins， & Pearlson， 1990)</u></u>， and psychomotor speed删除1:<u>(Cassens， Wolfe， & Zola， 1990)</u>. Both of these domains require effortful processing to some degree， arguing that this activation component may be responsible for some of the performance impairment noted in depressives. This possibility is supported by the finding of better memo-ry performance on recognition trials， which eliminate the need for more effortful recall strategies. Typically， these deficits are often associ-ated with more severe levels of depression that are accompanied by inpatient treatment for the disorder. Fischer， Sweet， and Pfaelzer-Smith(1986) found depressed patients were impaired on 10 of 14 measures， suggesting global rather than focal deficits. These authors go on to sug gest that clinicians may need to adjust their impairment criteria when working with depressed patients in order to prevent diagnostic misclas-sification. Even less is available concerning the cognitive impact of bipo-lar disorder. A study by Jones， Duncan， Mirsky， Post， and Theodore(1994) found that neurologically intact bipolar patients showed rela-tively specific impairment in the “focusing-executing domain”when assessed by tasks such as the Trail-Making Test， Stroop Color-Word Interference Test， or Purdue Pegboard. 【19】Definition Complete transposition of the great arteries(TGA) is defined by the presence of a discordant ven-triculoarterial connection， with the pulmonary artery arising posteriorly from the left ventricle and the aorta connected anteriorly to the right ventricle.

【20】Anatomy. The basic anomaly is the ventriculoarte-rial discordance. TGA can be isolated (simple TGA) or can be associated with VSDs， pulmonary outflow obstruction， or aortic arch anomalies (coarctation or interruption). Much more rarely， atrioventricular valve abnormalities， including straddling and overriding， may be present. In two-thirds of the cases， significant anomalies of the coronary pattern， which are not diag-nosable in utero， are associated.

Ultrasound diagnosis. The four-chamber view is unre-markable， as for all conotruncal anomalies， unless major anomalies of the atrioventricular junction are associated. The diagnosis is made on the outflow tract views： there is no crossover， and the two arteries follow a parallel course. The aorta arises from the anterior right ventricle， whereas the pulmonary artery is connected posteriorly with the left ventricle . If present， the VSD can also be displayed on the left outflow tract view. The sizes of the vessels should be compared in order to detect possible obstructions， which consist mainly of valvular anomalies for the pulmonary artery and arch coarctation and interruption for the aorta. On longitudinal views， the aortic arch has a wider angle of curvature because of the anteriorized connection of the ascending aorta (a“hockey stick”aspect， in compari-son with the “umbrella handle” aspect of the normal arch). Finally， particular attention should be paid， in the case of TGA with an intact ventricular septum， to signs indicative of a restrictive foramen ovale 通用删除1(英):<u>删除2:<u>(bulging or thickening； Figure 5.60c)</u></u> 通用删除6(英):<u>\[61\]</u>. Spectral Doppler may be used to quantify the transvalvular gradient. However the most interesting use of 4D echo-cardiography (STIC) is when it is employed to recon-struct the coronal plane of the four cardiac valves in order to demonstrate the spatial relationships of TGA 通用删除6(英):<u>\[62\]</u>. In fact， this assessment is impossi-ble or rather difficult with 2D echocardiography. The advantage of knowing the spatial orientation of the great arteries is due to the fact that an anomalous origin or course of the coronary arteries is strictly dependent on the former and coronary arteries abnormalities rep-resent a poor prognostic indicator 通用删除6(英):<u>\[62，63\]</u>.

Prostaglandin E1 infusion is always necessary to avoid closure of the arterial duct and increase oxygen saturation. 【1】人名段删除-1:<u>_Rachel Saunders-Pullman， MD，MPH_</u>

【2】**INTRODUCTION**

【3】**Chorea， a hyperkinetic movement disorder characterized by involuntary， sponta-neous， irregular flowing movements， may be caused by medications and drugs. Medication-induced chorea is most often observed as a side effect of dopaminer-gic medications (primarily levodopa \[L-dopa\]) used to treat Parkinson’s disease(PD) or as a sequela of treatment with antidopaminergic medications. It is seen much less frequently as an adverse effect from other medications， although a wide variety of medications may induce chorea .**

【4】**In this chapter we will focus primarily on the phenomenology， pathophysiol-ogy， and management of L-dopa-induced chorea (dyskinesias) and neuroleptic-induced tardive chorea. We will then review other medications most commonly associated with chorea as a side effect occurring at the time of administration， including dopaminomimetic stimulant agents such as cocaine， amphetamines， and methylphenidate.**

【5】**L-DOPA-INDUCED CHOREA**

【6】**Development of Dyskinesias in PD**

【7】In 1960 Hornykiewicz demonstrated a marked depletion of dopamine in the cau-date nucleus and putamen of patients with postencephalitic parkinsonism and PD

【8】**I4. MEDICATION-INDUCED CHOREA**

【10】**Most frequently cause chorea**

【11】·Dopaminergic drugs： L-Dopa and dopamine agonists， as well as other antiparkinsonian drugs
