【37】**Preface**

【38】**HIs is the third in a series of volumes that con- _cern Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology. The first， which was pub-_ lished in 1982， addressed mostly “old chestnuts” in histopathologic differen-tiation of skin diseases， e.g.， granuloma annulare vs. necrobiosis lipoidica， trichoepithelioma vs. basal-cell carcinoma， and dermatofibroma vs. der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans. A second vastly revised edition of Volume 1was issued in 1992. A second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Dermato-pathology appeared in 1988 and addressed more challenging problems than those in Volume I， e.g.， urticaria vs. the urticarial stage of pemphigold， nevi on the genitalia vs. melanoma on the genitalia， and desmoplastic trichoepi-thelioma vs. morpheiform basal-cell carcinoma. In this third volume， even more demanding problems of differential diagnosis are engaged， among them the conundrums of erythema multiforme vs. graft-versus-host reac-tion， pseudolymphoma with lymphoid follicles vs. follicular lymphoma， and trichoblastoma vs. basal-cell carcinoma.**

**Except for deliberate increase in gradation in difficulty of differential diagnosis， the purpose of this third volume is virtually identical to that of the previous ones， an intent stated in the Preface ofboth of them in these words：|删除换行|“In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a man-ner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphie statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted diseases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are reproduced in low and high magnification. Clinical photographs permit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【40】**“The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted discases have in common， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appearances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical presentation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【41】**“We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and some-times hundreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations， although we did not deliberately and completely disregard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45sections because the data presented here are our own.”**

【42】During the years in which this book was evolving， I had the good for-tune to collaborate with two splendid Fellows in Dermatopathology at New York University Medical Center： Pedro Briggs from Brazil and Francisco(“Paco”) Bravo from Peru. Pedro surveyed the territory and Paco completed the map. Both committed themselves to the endeavor with perseverance and passion， which made “working” with them pleasurable and exhilarating.

【43】Several colleagues kindly permitted us to use histopathologic sections， and we are pleased to acknowledge them： Tetsumori Kimura， Hiromaru Kiryu， Phillip LeBoit， Clifton White， Phillip Vogt，and Helmut Kerl. Ying Guo was invaluable in bringing the book to closure， especially in regard to design of the color plates. Bill Slue and Meryll Krolich were responsible for taking many of the clinical photographs， color corrections of which were done by Amy Feuerstein. As has been the case with all of my books published by Lea Febiger， Tom Colaiezzi shepherded the work from manuscript to bound book and Isabelle Clouser edited it scrupulously. Jim Harter not only typed and retyped the manuscript many times， but maintained order where otherwise chaos might have reigned， and did it all with remarkably good humor.

【44】**We hope that this book will be an instructive and useful adjunct to Sherlockian solving of histopathologic puzzles in dermatopathology and will enable differential diagnosis to become specific diagnosis.**

【148】RURITIC urticarialpapules and plaques of preg-nancy (PUPPP) and superficial responses to assaults by arthropods are in-flammatory diseases that share many clinical and histopathologic features. When viewed through a conventional microscope， both conditions may have superficial or superficial and mid-dermal perivascular and interstitial infil-trates composed of lymphocytes and eosinophils， as well as extravasated Ethrocytes and focal spongiosis. Clinically， PUPPP and superfic TC-sponses to assaults by arthropods both consist of urticarial papules that may be widespread.

【149】The clinical features of the two diseases， when assessed in constella-tion， however， are distinctive. Lesions of PUPPP usually consist of numerous discrete papules situated especially on the abdomen and distributed also on the thighs， whereas reactions to assaults by arthropods usually are few， a S single lesion sometimes being the only manifestation. In contrast to lesions ofPUPPP， insect “bitestend to be confined to parts of the body that are not covered by clothing. PUPPP occurs during the waning weeks of pregnancy， Responses to assaults by arthropods are independent of pregnancy.

【150】PUPPP is characterized histopatholocally by an infiltrate of inflamma-tory cells that nearly always extends across an entire front of a 4.0 mm punched-out biopsy specimen， unlike the situation in a biopsy specimen of similar size taken of a response to an assault by an arthropod in which the changes are focal and often fail to extend from one side of the specimen to the other. The infiltrate of inflammatory cells in sections of an insect “bite is wedge-shaped as a consequence of an arthropod’s headlong attack at high speed on the skin. A discrete focus of spongiosis or a spongiotic vesicle marks the site of the “bite." In contrast， spongiosis in PUPPP is slight and multifocal. Episodically， neutrophils may be found in mounds of scale-crusts in responses to assaults by arthropods， but there are neither neutro-phils nor scale-crusts in PUPPP.

【151】**An important clue to differentiation of these two very different patho-logic processes is the pattern of infiltration of inflammatory cells. In PUPPP， the infiltrate is mostly superficial， perivascular， and not wedge-shaped， whereas in assaults by arthropods it is superficial， equally interstitial and perivascular， and wedge-shaped. If step sections are cut into a specimen in which the infiltrate in response to an insect bite seems to be superficial， a deep component of the infiltrate may be revealed. In most instances， insect“bites”are characterized by superficial and deep， perivascular and intersti-tial， wedge-shaped infiltrates.**

【152】PUPPPmayshare somehistopathologic features with urticaria， namely， sparse perivascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrates of lympho-cytes and eosinophils. Unlike the situation in urticaria， however， the infil-trate in PUPPP is not joined by neutrophils.

【153】In times past， a variety of names have been given to PUPPP， among them toxemnic rash of pregnancy， late onset prurigo of pregnancy， toxic ery-thema of pregnancy， erythema multiforme of pregnancy， and papular erup-tion of pregnancy. In our opinion， these terms are confusing and should be avoided； PUPPP suffices.

【154】When they are viewed histopathologically， responses to assaults by ar-thropods vary enormously depending upon the offending organism， the age of the lesion， the capability of the host to reaci， and the portion of the lesion sampled. For example， a sand-flea bite is associated with neutrophils rather than eosinophils； a bee sting eventually may be associated with foreign body granulomatous reaction if a"stinger” has been left behind in the dermis； the mouth parts of a tick left in the dermis as the critter is pulled off may induce pseudolymnphomatous reaction； nodular lesions of scabies are denser and deeper than the usual response to arthropod assaults， and a biopsy speci-men from the center of an insect bite that consists clinically of a vesicle atop an urticarial papule or plaque will reveal a large central intra-epidermal vesicle with smaller intra-cpidermal vesicles that taper progressively in size toward the periphery， whereas a biopsy specimen from the periphery of the same lesion reveals no intra-epidermal vesiculation， but marked subepider-mal edema.

【155】Other organisms and objects may cause reactions in the skin that are indistinguishable from those of arthropods， e.g.， the larvae of creeping eruption， the cercariae of swimmer’s itch， the nematocysis of the Portu-guese man-of-war， the hairs of the puss caterpillar， and the spines ofsea anemones and of coral. When these agents are suspected， careful search should be undertaken in the cornified layer for a mite of scabies， in the spinous layer for a cercaria， and in and above the basal layer for a larva of hookwormn.

【37】**Preface**

【38】**HIs is the third in a series of volumes that con- _cern Differential Diagnosis in Dermatopathology. The first， which was pub-_ lished in 1982， addressed mostly “old chestnuts” in histopathologic differen-tiation of skin diseases， e.g.， granuloma annulare vs. necrobiosis lipoidica， trichoepithelioma vs. basal-cell carcinoma， and dermatofibroma vs. der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans. A second vastly revised edition of Volume 1was issued in 1992. A second volume of Differential Diagnosis in Dermato-pathology appeared in 1988 and addressed more challenging problems than those in Volume I， e.g.， urticaria vs. the urticarial stage of pemphigold， nevi on the genitalia vs. melanoma on the genitalia， and desmoplastic trichoepi-thelioma vs. morpheiform basal-cell carcinoma. In this third volume， even more demanding problems of differential diagnosis are engaged， among them the conundrums of erythema multiforme vs. graft-versus-host reac-tion， pseudolymphoma with lymphoid follicles vs. follicular lymphoma， and trichoblastoma vs. basal-cell carcinoma.**

**Except for deliberate increase in gradation in difficulty of differential diagnosis， the purpose of this third volume is virtually identical to that of the previous ones， an intent stated in the Preface ofboth of them in these words：|删除换行|“In this work， apparent histologic similarities are contrasted in a man-ner that establishes criteria for differentiating them. These distinctions are presented in capsule and table form by emphatic telegraphie statements. Photomicrographs of contrasted diseases that differentiate strikingly the histologic features are reproduced in low and high magnification. Clinical photographs permit the reader， particularly the pathologist， to visualize the pathologic condition in the gross.**

【40】**“The discussions that follow the tabulated points and counterpoints expatiate first on the histologic features that each pair of contrasted discases have in common， and then on the correlations between their histologic and clinical appearances， their usual clinical courses and， lastly， their histologic differential diagnoses. For simplification and teaching purposes， we have tended to use the classical presentation of fully developed lesions as our models.**

【41】**“We derived criteria by laboriously examining tens， scores， and some-times hundreds of histologic examples of the contrasted diseases. We were not swayed by traditional interpretations， although we did not deliberately and completely disregard them. No bibliography accompanies any of the 45sections because the data presented here are our own.”**

【42】During the years in which this book was evolving， I had the good for-tune to collaborate with two splendid Fellows in Dermatopathology at New York University Medical Center： Pedro Briggs from Brazil and Francisco(“Paco”) Bravo from Peru. Pedro surveyed the territory and Paco completed the map. Both committed themselves to the endeavor with perseverance and passion， which made “working” with them pleasurable and exhilarating.

【43】Several colleagues kindly permitted us to use histopathologic sections， and we are pleased to acknowledge them： Tetsumori Kimura， Hiromaru Kiryu， Phillip LeBoit， Clifton White， Phillip Vogt，and Helmut Kerl. Ying Guo was invaluable in bringing the book to closure， especially in regard to design of the color plates. Bill Slue and Meryll Krolich were responsible for taking many of the clinical photographs， color corrections of which were done by Amy Feuerstein. As has been the case with all of my books published by Lea Febiger， Tom Colaiezzi shepherded the work from manuscript to bound book and Isabelle Clouser edited it scrupulously. Jim Harter not only typed and retyped the manuscript many times， but maintained order where otherwise chaos might have reigned， and did it all with remarkably good humor.

【44】**We hope that this book will be an instructive and useful adjunct to Sherlockian solving of histopathologic puzzles in dermatopathology and will enable differential diagnosis to become specific diagnosis.**

【148】RURITIC urticarialpapules and plaques of preg-nancy (PUPPP) and superficial responses to assaults by arthropods are in-flammatory diseases that share many clinical and histopathologic features. When viewed through a conventional microscope， both conditions may have superficial or superficial and mid-dermal perivascular and interstitial infil-trates composed of lymphocytes and eosinophils， as well as extravasated Ethrocytes and focal spongiosis. Clinically， PUPPP and superfic TC-sponses to assaults by arthropods both consist of urticarial papules that may be widespread.

【149】The clinical features of the two diseases， when assessed in constella-tion， however， are distinctive. Lesions of PUPPP usually consist of numerous discrete papules situated especially on the abdomen and distributed also on the thighs， whereas reactions to assaults by arthropods usually are few， a S single lesion sometimes being the only manifestation. In contrast to lesions ofPUPPP， insect “bitestend to be confined to parts of the body that are not covered by clothing. PUPPP occurs during the waning weeks of pregnancy， Responses to assaults by arthropods are independent of pregnancy.

【150】PUPPP is characterized histopatholocally by an infiltrate of inflamma-tory cells that nearly always extends across an entire front of a 4.0 mm punched-out biopsy specimen， unlike the situation in a biopsy specimen of similar size taken of a response to an assault by an arthropod in which the changes are focal and often fail to extend from one side of the specimen to the other. The infiltrate of inflammatory cells in sections of an insect “bite is wedge-shaped as a consequence of an arthropod’s headlong attack at high speed on the skin. A discrete focus of spongiosis or a spongiotic vesicle marks the site of the “bite." In contrast， spongiosis in PUPPP is slight and multifocal. Episodically， neutrophils may be found in mounds of scale-crusts in responses to assaults by arthropods， but there are neither neutro-phils nor scale-crusts in PUPPP.

【151】**An important clue to differentiation of these two very different patho-logic processes is the pattern of infiltration of inflammatory cells. In PUPPP， the infiltrate is mostly superficial， perivascular， and not wedge-shaped， whereas in assaults by arthropods it is superficial， equally interstitial and perivascular， and wedge-shaped. If step sections are cut into a specimen in which the infiltrate in response to an insect bite seems to be superficial， a deep component of the infiltrate may be revealed. In most instances， insect“bites”are characterized by superficial and deep， perivascular and intersti-tial， wedge-shaped infiltrates.**

【152】PUPPPmayshare somehistopathologic features with urticaria， namely， sparse perivascular and interstitial mixed-cell infiltrates of lympho-cytes and eosinophils. Unlike the situation in urticaria， however， the infil-trate in PUPPP is not joined by neutrophils.

【153】In times past， a variety of names have been given to PUPPP， among them toxemnic rash of pregnancy， late onset prurigo of pregnancy， toxic ery-thema of pregnancy， erythema multiforme of pregnancy， and papular erup-tion of pregnancy. In our opinion， these terms are confusing and should be avoided； PUPPP suffices.

【154】When they are viewed histopathologically， responses to assaults by ar-thropods vary enormously depending upon the offending organism， the age of the lesion， the capability of the host to reaci， and the portion of the lesion sampled. For example， a sand-flea bite is associated with neutrophils rather than eosinophils； a bee sting eventually may be associated with foreign body granulomatous reaction if a"stinger” has been left behind in the dermis； the mouth parts of a tick left in the dermis as the critter is pulled off may induce pseudolymnphomatous reaction； nodular lesions of scabies are denser and deeper than the usual response to arthropod assaults， and a biopsy speci-men from the center of an insect bite that consists clinically of a vesicle atop an urticarial papule or plaque will reveal a large central intra-epidermal vesicle with smaller intra-cpidermal vesicles that taper progressively in size toward the periphery， whereas a biopsy specimen from the periphery of the same lesion reveals no intra-epidermal vesiculation， but marked subepider-mal edema.

【155】Other organisms and objects may cause reactions in the skin that are indistinguishable from those of arthropods， e.g.， the larvae of creeping eruption， the cercariae of swimmer’s itch， the nematocysis of the Portu-guese man-of-war， the hairs of the puss caterpillar， and the spines ofsea anemones and of coral. When these agents are suspected， careful search should be undertaken in the cornified layer for a mite of scabies， in the spinous layer for a cercaria， and in and above the basal layer for a larva of hookwormn.

【0】ed Carcinoma_ Differentiated thyroid carcinoma of both papillary and follicular type may progress to a more poorly differentiated phenotype. This poorly differen-tiated carcinoma may present as a more distinet morphologic entity referred to as insular carcinoma or a group of less-well-defined morphologic phenotype. The latter group of poorly dif-ferentiated thyroidcarcinoma， which has included entities such as columnar and tall variants of papillary carcinoma and tumors with solid and trabecular architecture， has been controversial. with its inclusion as a distinct category in question 通用删除6(英):<u>\[300\]</u>.

【1】INSULAR CARCINOMA Insular carcinoma is a morphologi-cally distinct form of tumor derived from the thyroid follicular cells having an aggressive biological course. The incidence of these tumors varies from being rare in the United States to about4% of all thyroid cancers seen in an Italian study 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. We have ourselves seen several cases of pure insular carcinoma in our practice， and it is not uncommon to see foci of insular growth associated with differentiated thyroid tumorsin someother cases(personal experience). These tumors tend to involve elderly patients with a slight female predilection 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【2】On gross examination these tumors are large in size and ex-hibit an invasive growth with associated areas of necrosis . On histology they are composed of well-defined islands of round or oval cells that lack significantpleomorphism. Small microfollicular structures may be seen within these islands， and it is notuncommon to see necrosis in the center of these islands. Foci of vascularinvasion are notinfrequent通用删除6(英):<u>\[30，132\]</u>.

【3】_Differential Diagnosis_ The tumor that insular carcinoma should be differentiated from and can pose problems on mor-phology is medullary carcinoma.Immunohistochemistry is very useful in these situations. Insular carcinoma cells are positive for thyroglobulin and negative for calcitonin and other neuro-endocrine markers. Another primary tumor that may have to be

通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 12Insular carcinoma.(A)Macroscopic appearance of thyroid gland with insula carcinoma； (B) solid islands of tumor cells with micro-follicular structure characteristic of insular carcinoma.</u>|删除换行|differentiated is the solid variant of papillary carcinoma， which is more common following exposure to nuclear radiation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[270，271\]</u>. In these cases the nuclear features of papillary carcinoma are helpful in differential diagnosis.

【5】_Anaplastic Carcinoma_ Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is a highly aggressive and rare thyroid tumor， accounting for 1.7%of all thyroid cancers in the United States 通用删除6(英):<u>\[165\]</u>. Its incidence is higher in regions endemic for goiter 通用删除6(英):<u>\[301\]</u>. The patients are usually elderly in their seventh or eight decade of life， with a female preponderance of approx 2.5：1 通用删除6(英):<u>\[165\]</u>. A personal his-tory of goiter may be seen in approx 25% of cases and prior exposure to radiation in 9.4% cases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[165\]</u>.Patients present with rapidly enlarging neck mass associated with compressingsymp-toms such as dysphagia， hoarseness， and stridor. Often signs and symptoms related to metastatic tumor may be the first pre-sentation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，165\]</u>. On gross examination the tumor is usually large， the majority being >4.0 cm 通用删除6(英):<u>\[165\]</u>， often replacing the entire thyroid and spreading into the perithyroidal soft tissues通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.On microscopic examination， the tumor may exhibit one of the three patterns or a mixture of more than one of these pat-terns including squamoid pattern resembling the nonkeratiniz-ing squamous cell carcinoma， spindle cell pattern resembling sarcoma， and giant cell type . All three types of pat-tern are associated with a high mitotic rate and focal necrosis may be seen. The spindle cell sarcomalike pattern may show paucicellular areas with dense fibrosis that may alternate with cellular areas， which aids in the diagnosis of anaplastic thyroid carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[30，132\]</u>. The giant cell pattern is associated with a marked degree of pleomorphism with large multinucleated cells including tumor giant cells. The tumors are highly inva-sive with infiltration of the perithyroidal soft tissues 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. In some cases heterologous stromal elements including cartilage or bone may be seen 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【6】On immunohistochemistry the squamoid-type tumors are positive for high-and low-molecular-weight keratin，EMA， and sometimes CEA. The spindle cell pattern shows variable posi-tivity with low-molecular-weight keratin ranging in incidence from 47% to 100% cases. Thyroglobulin staining is also vari-able， ranging from 9% to 71% cases and is usually focal and weak 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. Ultrastructurally evidence of epithelial differenti-ation is seen in most tumors \[1321.

【7】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS OF ANAPLASTIC CARCINOMA Thesqua-moid type anaplastic carcinoma should be differentiated from metastatic carcinoma from primary sites such as lung，esopha-gus，and upper aerodigestive tract. The history of arapidly grow-ing mass in the region of the thyroid together with the finding of differentiated thyroid carcinoma in some areas and positive immunostaining with thyroglobulin may be helpful in the dif-ferential diagnosis.

【8】The spindle-cell-type tumor should be differentiated from _true sarcoma such as fibrosarcoma， malignant fibrous histio-cytoma， angiosarcoma， and hemangiopericytoma. This may_ pose the greatest difficulty especially in cases where the entire tumor is of spindle cell type and is paucicellular. Features that favor anaplastic thyroid carcinoma include foci of better-dif-ferentiated areas， justifying thorough sampling of the tumor and evidence of epithelial differentiation on immunohis-tochemistry and electron microscopy. In addition， metaplastic spindle cell proliferation， which can sometimes be seen asso-ciated with papillary carcinoma and follicular adenoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[183\]</u>， should also be differentiated from spindle-cell-type anaplastic carcinoma because of the significant difference in the biologi-cal behavior and management of the two entities.

【9】_Medullary thyroid carcinoma may show a variety of growth_ patterns， and this may have to be differentiated from the spindle cell type and pleomorphic variants of anaplastic carcinoma.

【10】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 13 Anaplastic carcinoma. (A) Giant cell type with necrosis； (B) spindle cell type.**</u>

【11】Immunohistochemistry plays a very important role in this dif-ferentiation and must be performed using antibodies to calcito-nin， chromogranin， and CEA， which are all positive in medullary carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【12】Malignant lymphoma may also be considered in cases with small cells； however， the even distribution of smaller， uniform cells in lymphoma and lack of focal epithelial islands is helpful in this differential diagnosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【13】Riedel's thyroiditis may be confused with the paucicellular spindle-cell-typeanaplastic thyroid carcinoma， which may show marked sclerosis and lack significant pleomorphism and mito-tic activity. In these cases， features that favor anaplastic carci-noma include the presence of necrosis， more cellular areas，and evidence of vascular invasion and metastases 通用删除6(英):<u>\[30\]</u>. The more cellular areas and better differentiated thyroid carcinoma may be seen on extensive sampling，whichis crucial in the diagnosis of anaplastic carcinoma in these problematic cases.

【14】The prognosis in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is extremely poor， with mean survival of 7.2±10 mo 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【15】人名段删除-1:<u>**_Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma_**</u>

CLINICAL FEATURES ANDETIOLOGYThe tumorderived from the thyroid C cells that is now referred to as medullary carcinoma was first regarded as an unusual variant of anaplastic carcinoma通用删除6(英):<u>\[30\]</u>. The term medullary carcinoma was coined by Hazard et al. in 1959， who reviewed 600 cases of thyroid cancer over a31-yr period at the Cleveland Clinic， reported 21 tumors with unique morphological features including solid growth pattern and amyloid stroma， and called them medullary carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[302\]</u>. Later Williams in 1966 identified the cell of origin of these tumors as C cells \[3031.Medullary thyroid carcinoma is a rare tumor with a incidence of 3.2%(0.5% familial and 2.7%spora-dic) of all thyroid cancers in acohort of more than 5500 patients in the United States 通用删除6(英):<u>\[165\]</u>. One of the unique features of this tumor is that it occurs both in a familial setting associated other endocrine neoplasms as part of the multiple endocrine neo-|删除0换行|plasia syndrome (MEN) and also as sporadic tumors in a non-familial setting 通用删除6(英):<u>\[304，305\]</u>.**

【17】Sporadic medullary carcinoma is the more common form of tumor， representing approx 80% of all medullary carcinomas. The remaining 20% are familial and are inherited as autosomal dominant trait with high penetrance 通用删除6(英):<u>\[30，165\]</u>. The latter may either occur in association with other endocrine tumors as part ofMEN2A，which includes in addition to medullary carcinoma， adrenal medullary hyperplasia-pheochromocytoma and para-thyroid hyperplasia-adenoma and MEN 2B 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>，which includes， in addition to pheochromocytoma， mucosal ganglioneuroma and skeletal abnormalities. In addition these may occur as fa-milial non-MEN medullary thyroid carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[306-309\]</u>.The gene for MEN 2A and 2B syndrome is called the RET proto-oncogene， which is located on chromosome 10. Germline mis-sense mutation of this gene is seen in patients with MEN2A and MEN 2B 通用删除6(英):<u>\[306，307，310-312\]</u>. Sporadic tumors may sometime show mutation in the RET protooncogene 通用删除6(英):<u>\[312\]</u>.

【18】The age at presentation in the familial form of medullary carcinoma is younger than in the sporadic form and both show a slight female predilection 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. With increased prospective screening of family members of MEN patients， the age at pres-entation of familial form of medullary carcinoma is becoming progressively younger 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. The sporadic form presents with a solitary mass with or without lymph node metastases. The familial form is usually multicentric and bilateral. In addition， patients may have diarrhea and both carcinoid and Cushing's syndromes have been reported 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，304，305\]</u>.Increased levels of serum calcitonin and CEA are seen in both familial and spora-dicmedullary carcinoma and are important diagnostictests 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

PATHOLOGY OF MEDULLARY CARCINOMA The tumors vary in size from barely visible to large tumors that may replace the entire lobe； the smaller tumors are often seen in patients with MEN 2 syndrome who undergo prophylactic thyroidectomy for high serum calcitonin levels that are discovered at routine|删除0换行|screening. The small tumors， which are <1.0 cm， are referred to as medullary microcarcinoma and are commonly seen at the junction of upper and middle thirds of the lobes 通用删除6(英):<u>\[304，313-315\]</u>. In these cases it is important that the entire gland be submitted so that small tumors that may not be apparent grossly are not missed. On sectioning the tumors have firm yellow white cut surface.Thelarge tumors usually have an indistinct border and most are not encapsulated. However， rarely a thick fibrous capsule may sometimes be seen and may sometimes be associ-ated with cystic and papillary change 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，316\]</u>.

【20】On microscopic examination medullary carcinomas are usu-ally circumscribed and show a variety of growth patterns that may mimic follicular，papillary，insular， and anaplastic thyroid carcinoma， emphasizing the importance of careful morpho-logic evaluation and use of immunostaining to differentiate it from these follicular-cell-derived tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[30，132，317\]</u>. The most typical growth pattern includes solid nests or trabeculae or an insular pattern separated with thin fibrovascular core. The cells within these nests are round， oval， or spindle shaped， with a finely granular dispersed chromatin typical of neuroendocrine cells； giant multinucleated cells may sometimes be seen. The cytoplasmis amphophilic or eosinophilic and may appear clear， sometimes with occasional mucin positive intracytoplasmic vacuoles 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>. Amyloid  may be seen in the stroma in up to 80% of tumors， and stains positively with calcitonin on immunohistochemistry. In the familial type of medullary car-cinoma areas of C-cell hyperplasia are usually seen associated with the tumor， which is a feature not seen in sporadic tumors通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，296，318\]</u>.On immunohistochemistry， the tumor cells are negative for thyroglobulin and positive for panneuroendocrine markers such as synaptophysin and chromogranin， and more specific markers such as calcitonin and calcitonin gene-related peptide. In addition， CEA is another useful marker that is posi-tive in medullary carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，317\]</u>. Sex steroid receptors， especially the progesterone receptor， may be seen in medullary carcinoma on immunohistochemistry 通用删除6(英):<u>\[319\]</u>. Ultrastructurally the characteristic membrane-bound neurosecretory granules are seen in the cytoplasm 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【21】Medullary carcinoma variants include follicular variant， papillary variant， oncocytic variant ， small cell vari- _ant， giant cell variant， clear cell variant， melanotic variant，_ _squamous variant， encapsulated variant， and paraganglioma-_ like variant 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，316，320\]</u>. The presence of all these variants makes medullary carcinoma the great mimicker of other thy-roid carcinoma； therefore immunohistochemistry should be performed in all cases when the diagnosis is in doubt or some atypical features are present.

【22】**The prognosis in medullary carcinoma shows considerable variation. The 5-and 10-yr survival rates are 60-70% and 40-50%， respectively. Better prognostic factors include younger age， females，early tumor stage， and familial tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132，321\]</u>.**

【23】**_C-Cell Hyperplasia and Medullary Microcarcinoma_ C-CELL HYPERPLASIA**

【24】_General Considerations_ The calcitonin-producing Ccells are derived from the neural crest and descend down into the thyroid with the ultimobranchial body； therefore，they are found mainly at the junction of the upper and middle third of the two thyroid lobes， frequently associated with solid cell nests 通用删除6(英):<u>\[14\]</u>.

【25】C cells are usually visualized on routine hematoxylin and eosin stains but may be easily seen on immunohistochemistry . Theincreasein the numbers of C cells is referred to as C-cell hyperplasia. C-cell hyperplasia， which was first described by Wolfe in 1973 in patients with MEN 2A 通用删除6(英):<u>\[322\]</u>， can also be seen to be associated in certain other situations with no evidence of MEN 2. Whereas the former is referred to as familial C-cell hyperplasia， thought to be a neoplastic proliferation， the latter is called physiological or secondary C-cell hyperplasia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，324\]</u>.

【26】_The familial C-cell hyperplasia is thought to be neoplastic_ and is regarded as a precursor of familial type of medullary+hatarcarcinoma； therefore the term hyperplasia for these lesions is a misnomer and has been questioned 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，325\]</u>. It is thought to represent the preinvasive stage (carcinoma in situ) of medul-ISIYE lary carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[324\]</u>. The neoplastic nature of this form of“hyperplasia”is further supported by the fact that C cells are clonal 通用删除6(英):<u>\[326\]</u> and show a polysialic acid immunostaining pat-tern that is distinct from the physiological/reactive C-cell hyper-plasia \[3271.

【27】_Physiological C-cell hyperplasia， also referred to as reac-_ tive or secondary C-cell hyperplasia， has been associated with conditions causing hypercalcemia such as hyperparathyroid-ism 通用删除6(英):<u>\[328，329\]</u>. This form of C-cell hyperplasia has also been seen associated with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[330，331\]</u>， multi-nodular goiter， hyperthyroidism，lymphoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[332，333\]</u>，around thyroid tumors of follicular cell origin 通用删除6(英):<u>\[334\]</u>， and following subtotal thyroidectomy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[335\]</u>.

【28】_Diagnosis_ SThe diagnostic criteria for what constitutes C-cell hyperplasia are not clearly established. It includes defini-tions ranging from imprecise descriptions of C-cell volume， which can be very subjective 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，336\]</u>， to semiquantatative estimates such as>50 cells per 50 low-power fields to>50 cells per l low-power field 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323\]</u>. Guyent et al. have proposed more precise quantitative criteria that include >40 cells/cm² or>50cells in 3 low-power (×100) fields 通用删除6(英):<u>\[337\]</u>. We believe that for practical purposes if one can see C cells on routine hematoxylin and eosin stain that are later confirmed as C cells on immuno-histochemistry， this should be considered C-cell hyperplasia. In patients with MEN 2 who undergo thyroidec-tomy for rising serum calcitonin levels， the entire thyroid gland should be submitted to identify areas of C-cell hyperplasia and immunohistochemistry should be performed. C-cell hyperpla-sia can be focal， diffuse， or nodular depending on the extent of follicular involvement and morphology 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.On immu-nohistochemistry， C cells stain positively for chromogranin， synaptophysin， calcitonin， calcitonin gene related peptide，and CEA 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【29】_Differential Diagnosis_ C-cell hyperplasia should be dis-tinguished from solid cell nests， islands of squamous metapla-sia that can be seen in Hashimoto’s thyroiditis or in remnants of branchial clefts， intrathyroidal remnants of thymus and para-thyroid tissue， and finally follicular cells appearing as solid clusters as aresult of tangential sectioning. Immunohistochem-istry can be very useful to distinguish these conditions from C-cell hyperplasia. However， one important lesion that has to be distinguished from nodular-type C-cell hyperplasia and can be challenging sometimes is a small medullary microcarcinoma described below.

【30】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 14C-cell hyperplasia and medullary carcinoma. (A) C-cell hyperplasia (H&E)； (B) C-cell hyperplasia showing positive immu-nostaining with calcitonin stain (immunoperoxidase)； (C) medullary microcarcinoma in a familial case associated with C-cell hyperplasia；(D) same case as in C showing central portion of the medullary microcarcinoma； (E) medullary carcinoma， oncocytic variant； (F) same tumor as in E showing amyloid in the stroma. 删除2:<u>(Color illustration appears in insert following p. 148.)</u></u>

【31】MEDULLARY MICROCARCINOMA

【32】_General Considerations_ Medullary thyroid microcarcinoma is defined as a tumor <1.0 cm in size. Its frequency is directly related to screening of MEN 2 family members using genetic testing for RET proto-oncogene mutation and is likely to increase with more widespread genetic testing 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323\]</u>. Medullary miero-carcinoma can be seen both in familial setting and also as spo-radic tumor.

**_The sporadic medullary microcarcinoma are more likely to_ be unilateral and solitary and most of the time areidentified either as an incidental finding in thyroidectomy specimens or at autopsy|删除0换行|or by elevated serum calcitonin levels. Rarely， these tumors can be symptomatic and the symptoms may include diarrhea， palpable mass， enlarged cervical lymph nodes 通用删除6(英):<u>\[313，315，323，338\]</u>， or lung metastases as seen in one series 通用删除6(英):<u>\[313\]</u>. In view of the high incidence of lymph node metastases， aggressive surgi-cal management has been proposed in these patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[314\]</u>.Ad-verse prognostic factors include symptomatic cases， high serum calcitonin level， amyloid stroma， and desmoplasia

C-cell hyperplasia， which was first described by Wolfe in 1973 in patients with MEN 2A 通用删除6(英):<u>\[322\]</u>， can also be seen to be associated in certain other situations with no evidence of MEN 2. Whereas the former is referred to as familial C-cell hyperplasia， thought to be a neoplastic proliferation， the latter is called physiological or secondary C-cell hyperplasia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，324\]</u>.

【26】_The familial C-cell hyperplasia is thought to be neoplastic_ and is regarded as a precursor of familial type of medullary+hatarcarcinoma； therefore the term hyperplasia for these lesions is a misnomer and has been questioned 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，325\]</u>. It is thought to represent the preinvasive stage (carcinoma in situ) of medul-ISIYE lary carcinoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[324\]</u>. The neoplastic nature of this form of“hyperplasia”is further supported by the fact that C cells are clonal 通用删除6(英):<u>\[326\]</u> and show a polysialic acid immunostaining pat-tern that is distinct from the physiological/reactive C-cell hyper-plasia \[3271.

【27】_Physiological C-cell hyperplasia， also referred to as reac-_ tive or secondary C-cell hyperplasia， has been associated with conditions causing hypercalcemia such as hyperparathyroid-ism 通用删除6(英):<u>\[328，329\]</u>. This form of C-cell hyperplasia has also been seen associated with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[330，331\]</u>， multi-nodular goiter， hyperthyroidism，lymphoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[332，333\]</u>，around thyroid tumors of follicular cell origin 通用删除6(英):<u>\[334\]</u>， and following subtotal thyroidectomy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[335\]</u>.

【28】_Diagnosis_ SThe diagnostic criteria for what constitutes C-cell hyperplasia are not clearly established. It includes defini-tions ranging from imprecise descriptions of C-cell volume， which can be very subjective 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323，336\]</u>， to semiquantatative estimates such as>50 cells per 50 low-power fields to>50 cells per l low-power field 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323\]</u>. Guyent et al. have proposed more precise quantitative criteria that include >40 cells/cm² or>50cells in 3 low-power (×100) fields 通用删除6(英):<u>\[337\]</u>. We believe that for practical purposes if one can see C cells on routine hematoxylin and eosin stain that are later confirmed as C cells on immuno-histochemistry， this should be considered C-cell hyperplasia. In patients with MEN 2 who undergo thyroidec-tomy for rising serum calcitonin levels， the entire thyroid gland should be submitted to identify areas of C-cell hyperplasia and immunohistochemistry should be performed. C-cell hyperpla-sia can be focal， diffuse， or nodular depending on the extent of follicular involvement and morphology 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.On immu-nohistochemistry， C cells stain positively for chromogranin， synaptophysin， calcitonin， calcitonin gene related peptide，and CEA 通用删除6(英):<u>\[132\]</u>.

【29】_Differential Diagnosis_ C-cell hyperplasia should be dis-tinguished from solid cell nests， islands of squamous metapla-sia that can be seen in Hashimoto’s thyroiditis or in remnants of branchial clefts， intrathyroidal remnants of thymus and para-thyroid tissue， and finally follicular cells appearing as solid clusters as aresult of tangential sectioning. Immunohistochem-istry can be very useful to distinguish these conditions from C-cell hyperplasia. However， one important lesion that has to be distinguished from nodular-type C-cell hyperplasia and can be challenging sometimes is a small medullary microcarcinoma described below.

【31】MEDULLARY MICROCARCINOMA

【32】_General Considerations_ Medullary thyroid microcarcinoma is defined as a tumor <1.0 cm in size. Its frequency is directly related to screening of MEN 2 family members using genetic testing for RET proto-oncogene mutation and is likely to increase with more widespread genetic testing 通用删除6(英):<u>\[323\]</u>. Medullary miero-carcinoma can be seen both in familial setting and also as spo-radic tumor.

**_The sporadic medullary microcarcinoma are more likely to_ be unilateral and solitary and most of the time areidentified either as an incidental finding in thyroidectomy specimens or at autopsy|删除0换行|or by elevated serum calcitonin levels. Rarely， these tumors can be symptomatic and the symptoms may include diarrhea， palpable mass， enlarged cervical lymph nodes 通用删除6(英):<u>\[313，315，323，338\]</u>， or lung metastases as seen in one series 通用删除6(英):<u>\[313\]</u>. In view of the high incidence of lymph node metastases， aggressive surgi-cal management has been proposed in these patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[314\]</u>.Ad-verse prognostic factors include symptomatic cases， high serum calcitonin level， amyloid stroma， and desmoplasia

【1】### 11.7.4 Clinical Manifestations

【2】Typical cutaneous lesions are well-defined scaly erythematous plaques that are either isolated or grouped, predominantly around the surfaces of the articular extensors, the trunk, the sacral region and the scalp (psoriasis vulgaris). There are also less common forms that predominantly affect the skin folds (inverse psoriasis) and generalized, pustular forms (erythrodermic psoriasis), among others. The nails are affected in various ways and intensities in up to a half of patients with psoriasis vulgaris, however, the nails are affected in over 80% of psoriasis sufferers whose joints are affected (psoriatic arthritis). Symptomatically, itching is variable and occurs in around 80% of patients.

【3】It mainly affects the folded areas of the genitalia (the inguinal regions, the foreskin and the keratinized parts of the vulva) and manifests as well-defined erythematous plaques without desquamation. Isolated genital lesions may be the initial manifestation of the disease and there may be a family history. Pustular psoriasis may occasionally affect the mucosa of the vulva, vagina and cervix.

【4】### 11.7.5 Laboratory Diagnosis

【5】Diagnosis involves clinical and histopathalogical examination of the skin: parakeratosis, uniform acanthosis, elongation of interpapillary cones, small clusters of neutrophils on the inside of the epithelium which may form intraepithelial abscesses (Munro’s abscesses), hyperkeratosis or dermis with elongated, broad or twisted papillae with dilated capillaries.

【6】### 11.7.6 Treatment and Control of Cure

【7】Various drugs and therapeutic regimes may be applied to treat psoriasis, which would go beyond the scope of this text. Specific treatment for genital psoriasis is difficult to control, as it is based on medium-strength topical corticosteroids.

【8】### 11.7.7 Differential Diagnosis

【9】In most cases psoriasis has an easy clinical diagnosis and the semiotic technique of the Brocq cutterage method can also be applied. However, differential diagnosis for psoriasis includes seborrheic dermatitis, palmar-plantar eczema, erythrodermic cases with other etiologies, hanseniasis and various onychopathies, etc.

【10】Differential diagnosis for vulvar and penile psoriasis includes candidiasis (which can also occur at the same time as psoriasis), dermatophytosis, seborrheic dermatitis and contact eczema.

【29】**Case Study Analysis**

【30】A 70-year-old female， after eating a fatty， spicy meal， wakes up at 3 a.m. with substernal chest pain associated with burning in the chest that was relieved on sitting up and also on taking antacids. Her pertinent negatives are the absence of exertional chest pain， dyspnea， and lower extremity edema. She started taking a new medication， Procardia， which can cause relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter， leading to acid reflux and esophageal spasm. Her differential diagnosis includes atypical chest pain， cardiac ischemia， or gastric acid reflux. Her cardiac enzymes， EKG， and echocardiogram are normal.

【31】The combination of high-fat content meal， and pain relieved when sitting up and after taking an antacid all indicate acute onset or exacerbation of GERD. In addition， the adverse effect of Procardia may have precipitated the episode.

The advanced practice provider provides teaching about the need to avoid foods with a high-fat content and that are spicy. The patient should also sit upright for at least 60 minutes|删除0换行|after eating， avoid eating for several hours before going to sleep， and limit the intake of alco-hol and caffeine. Should the symptoms continue， the cardiologist should be notified of the11010patient's adverse effect to determine if a medication change would be indicated.

A， often associated with dif-ferentiation syndrome (DS； previously called “retinoic acid syndrome"). It is a potentially fatal complication of induc-tion chemotherapy in patients with APL. Clinically， DS is characterized by weight gain (peripheral edema)， fever not attributable to infection， respiratory distress (+hypox-emia)， cardiac involvement， hypotension， hepatic dysfunc-tion， and/or acute renal failure. Morphologically， there is an extensive interstitial and intra-alveolar pulmonary infil-tration by maturing myeloid cells， endothelial cell damage，|删除0换行|intra-alveolar edema， interalveolar hemorrhage， and fibrin-ous exudates.**

【1】**FC Differential Diagnosis**

Classic APL has a well-recognized FC pattern with increased SSC and lack of expression of HLA-DR， CD1lc， CD11b， CD18， positive CD117， negative or weakly positive CD15 and CD65， negative CD34， often positive CD64， variable (het-erogeneous) CD13， and bright CD33 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，32-35\]</u>. The differ-ential diagnosis of hypergranular APL (pattern 1) includes normally maturing myeloid cells， BM with myelodysplasia， chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms with myeloid leftward shift， benign marrow proliferations (e.g.， recovering marrow after treatment)， occasional cases of acute monoblastic leu-kemia， and rare cases of AML with maturation， which have|删除0换行|high SSC and lack HLA-DR expression. The differential diagnosis of hypogranular APL (pattern 2) includes AML with or without maturation， acute monoblastic leukemia， and MDS with prominent dysgranulopoiesis (e.g.， hypogranular cytoplasm).

【3】**Blasts in non-APL AML usually have low SSC and are positive for HLA-DR， whereas atypical hypergranular pro-myelocytes in APL have high SSC (they are located in the same area as normal granulocytes on CD45 vs. SSC dot plot display) and lack the expression of HLA-DR. The subset of AMLs with or without maturation may be HLA-DR-， but they differ from hypogranular APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and negative CD2， and from hypergranular(classic) APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and low SSC. Rare cases of AML with maturation may be char-acterized by high SSC (“granulocytic” gate)； these blasts may lack CD34 and CD117 expression. The morphologic evaluation of aspirate smear at the time of FC analysis is often crucial for proper interpretation of flow findings. HLA-DR-/CD34- phenotype in AML with normal karyo-type by conventional cytogeneties is associated with FLT3-ITD 通用删除6(英):<u>\[36\]</u>. Albano et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u> reported the association of CD34 expression with the APLv and higher proportion of CD2+ and HLA-DR+ cases. In the same study， CD34+ APL patients had a significantly higher percentage of peripheral blood leukemic promyelocytes at presentation， were more frequently female， and had a higher proportion of ber3expression， but there were no differences between the two groups in terms of complete remission， overall survival， and disease-free survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u>.**

【4】Expression of HLA-DR， CD11b， CD11c， CD14， and CD64 helps to differentiate phenotypically acute mono-blastic leukemia (HLA-DR+， CD11b+， CD11c+， CD14+(variable)/， CD64+ (bright) from the APLv (HLA-DR-， CD11b-， CD11c-， CD14-， CD64+dim). Monoblasts are often positive for CD11b， have bright CD11c， may show positive， variable (smeary) expression of CD14， and are often positive for CD56， whereas CD56 is only rarely expressed in APL. All APL cases express CD117， whereas CD117 is positive only in the subset of acute monoblastic leukemias. The majority of acute monoblastic leukemias show moderate to bright HLA-DR； only rare cases are HLA-DR-. Acute monoblastic leukemia expresses CD64(bright)， and APL usually shows only dim expression of CD64. In most cases of acute monoblastic leukemia， the expression of CD45 is brighter than in APL. The SSC of monoblastic leukemia is only slightly increased (in con-trast to classic APL). Only occasional cases of acute mono-blastic leukemia show high SSC.

**Analysis of CD10， CD11b， CD11c， CD16， CD117， and HLA-DR helps to distinguish benign process from APL. Neutrophilic maturation from blasts through promyelo-cytes， myelocytes， metamyelocytes， bands， and neutrophils is characterized by loss of CD34 and HLA-DR expres-sion at promyelocytic stage and loss of CD117 expres-sion at myelocytic stage， and acquisition of CDllb and CD11c expression at myelocytic stage， and CD10 and CD16|删除0换行|expression by neutrophils. CD64 is expressed by promy-elocytes through metamyelocytes. In contrast to APL， granulocytes are positive for CD10， CD11b， CD11c， and CD16， and are negative for CD117. Granulocytes/matur-ing myeloid precursors with dyspoiesis (e.g.， MDS) and/or leftward shift (e.g.， CML) may display an aberrant down-regulation of CD10， CD11b， and CD16， but in contrast to neoplastic promyelocytes lack CD117 expression and are(at least partially) CD11c+.

【6】**_AML WITH RUNX1-RUNX1T1_**

【7】**MORPHOLOGY**

【8】AML with t(8；21)(q22；q22) (RUNXI-RUNXITI) most often display the morphology of AML with maturation \[former French-American-British (FAB) M2 category\]通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，38，39\]</u>. Blasts are large with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and variable， and often increased numbers of azurophilic granules and frequent Auer rods. Large granules (pseudo Chediak-Higashi granules) are often present. Maturing elements often show dysgranulopoiesis (including pseudo Pelger-Huet nuclei). AML with t(8；21) is associated with a higher incidence of myeloid sarcoma (extramedullary myeloid tumor) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>.

【9】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【10】Phenotypically， AML with t(8；21) is positive for pan-myeloid antigens (CD13， CD33)， HLA-DR， and blastic markers(CD34， CD117)， and characteristically for B-cell antigens(CD19， PAX5， and/or CD79a) and often also CD56 and/or CD7 . Rare cases may be dimly terminaldeoxynucleotidyl _1_ transferase(TdT))Ppositive. Occasional cases may show dim CD33， lack of surface pan-myeloid antigens， or aberrant expression of CD15 and/or CD65. The expression of CD34 is often strong.

【11】**CYTOGENETICS/FISH**

【12】The t(8；21)  is one of the most frequent struc-tural chromosomal abnormalities seen in AML. AML with t(8；21) represents ~5%-12% of de novo AMLs 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.Thet(8；21) results in fusion between RUNXI gene (Runt-related gene family； formerly termed AMLI gene) and RUNXITI gene(also known as ETO gene for eight twenty-one) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[39，41，42\]</u>. AML with t(8；21) belongs to a group of core-binding fac-tor (CBF) leukemias. CBF is also rearranged in AML with t(3；21) and t(16；16)/inv(16). This subtype of AML is associ-ated with favorable prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[42-44\]</u>.

【13】Gustafson et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[45\]</u> studied 13 cases of therapy-related AML (t-AML)/t(8；21) and 38 adult cases of de novo AML/t(8；21). Morphologically， it has the most common features of AML with maturation or acute myelomonocytic leukemia， but it may have features of any other leukemia type except for APL and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recognized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. It is associ-ated with fusion of EVII (ecotropic virus integration-1) with RPNI gene. These patients often present with anemia and the platelet count can be normal or increased. The BM often shows an increased number of small hypolobated (or|删除0换行|monolobated) megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. There are no specific immunophenotypic findings， as blasts may display myeloid， megakaryocytic， or monocytic differ-entiation. Patients are often refractory to conventional ther-apy and have short overall survival.

【46】**AML WITH NPM1 MUTATIONS OR BIALLELIC MUTATIONS OF CEBPA**

【48】AMLwith NPMI mutation is associated with good prognosis. The NPM1 gene is located on chromosome 5q35. AMLs with NPM I mutations often show monocytic differentiation， but sporadically other morphologic variants of AML have been reported. Blasts show monocytic immu-nophenotype and are typically CD34-. AML with NPM1or biallelic mutations of CEBPA is considered low-risk leu-kemia (in both adults and children). NPMI mutations are more common in adults； they have been detected in 5%-8%of children with AML and ~30% of adults with AML (~50%of AMLs with normal karyotype). NPMI mutations may be associated with internal tandem duplication of FLT3 and normal karyotype. Prognosis in children is similar to CBF leukemia (overall survival >80%).

text.content:
A， often associated with dif-ferentiation syndrome (DS； previously called “retinoic acid syndrome"). It is a potentially fatal complication of induc-tion chemotherapy in patients with APL. Clinically， DS is characterized by weight gain (peripheral edema)， fever not attributable to infection， respiratory distress (+hypox-emia)， cardiac involvement， hypotension， hepatic dysfunc-tion， and/or acute renal failure. Morphologically， there is an extensive interstitial and intra-alveolar pulmonary infil-tration by maturing myeloid cells， endothelial cell damage，|删除0换行|intra-alveolar edema， interalveolar hemorrhage， and fibrin-ous exudates.**

【1】**FC Differential Diagnosis**

Classic APL has a well-recognized FC pattern with increased SSC and lack of expression of HLA-DR， CD1lc， CD11b， CD18， positive CD117， negative or weakly positive CD15 and CD65， negative CD34， often positive CD64， variable (het-erogeneous) CD13， and bright CD33 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，32-35\]</u>. The differ-ential diagnosis of hypergranular APL (pattern 1) includes normally maturing myeloid cells， BM with myelodysplasia， chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms with myeloid leftward shift， benign marrow proliferations (e.g.， recovering marrow after treatment)， occasional cases of acute monoblastic leu-kemia， and rare cases of AML with maturation， which have|删除0换行|high SSC and lack HLA-DR expression. The differential diagnosis of hypogranular APL (pattern 2) includes AML with or without maturation， acute monoblastic leukemia， and MDS with prominent dysgranulopoiesis (e.g.， hypogranular cytoplasm).

【3】**Blasts in non-APL AML usually have low SSC and are positive for HLA-DR， whereas atypical hypergranular pro-myelocytes in APL have high SSC (they are located in the same area as normal granulocytes on CD45 vs. SSC dot plot display) and lack the expression of HLA-DR. The subset of AMLs with or without maturation may be HLA-DR-， but they differ from hypogranular APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and negative CD2， and from hypergranular(classic) APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and low SSC. Rare cases of AML with maturation may be char-acterized by high SSC (“granulocytic” gate)； these blasts may lack CD34 and CD117 expression. The morphologic evaluation of aspirate smear at the time of FC analysis is often crucial for proper interpretation of flow findings. HLA-DR-/CD34- phenotype in AML with normal karyo-type by conventional cytogeneties is associated with FLT3-ITD 通用删除6(英):<u>\[36\]</u>. Albano et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u> reported the association of CD34 expression with the APLv and higher proportion of CD2+ and HLA-DR+ cases. In the same study， CD34+ APL patients had a significantly higher percentage of peripheral blood leukemic promyelocytes at presentation， were more frequently female， and had a higher proportion of ber3expression， but there were no differences between the two groups in terms of complete remission， overall survival， and disease-free survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u>.**

【4】Expression of HLA-DR， CD11b， CD11c， CD14， and CD64 helps to differentiate phenotypically acute mono-blastic leukemia (HLA-DR+， CD11b+， CD11c+， CD14+(variable)/， CD64+ (bright) from the APLv (HLA-DR-， CD11b-， CD11c-， CD14-， CD64+dim). Monoblasts are often positive for CD11b， have bright CD11c， may show positive， variable (smeary) expression of CD14， and are often positive for CD56， whereas CD56 is only rarely expressed in APL. All APL cases express CD117， whereas CD117 is positive only in the subset of acute monoblastic leukemias. The majority of acute monoblastic leukemias show moderate to bright HLA-DR； only rare cases are HLA-DR-. Acute monoblastic leukemia expresses CD64(bright)， and APL usually shows only dim expression of CD64. In most cases of acute monoblastic leukemia， the expression of CD45 is brighter than in APL. The SSC of monoblastic leukemia is only slightly increased (in con-trast to classic APL). Only occasional cases of acute mono-blastic leukemia show high SSC.

**Analysis of CD10， CD11b， CD11c， CD16， CD117， and HLA-DR helps to distinguish benign process from APL. Neutrophilic maturation from blasts through promyelo-cytes， myelocytes， metamyelocytes， bands， and neutrophils is characterized by loss of CD34 and HLA-DR expres-sion at promyelocytic stage and loss of CD117 expres-sion at myelocytic stage， and acquisition of CDllb and CD11c expression at myelocytic stage， and CD10 and CD16|删除0换行|expression by neutrophils. CD64 is expressed by promy-elocytes through metamyelocytes. In contrast to APL， granulocytes are positive for CD10， CD11b， CD11c， and CD16， and are negative for CD117. Granulocytes/matur-ing myeloid precursors with dyspoiesis (e.g.， MDS) and/or leftward shift (e.g.， CML) may display an aberrant down-regulation of CD10， CD11b， and CD16， but in contrast to neoplastic promyelocytes lack CD117 expression and are(at least partially) CD11c+.

【6】**_AML WITH RUNX1-RUNX1T1_**

【7】**MORPHOLOGY**

【8】AML with t(8；21)(q22；q22) (RUNXI-RUNXITI) most often display the morphology of AML with maturation \[former French-American-British (FAB) M2 category\]通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，38，39\]</u>. Blasts are large with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and variable， and often increased numbers of azurophilic granules and frequent Auer rods. Large granules (pseudo Chediak-Higashi granules) are often present. Maturing elements often show dysgranulopoiesis (including pseudo Pelger-Huet nuclei). AML with t(8；21) is associated with a higher incidence of myeloid sarcoma (extramedullary myeloid tumor) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>.

【9】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【10】Phenotypically， AML with t(8；21) is positive for pan-myeloid antigens (CD13， CD33)， HLA-DR， and blastic markers(CD34， CD117)， and characteristically for B-cell antigens(CD19， PAX5， and/or CD79a) and often also CD56 and/or CD7 . Rare cases may be dimly terminaldeoxynucleotidyl _1_ transferase(TdT))Ppositive. Occasional cases may show dim CD33， lack of surface pan-myeloid antigens， or aberrant expression of CD15 and/or CD65. The expression of CD34 is often strong.

【11】**CYTOGENETICS/FISH**

【12】The t(8；21)  is one of the most frequent struc-tural chromosomal abnormalities seen in AML. AML with t(8；21) represents ~5%-12% of de novo AMLs 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.Thet(8；21) results in fusion between RUNXI gene (Runt-related gene family； formerly termed AMLI gene) and RUNXITI gene(also known as ETO gene for eight twenty-one) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[39，41，42\]</u>. AML with t(8；21) belongs to a group of core-binding fac-tor (CBF) leukemias. CBF is also rearranged in AML with t(3；21) and t(16；16)/inv(16). This subtype of AML is associ-ated with favorable prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[42-44\]</u>.

【13】Gustafson et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[45\]</u> studied 13 cases of therapy-related AML (t-AML)/t(8；21) and 38 adult cases of de novo AML/t(8；21). Of 13 t-AML/t(8；21) cases， 11 had previ-ously received chemotherapy with or without radiation for malignant neoplasms and 2 received radiation alone. 【19】**PROGNOSIS**

【20】The prognosis of AML with t(8；21) is good. Despite the over-all good prognosis， ~40% of cases relapse. The WBC count at initial diagnosis， additional chromosomal aberrations such as del(9)， loss of sex chromosomes， and CD56 positivity have been reported as adverse prognostic factors. The presence of KIT mutations is associated with worse outcome (intermedi-ate prognosis) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[46-48\]</u>.

【24】This leukemia has increased blasts and monocytic cells and is characterized by increased atypical (often immature) eosinophils with large basophilic granules intermixed with more typical eosinophilic granules .

【25】**CYTOGENETICS/FISH**

【26】**The diagnosis of AML with CBFB-MYHII is confirmed by metaphase cytogenetic and/or FISH studies .**

【27】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【28】FC shows mixed populations of blasts， monocytes， maturing myeloid cells， and atypical and immature (CD123+) eosin-ophils . Blasts are positive for CD13， CD33， CD34， and CD117， and often also HLA-DR and CD2. They may display an aberrant expression of CD7， CD15， CD56， and CD65， and/or lack of HLA-DR. Monocytic cells are most often positive for CD11b， CD11c， CD13， CD14， CD64， and HLA-DR.

【42】页码段删除-1:<u>**AML WITH DEK-NUP214**</u>

【43】AML with t(6；9)通用删除11(英):<u>(p23；q34)</u> (DEK-NUP214) is a rare variant of AML with or without monocytic features that are often associated with basophilia (>2% basophils) and multilineage dysplasia. It presents with anemia and thrombocytopenia， and often pancytopenia. It occurs in children and younger adults. Morphologically， it has the most common features of AML with maturation or acute myelomonocytic leukemia， but it may have features of any other leukemia type except for APL and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. The translocation t(6；9) is usually the only cytogenetic abnormality detected.

【44】页码间删除-1:<u>**AML WITH RPN1-EV1**</u>

AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recognized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. It is associ-ated with fusion of EVII (ecotropic virus integration-1) with RPNI gene. These patients often present with anemia and the platelet count can be normal or increased. The BM often shows an increased number of small hypolobated (or|删除0换行|monolobated) megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. There are no specific immunophenotypic findings， as blasts may display myeloid， megakaryocytic， or monocytic differ-entiation. Patients are often refractory to conventional ther-apy and have short overall survival.

【47】页码段删除-1:<u>**AML WITH MUTATED NPM1**</u>

【48】AMLwith NPMI mutation is associated with good prognosis. The NPM1 gene is located on chromosome 5q35. AMLs with NPM I mutations often show monocytic differentiation， but sporadically other morphologic variants of AML have been reported. Blasts show monocytic immu-nophenotype and are typically CD34-. AML with NPM1or biallelic mutations of CEBPA is considered low-risk leu-kemia (in both adults and children). NPMI mutations are more common in adults； they have been detected in 5%-8%of children with AML and ~30% of adults with AML (~50%of AMLs with normal karyotype). NPMI mutations may be associated with internal tandem duplication of FLT3 and normal karyotype. Prognosis in children is similar to CBF leukemia (overall survival >80%).

A， often associated with dif-ferentiation syndrome (DS； previously called “retinoic acid syndrome"). It is a potentially fatal complication of induc-tion chemotherapy in patients with APL. Clinically， DS is characterized by weight gain (peripheral edema)， fever not attributable to infection， respiratory distress (+hypox-emia)， cardiac involvement， hypotension， hepatic dysfunc-tion， and/or acute renal failure. Morphologically， there is an extensive interstitial and intra-alveolar pulmonary infil-tration by maturing myeloid cells， endothelial cell damage，|删除0换行|intra-alveolar edema， interalveolar hemorrhage， and fibrin-ous exudates.**

【1】**FC Differential Diagnosis**

Classic APL has a well-recognized FC pattern with increased SSC and lack of expression of HLA-DR， CD1lc， CD11b， CD18， positive CD117， negative or weakly positive CD15 and CD65， negative CD34， often positive CD64， variable (het-erogeneous) CD13， and bright CD33 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，32-35\]</u>. The differ-ential diagnosis of hypergranular APL (pattern 1) includes normally maturing myeloid cells， BM with myelodysplasia， chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms with myeloid leftward shift， benign marrow proliferations (e.g.， recovering marrow after treatment)， occasional cases of acute monoblastic leu-kemia， and rare cases of AML with maturation， which have|删除0换行|high SSC and lack HLA-DR expression. The differential diagnosis of hypogranular APL (pattern 2) includes AML with or without maturation， acute monoblastic leukemia， and MDS with prominent dysgranulopoiesis (e.g.， hypogranular cytoplasm).

【3】**Blasts in non-APL AML usually have low SSC and are positive for HLA-DR， whereas atypical hypergranular pro-myelocytes in APL have high SSC (they are located in the same area as normal granulocytes on CD45 vs. SSC dot plot display) and lack the expression of HLA-DR. The subset of AMLs with or without maturation may be HLA-DR-， but they differ from hypogranular APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and negative CD2， and from hypergranular(classic) APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and low SSC. Rare cases of AML with maturation may be char-acterized by high SSC (“granulocytic” gate)； these blasts may lack CD34 and CD117 expression. The morphologic evaluation of aspirate smear at the time of FC analysis is often crucial for proper interpretation of flow findings. HLA-DR-/CD34- phenotype in AML with normal karyo-type by conventional cytogeneties is associated with FLT3-ITD 通用删除6(英):<u>\[36\]</u>. Albano et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u> reported the association of CD34 expression with the APLv and higher proportion of CD2+ and HLA-DR+ cases. In the same study， CD34+ APL patients had a significantly higher percentage of peripheral blood leukemic promyelocytes at presentation， were more frequently female， and had a higher proportion of ber3expression， but there were no differences between the two groups in terms of complete remission， overall survival， and disease-free survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u>.**

【4】Expression of HLA-DR， CD11b， CD11c， CD14， and CD64 helps to differentiate phenotypically acute mono-blastic leukemia (HLA-DR+， CD11b+， CD11c+， CD14+(variable)/， CD64+ (bright) from the APLv (HLA-DR-， CD11b-， CD11c-， CD14-， CD64+dim). Monoblasts are often positive for CD11b， have bright CD11c， may show positive， variable (smeary) expression of CD14， and are often positive for CD56， whereas CD56 is only rarely expressed in APL. All APL cases express CD117， whereas CD117 is positive only in the subset of acute monoblastic leukemias. The majority of acute monoblastic leukemias show moderate to bright HLA-DR； only rare cases are HLA-DR-. Acute monoblastic leukemia expresses CD64(bright)， and APL usually shows only dim expression of CD64. In most cases of acute monoblastic leukemia， the expression of CD45 is brighter than in APL. The SSC of monoblastic leukemia is only slightly increased (in con-trast to classic APL). Only occasional cases of acute mono-blastic leukemia show high SSC.

**Analysis of CD10， CD11b， CD11c， CD16， CD117， and HLA-DR helps to distinguish benign process from APL. Neutrophilic maturation from blasts through promyelo-cytes， myelocytes， metamyelocytes， bands， and neutrophils is characterized by loss of CD34 and HLA-DR expres-sion at promyelocytic stage and loss of CD117 expres-sion at myelocytic stage， and acquisition of CDllb and CD11c expression at myelocytic stage， and CD10 and CD16|删除0换行|expression by neutrophils. CD64 is expressed by promy-elocytes through metamyelocytes. In contrast to APL， granulocytes are positive for CD10， CD11b， CD11c， and CD16， and are negative for CD117. Granulocytes/matur-ing myeloid precursors with dyspoiesis (e.g.， MDS) and/or leftward shift (e.g.， CML) may display an aberrant down-regulation of CD10， CD11b， and CD16， but in contrast to neoplastic promyelocytes lack CD117 expression and are(at least partially) CD11c+.

【6】**_AML WITH RUNX1-RUNX1T1_**

【7】**MORPHOLOGY**

【8】AML with t(8；21)(q22；q22) (RUNXI-RUNXITI) most often display the morphology of AML with maturation \[former French-American-British (FAB) M2 category\]通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，38，39\]</u>. Blasts are large with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and variable， and often increased numbers of azurophilic granules and frequent Auer rods. Large granules (pseudo Chediak-Higashi granules) are often present. Maturing elements often show dysgranulopoiesis (including pseudo Pelger-Huet nuclei). AML with t(8；21) is associated with a higher incidence of myeloid sarcoma (extramedullary myeloid tumor) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>.

【9】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【10】Phenotypically， AML with t(8；21) is positive for pan-myeloid antigens (CD13， CD33)， HLA-DR， and blastic markers(CD34， CD117)， and characteristically for B-cell antigens(CD19， PAX5， and/or CD79a) and often also CD56 and/or CD7 . Rare cases may be dimly terminaldeoxynucleotidyl _1_ transferase(TdT))Ppositive. Occasional cases may show dim CD33， lack of surface pan-myeloid antigens， or aberrant expression of CD15 and/or CD65. The expression of CD34 is often strong.

【11】**CYTOGENETICS/FISH**

【12】The t(8；21)  is one of the most frequent struc-tural chromosomal abnormalities seen in AML. AML with t(8；21) represents ~5%-12% of de novo AMLs 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.Thet(8；21) results in fusion between RUNXI gene (Runt-related gene family； formerly termed AMLI gene) and RUNXITI gene(also known as ETO gene for eight twenty-one) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[39，41，42\]</u>. AML with t(8；21) belongs to a group of core-binding fac-tor (CBF) leukemias. CBF is also rearranged in AML with t(3；21) and t(16；16)/inv(16). This subtype of AML is associ-ated with favorable prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[42-44\]</u>.

【13】Gustafson et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[45\]</u> studied 13 cases of therapy-related AML (t-AML)/t(8；21) and 38 adult cases of de novo AML/t(8；21). Of 13 t-AML/t(8；21) cases， 11 had previ-ously received chemotherapy with or without radiation for malignant neoplasms and 2 received radiation alone. The WBC count at initial diagnosis， additional chromosomal aberrations such as del(9)， loss of sex chromosomes， and CD56 positivity have been reported as adverse prognostic factors. 【42】页码段删除-1:<u>**AML WITH DEK-NUP214**</u>

【43】AML with t(6；9)通用删除11(英):<u>(p23；q34)</u> (DEK-NUP214) is a rare variant of AML with or without monocytic features that are often associated with basophilia (>2% basophils) and multilineage dysplasia. It presents with anemia and thrombocytopenia， and often pancytopenia. It occurs in children and younger adults. Morphologically， it has the most common features of AML with maturation or acute myelomonocytic leukemia， but it may have features of any other leukemia type except for APL and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. The translocation t(6；9) is usually the only cytogenetic abnormality detected.

【44】页码间删除-1:<u>**AML WITH RPN1-EV1**</u>

AML with inv(3)(q21q26.2) or t(3；3)(q21；q26.2) is recognized as a distinct entity in the WHO classification. It is associ-ated with fusion of EVII (ecotropic virus integration-1) with RPNI gene. These patients often present with anemia and the platelet count can be normal or increased. The BM often shows an increased number of small hypolobated (or|删除0换行|monolobated) megakaryocytes and multilineage dysplasia. There are no specific immunophenotypic findings， as blasts may display myeloid， megakaryocytic， or monocytic differ-entiation. Patients are often refractory to conventional ther-apy and have short overall survival.

【46】**AML WITH NPM1 MUTATIONS OR BIALLELIC MUTATIONS OF CEBPA**

【47】页码段删除-1:<u>**AML WITH MUTATED NPM1**</u>

【48】AMLwith NPMI mutation is associated with good prognosis. The NPM1 gene is located on chromosome 5q35. AMLs with NPM I mutations often show monocytic differentiation， but sporadically other morphologic variants of AML have been reported. Blasts show monocytic immu-nophenotype and are typically CD34-. AML with NPM1or biallelic mutations of CEBPA is considered low-risk leu-kemia (in both adults and children). NPMI mutations are more common in adults； they have been detected in 5%-8%of children with AML and ~30% of adults with AML (~50%of AMLs with normal karyotype). NPMI mutations may be associated with internal tandem duplication of FLT3 and normal karyotype. Prognosis in children is similar to CBF leukemia (overall survival >80%).

【50】**AML WITH MUTATED CEBPA**

【51】The prognosis of AML with mutated CEBPA is favorable. The CEBPA gene is located on chromosome 19q31.1.CEBPA mutations are detected in 10% of AMLs. Classic APL has a well-recognized FC pattern with increased SSC and lack of expression of HLA-DR， CD1lc， CD11b， CD18， positive CD117， negative or weakly positive CD15 and CD65， negative CD34， often positive CD64， variable (het-erogeneous) CD13， and bright CD33 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，32-35\]</u>. The differ-ential diagnosis of hypergranular APL (pattern 1) includes normally maturing myeloid cells， BM with myelodysplasia， chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms with myeloid leftward shift， benign marrow proliferations (e.g.， recovering marrow after treatment)， occasional cases of acute monoblastic leu-kemia， and rare cases of AML with maturation， which have|删除0换行|high SSC and lack HLA-DR expression. The differential diagnosis of hypogranular APL (pattern 2) includes AML with or without maturation， acute monoblastic leukemia， and MDS with prominent dysgranulopoiesis (e.g.， hypogranular cytoplasm).

【3】**Blasts in non-APL AML usually have low SSC and are positive for HLA-DR， whereas atypical hypergranular pro-myelocytes in APL have high SSC (they are located in the same area as normal granulocytes on CD45 vs. SSC dot plot display) and lack the expression of HLA-DR. The subset of AMLs with or without maturation may be HLA-DR-， but they differ from hypogranular APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and negative CD2， and from hypergranular(classic) APL by often positive CD11c and/or CD11b and low SSC. Rare cases of AML with maturation may be char-acterized by high SSC (“granulocytic” gate)； these blasts may lack CD34 and CD117 expression. The morphologic evaluation of aspirate smear at the time of FC analysis is often crucial for proper interpretation of flow findings. HLA-DR-/CD34- phenotype in AML with normal karyo-type by conventional cytogeneties is associated with FLT3-ITD 通用删除6(英):<u>\[36\]</u>. Albano et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u> reported the association of CD34 expression with the APLv and higher proportion of CD2+ and HLA-DR+ cases. In the same study， CD34+ APL patients had a significantly higher percentage of peripheral blood leukemic promyelocytes at presentation， were more frequently female， and had a higher proportion of ber3expression， but there were no differences between the two groups in terms of complete remission， overall survival， and disease-free survival 通用删除6(英):<u>\[37\]</u>.**

【4】Expression of HLA-DR， CD11b， CD11c， CD14， and CD64 helps to differentiate phenotypically acute mono-blastic leukemia (HLA-DR+， CD11b+， CD11c+， CD14+(variable)/， CD64+ (bright) from the APLv (HLA-DR-， CD11b-， CD11c-， CD14-， CD64+dim). Monoblasts are often positive for CD11b， have bright CD11c， may show positive， variable (smeary) expression of CD14， and are often positive for CD56， whereas CD56 is only rarely expressed in APL. All APL cases express CD117， whereas CD117 is positive only in the subset of acute monoblastic leukemias. The majority of acute monoblastic leukemias show moderate to bright HLA-DR； only rare cases are HLA-DR-. Acute monoblastic leukemia expresses CD64(bright)， and APL usually shows only dim expression of CD64. In most cases of acute monoblastic leukemia， the expression of CD45 is brighter than in APL. The SSC of monoblastic leukemia is only slightly increased (in con-trast to classic APL). Only occasional cases of acute mono-blastic leukemia show high SSC.

**Analysis of CD10， CD11b， CD11c， CD16， CD117， and HLA-DR helps to distinguish benign process from APL. Neutrophilic maturation from blasts through promyelo-cytes， myelocytes， metamyelocytes， bands， and neutrophils is characterized by loss of CD34 and HLA-DR expres-sion at promyelocytic stage and loss of CD117 expres-sion at myelocytic stage， and acquisition of CDllb and CD11c expression at myelocytic stage， and CD10 and CD16|删除0换行|expression by neutrophils. CD64 is expressed by promy-elocytes through metamyelocytes. In contrast to APL， granulocytes are positive for CD10， CD11b， CD11c， and CD16， and are negative for CD117. Granulocytes/matur-ing myeloid precursors with dyspoiesis (e.g.， MDS) and/or leftward shift (e.g.， CML) may display an aberrant down-regulation of CD10， CD11b， and CD16， but in contrast to neoplastic promyelocytes lack CD117 expression and are(at least partially) CD11c+.

【6】**_AML WITH RUNX1-RUNX1T1_**

【7】**MORPHOLOGY**

【8】AML with t(8；21)(q22；q22) (RUNXI-RUNXITI) most often display the morphology of AML with maturation \[former French-American-British (FAB) M2 category\]通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，38，39\]</u>. Blasts are large with abundant basophilic cytoplasm and variable， and often increased numbers of azurophilic granules and frequent Auer rods. Large granules (pseudo Chediak-Higashi granules) are often present. Maturing elements often show dysgranulopoiesis (including pseudo Pelger-Huet nuclei). AML with t(8；21) is associated with a higher incidence of myeloid sarcoma (extramedullary myeloid tumor) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40\]</u>.
