【35】页码间删除-1:<u>**INTRODUCTION**</u>

【36】Essential thrombocythemia (ET) is a relatively indolent and often _C_ asymptomatic clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm(MPN) that involves predominantly megakaryocytic lineage characterized primarily by a sustained elevation in platelets(<450×10L)， megakaryocytosis， and minimal to absent bone marrow (BM) fibrosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-10\]</u>. The acquired mutations in the JAK2 and MPL genes occur in 50% and 4% of cases， respectively.

【37】Since other MPNs， especially chronic myeloid leukemia(CML)， polycythemia vera (PV)， and early primary myelo-fibrosis (PMF)， often present with thrombocytosis， mor-phologic evaluation of the BM plays an important role in the diagnosis of ET. Increase and loose clustering of large megakaryocytes with mature cytoplasm and multilobulated staghorn-like nuclei in a normocellular or only slightly hyper-cellular BM represent the major hallmarks of ET 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5，11，12\]</u>. Early (prefibrotic) phase of PMF differs by marrow hyper-cellularity and cohesive clusters of megakaryocytes with often bulbous， bizarre nuclei with maturation defect 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>. Diagnosis has to be based on clinical and laboratory features， taking into consideration the dynamics of this disorder.

【38】The currently proposed World Health Organization (WHO)/European clinical， molecular， and pathological (ECMP) cri-teria for the diagnosis of ET include (C1) sustained platelet count above the upper limit of normal (<450×10/L)； (C2) presence of large or giant platelets in blood smear； (C3) nor-mal values of hemoglobin， hematocrit， erythrocytes， and white blood cell differential count； (C4) presence of JAK2mutation or MPL mutation； (C5) absence of Ph chromo-some or any other cytogenetic fusion gene abnormality；(PI) increase of dispersed or loosely clustered， predominantly enlarged megakaryocytes with mature cytoplasm and hyper-lobulated nuclei； and 通用删除11(英):<u>(P2)</u> no proliferation or immaturity of erythropoiesis and granulopoiesis and no or borderline increase of reticulin (myelofibrosis grade 0). According to the proposed WHO/ECMP criteria， Cl + Pl and P2 estab-lish the diagnosis of true ET 通用删除6(英):<u>\[14，15\]</u>.Table 29.1 presents the current WHO criteria for ET. Generally， ET can be diag-nosed in patients with sustained platelet ≥450 ×10/L with

【39】**JAK2 V617F (or other clonal marker) who do not meet the criteria for the diagnosis of PV， CML， PMF， myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)， and other MPNs， and whose biopsy shows atypical large and mature megakaryocytes not accompanied by BM fibrosis (in the absence of clonal marker， there should be no evidence for reactive thrombocytosis). 【40】页码间删除-1:<u>**MORPHOLOGY**</u>

【41】The blood shows an increase in the number of platelets， which may display atypia and anisocytosis. Leukocytosis， if present， is mild. The BM aspirate is normocellular to slightly hyper-cellular with increased megakaryocytes， which often cluster within spicules. Megakaryocytes are large and occasionally giant with mature cytoplasm and irregular (hyperlobulated) nuclei (staghorn-like). The biopsy shows normocellular to hypercellular marrow  without sig-nificant leftward shift of neutrophil granulopoiesis or eryth-ropoiesis. There is megakaryocytic hyperplasia with atypia， but without overt maturation defects (typical for PMF). Megakaryocytes may be seen abnormally close to the bony trabeculae； usually they are located in the deep interstitium. In rare cases， reticulin fibers may be focally increased (<25%of the marrow area)， but typical ET usually lacks reticulin or collagen fibrosis. The granulocytic series does not show the leftward shift.

【35】页码间删除-1:<u>**INTRODUCTION**</u>

【36】Essential thrombocythemia (ET) is a relatively indolent and often _C_ asymptomatic clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm(MPN) that involves predominantly megakaryocytic lineage characterized primarily by a sustained elevation in platelets(<450×10L)， megakaryocytosis， and minimal to absent bone marrow (BM) fibrosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-10\]</u>. The acquired mutations in the JAK2 and MPL genes occur in 50% and 4% of cases， respectively.

【37】Since other MPNs， especially chronic myeloid leukemia(CML)， polycythemia vera (PV)， and early primary myelo-fibrosis (PMF)， often present with thrombocytosis， mor-phologic evaluation of the BM plays an important role in the diagnosis of ET. Increase and loose clustering of large megakaryocytes with mature cytoplasm and multilobulated staghorn-like nuclei in a normocellular or only slightly hyper-cellular BM represent the major hallmarks of ET 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5，11，12\]</u>. Early (prefibrotic) phase of PMF differs by marrow hyper-cellularity and cohesive clusters of megakaryocytes with often bulbous， bizarre nuclei with maturation defect 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>. Diagnosis has to be based on clinical and laboratory features， taking into consideration the dynamics of this disorder.

【38】The currently proposed World Health Organization (WHO)/European clinical， molecular， and pathological (ECMP) cri-teria for the diagnosis of ET include (C1) sustained platelet count above the upper limit of normal (<450×10/L)； (C2) presence of large or giant platelets in blood smear； (C3) nor-mal values of hemoglobin， hematocrit， erythrocytes， and white blood cell differential count； (C4) presence of JAK2mutation or MPL mutation； (C5) absence of Ph chromo-some or any other cytogenetic fusion gene abnormality；(PI) increase of dispersed or loosely clustered， predominantly enlarged megakaryocytes with mature cytoplasm and hyper-lobulated nuclei； and 通用删除11(英):<u>(P2)</u> no proliferation or immaturity of erythropoiesis and granulopoiesis and no or borderline increase of reticulin (myelofibrosis grade 0). According to the proposed WHO/ECMP criteria， Cl + Pl and P2 estab-lish the diagnosis of true ET 通用删除6(英):<u>\[14，15\]</u>.Table 29.1 presents the current WHO criteria for ET. Generally， ET can be diag-nosed in patients with sustained platelet ≥450 ×10/L with

【39】**JAK2 V617F (or other clonal marker) who do not meet the criteria for the diagnosis of PV， CML， PMF， myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)， and other MPNs， and whose biopsy shows atypical large and mature megakaryocytes not accompanied by BM fibrosis (in the absence of clonal marker， there should be no evidence for reactive thrombocytosis). This means that to diagnose ET one has to exclude BCR-ABLI fusion， a sig-nificant BM reticulin or collagen fibrosis and dyserythropoi-esis and dysgranulopoiesis， and to prove the failure of iron replacement therapy to increase the hemoglobin level to the PV range in the presence of decreased serum ferritin.**

【40】页码间删除-1:<u>**MORPHOLOGY**</u>

【41】The blood shows an increase in the number of platelets， which may display atypia and anisocytosis. Leukocytosis， if present， is mild. The BM aspirate is normocellular to slightly hyper-cellular with increased megakaryocytes， which often cluster within spicules. Megakaryocytes are large and occasionally giant with mature cytoplasm and irregular (hyperlobulated) nuclei (staghorn-like). The biopsy shows normocellular to hypercellular marrow  without sig-nificant leftward shift of neutrophil granulopoiesis or eryth-ropoiesis. There is megakaryocytic hyperplasia with atypia， but without overt maturation defects (typical for PMF). Megakaryocytes may be seen abnormally close to the bony trabeculae； usually they are located in the deep interstitium. In rare cases， reticulin fibers may be focally increased (<25%of the marrow area)， but typical ET usually lacks reticulin or collagen fibrosis. The granulocytic series does not show the leftward shift.

【54】**DISEASE PROGRESSION**

【55】A transformation of ET to acute myeloid leukemia (AML)， MDS， or myelofibrosis is a relatively rare event and occurs in1%-5% of all patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，18，24-28\]</u>. The diagnostic criteria for post-ETmyelofibrosis (post-ET-MF) are presented in Table 29.2.

Cytogenetic changes that may be associated with the transformation to AML are common and include t(2；3)， del(1；7)(q10；p10)， t(2；17)， del(17p)， trisomy 8， trisomy 21， and chromosome 7 and 13q abnormalities 通用删除6(英):<u>\[29-35\]</u>. 【2】**The commonest nerve roots affected are the L5 nerve from compression of a degenerative L4/L5 disc and the S1 nerve from compression of a degenerative L5/S1 disc .**

【3】**Other causes of nerve root compression include spinal stenosis and the cauda equina syndrome. The spinal column ends at the level of the L1/L2 vertebrae and the bundle of nerve fibres that continues in the spinal canal is named the cauda equina. Cauda equina syndrome relates to the compression of the cauda equina most commonly by the central prolapse of an intervertebral disc. Cauda equina syndrome is a true emergency and must be considered in any patient presenting with back pain. Typically the patient complains of bilateral leg pain， with limited straight leg raising and there may be bilat-eral leg weakness and absent reflexes. The development of bladder or bowel dysfunction and paraesthesiae in the saddle distribution indicates the involvement of the sacral nerve roots S2-4 and is a surgical emergency. Nerve root compression of S2-4 gives rise to laxity of anal tone and loss of perianal sensation .**

【59】**Stroke/head injury**

【60】**In the elderly， ischaemic stroke is common and acute confusion often accompanies this if the speech area from an anterior circula-tion infarction is affected. A history of rapid onset， along with risk factors such as hypertension， hypercholesterolaemia， or diabetes points to stroke， and there is usually a focal neurological deficit if you look carefully. In all age groups subarachnoid or intra-cerebral bleeding can occur spontaneously and， although more typically presenting as severe headache or loss of consciousness， may present as acute confusion.**

【61】Concussive head injuries may cause transient disorientation， whileintracranial injuries (cerebral contusion，cerebral haematoma， extradural or subdural haematoma) may cause more prolonged confusion that progresses to coma. Trauma may be obvious， but delays in diagnosis are frequent when the patient is intoxicated(acute extradural haematoma) or elderly (chronic subdural hae-matoma) because external injury is not always obvious. Subdural haematomas can develop after as apparently innocuous a mecha-nism as a stumble when there is cerebral atrophy and dural veins are vulnerable to tearing.

**Lack of vital elements for cerebral function|删除0换行|1 Hypoxia. Patients with confusion due to hypoxia are typically agitated， anxious and breathless. Common causes include pneumo-nia， heart failure， pulmonary embolus and bronchoconstriction.**

【64】2 Shock. Inadequate circulation leading to inadequate cerebral perfusion. Patients who are shocked are likely to be pale， clammy and have cool peripheries. Low blood pressure is a late sign. Depending upon the cause， the patient may be tachycardic.

**Systemic factors that impair cerebral function|删除0换行|1 Metabolic causes. Hyponatraemia or hypercalcaemia may present with acute confusion， particularly if the electrolyte disturbance develops rapidly： clinical diagnosis may be difficult with little history. A careful drug history may point to a metabolic cause. High blood urea due to renal failure can cause confusion and uraemia is usually associated with muscular twitching and signs of dehydration.

**Patients with hepatic encephalopathy are jaundiced and may have a flapping tremor. Since alcohol is a common cause， patients|删除0换行|may also show features ofother alcohol-related disorders， such as alcohol withdrawal or delirium tremens.

【67】2 Drugs. Routine or excessive use of a wide variety of prescribed drugs can cause patients to become confused， especially the elderly.Drugoverdose or intoxicationtypicallycauses a depressed conscious level， but some drug effects may present as acute con-fusion. These might include recreational use of amphetamines， cocaine or LSD， or overdose of tricyclic antidepressants. Patients would be younger than the case presented and would typically be agitated with a rapid pulse and dilated pupils.

【68】Drugs can also cause confusion if they are withdrawn from a dependent patient. The most common occurrence of this sort would be alcohol withdrawal. This is typically associated with coarse tremor， tachycardia， sweating， agitation and occasionally fitting.

【69】**3 Hypothermia. Young， healthy patients are unlikely to develop hypothermia unless they suffer prolonged exposure to very cold conditions or are immersed in water. In these cases hypothermia is easy to recognise. 【75】Psychiatric illness， almost by definition， does not cause acute confusion states. However， it is important to distinguish between acute confusion due to an organic cause and acute psychosis due to a psychiatric cause. The presence of auditory hallucinations and evidence of thought disorder suggest psychiatric illness.

【58】A comprehensive physical examination is necessary in all cases of acute delirium. If sepsis is the cause， there may be abdominal tenderness or urinary retention in urinary tract infection， or crackles， tachypnoea and hypoxia in respiratory infection. Signs of meningism， such as neck stiffness， photophobia， papilloedema， or Kernig’s sign， can be subtle especially in the elderly.

【59】**Stroke/head injury**

【60】**In the elderly， ischaemic stroke is common and acute confusion often accompanies this if the speech area from an anterior circula-tion infarction is affected. A history of rapid onset， along with risk factors such as hypertension， hypercholesterolaemia， or diabetes points to stroke， and there is usually a focal neurological deficit if you look carefully. In all age groups subarachnoid or intra-cerebral bleeding can occur spontaneously and， although more typically presenting as severe headache or loss of consciousness， may present as acute confusion.**

【61】Concussive head injuries may cause transient disorientation， whileintracranial injuries (cerebral contusion，cerebral haematoma， extradural or subdural haematoma) may cause more prolonged confusion that progresses to coma. Trauma may be obvious， but delays in diagnosis are frequent when the patient is intoxicated(acute extradural haematoma) or elderly (chronic subdural hae-matoma) because external injury is not always obvious. Subdural haematomas can develop after as apparently innocuous a mecha-nism as a stumble when there is cerebral atrophy and dural veins are vulnerable to tearing.

【62】**Other causes of acute delirium not suggested by the history**

**Lack of vital elements for cerebral function|删除0换行|1 Hypoxia. Patients with confusion due to hypoxia are typically agitated， anxious and breathless. Common causes include pneumo-nia， heart failure， pulmonary embolus and bronchoconstriction.**

【64】2 Shock. Inadequate circulation leading to inadequate cerebral perfusion. Patients who are shocked are likely to be pale， clammy and have cool peripheries. Low blood pressure is a late sign. Depending upon the cause， the patient may be tachycardic.

**Systemic factors that impair cerebral function|删除0换行|1 Metabolic causes. Hyponatraemia or hypercalcaemia may present with acute confusion， particularly if the electrolyte disturbance develops rapidly： clinical diagnosis may be difficult with little history. A careful drug history may point to a metabolic cause. High blood urea due to renal failure can cause confusion and uraemia is usually associated with muscular twitching and signs of dehydration.

**Patients with hepatic encephalopathy are jaundiced and may have a flapping tremor. Since alcohol is a common cause， patients|删除0换行|may also show features ofother alcohol-related disorders， such as alcohol withdrawal or delirium tremens.

【67】2 Drugs. Routine or excessive use of a wide variety of prescribed drugs can cause patients to become confused， especially the elderly.Drugoverdose or intoxicationtypicallycauses a depressed conscious level， but some drug effects may present as acute con-fusion. These might include recreational use of amphetamines， cocaine or LSD， or overdose of tricyclic antidepressants. Patients would be younger than the case presented and would typically be agitated with a rapid pulse and dilated pupils.

【68】Drugs can also cause confusion if they are withdrawn from a dependent patient. The most common occurrence of this sort would be alcohol withdrawal. This is typically associated with coarse tremor， tachycardia， sweating， agitation and occasionally fitting.

【69】**3 Hypothermia. Young， healthy patients are unlikely to develop hypothermia unless they suffer prolonged exposure to very cold conditions or are immersed in water. In these cases hypothermia is easy to recognise. The diagnosis is more difficult in the elderly， those dependent on alcohol， or those with chronic diseases， who may suffer hypothermia in association with other chronic illness， falls， or poor social conditions.**

【70】4 Pain. The superimposition of pain onto another medical problem (such as dementia) can lead to a sudden worsening of confusion. A careful history and comprehensive examination should establish if there is an acute injury or an occult painful problem such asperitonitis. Remember to check the hips of elderly patients who have fallen： impacted fractures are common.

【71】_Local factors that impair cerebral function_

【72】1 Tumours. Primary brain tumours and secondary metastases may cause acute confusion through direct cerebral effects or raised intracranial pressure. The diagnosis is suggested by an associated headache that is worse on coughing and straining， and associated vomiting. Frontal tumours may present as unusual behaviour without other symptoms or signs. The onset is usually insidious， however.

【73】2 Epilepsy. Following a seizure most patients will undergo a period of confusion as they regain consciousness. This usually resolves within an hour. If it does not resolve then alternative causes should be sought.

【74】**Psychiatric causes**

【75】Psychiatric illness， almost by definition， does not cause acute confusion states. However， it is important to distinguish between acute confusion due to an organic cause and acute psychosis due to a psychiatric cause. The presence of auditory hallucinations and evidence of thought disorder suggest psychiatric illness.

【76】Returning to our case， the diagnosis is not clear： many possible differentials could apply. Although it may be difficult to establish， a history of possible drug overdose should be ruled out through a thorough review of medication. A history of transient neurological symptoms or fluctuating confusion recently， points more toward a

【1】**Fibroepithelial tumor is that form of basal-cell carcinoma in which extensive stroma is coupled with an anastomosing pattern of cords and columns of basaloid and squamous cells. In some specimens， the stroma actually predominates over the epithelial component. Squamous and basa-loid elements are invariable， and the squamous constituent of fibroepithe-lial tumor is similar to the squamous-cell proliferation seen in tumor of follicular infundibulum. Although fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinomas may attain large size， even becoming nodular， hardly ever are they destruc-tive like nodular and morpheiform types of basal-cell carcinoma.**

【2】**In sum， tumor of follicular infundibulum is a benign neoplasm that， ironically， differentiates mostly toward the isthmus， whereas fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus is fundamentally a basal-cell carcinoma that differentiates toward several follicular structures， most notably germs. Rarely， tumor of follicular infundibulum may produce a follicular germ that almost always is accompanied by a follicular papilla. In contrast， fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus routinely demonstrates follicular germs that practically never are associated with follicular papillae. As a rule， follicular germs in benign neoplasms almost always are wedded to follicular papillae， whereas follicu-lar germs in carcinomas， such as infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma and fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinoma， are devoid of corresponding papil-lae. The follicular “germs” in fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus actually are incipient basal-cell carcinomas. Not uncommonly and not surprisingly， fi-broepithelial tumor of Pinkus is found in continuity with nodular basal-cell carcinoma， a malignant neoplasm of follicular germinative cells.**

【26】RICHOFOLLICULOMA， a follicular hamartoma， and pilar sheath acanthoma， a benign follicular neoplasm， have many histo-pathologic features in common. Both display a central， widely dilated os-tium which connects to a crater formed by one or more contiguous infun-dibula filled with innumerable cornified cells， both may be oriented either vertically or horizontally to the surface of the skin， both may extend deep into the reticular dermis and into the subcutaneous fat， and both may be surrounded by connective tissue like that of perifollicular sheath. The most striking similarity between them， however， is a silhouette composed of an upper infundibular cystic component from which radiate， as in caput me-dusae， follicular epithelial cells.

【27】To diagnose correctly any follicular proliferation it is helpful to under-stand the embryologic， histologic， and anatomic aspects of a normal hair follicle. Differentiation of follicular proliferations is predicated upon attri-butes of a normal follicle， which can be divided into an upper and a lower segment based upon histologic and biologic considerations. The upper seg-ment is immobile and consists of infundibulum and isthmus. The lower segment participates in follicular cycles and consists of an entire follicle below the isthmus， which can be separated into a stem and a lowermost bulb. The boundaries of the parts of a follicle are as follows：

【28】Infundibulum： from the ostium of the follicle above to the entry of the sebaceous duct below.

【29】Isthmus： from the entry of the sebaceous duct above to the site of attachment of a muscle of hair erection at the bulge below.

【30】**Stemn： from the site of attachment of the muscle of hair erection to Adamson’s fringe (the boundary between non-cornifying and cornify-ing cells in the lower segment of a follicle).**

【31】**Bulb： from Adamson’s fringe to the base of a follicle，**

【32】The infundibulum is lined by stratified squamous cpithelium virtually identical to that of the epidermis； both epithelia exhibit cornified， granular， spinous， and basal layers. Below the infundibulum is the isthmus composed of cornified cells arranged compactly adjacent to squamous epithelium con-stituted of pale cells and devoid of an intervening granular layer. The stem COM consists of an eosinophilic outer sheath that envelops compactly arranged blue-gray corneocytes of the inner sheath. The follicular bulb enclosespar-tially a connective tissue papilla and consists at its base of matrical cells that differentiate along six separate pathways： the three layers of the inner sheath (Henle’s， Huxley's， and the cuticle of the inner sheath)， and the three layers of the hair itself (the cuticle of the hair， the cortex， and the medulla).

【33】**An outer sheath encompasses the entire follicle below the infundibulum and traverses a course from the top of the isthmus to the base of the bulb. Abundant glycogen in the lower part of the outer sheath causes the epithe-lium to appear pale or clear.**

【34】**Armed with knowledge of the histologic aspects of a normal hair folli-cle， a dermatopathologist can identify differentiation of trichofolliculomas as being toward both upper and lower segments of a follicle， and that of pilar sheath acanthomas as being toward the upper segment only. Sigins of sebaceous differentiation are detectable within bulbous aggregations of is-thmic epithelium in pilar sheath acanthoma. They are manifested as small， discrete sebaceous ductal structures and， episodically， as individual sebo-cytes. Sebaceous elements are not present within the substance of follicular structures of trichofolliculoma and rarely are they found anywhere within a specimen of that distinctive hamartoma.**

【35】Trichofolliculoma fulfills the definition of a hamartoma because the elements that constitute it resemble those of normal skin， but they are ab-normal and are arranged in aberrant fashion. Pilar sheath acanthoma is a benign neoplasm because most of its elements do not resemble structures recognizable in normal skin. Despite the close similarity of many vellus follicles that comprise trichofolliculoma to those in normal skin， nearly every vellus follicle in that hamartoma is abnormal. Some have peculiar shapes， others have bizarre follicular bulbs and papillae， still others have a glut of trichohyalin granules， and practically none have an associated seba-ceous duct or a muscle of hair erection. In brief， what at scanning magnifi-cation resembles radial arrangement of normal vellus follicles is actually a strange array of completely abnormal ones.

【36】**Each follicle of trichofolliculoma produces a vellus hair， each of which is propelled into the infundibular crater. When vellus hairs emerge from the patulous ostium， they are seen clinically as tufts of silken threads that issue from a button-like papule. It is difficult for an observer to restrain the urge to pluck them out， so much do they resemble a cosmetic artefact. No hairs are produced in pilar sheath acanthoma， which is a nondescript papule situated usually on a lip.**

【37】**Virtually all textbooks of dermatopathology make a distinction between trichofolliculoma and a hair follicle nevus. What is described and pictured as a hair follicle nevus is merely the periphery of a trichofolliculoma cut on end.**

【103】**ARGE-CELL acanthoma and pigmented solar ker-atosis are very different proliferations of keratinocytes that have several his-topathologic features in common. In addition to presence of large keratino-cytes， both neoplasms may show alterations in the cornified layer， focal decrease in the granular zone， lymphocytic infiltrates， melanophages， and marked solar elastosis.**

【104】**Differentiation of large-cell acanthoma from pigmented solar keratosis turns on their respective architecturalpatterns and their own distinctive cytologic features. Unlike pigmented solar keratosis， large-cell acanthoma， when viewed at scanning magnification， lacks regular alternation of ortho-and parakeratosis because its acrosyringia and acrotrichia have been swal-owed up by the pathologic process， lacks crowded nuclei because of abun-dant cytoplasm of keratinocytes， and lacks suprabasal clefts. Although both large cell acanthoma and pigmented solar keratosis possess large keratinocytes， the nuclei of those cells in large-cell acanthoma are monomorphous， whereas those in pigmented solar keratoses are pleomorphic. Keratinocytes in the lower portion of the epidermis of pigmented solar keratosis display variable degrees of nuclear atypia as well as mitotic figures， some of which may be abnormal. Multinucleate keratinocytes are seen often in pigmented solar keratoses， but not at all in large-cell acanthomas.**

【105】**Although large-cell acanthomas exhibit slight， if any， increase in the number of melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction， they are associ-ated with prominent pigmentation of keratinocytes by melanin. As a rule， melanin in pigmented solar keratosis is much less noticeable than that in large-cel acanthoma.**

【106】**Clinically， large-cell acanthomas are indistinguishable from solar len-tigines because they are solar lentigines whose nuclei are larger than usual for that condition. They are brown macules， papules， or plaques that tend to be free of scale or possess little of it. Lesions may become pink to violaceous when they evolve toward lichen planus-like keratoses， which simply are solar lentigines to which a band of lymphocytes has been attracted. Solar keratoses are keratotic papules situated on reddish bases. Both large-cell acanthoma and solar keratosis are stationed on skin that has been damaged by sunlight.**

**Superfluous synonymy abounds in dermatology and pathology， and large-cell acanthoma is a superb example of it. In our estimation， large-cell acanthoma is a solar lentigo， a solar lentigo is an embryonic seborrheic keratosis， and a lichen planus-like keratosis is a solar lentigo/large-cell acan-thoma/seborrheic keratosis in the process of regressing under an assault by|删除0换行|lymphocytes. Analogously， pigmented solar keratosis is an embryonic squa-mous-cell carcinoma. It makes as little sense to interrupt the continuum ofspecific pathologic pprroocceessss by assigning it different names as it would be to give to a single human being a different name at birth， infancy， child-hood， adolescence， and adulthood.**

【108】**Several types of solar keratoses have distinct histopathologic features. The usual type of solar keratosis is without pronounced pigmentation by melanin， but is constituted of atypical keratinocytes that form buds in the ower part of an epidermis that is topped by alternating columns of ortho-and parakeratosis. Atypical keratinocytes may extend throughout the entire thickness of a thickened epidermis of a solar keratosis， but that latter neo-plasm can still be distinguished from Bowen’s disease by different silhou-ettes. Uncommonly， the cornified layer of some solar keratoses may show no parakeratosis，i.e.， it is compactly orthokeratotic. Other solar keratoses may have pronounced verrucous features， i.e.， they are digitated. Occasionally， buds of atypical keratinocytes are marked by suprabasal clefts above which are assembled acantholytic dyskeratotic cells that produce a“pseudo-glan-dular” pattern in a solar keratosis.**

【109】**In sum， solar keratosis， like Bowen’s disease， is an evolving squamous-cell carcinoma. At an early stage in their course， most cutaneous squarnous-cell carcinomas are called solar keratoses. Most solar keratoses are not pig-mented by melanin， but those that are must be differentiated， at times， from that variant of solar lentigo known as large-cell acanthoma.**

【110】**What has been written about the epithelial aspects of solar keratoses applies equally to their analogues， arsenical keratoses and radiation kera-tOses，**

**YRINGOMATOUs carcinoma is such a well-differen-|删除0换行|tiated malignant neoplasm that it shares many features with its benign counterpart， syringoma. These two neoplasms consist of aggregations of epithelial cells that are thought to represent eccrine differentiation in the form of clusters of pale epithelial cells that assume the shapes of “commas’and"tadpoles，”columns and cords， and tubular structures. Cornification in cystic structures， a consequence of capability of ductal keratinocytes to ma-ture fully， is seen in both neoplasms，particularly in the upper part of them. Lumina of neoplastic tubules often contain pale， amphophilic-staining， amorphous material. Epithelial cells that line those tubules are the types seen normally in eccrine glands， namely， small dark-staining cells that con-tain mucosubstances and larger pale cells that house glycogen. Nuclei of neoplastic cells in both syringoma and syringomatous carcinoma exhibit no atypia. An infiltrate of lymphocytes may be present in both the benign and malignant neoplasm， although it tends to be scant in syringoma.**

In ade-quate biopsy specimens， however， the criteria enumerated at the outset of this chapter enable a correct diagnosis to be made in nearly all instances.**

【27】To diagnose correctly any follicular proliferation it is helpful to under-stand the embryologic， histologic， and anatomic aspects of a normal hair follicle. Differentiation of follicular proliferations is predicated upon attri-butes of a normal follicle， which can be divided into an upper and a lower segment based upon histologic and biologic considerations. The upper seg-ment is immobile and consists of infundibulum and isthmus. The lower segment participates in follicular cycles and consists of an entire follicle below the isthmus， which can be separated into a stem and a lowermost bulb. The boundaries of the parts of a follicle are as follows：

【103】**ARGE-CELL acanthoma and pigmented solar ker-atosis are very different proliferations of keratinocytes that have several his-topathologic features in common. In addition to presence of large keratino-cytes， both neoplasms may show alterations in the cornified layer， focal decrease in the granular zone， lymphocytic infiltrates， melanophages， and marked solar elastosis.**

【104】**Differentiation of large-cell acanthoma from pigmented solar keratosis turns on their respective architecturalpatterns and their own distinctive cytologic features. Unlike pigmented solar keratosis， large-cell acanthoma， when viewed at scanning magnification， lacks regular alternation of ortho-and parakeratosis because its acrosyringia and acrotrichia have been swal-owed up by the pathologic process， lacks crowded nuclei because of abun-dant cytoplasm of keratinocytes， and lacks suprabasal clefts. Although both large cell acanthoma and pigmented solar keratosis possess large keratinocytes， the nuclei of those cells in large-cell acanthoma are monomorphous， whereas those in pigmented solar keratoses are pleomorphic. Keratinocytes in the lower portion of the epidermis of pigmented solar keratosis display variable degrees of nuclear atypia as well as mitotic figures， some of which may be abnormal. Multinucleate keratinocytes are seen often in pigmented solar keratoses， but not at all in large-cell acanthomas.**

【105】**Although large-cell acanthomas exhibit slight， if any， increase in the number of melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction， they are associ-ated with prominent pigmentation of keratinocytes by melanin. As a rule， melanin in pigmented solar keratosis is much less noticeable than that in large-cel acanthoma.**

【106】**Clinically， large-cell acanthomas are indistinguishable from solar len-tigines because they are solar lentigines whose nuclei are larger than usual for that condition. They are brown macules， papules， or plaques that tend to be free of scale or possess little of it. Lesions may become pink to violaceous when they evolve toward lichen planus-like keratoses， which simply are solar lentigines to which a band of lymphocytes has been attracted. Solar keratoses are keratotic papules situated on reddish bases. Both large-cell acanthoma and solar keratosis are stationed on skin that has been damaged by sunlight.**

**Superfluous synonymy abounds in dermatology and pathology， and large-cell acanthoma is a superb example of it. In our estimation， large-cell acanthoma is a solar lentigo， a solar lentigo is an embryonic seborrheic keratosis， and a lichen planus-like keratosis is a solar lentigo/large-cell acan-thoma/seborrheic keratosis in the process of regressing under an assault by|删除0换行|lymphocytes. Analogously， pigmented solar keratosis is an embryonic squa-mous-cell carcinoma. It makes as little sense to interrupt the continuum ofspecific pathologic pprroocceessss by assigning it different names as it would be to give to a single human being a different name at birth， infancy， child-hood， adolescence， and adulthood.**

The usual type of solar keratosis is without pronounced pigmentation by melanin， but is constituted of atypical keratinocytes that form buds in the ower part of an epidermis that is topped by alternating columns of ortho-and parakeratosis. Atypical keratinocytes may extend throughout the entire thickness of a thickened epidermis of a solar keratosis， but that latter neo-plasm can still be distinguished from Bowen’s disease by different silhou-ettes. Uncommonly， the cornified layer of some solar keratoses may show no parakeratosis，i.e.， it is compactly orthokeratotic. Other solar keratoses may have pronounced verrucous features， i.e.， they are digitated. Occasionally， buds of atypical keratinocytes are marked by suprabasal clefts above which are assembled acantholytic dyskeratotic cells that produce a“pseudo-glan-dular” pattern in a solar keratosis.**

Most solar keratoses are not pig-mented by melanin， but those that are must be differentiated， at times， from that variant of solar lentigo known as large-cell acanthoma.**

**YRINGOMATOUs carcinoma is such a well-differen-|删除0换行|tiated malignant neoplasm that it shares many features with its benign counterpart， syringoma. These two neoplasms consist of aggregations of epithelial cells that are thought to represent eccrine differentiation in the form of clusters of pale epithelial cells that assume the shapes of “commas’and"tadpoles，”columns and cords， and tubular structures. 【103】**ARGE-CELL acanthoma and pigmented solar ker-atosis are very different proliferations of keratinocytes that have several his-topathologic features in common. In addition to presence of large keratino-cytes， both neoplasms may show alterations in the cornified layer， focal decrease in the granular zone， lymphocytic infiltrates， melanophages， and marked solar elastosis.**

【104】**Differentiation of large-cell acanthoma from pigmented solar keratosis turns on their respective architecturalpatterns and their own distinctive cytologic features. Unlike pigmented solar keratosis， large-cell acanthoma， when viewed at scanning magnification， lacks regular alternation of ortho-and parakeratosis because its acrosyringia and acrotrichia have been swal-owed up by the pathologic process， lacks crowded nuclei because of abun-dant cytoplasm of keratinocytes， and lacks suprabasal clefts. Although both large cell acanthoma and pigmented solar keratosis possess large keratinocytes， the nuclei of those cells in large-cell acanthoma are monomorphous， whereas those in pigmented solar keratoses are pleomorphic. Keratinocytes in the lower portion of the epidermis of pigmented solar keratosis display variable degrees of nuclear atypia as well as mitotic figures， some of which may be abnormal. Multinucleate keratinocytes are seen often in pigmented solar keratoses， but not at all in large-cell acanthomas.**

【105】**Although large-cell acanthomas exhibit slight， if any， increase in the number of melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction， they are associ-ated with prominent pigmentation of keratinocytes by melanin. As a rule， melanin in pigmented solar keratosis is much less noticeable than that in large-cel acanthoma.**

【106】**Clinically， large-cell acanthomas are indistinguishable from solar len-tigines because they are solar lentigines whose nuclei are larger than usual for that condition. They are brown macules， papules， or plaques that tend to be free of scale or possess little of it. Lesions may become pink to violaceous when they evolve toward lichen planus-like keratoses， which simply are solar lentigines to which a band of lymphocytes has been attracted. Solar keratoses are keratotic papules situated on reddish bases. Both large-cell acanthoma and solar keratosis are stationed on skin that has been damaged by sunlight.**

**Superfluous synonymy abounds in dermatology and pathology， and large-cell acanthoma is a superb example of it. In our estimation， large-cell acanthoma is a solar lentigo， a solar lentigo is an embryonic seborrheic keratosis， and a lichen planus-like keratosis is a solar lentigo/large-cell acan-thoma/seborrheic keratosis in the process of regressing under an assault by|删除0换行|lymphocytes. Analogously， pigmented solar keratosis is an embryonic squa-mous-cell carcinoma. It makes as little sense to interrupt the continuum ofspecific pathologic pprroocceessss by assigning it different names as it would be to give to a single human being a different name at birth， infancy， child-hood， adolescence， and adulthood.**

【108】**Several types of solar keratoses have distinct histopathologic features. The usual type of solar keratosis is without pronounced pigmentation by melanin， but is constituted of atypical keratinocytes that form buds in the ower part of an epidermis that is topped by alternating columns of ortho-and parakeratosis. Both display a central， widely dilated os-tium which connects to a crater formed by one or more contiguous infun-dibula filled with innumerable cornified cells， both may be oriented either vertically or horizontally to the surface of the skin， both may extend deep into the reticular dermis and into the subcutaneous fat， and both may be surrounded by connective tissue like that of perifollicular sheath. The boundaries of the parts of a follicle are as follows：

【28】Infundibulum： from the ostium of the follicle above to the entry of the sebaceous duct below.

【29】Isthmus： from the entry of the sebaceous duct above to the site of attachment of a muscle of hair erection at the bulge below.

【30】**Stemn： from the site of attachment of the muscle of hair erection to Adamson’s fringe (the boundary between non-cornifying and cornify-ing cells in the lower segment of a follicle).**

【31】**Bulb： from Adamson’s fringe to the base of a follicle，**

【1】**Fibroepithelial tumor is that form of basal-cell carcinoma in which extensive stroma is coupled with an anastomosing pattern of cords and columns of basaloid and squamous cells. In some specimens， the stroma actually predominates over the epithelial component. Squamous and basa-loid elements are invariable， and the squamous constituent of fibroepithe-lial tumor is similar to the squamous-cell proliferation seen in tumor of follicular infundibulum. Although fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinomas may attain large size， even becoming nodular， hardly ever are they destruc-tive like nodular and morpheiform types of basal-cell carcinoma.**

【2】**In sum， tumor of follicular infundibulum is a benign neoplasm that， ironically， differentiates mostly toward the isthmus， whereas fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus is fundamentally a basal-cell carcinoma that differentiates toward several follicular structures， most notably germs. Rarely， tumor of follicular infundibulum may produce a follicular germ that almost always is accompanied by a follicular papilla. In contrast， fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus routinely demonstrates follicular germs that practically never are associated with follicular papillae. As a rule， follicular germs in benign neoplasms almost always are wedded to follicular papillae， whereas follicu-lar germs in carcinomas， such as infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma and fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinoma， are devoid of corresponding papil-lae. The follicular “germs” in fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus actually are incipient basal-cell carcinomas. Not uncommonly and not surprisingly， fi-broepithelial tumor of Pinkus is found in continuity with nodular basal-cell carcinoma， a malignant neoplasm of follicular germinative cells.**

【26】RICHOFOLLICULOMA， a follicular hamartoma， and pilar sheath acanthoma， a benign follicular neoplasm， have many histo-pathologic features in common. Both display a central， widely dilated os-tium which connects to a crater formed by one or more contiguous infun-dibula filled with innumerable cornified cells， both may be oriented either vertically or horizontally to the surface of the skin， both may extend deep into the reticular dermis and into the subcutaneous fat， and both may be surrounded by connective tissue like that of perifollicular sheath. The most striking similarity between them， however， is a silhouette composed of an upper infundibular cystic component from which radiate， as in caput me-dusae， follicular epithelial cells.

【27】To diagnose correctly any follicular proliferation it is helpful to under-stand the embryologic， histologic， and anatomic aspects of a normal hair follicle. Differentiation of follicular proliferations is predicated upon attri-butes of a normal follicle， which can be divided into an upper and a lower segment based upon histologic and biologic considerations. The upper seg-ment is immobile and consists of infundibulum and isthmus. The lower segment participates in follicular cycles and consists of an entire follicle below the isthmus， which can be separated into a stem and a lowermost bulb. The boundaries of the parts of a follicle are as follows：

【28】Infundibulum： from the ostium of the follicle above to the entry of the sebaceous duct below.

【29】Isthmus： from the entry of the sebaceous duct above to the site of attachment of a muscle of hair erection at the bulge below.

【30】**Stemn： from the site of attachment of the muscle of hair erection to Adamson’s fringe (the boundary between non-cornifying and cornify-ing cells in the lower segment of a follicle).**

【31】**Bulb： from Adamson’s fringe to the base of a follicle，**

【32】The infundibulum is lined by stratified squamous cpithelium virtually identical to that of the epidermis； both epithelia exhibit cornified， granular， spinous， and basal layers. Below the infundibulum is the isthmus composed of cornified cells arranged compactly adjacent to squamous epithelium con-stituted of pale cells and devoid of an intervening granular layer. The stem COM consists of an eosinophilic outer sheath that envelops compactly arranged blue-gray corneocytes of the inner sheath. The follicular bulb enclosespar-tially a connective tissue papilla and consists at its base of matrical cells that differentiate along six separate pathways： the three layers of the inner sheath (Henle’s， Huxley's， and the cuticle of the inner sheath)， and the three layers of the hair itself (the cuticle of the hair， the cortex， and the medulla).

【33】**An outer sheath encompasses the entire follicle below the infundibulum and traverses a course from the top of the isthmus to the base of the bulb. Abundant glycogen in the lower part of the outer sheath causes the epithe-lium to appear pale or clear.**

【34】**Armed with knowledge of the histologic aspects of a normal hair folli-cle， a dermatopathologist can identify differentiation of trichofolliculomas as being toward both upper and lower segments of a follicle， and that of pilar sheath acanthomas as being toward the upper segment only. Sigins of sebaceous differentiation are detectable within bulbous aggregations of is-thmic epithelium in pilar sheath acanthoma. They are manifested as small， discrete sebaceous ductal structures and， episodically， as individual sebo-cytes. Sebaceous elements are not present within the substance of follicular structures of trichofolliculoma and rarely are they found anywhere within a specimen of that distinctive hamartoma.**

【35】Trichofolliculoma fulfills the definition of a hamartoma because the elements that constitute it resemble those of normal skin， but they are ab-normal and are arranged in aberrant fashion. Pilar sheath acanthoma is a benign neoplasm because most of its elements do not resemble structures recognizable in normal skin. Despite the close similarity of many vellus follicles that comprise trichofolliculoma to those in normal skin， nearly every vellus follicle in that hamartoma is abnormal. Some have peculiar shapes， others have bizarre follicular bulbs and papillae， still others have a glut of trichohyalin granules， and practically none have an associated seba-ceous duct or a muscle of hair erection. In brief， what at scanning magnifi-cation resembles radial arrangement of normal vellus follicles is actually a strange array of completely abnormal ones.

【36】**Each follicle of trichofolliculoma produces a vellus hair， each of which is propelled into the infundibular crater. When vellus hairs emerge from the patulous ostium， they are seen clinically as tufts of silken threads that issue from a button-like papule. It is difficult for an observer to restrain the urge to pluck them out， so much do they resemble a cosmetic artefact. No hairs are produced in pilar sheath acanthoma， which is a nondescript papule situated usually on a lip.**

【37】**Virtually all textbooks of dermatopathology make a distinction between trichofolliculoma and a hair follicle nevus. What is described and pictured as a hair follicle nevus is merely the periphery of a trichofolliculoma cut on end.**

【1】**Fibroepithelial tumor is that form of basal-cell carcinoma in which extensive stroma is coupled with an anastomosing pattern of cords and columns of basaloid and squamous cells. In some specimens， the stroma actually predominates over the epithelial component. Squamous and basa-loid elements are invariable， and the squamous constituent of fibroepithe-lial tumor is similar to the squamous-cell proliferation seen in tumor of follicular infundibulum. Although fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinomas may attain large size， even becoming nodular， hardly ever are they destruc-tive like nodular and morpheiform types of basal-cell carcinoma.**

【2】**In sum， tumor of follicular infundibulum is a benign neoplasm that， ironically， differentiates mostly toward the isthmus， whereas fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus is fundamentally a basal-cell carcinoma that differentiates toward several follicular structures， most notably germs. Rarely， tumor of follicular infundibulum may produce a follicular germ that almost always is accompanied by a follicular papilla. In contrast， fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus routinely demonstrates follicular germs that practically never are associated with follicular papillae. As a rule， follicular germs in benign neoplasms almost always are wedded to follicular papillae， whereas follicu-lar germs in carcinomas， such as infundibulo-cystic basal-cell carcinoma and fibroepithelial basal-cell carcinoma， are devoid of corresponding papil-lae. The follicular “germs” in fibroepithelial tumor of Pinkus actually are incipient basal-cell carcinomas. Not uncommonly and not surprisingly， fi-broepithelial tumor of Pinkus is found in continuity with nodular basal-cell carcinoma， a malignant neoplasm of follicular germinative cells.**

【26】RICHOFOLLICULOMA， a follicular hamartoma， and pilar sheath acanthoma， a benign follicular neoplasm， have many histo-pathologic features in common. Both display a central， widely dilated os-tium which connects to a crater formed by one or more contiguous infun-dibula filled with innumerable cornified cells， both may be oriented either vertically or horizontally to the surface of the skin， both may extend deep into the reticular dermis and into the subcutaneous fat， and both may be surrounded by connective tissue like that of perifollicular sheath. The most striking similarity between them， however， is a silhouette composed of an upper infundibular cystic component from which radiate， as in caput me-dusae， follicular epithelial cells.

【27】To diagnose correctly any follicular proliferation it is helpful to under-stand the embryologic， histologic， and anatomic aspects of a normal hair follicle. Differentiation of follicular proliferations is predicated upon attri-butes of a normal follicle， which can be divided into an upper and a lower segment based upon histologic and biologic considerations. The upper seg-ment is immobile and consists of infundibulum and isthmus. The lower segment participates in follicular cycles and consists of an entire follicle below the isthmus， which can be separated into a stem and a lowermost bulb. The boundaries of the parts of a follicle are as follows：

【28】Infundibulum： from the ostium of the follicle above to the entry of the sebaceous duct below.

【29】Isthmus： from the entry of the sebaceous duct above to the site of attachment of a muscle of hair erection at the bulge below.

【30】**Stemn： from the site of attachment of the muscle of hair erection to Adamson’s fringe (the boundary between non-cornifying and cornify-ing cells in the lower segment of a follicle).**

【31】**Bulb： from Adamson’s fringe to the base of a follicle，**

【32】The infundibulum is lined by stratified squamous cpithelium virtually identical to that of the epidermis； both epithelia exhibit cornified， granular， spinous， and basal layers. Below the infundibulum is the isthmus composed of cornified cells arranged compactly adjacent to squamous epithelium con-stituted of pale cells and devoid of an intervening granular layer. The stem COM consists of an eosinophilic outer sheath that envelops compactly arranged blue-gray corneocytes of the inner sheath. The follicular bulb enclosespar-tially a connective tissue papilla and consists at its base of matrical cells that differentiate along six separate pathways： the three layers of the inner sheath (Henle’s， Huxley's， and the cuticle of the inner sheath)， and the three layers of the hair itself (the cuticle of the hair， the cortex， and the medulla).

【33】**An outer sheath encompasses the entire follicle below the infundibulum and traverses a course from the top of the isthmus to the base of the bulb. Abundant glycogen in the lower part of the outer sheath causes the epithe-lium to appear pale or clear.**

【34】**Armed with knowledge of the histologic aspects of a normal hair folli-cle， a dermatopathologist can identify differentiation of trichofolliculomas as being toward both upper and lower segments of a follicle， and that of pilar sheath acanthomas as being toward the upper segment only. Sigins of sebaceous differentiation are detectable within bulbous aggregations of is-thmic epithelium in pilar sheath acanthoma. They are manifested as small， discrete sebaceous ductal structures and， episodically， as individual sebo-cytes. Sebaceous elements are not present within the substance of follicular structures of trichofolliculoma and rarely are they found anywhere within a specimen of that distinctive hamartoma.**

【35】Trichofolliculoma fulfills the definition of a hamartoma because the elements that constitute it resemble those of normal skin， but they are ab-normal and are arranged in aberrant fashion. Pilar sheath acanthoma is a benign neoplasm because most of its elements do not resemble structures recognizable in normal skin. Despite the close similarity of many vellus follicles that comprise trichofolliculoma to those in normal skin， nearly every vellus follicle in that hamartoma is abnormal. Some have peculiar shapes， others have bizarre follicular bulbs and papillae， still others have a glut of trichohyalin granules， and practically none have an associated seba-ceous duct or a muscle of hair erection. In brief， what at scanning magnifi-cation resembles radial arrangement of normal vellus follicles is actually a strange array of completely abnormal ones.

【36】**Each follicle of trichofolliculoma produces a vellus hair， each of which is propelled into the infundibular crater. When vellus hairs emerge from the patulous ostium， they are seen clinically as tufts of silken threads that issue from a button-like papule. It is difficult for an observer to restrain the urge to pluck them out， so much do they resemble a cosmetic artefact. No hairs are produced in pilar sheath acanthoma， which is a nondescript papule situated usually on a lip.**

【37】**Virtually all textbooks of dermatopathology make a distinction between trichofolliculoma and a hair follicle nevus. What is described and pictured as a hair follicle nevus is merely the periphery of a trichofolliculoma cut on end.**

【103】**ARGE-CELL acanthoma and pigmented solar ker-atosis are very different proliferations of keratinocytes that have several his-topathologic features in common. In addition to presence of large keratino-cytes， both neoplasms may show alterations in the cornified layer， focal decrease in the granular zone， lymphocytic infiltrates， melanophages， and marked solar elastosis.**

【104】**Differentiation of large-cell acanthoma from pigmented solar keratosis turns on their respective architecturalpatterns and their own distinctive cytologic features. Unlike pigmented solar keratosis， large-cell acanthoma， when viewed at scanning magnification， lacks regular alternation of ortho-and parakeratosis because its acrosyringia and acrotrichia have been swal-owed up by the pathologic process， lacks crowded nuclei because of abun-dant cytoplasm of keratinocytes， and lacks suprabasal clefts. Although both large cell acanthoma and pigmented solar keratosis possess large keratinocytes， the nuclei of those cells in large-cell acanthoma are monomorphous， whereas those in pigmented solar keratoses are pleomorphic. Keratinocytes in the lower portion of the epidermis of pigmented solar keratosis display variable degrees of nuclear atypia as well as mitotic figures， some of which may be abnormal. Multinucleate keratinocytes are seen often in pigmented solar keratoses， but not at all in large-cell acanthomas.**

【105】**Although large-cell acanthomas exhibit slight， if any， increase in the number of melanocytes at the dermo-epidermal junction， they are associ-ated with prominent pigmentation of keratinocytes by melanin. As a rule， melanin in pigmented solar keratosis is much less noticeable than that in large-cel acanthoma.**

【106】**Clinically， large-cell acanthomas are indistinguishable from solar len-tigines because they are solar lentigines whose nuclei are larger than usual for that condition. They are brown macules， papules， or plaques that tend to be free of scale or possess little of it. Lesions may become pink to violaceous when they evolve toward lichen planus-like keratoses， which simply are solar lentigines to which a band of lymphocytes has been attracted. Solar keratoses are keratotic papules situated on reddish bases. Both large-cell acanthoma and solar keratosis are stationed on skin that has been damaged by sunlight.**

**Superfluous synonymy abounds in dermatology and pathology， and large-cell acanthoma is a superb example of it. In our estimation， large-cell acanthoma is a solar lentigo， a solar lentigo is an embryonic seborrheic keratosis， and a lichen planus-like keratosis is a solar lentigo/large-cell acan-thoma/seborrheic keratosis in the process of regressing under an assault by|删除0换行|lymphocytes. Analogously， pigmented solar keratosis is an embryonic squa-mous-cell carcinoma. It makes as little sense to interrupt the continuum ofspecific pathologic pprroocceessss by assigning it different names as it would be to give to a single human being a different name at birth， infancy， child-hood， adolescence， and adulthood.**

【108】**Several types of solar keratoses have distinct histopathologic features. The usual type of solar keratosis is without pronounced pigmentation by melanin， but is constituted of atypical keratinocytes that form buds in the ower part of an epidermis that is topped by alternating columns of ortho-and parakeratosis. Atypical keratinocytes may extend throughout the entire thickness of a thickened epidermis of a solar keratosis， but that latter neo-plasm can still be distinguished from Bowen’s disease by different silhou-ettes. Uncommonly， the cornified layer of some solar keratoses may show no parakeratosis，i.e.， it is compactly orthokeratotic. Other solar keratoses may have pronounced verrucous features， i.e.， they are digitated. Occasionally， buds of atypical keratinocytes are marked by suprabasal clefts above which are assembled acantholytic dyskeratotic cells that produce a“pseudo-glan-dular” pattern in a solar keratosis.**

【109】**In sum， solar keratosis， like Bowen’s disease， is an evolving squamous-cell carcinoma. At an early stage in their course， most cutaneous squarnous-cell carcinomas are called solar keratoses. Most solar keratoses are not pig-mented by melanin， but those that are must be differentiated， at times， from that variant of solar lentigo known as large-cell acanthoma.**

【110】**What has been written about the epithelial aspects of solar keratoses applies equally to their analogues， arsenical keratoses and radiation kera-tOses，**

【0】onment. A Qigong doctor should understand why every time he or she connects with a patient, the patient's energetic fields will automatically be energetically ingested by the doctor. The doctor does this consciously in order to analyze the patient's emotional past and present (as well as suppressed emotions). Although the doctor and patient's energies fuse together, the fields of energy around the doctor's internal organs protect the doctor from absorbing negative emotions. These energetic boundaries also extend out into the doctor's Wei Qi field.

【1】Both the patient's and doctor's Wei Qi fields are fused during interaction and treatment. It is therefore imperative that the doctor's energetic boundary system maintain its structure (both internally and externally), yet be permeable while treating the patient. The doctor must not lose sight of his or her purpose. Any criticism aimed at the doctor should not be taken seriously, nor should any inappropriate behavior by the patient. The doctor's Wei Qi field should be at maximum strength. If not, the cords of energetic attachment flowing from both the doctor and the patient allow energetic emotional transference to happen. If the doctor, for example, has a preexisting Liver Heat condition, it can be further compounded by a patient's release of anger and rage. Once this happens, the patient may feel relieved, but the doctor will become quite agitated.

【2】Strengthening the Doctor’s Energetic boundaries

【3】It is important for Qigong doctors to allow the patients' emotions to constantly flow through their own bodies, feeling, understanding, then releasing these emotions. If at any one point in this transition, a doctor (because of personal issues) suddenly stops the flow of emotions and begins to focus or dwell on a particular type of energetic charge, the patients' discharged emotions will invade the doctor's body.

【4】To avoid energetic boundary invasion the doctor should maintain a regular Qigong meditation and exercise program. This program should include the following exercises and meditations.

【5】1\.    Practice Qi dredging and emotional dispersing exercises and meditations to release your own emotional traumas.

【6】2\.    Perform Qi and organ strengthening exercises and meditations to strengthen your internal organ energies and the three fields of Wei Qi. Since the emotions are stored within the body's internal organs, strengthening these organs will facilitate a stronger control over the body's emotional energy.

【7】3\.    Practice Qi regulation and balancing exercises and meditations to balance the body's Yin and Yang, and regulate the internal and external energetic channels, organs, and organ systems. This helps to control the energetic surges released from internal emotional discharges.

【8】4\.    Maintain emphasis on energetic grounding and the divine hookup meditations before treating patients. These meditations are important for establishing an emotional and spiritual boundary and will assist the doctor in avoiding clinical burnout and energetic boundary invasion.

【9】5\.    Maintain emphasis on personal time, including spiritual, social, and recreational times away from the clinic.

【10】STRENGTHENING THE SPIRITUAL. LIGHT of the Doctor’s Righteous Qi

【11】It is important to remember that the body radiates a spiritual light that both enhances the physical tissues and vibrates, as well as communicates with the energetic and spiritual fields of the universe. It is this spiritually cultivated light that protects the Medical Qigong doctor from evil pathogenic influences. In ancient China, the Dao-ists believed that the spiritual cultivation of the Five Virtues (love, order, truth, integrity, and wisdom) and good Karma protected them from "evil." That is one reason why, in certain Medical Qigong clinics in China, doctors still believe that when they treat a patient they are actually increasing the patient's "Righteous Qi" by sharing their

【12】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 30.17. After the Five Lights escort the human soul into the world of matter, the Eternal Soul’s De (virtue) rises upward, to later become the spiritual energy of the Five Agents, rooted within the five Yin organs. Simultaneously, the Eternal Soul’s Ming (destiny) sinks downward to become stored between the Kidneys, rooted within the individual’s Ministerial Fire.</u>

通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 30.18. The Five Main Causes of Spiritual Dryness|删除0换行|spiritually-cultivated inner goodness or virtue (which initiates the cure).</u>

【14】The Concept of Spiritual Virtue

【15】In ancient China, the concept of an individual's virtue (De) and his or her destiny (Ming) were closely connected. Destiny (associated with the Yuan Jing, Qi, and Shen) was believed to originate from Heaven at the time of birth, after which it was stored in the individual's Mingmen (Gate of Destiny) area between the Kidneys . The individual's Ming becomes the spark of life and the dynamic potential underlying his or her thoughts and actions. Although the subtle impulses emanating from the individual's Ming are hidden from the conscious mind, through Shengong meditations a deeper level of understanding can be intuitively discovered and accessed.

【16】It is up to the individual to consistently act in accordance with his or her Ming throughout life. This action is based on the individual's conscious use of his or her intention (Yi). The intent to remain consistent with the "will and intent of heaven" (Zhi Yi Tian) is what gives the individual virtue (De). It is through the development of his or her virtue that the individual establishes a healthy relationship with the Dao, Heaven and the spirit world.

【17】According to the ancient Daoist text, Redoubled Yang's Fifteen Discourses, "an individual's Xing (innate nature, expressed through the original five virtues of the Wu Jing Shen) is manifested within the

【18】Shen (Spirit); an individual's Ming (life destiny, Heavenly mandate, or decree given as one's life purpose) is manifested within the Qi. When an individual's innate nature combines with his or her life destiny, it is like wild birds obtaining the wind. They use it to float, rising lightly to soar within the Heavens. Saving their strength, they effortlessly complete their flight." Therefore, the spiritual cultivation of one's innate nature (Wu Jing Shen) and life destiny (Ming) are at the root of all Medical Qigong cultivations and clinical practice.

【19】CAUSES OF SPIRITUAL DRYNESS

【20】Sometimes clinical burnout can result from "spiritual dryness." This type of spiritual and energetic burnout can result from experiencing a "dry period" of spiritual insight and perception. It can occur during clinical observations and treatments, resulting in frustration for the doctor. Spiritual dryness is commonly due to one or more of the following five conditions .

【67】Through the use of repeated visualization and imagery triggered by experiential affirmation, the Qigong doctors will be able to change their present reality on a subconscious level and achieve the goals that they are striving toward.

【69】**Imaging of Pancreatic Cystic Neoplasms**

【70】Dimitrios Kechagias and Fotios Laspas

【71】**5.1 Introduction**

【72】The incidental detection of cystic pancreatic lesions has increased with the wide-spread and frequent use of cross-sectional imaging. Indeed， one or more“cystic lesions” may be noted in up to 27 % of all patients/subjects undergoing modern， state-of-the-art cross-sectional imaging for whatever reason， thereby complicating the job of the radiologist in suggesting who does and who does not need further investigation. Although cystic pancreatic neoplasms are relatively rare medical entity and the vast majority of these cystic“lesions” are benign 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>， accurate char-acterization of a cystic lesion of the pancreas is crucial in determining the appropri-ate management (imaging follow-up or operative excision). With recent advances in imaging technology， the accuracy of preoperative diagnosis of cystic pancreatic tumors has increased. In many cases， cystic pancreatic neoplasms have characteris-tic， morphologic imaging features which can suggest or confirm a diagnosis； how-ever， the proper evaluation of these lesions can often be difficult due to morphologic overlap at imaging between benign and malignant tumors.

【73】**5.2 Cross-Sectional Imaging (US， CT， MRI)**

【74】Cross-sectional imaging modalities remain the mainstay in the detection and assess-ment of cystic pancreatic tumors. Transabdominal ultrasonography (US) can detect pancreatic cystic lesions； however， given its limited spatial resolution and soft-tissue contrast 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>， US is often not very helpful in the evaluation of cystic neoplasms of the pancreas. Multidetector computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imag-ing (MRI) are the most common radiologic methods used for characterization of

**D. Kechagias ()·F.Laspas ()|删除换行|these lesions. Many authors argue that MRI due to its greater contrast between fluid and soft tissue allows optical depiction of the morphologic features of cystic pancre-atic lesions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2， 3\]</u>； however， recent studies suggest that both multidetector CT and MRI provide high-quality images of cystic pancreatic lesions with comparable diagnostic accuracy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4，5\]</u>. Although the accuracy of these methods ranges from 40to 60 % in providing the correct histologic diagnosis of cystic lesions of the pan-creas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>， Visser et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5\]</u> found that multidetector CT and MRI had an accuracy of76-82 % and 85-91 % respectively in establishing the diagnosis of malignancy in cystic pancreatic masses. The use of advanced MRI techniques， such as diffusion-weighted imaging and ADC measurements， are less helpful currently in distinguish-ing neoplasmatic from non-neoplasmatic pancreatic cysts than originally hoped 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>.

【76】Several important morphologic features of cross-sectional imaging have been shown to be useful in the diagnostic approach to cystic lesions of the pancreas， including the presence of septa (unilocular， oligolocular <6 internal cysts， multi-locular ≥6 internal cysts)， the size of internal cysts (microcystic <2 cm， macrocystic≥2 cm)， the presence of calcification or mural nodules， and communication of the cystic lesion with the main pancreatic duct 通用删除6(英):<u>\[7-9\]</u>.

【77】Serous cystic neoplasm (SCN) is a benign cystic neoplasm of the pancreas that is more frequently found in older women 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. The most common pattern (70 % of the cases) of SCN is a lobulated lesion consisting of numerous cysts (more than 6) varying from a few millimeters to 2 cm in diameter (but typically less than 1 cm) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2，10， 11\]</u> . 【69】**Imaging of Pancreatic Cystic Neoplasms**

【70】Dimitrios Kechagias and Fotios Laspas

【71】**5.1 Introduction**

【72】The incidental detection of cystic pancreatic lesions has increased with the wide-spread and frequent use of cross-sectional imaging. Indeed， one or more“cystic lesions” may be noted in up to 27 % of all patients/subjects undergoing modern， state-of-the-art cross-sectional imaging for whatever reason， thereby complicating the job of the radiologist in suggesting who does and who does not need further investigation. Although cystic pancreatic neoplasms are relatively rare medical entity and the vast majority of these cystic“lesions” are benign 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>， accurate char-acterization of a cystic lesion of the pancreas is crucial in determining the appropri-ate management (imaging follow-up or operative excision). With recent advances in imaging technology， the accuracy of preoperative diagnosis of cystic pancreatic tumors has increased. In many cases， cystic pancreatic neoplasms have characteris-tic， morphologic imaging features which can suggest or confirm a diagnosis； how-ever， the proper evaluation of these lesions can often be difficult due to morphologic overlap at imaging between benign and malignant tumors.

【73】**5.2 Cross-Sectional Imaging (US， CT， MRI)**

【74】Cross-sectional imaging modalities remain the mainstay in the detection and assess-ment of cystic pancreatic tumors. Transabdominal ultrasonography (US) can detect pancreatic cystic lesions； however， given its limited spatial resolution and soft-tissue contrast 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>， US is often not very helpful in the evaluation of cystic neoplasms of the pancreas. Multidetector computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imag-ing (MRI) are the most common radiologic methods used for characterization of

**D. Kechagias ()·F.Laspas ()|删除换行|these lesions. Many authors argue that MRI due to its greater contrast between fluid and soft tissue allows optical depiction of the morphologic features of cystic pancre-atic lesions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2， 3\]</u>； however， recent studies suggest that both multidetector CT and MRI provide high-quality images of cystic pancreatic lesions with comparable diagnostic accuracy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[4，5\]</u>. Although the accuracy of these methods ranges from 40to 60 % in providing the correct histologic diagnosis of cystic lesions of the pan-creas 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>， Visser et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[5\]</u> found that multidetector CT and MRI had an accuracy of76-82 % and 85-91 % respectively in establishing the diagnosis of malignancy in cystic pancreatic masses. The use of advanced MRI techniques， such as diffusion-weighted imaging and ADC measurements， are less helpful currently in distinguish-ing neoplasmatic from non-neoplasmatic pancreatic cysts than originally hoped 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>.

【76】Several important morphologic features of cross-sectional imaging have been shown to be useful in the diagnostic approach to cystic lesions of the pancreas， including the presence of septa (unilocular， oligolocular <6 internal cysts， multi-locular ≥6 internal cysts)， the size of internal cysts (microcystic <2 cm， macrocystic≥2 cm)， the presence of calcification or mural nodules， and communication of the cystic lesion with the main pancreatic duct 通用删除6(英):<u>\[7-9\]</u>.

【77】Serous cystic neoplasm (SCN) is a benign cystic neoplasm of the pancreas that is more frequently found in older women 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>. The most common pattern (70 % of the cases) of SCN is a lobulated lesion consisting of numerous cysts (more than 6) varying from a few millimeters to 2 cm in diameter (but typically less than 1 cm) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2，10， 11\]</u> . A central fibrous scar that may be calcified is seen up to30 % of cases and is considered to be characteristic and virtually pathognomonic 通用删除6(英):<u>\[9，10\]</u>. Calcification is better depicted on CT . The presence of a large number of very small cysts with innumerable enhancing septa may actually produce what may look like a solid appearance on CT 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10-12\]</u>. In these cases，clear depiction of numerous discrete small fluid-filled cysts at MRI (due to the high sen-sitivity of the method in detecting fluid) will usually be diagnostic 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，12\]</u>. Uncommonly， an SCN may have an oligolocular or macrocystic appearance that is difficult to differentiate from other mucinous forms of cystic neoplasms.

【10】Muscle/Tendon Channel Pathology

【11】The pathology of the Muscle / Tendon Channels also reflects the symptoms of corresponding groups of muscles and other connective tissues. The connective tissues are divided into three groups: the large, the small, and the membranous connective tissue.

【12】Being superficial, the Twelve Muscle / Tendon Channels contain Wei Qi; thus, they provide the body's Third line of defense against any unfavorable exogenous influence (the first being the body's three external Wei Qi fields, and the second being the Wei Qi stored within the skin). Only after overcoming the resistance of the body's Muscle/Tendon Wei Qi can the Evil Exogenous pathogens travel down the length of the channel to penetrate the corresponding primary channel at the Jing-Well point. Jing-Well points are points of energetic union, connecting primary channel points together with the points where the Muscle / Tendon Channel have their origin.

【13】Clinical, application

【14】There are points of connection, as well as intersecting points found along the Muscle / Tendon Channels. Treatment at these conjunctive points can create a favorable response, allowing for a greater response to Purgation and Tonification techniques. Therefore, the Qigong doctor can effectively apply Jing Point Therapy to specific areas and points along the Muscle/Tendon Channels using both Purgation and Tonification tissue stimulation. These channels are also responsible for extending and flexing the muscles, tendons, ligaments, and joints. Their pathology is reflected in symptoms of impaired movement (i.e. pulled, twisted, strained, cramped, or atrophied muscles, spasms, etc.).

【15】Therapeutically, a local Muscle/Tendon Channel symptom can be treated by stimulating an area located next to the origin of the pain; for example, if the area is Yang (lateral) and overactive, then the Yin (medial) will be underactive and
