M.ANY diseases mimic lichen planus clinically|删除换行|and histopathologically， among them lichen planus-like keratosis， lichenoid discoid lupus erythematosus， lichenoid photo-dermatitis， lichenoid second-ary syphilis， and lichenoid drug eruptions， most notably， lichenoidgold dermatitis. Of all the drugeruptions that simulate lichen planus， gold is probably the most common and， therefore， will serve as the stereotype in this discussion of lichenoid drug eruptions. In general， the principles that apply to lichenoid gold dermatitis obtain also for lichenoid eruptions caused by drugs such as thiazides and phenothiazides. Lichenoid gold dermatitis and lichen planus share many features in addition to mostly superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes that also fill the papillary dermis in a band (lichenoid pattern) and obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic keratinocytes. Both may be associ-ated with compact orthokeratosis， focal hypergranulosis， irregular epider-mal hyperplasia， clefts at the dermo-epidermal junction， and extravasation of erythrocytes and presence of melanophages in a thickened papillary der-mis.

【56】Although lichen planus and lichenoid gold dermatitis have many fea-tures in common， they still can be differentiated from one another histo-oathologically by a few findings that tend to be repeatable. In contrast to lichen planus， lichenoid gold dermatitis often is accompanied by focal para-keratosis， a granular zone that is diminished or absent focally， innumerable necrotic keratinocytes within the epidermis， some of them even in the gran-ular zone， and， almost always， some eosinophils within the infiltrate of inflammatory cells. This constellation of findings usually permits differenti-ation of lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus with assurance.

【57】Typical lichen planus is characterized by violaceouspapules that have polygonal outlines， flat surfaces， and slightly scaly coverings. Sometimes， white lines， known as Wickham's striaie， crisscross the surface of lesions of lichen planus. When a patient with eruptive lichen planus is scratched or injured in another fashion， lesions of true lichen planus tend to arise at the sites of injury. That happening is known as Koebner’s， or isomorphic， phe-nomenon. Although lichen planus may affect any anatomic site， lesions favor the wrists， the lumbar region， and the ankles. Commonly， lesions of lichen planus affect mucous membranes of the oral cavity and sometimes other mucous membranes.

**Lesions of lichen planusare notoriously pruritic， and when they are rubbedoersistently for longperiods， especially on the legs， a condition termed1“hypertrophic lichen polanus _r_ results. When lesions of lichen planus|删除0换行|resolve with slightly atrophic macules， the condition is referred to as atrophic lichen planus. When the process of lichen planus is accelerated markedly， vesicles of the disease may appear， the blisters being subepider-mal. Lesions of lichen planus also may take on various shapes， among thern rings， i.e.， annular lichen planus. In contrast to authentic lichen planus， lichenoid drug eruptions may not be pruritic， have no predilection for any particular anatomic site， tend to be widespread， and lesions are not covered by Wickham’s striae. Because individual lesions are not long-lasting， none become hypertrophic or atrophie. There are no blisters as a rule in lichenoid drug eruptions. Curiously， despite the fact that the histopathologic appear-ance of lesions induced by drugs may be lichenoid， the clinical appearance of those lesions often is psoriasiform. Plaques may be more numerous than papules. Lesions of lichenoid drug cruptions， like those of authentic lichen planus， often resolve with prominent and often long-lasting hyperpigmenta-tion.

【59】A host of agents may induce lichenoid drug eruptions. They range from topical agents， such as developers used in the processing of color films， to systemic medications， such as anti-malarial agents， like chloroquine， anti-tuberculitic agents like PAS and streptomycin， and a variety of other drugs such as beta blockers， quinidine， quinine， methyldopa， dapsone， thiazide， and penicillamine. The list of those drugs is long and is lengthening.

【60】One of the important clues to differentiating lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus and from other lichenoid inflammatory processes in the skin is the presence， above the lichenoid infiltrate， ofextensive necrosis of individual keratinocytes in the epidermis. The changes seen at the junction between epidermis and dermis are found also at the interface between adnexal epithelia and dermis.

【105】Despite these many similarities， discoid lupus erythematosus may be differentiated nearly always from dermatomyositis because it tends to have a denser and deeper infiltrate of lymphocytes， plugging by cornified cells of dilated infundibuila， and， in late lesions， extensive sclerosis in the upper part of the dermis. For practical purposes， none of these four features ispresent in dermatomyositis， but there are exceptions. For example， some sclerosis is apparent in the upper part of the dermis of long-standing lesions of Got-tron's papules， distinctive lesions on the acra of some patients with derma-tomyositis.

【106】Clinically， discoid lupus erythernatosus evolves through early， fully de-veloped， and late stages， just as does dermatomyositis. Poikilodermatous changes， however， are more common in dermatomnyositis than in discoid lupus erythematosus. It may well be that the “butterfly blush" of systemic lupus erythematosus is merely an evanescent form of acute discoid lupus erythematosus and that bullous systemic lupus erythemnatosus is simply a caricature of the process oid lupus erythematosus， analogous to pustular psoriassiiss as an exag geration of papular psoriasis vulgaris and bullous lichen planus of papular lichen planus.

【154】ATROPHIC lichen planus and atrophic discoid

【155】lupus erythematosis pose rproblems in histopathologic differential diagnosis because they have several fealures in common， among them compact ortho-keratosis， focal hypergranulosis， epidermis thinned and accompanied by flattened rete ridges and dermalpapillae， vacuolar alteration along the dermo-epidermalijunction， individual necrotic keratinocytes， lymphocytic infiltrates of variable density， melanophages， and altered bundles of col-lagen in the upper part of the dermis. Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. If attention is paid to the criteria listed on the first page of this chapter， histopathologic differentiation can be accomplished with facility in most instances.

M.ANY diseases mimic lichen planus clinically|删除换行|and histopathologically， among them lichen planus-like keratosis， lichenoid discoid lupus erythematosus， lichenoid photo-dermatitis， lichenoid second-ary syphilis， and lichenoid drug eruptions， most notably， lichenoidgold dermatitis. Of all the drugeruptions that simulate lichen planus， gold is probably the most common and， therefore， will serve as the stereotype in this discussion of lichenoid drug eruptions. In general， the principles that apply to lichenoid gold dermatitis obtain also for lichenoid eruptions caused by drugs such as thiazides and phenothiazides. Lichenoid gold dermatitis and lichen planus share many features in addition to mostly superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes that also fill the papillary dermis in a band (lichenoid pattern) and obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic keratinocytes. Both may be associ-ated with compact orthokeratosis， focal hypergranulosis， irregular epider-mal hyperplasia， clefts at the dermo-epidermal junction， and extravasation of erythrocytes and presence of melanophages in a thickened papillary der-mis.

【56】Although lichen planus and lichenoid gold dermatitis have many fea-tures in common， they still can be differentiated from one another histo-oathologically by a few findings that tend to be repeatable. In contrast to lichen planus， lichenoid gold dermatitis often is accompanied by focal para-keratosis， a granular zone that is diminished or absent focally， innumerable necrotic keratinocytes within the epidermis， some of them even in the gran-ular zone， and， almost always， some eosinophils within the infiltrate of inflammatory cells. This constellation of findings usually permits differenti-ation of lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus with assurance.

【57】Typical lichen planus is characterized by violaceouspapules that have polygonal outlines， flat surfaces， and slightly scaly coverings. Sometimes， white lines， known as Wickham's striaie， crisscross the surface of lesions of lichen planus. When a patient with eruptive lichen planus is scratched or injured in another fashion， lesions of true lichen planus tend to arise at the sites of injury. That happening is known as Koebner’s， or isomorphic， phe-nomenon. Although lichen planus may affect any anatomic site， lesions favor the wrists， the lumbar region， and the ankles. Commonly， lesions of lichen planus affect mucous membranes of the oral cavity and sometimes other mucous membranes.

**Lesions of lichen planusare notoriously pruritic， and when they are rubbedoersistently for longperiods， especially on the legs， a condition termed1“hypertrophic lichen polanus _r_ results. When lesions of lichen planus|删除0换行|resolve with slightly atrophic macules， the condition is referred to as atrophic lichen planus. When the process of lichen planus is accelerated markedly， vesicles of the disease may appear， the blisters being subepider-mal. Lesions of lichen planus also may take on various shapes， among thern rings， i.e.， annular lichen planus. In contrast to authentic lichen planus， lichenoid drug eruptions may not be pruritic， have no predilection for any particular anatomic site， tend to be widespread， and lesions are not covered by Wickham’s striae. Because individual lesions are not long-lasting， none become hypertrophic or atrophie. There are no blisters as a rule in lichenoid drug eruptions. Curiously， despite the fact that the histopathologic appear-ance of lesions induced by drugs may be lichenoid， the clinical appearance of those lesions often is psoriasiform. Plaques may be more numerous than papules. Lesions of lichenoid drug cruptions， like those of authentic lichen planus， often resolve with prominent and often long-lasting hyperpigmenta-tion.

【59】A host of agents may induce lichenoid drug eruptions. They range from topical agents， such as developers used in the processing of color films， to systemic medications， such as anti-malarial agents， like chloroquine， anti-tuberculitic agents like PAS and streptomycin， and a variety of other drugs such as beta blockers， quinidine， quinine， methyldopa， dapsone， thiazide， and penicillamine. The list of those drugs is long and is lengthening.

【60】One of the important clues to differentiating lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus and from other lichenoid inflammatory processes in the skin is the presence， above the lichenoid infiltrate， ofextensive necrosis of individual keratinocytes in the epidermis. Of course， true lichen planus and other lichenoid dermatitides may be associated with necrotic keratinocytes， but no lichenoid dermnatitis is associated so consistently with so many ne-crotic keratinocytes as is lichenoid gold dermatitis. Although that is particu-larly true of gold-induced dermatitis， it applies to other lichenoid drug erup-tions， but less dramatically.

【61】An oft-asked question by students of lichen planus is， “what accounts for Wickham’s striae histopathologically?" Those white streaks arranged in reticulated pattern seem to correspond to exaggerations of already-existing compact orthokeratosis above wedges of hypergranulosis restricted to sites of acrosyringia and acrotrichia.

Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. If attention is paid to the criteria listed on the first page of this chapter， histopathologic differentiation can be accomplished with facility in most instances.

M.ANY diseases mimic lichen planus clinically|删除换行|and histopathologically， among them lichen planus-like keratosis， lichenoid discoid lupus erythematosus， lichenoid photo-dermatitis， lichenoid second-ary syphilis， and lichenoid drug eruptions， most notably， lichenoidgold dermatitis. Of all the drugeruptions that simulate lichen planus， gold is probably the most common and， therefore， will serve as the stereotype in this discussion of lichenoid drug eruptions. In general， the principles that apply to lichenoid gold dermatitis obtain also for lichenoid eruptions caused by drugs such as thiazides and phenothiazides. Lichenoid gold dermatitis and lichen planus share many features in addition to mostly superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes that also fill the papillary dermis in a band (lichenoid pattern) and obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic keratinocytes. Both may be associ-ated with compact orthokeratosis， focal hypergranulosis， irregular epider-mal hyperplasia， clefts at the dermo-epidermal junction， and extravasation of erythrocytes and presence of melanophages in a thickened papillary der-mis.

【56】Although lichen planus and lichenoid gold dermatitis have many fea-tures in common， they still can be differentiated from one another histo-oathologically by a few findings that tend to be repeatable. In contrast to lichen planus， lichenoid gold dermatitis often is accompanied by focal para-keratosis， a granular zone that is diminished or absent focally， innumerable necrotic keratinocytes within the epidermis， some of them even in the gran-ular zone， and， almost always， some eosinophils within the infiltrate of inflammatory cells. This constellation of findings usually permits differenti-ation of lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus with assurance.

【57】Typical lichen planus is characterized by violaceouspapules that have polygonal outlines， flat surfaces， and slightly scaly coverings. Sometimes， white lines， known as Wickham's striaie， crisscross the surface of lesions of lichen planus. When a patient with eruptive lichen planus is scratched or injured in another fashion， lesions of true lichen planus tend to arise at the sites of injury. That happening is known as Koebner’s， or isomorphic， phe-nomenon. Although lichen planus may affect any anatomic site， lesions favor the wrists， the lumbar region， and the ankles. Commonly， lesions of lichen planus affect mucous membranes of the oral cavity and sometimes other mucous membranes.

**Lesions of lichen planusare notoriously pruritic， and when they are rubbedoersistently for longperiods， especially on the legs， a condition termed1“hypertrophic lichen polanus _r_ results. When lesions of lichen planus|删除0换行|resolve with slightly atrophic macules， the condition is referred to as atrophic lichen planus. When the process of lichen planus is accelerated markedly， vesicles of the disease may appear， the blisters being subepider-mal. Lesions of lichen planus also may take on various shapes， among thern rings， i.e.， annular lichen planus. In contrast to authentic lichen planus， lichenoid drug eruptions may not be pruritic， have no predilection for any particular anatomic site， tend to be widespread， and lesions are not covered by Wickham’s striae. Because individual lesions are not long-lasting， none become hypertrophic or atrophie. There are no blisters as a rule in lichenoid drug eruptions. Curiously， despite the fact that the histopathologic appear-ance of lesions induced by drugs may be lichenoid， the clinical appearance of those lesions often is psoriasiform. Plaques may be more numerous than papules. Lesions of lichenoid drug cruptions， like those of authentic lichen planus， often resolve with prominent and often long-lasting hyperpigmenta-tion.

【59】A host of agents may induce lichenoid drug eruptions. They range from topical agents， such as developers used in the processing of color films， to systemic medications， such as anti-malarial agents， like chloroquine， anti-tuberculitic agents like PAS and streptomycin， and a variety of other drugs such as beta blockers， quinidine， quinine， methyldopa， dapsone， thiazide， and penicillamine. The list of those drugs is long and is lengthening.

【60】One of the important clues to differentiating lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus and from other lichenoid inflammatory processes in the skin is the presence， above the lichenoid infiltrate， ofextensive necrosis of individual keratinocytes in the epidermis. Of course， true lichen planus and other lichenoid dermatitides may be associated with necrotic keratinocytes， but no lichenoid dermnatitis is associated so consistently with so many ne-crotic keratinocytes as is lichenoid gold dermatitis. Although that is particu-larly true of gold-induced dermatitis， it applies to other lichenoid drug erup-tions， but less dramatically.

【61】An oft-asked question by students of lichen planus is， “what accounts for Wickham’s striae histopathologically?" Those white streaks arranged in reticulated pattern seem to correspond to exaggerations of already-existing compact orthokeratosis above wedges of hypergranulosis restricted to sites of acrosyringia and acrotrichia.

【104】ISCOID lupus erythematosus and dermatomyo-sitis have more histopathologic features in common than they have ones that differentiate them. Both diseases are characterized by compact ortho-keratosis， an epidermis thinned focally， a pattern of rete ridges and dermal papillae that is muted markedly， focal hypergranulosis， necrotic keratino-cytes at the dermo-epidermal junction and as colloid bodies in the upper-most dermis， vacuolar alteration at the dermo-epidermal junction， a thick-ened bascmeIImembrane， a sprinkling of _1_ lymphocytes2alongthe dermo-epidermal junction， subepidermal clefts， telangiectases， deposits of abundant mucin in the reticular dermis especially， stellate fibrocytes， ex-travasated erythrocytes， melanophages and siderophages in the upper part of the dermis， and edema in the upper part of the dermis. The changes seen at the junction between epidermis and dermis are found also at the interface between adnexal epithelia and dermis.

【105】Despite these many similarities， discoid lupus erythematosus may be differentiated nearly always from dermatomyositis because it tends to have a denser and deeper infiltrate of lymphocytes， plugging by cornified cells of dilated infundibuila， and， in late lesions， extensive sclerosis in the upper part of the dermis. For practical purposes， none of these four features ispresent in dermatomyositis， but there are exceptions. For example， some sclerosis is apparent in the upper part of the dermis of long-standing lesions of Got-tron's papules， distinctive lesions on the acra of some patients with derma-tomyositis.

【106】Clinically， discoid lupus erythernatosus evolves through early， fully de-veloped， and late stages， just as does dermatomyositis. In discoid lupus erythematosus， reddish macules becomepatches and plaques that， in time， are marked by dilated ostia of infundibula within which are “carpet-tack”scales， and， as the processprogresses， the appearance of atrophy， hyper-and hypopigmentation， and telangiectases. Poikilodermatous changes， however， are more common in dermatomnyositis than in discoid lupus erythematosus. It may well be that the “butterfly blush" of systemic lupus erythematosus is merely an evanescent form of acute discoid lupus erythematosus and that bullous systemic lupus erythemnatosus is simply a caricature of the process oid lupus erythematosus， analogous to pustular psoriassiiss as an exag geration of papular psoriasis vulgaris and bullous lichen planus of papular lichen planus.

Dermatomyositis expresses itself differently on different anatomic sites. In an early stage， the eyelids are swollen markedly by edema and covered by telangiectases， findings that impart to the skin of the eyelids a color like|删除0换行|heliotrope. In time， those changes and those on other anatomic sites， especiallysun-exposedsites。 resolvewith poikiloderma (poikiloder-matomyositis) typified by hyper- and hypopigmentation， atrophy， and tel-angiectases. Biopsy of lesions of poikilodermatomyositis， as well as of Got-tron’s papules， shows histopathologic findings at the interface of dermis and epidermis that are common to non-poikilodermatous lesions of' discoid lupus crythematosus and dermatomyositis.**

【108】**In sum， changes in the epidermis and at the dermo-epidermaljunction of discoid lupus erythematosus and dermatomyositis are identical， just as are those within the epidermis and at the dermo-epidermal interface of erythema multiforme and fixed drug eruption. In both sets of look-alikes， the differentiating histopathologic findings arepresent within the dermis(and， in the case of erythema multiforme and fixed drug eruption， in the character of the infiltrates that comprise them).**

M.ANY diseases mimic lichen planus clinically|删除换行|and histopathologically， among them lichen planus-like keratosis， lichenoid discoid lupus erythematosus， lichenoid photo-dermatitis， lichenoid second-ary syphilis， and lichenoid drug eruptions， most notably， lichenoidgold dermatitis. Of all the drugeruptions that simulate lichen planus， gold is probably the most common and， therefore， will serve as the stereotype in this discussion of lichenoid drug eruptions. In general， the principles that apply to lichenoid gold dermatitis obtain also for lichenoid eruptions caused by drugs such as thiazides and phenothiazides. Lichenoid gold dermatitis and lichen planus share many features in addition to mostly superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes that also fill the papillary dermis in a band (lichenoid pattern) and obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic keratinocytes. Both may be associ-ated with compact orthokeratosis， focal hypergranulosis， irregular epider-mal hyperplasia， clefts at the dermo-epidermal junction， and extravasation of erythrocytes and presence of melanophages in a thickened papillary der-mis.

【56】Although lichen planus and lichenoid gold dermatitis have many fea-tures in common， they still can be differentiated from one another histo-oathologically by a few findings that tend to be repeatable. In contrast to lichen planus， lichenoid gold dermatitis often is accompanied by focal para-keratosis， a granular zone that is diminished or absent focally， innumerable necrotic keratinocytes within the epidermis， some of them even in the gran-ular zone， and， almost always， some eosinophils within the infiltrate of inflammatory cells. This constellation of findings usually permits differenti-ation of lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus with assurance.

【57】Typical lichen planus is characterized by violaceouspapules that have polygonal outlines， flat surfaces， and slightly scaly coverings. Sometimes， white lines， known as Wickham's striaie， crisscross the surface of lesions of lichen planus. When a patient with eruptive lichen planus is scratched or injured in another fashion， lesions of true lichen planus tend to arise at the sites of injury. That happening is known as Koebner’s， or isomorphic， phe-nomenon. Although lichen planus may affect any anatomic site， lesions favor the wrists， the lumbar region， and the ankles. Commonly， lesions of lichen planus affect mucous membranes of the oral cavity and sometimes other mucous membranes.

**Lesions of lichen planusare notoriously pruritic， and when they are rubbedoersistently for longperiods， especially on the legs， a condition termed1“hypertrophic lichen polanus _r_ results. When lesions of lichen planus|删除0换行|resolve with slightly atrophic macules， the condition is referred to as atrophic lichen planus. When the process of lichen planus is accelerated markedly， vesicles of the disease may appear， the blisters being subepider-mal. Lesions of lichen planus also may take on various shapes， among thern rings， i.e.， annular lichen planus. In contrast to authentic lichen planus， lichenoid drug eruptions may not be pruritic， have no predilection for any particular anatomic site， tend to be widespread， and lesions are not covered by Wickham’s striae. Because individual lesions are not long-lasting， none become hypertrophic or atrophie. There are no blisters as a rule in lichenoid drug eruptions. Curiously， despite the fact that the histopathologic appear-ance of lesions induced by drugs may be lichenoid， the clinical appearance of those lesions often is psoriasiform. Plaques may be more numerous than papules. Lesions of lichenoid drug cruptions， like those of authentic lichen planus， often resolve with prominent and often long-lasting hyperpigmenta-tion.

【59】A host of agents may induce lichenoid drug eruptions. They range from topical agents， such as developers used in the processing of color films， to systemic medications， such as anti-malarial agents， like chloroquine， anti-tuberculitic agents like PAS and streptomycin， and a variety of other drugs such as beta blockers， quinidine， quinine， methyldopa， dapsone， thiazide， and penicillamine. The list of those drugs is long and is lengthening.

【60】One of the important clues to differentiating lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus and from other lichenoid inflammatory processes in the skin is the presence， above the lichenoid infiltrate， ofextensive necrosis of individual keratinocytes in the epidermis. Of course， true lichen planus and other lichenoid dermatitides may be associated with necrotic keratinocytes， but no lichenoid dermnatitis is associated so consistently with so many ne-crotic keratinocytes as is lichenoid gold dermatitis. Although that is particu-larly true of gold-induced dermatitis， it applies to other lichenoid drug erup-tions， but less dramatically.

【61】An oft-asked question by students of lichen planus is， “what accounts for Wickham’s striae histopathologically?" Those white streaks arranged in reticulated pattern seem to correspond to exaggerations of already-existing compact orthokeratosis above wedges of hypergranulosis restricted to sites of acrosyringia and acrotrichia.

【104】ISCOID lupus erythematosus and dermatomyo-sitis have more histopathologic features in common than they have ones that differentiate them. Both diseases are characterized by compact ortho-keratosis， an epidermis thinned focally， a pattern of rete ridges and dermal papillae that is muted markedly， focal hypergranulosis， necrotic keratino-cytes at the dermo-epidermal junction and as colloid bodies in the upper-most dermis， vacuolar alteration at the dermo-epidermal junction， a thick-ened bascmeIImembrane， a sprinkling of _1_ lymphocytes2alongthe dermo-epidermal junction， subepidermal clefts， telangiectases， deposits of abundant mucin in the reticular dermis especially， stellate fibrocytes， ex-travasated erythrocytes， melanophages and siderophages in the upper part of the dermis， and edema in the upper part of the dermis. The changes seen at the junction between epidermis and dermis are found also at the interface between adnexal epithelia and dermis.

【105】Despite these many similarities， discoid lupus erythematosus may be differentiated nearly always from dermatomyositis because it tends to have a denser and deeper infiltrate of lymphocytes， plugging by cornified cells of dilated infundibuila， and， in late lesions， extensive sclerosis in the upper part of the dermis. For practical purposes， none of these four features ispresent in dermatomyositis， but there are exceptions. For example， some sclerosis is apparent in the upper part of the dermis of long-standing lesions of Got-tron's papules， distinctive lesions on the acra of some patients with derma-tomyositis.

【106】Clinically， discoid lupus erythernatosus evolves through early， fully de-veloped， and late stages， just as does dermatomyositis. In discoid lupus erythematosus， reddish macules becomepatches and plaques that， in time， are marked by dilated ostia of infundibula within which are “carpet-tack”scales， and， as the processprogresses， the appearance of atrophy， hyper-and hypopigmentation， and telangiectases. Poikilodermatous changes， however， are more common in dermatomnyositis than in discoid lupus erythematosus. It may well be that the “butterfly blush" of systemic lupus erythematosus is merely an evanescent form of acute discoid lupus erythematosus and that bullous systemic lupus erythemnatosus is simply a caricature of the process oid lupus erythematosus， analogous to pustular psoriassiiss as an exag geration of papular psoriasis vulgaris and bullous lichen planus of papular lichen planus.

Dermatomyositis expresses itself differently on different anatomic sites. In an early stage， the eyelids are swollen markedly by edema and covered by telangiectases， findings that impart to the skin of the eyelids a color like|删除0换行|heliotrope. In time， those changes and those on other anatomic sites， especiallysun-exposedsites。 resolvewith poikiloderma (poikiloder-matomyositis) typified by hyper- and hypopigmentation， atrophy， and tel-angiectases. Biopsy of lesions of poikilodermatomyositis， as well as of Got-tron’s papules， shows histopathologic findings at the interface of dermis and epidermis that are common to non-poikilodermatous lesions of' discoid lupus crythematosus and dermatomyositis.**

【108】**In sum， changes in the epidermis and at the dermo-epidermaljunction of discoid lupus erythematosus and dermatomyositis are identical， just as are those within the epidermis and at the dermo-epidermal interface of erythema multiforme and fixed drug eruption. In both sets of look-alikes， the differentiating histopathologic findings arepresent within the dermis(and， in the case of erythema multiforme and fixed drug eruption， in the character of the infiltrates that comprise them).**

【155】lupus erythematosis pose rproblems in histopathologic differential diagnosis because they have several fealures in common， among them compact ortho-keratosis， focal hypergranulosis， epidermis thinned and accompanied by flattened rete ridges and dermalpapillae， vacuolar alteration along the dermo-epidermalijunction， individual necrotic keratinocytes， lymphocytic infiltrates of variable density， melanophages， and altered bundles of col-lagen in the upper part of the dermis. Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. Of all the drugeruptions that simulate lichen planus， gold is probably the most common and， therefore， will serve as the stereotype in this discussion of lichenoid drug eruptions. In general， the principles that apply to lichenoid gold dermatitis obtain also for lichenoid eruptions caused by drugs such as thiazides and phenothiazides. Lichenoid gold dermatitis and lichen planus share many features in addition to mostly superficial perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes that also fill the papillary dermis in a band (lichenoid pattern) and obscure the dermo-epidermal junction where there are vacuolar alteration and necrotic keratinocytes. Both may be associ-ated with compact orthokeratosis， focal hypergranulosis， irregular epider-mal hyperplasia， clefts at the dermo-epidermal junction， and extravasation of erythrocytes and presence of melanophages in a thickened papillary der-mis.

【56】Although lichen planus and lichenoid gold dermatitis have many fea-tures in common， they still can be differentiated from one another histo-oathologically by a few findings that tend to be repeatable. In contrast to lichen planus， lichenoid gold dermatitis often is accompanied by focal para-keratosis， a granular zone that is diminished or absent focally， innumerable necrotic keratinocytes within the epidermis， some of them even in the gran-ular zone， and， almost always， some eosinophils within the infiltrate of inflammatory cells. This constellation of findings usually permits differenti-ation of lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus with assurance.

【57】Typical lichen planus is characterized by violaceouspapules that have polygonal outlines， flat surfaces， and slightly scaly coverings. Sometimes， white lines， known as Wickham's striaie， crisscross the surface of lesions of lichen planus. When a patient with eruptive lichen planus is scratched or injured in another fashion， lesions of true lichen planus tend to arise at the sites of injury. That happening is known as Koebner’s， or isomorphic， phe-nomenon. Although lichen planus may affect any anatomic site， lesions favor the wrists， the lumbar region， and the ankles. Commonly， lesions of lichen planus affect mucous membranes of the oral cavity and sometimes other mucous membranes.

**Lesions of lichen planusare notoriously pruritic， and when they are rubbedoersistently for longperiods， especially on the legs， a condition termed1“hypertrophic lichen polanus _r_ results. When lesions of lichen planus|删除0换行|resolve with slightly atrophic macules， the condition is referred to as atrophic lichen planus. When the process of lichen planus is accelerated markedly， vesicles of the disease may appear， the blisters being subepider-mal. Lesions of lichen planus also may take on various shapes， among thern rings， i.e.， annular lichen planus. In contrast to authentic lichen planus， lichenoid drug eruptions may not be pruritic， have no predilection for any particular anatomic site， tend to be widespread， and lesions are not covered by Wickham’s striae. Because individual lesions are not long-lasting， none become hypertrophic or atrophie. There are no blisters as a rule in lichenoid drug eruptions. Curiously， despite the fact that the histopathologic appear-ance of lesions induced by drugs may be lichenoid， the clinical appearance of those lesions often is psoriasiform. Plaques may be more numerous than papules. Lesions of lichenoid drug cruptions， like those of authentic lichen planus， often resolve with prominent and often long-lasting hyperpigmenta-tion.

The list of those drugs is long and is lengthening.

【60】One of the important clues to differentiating lichenoid gold dermatitis from lichen planus and from other lichenoid inflammatory processes in the skin is the presence， above the lichenoid infiltrate， ofextensive necrosis of individual keratinocytes in the epidermis. Of course， true lichen planus and other lichenoid dermatitides may be associated with necrotic keratinocytes， but no lichenoid dermnatitis is associated so consistently with so many ne-crotic keratinocytes as is lichenoid gold dermatitis. 【61】An oft-asked question by students of lichen planus is， “what accounts for Wickham’s striae histopathologically?" Those white streaks arranged in reticulated pattern seem to correspond to exaggerations of already-existing compact orthokeratosis above wedges of hypergranulosis restricted to sites of acrosyringia and acrotrichia.

【154】ATROPHIC lichen planus and atrophic discoid

【155】lupus erythematosis pose rproblems in histopathologic differential diagnosis because they have several fealures in common， among them compact ortho-keratosis， focal hypergranulosis， epidermis thinned and accompanied by flattened rete ridges and dermalpapillae， vacuolar alteration along the dermo-epidermalijunction， individual necrotic keratinocytes， lymphocytic infiltrates of variable density， melanophages， and altered bundles of col-lagen in the upper part of the dermis. Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. If attention is paid to the criteria listed on the first page of this chapter， histopathologic differentiation can be accomplished with facility in most instances.

【155】lupus erythematosis pose rproblems in histopathologic differential diagnosis because they have several fealures in common， among them compact ortho-keratosis， focal hypergranulosis， epidermis thinned and accompanied by flattened rete ridges and dermalpapillae， vacuolar alteration along the dermo-epidermalijunction， individual necrotic keratinocytes， lymphocytic infiltrates of variable density， melanophages， and altered bundles of col-lagen in the upper part of the dermis. Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. If attention is paid to the criteria listed on the first page of this chapter， histopathologic differentiation can be accomplished with facility in most instances.

In discoid lupus erythematosus， reddish macules becomepatches and plaques that， in time， are marked by dilated ostia of infundibula within which are “carpet-tack”scales， and， as the processprogresses， the appearance of atrophy， hyper-and hypopigmentation， and telangiectases. 【154】ATROPHIC lichen planus and atrophic discoid

【155】lupus erythematosis pose rproblems in histopathologic differential diagnosis because they have several fealures in common， among them compact ortho-keratosis， focal hypergranulosis， epidermis thinned and accompanied by flattened rete ridges and dermalpapillae， vacuolar alteration along the dermo-epidermalijunction， individual necrotic keratinocytes， lymphocytic infiltrates of variable density， melanophages， and altered bundles of col-lagen in the upper part of the dermis. Despite the many features shared by these two very different atrophic discases， they can be differentiated histo-pathologically by an exceedingly thin epidermis in discoid lupus erythema-tosus， overtly wedge-shaped hypergranulosis in lichen planus， a thickened basement membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， peri-infundibular fi-brosis in lichen planus， and melanophages aligned below a thickened base-ment membrane in discoid lupus erythematosus， but scattered throughout an apparently thickened papillary dermis in lichen planus.

【156】Atrophic discoid lupus erythematosus tends to appear not only at sites exposed to sunlight， e.g.， malar cminences， nose， and checks， but also on covered places such as the scalp， in the ears， and， sometimes， on mucous membranes. In contrast， lesions of lichen planus have no predilection for sites exposed to sunlight and tend to favor flexor surfaces of the forearms， glans penis， and oral mucosa. When lesions of discoid lupus erythematosus pass through all of the stages in their chronologic sequence， they come to atrophy， the end stage that follows macules and patches of erythema， pap-ules and plaques， scales， including follicular plugs， and hyper- and hypopig. mentation， In contrast， lichen planus does not eventuate in atrophy often， but resolves usually with hyperpigmentation only. When lesions of lichen planus proceed to atrophy， they appear as hyperpigmented macules that are depressed slightly beneath the surface of the skin. Those atrophic lesions represent regression of typical violaceous polygonal papules that constitute fully developed lesions of lichen planus.

【157】It also must be noted that the epidermis in early lesions of discoid lupus erythemalosus may be thinned， but not as dramatically as in late ones. Furthermore， in early lesions， there is no fibrosis in the upper part of the dermis and no signs of atrophy clinically.

Atrophy in lichen planus and in discoid lupus erythematosus is of the superficial type. Superficial atrophy is characterized clinically by a slight depression beneath the skin surface， shininess， wrinkled appearance， ab-sence of hairs， and telangiectases. Superficial atrophy results largely from obliteration of dermal papillae by fibrosis and only slightly from secondary|删除0换行|loss of epidermis. The loss of volume of dermal papillae accounts for most of the atrophy seen clinically. A second type of atrophy， not at play in either discoid lupus erythematosus or lichen planus， is characterized by loss not only of collagen bundles， but also of elastic fibers from the reticular dermis. The clinical manifestations of this deeper type of atrophy are anetodermas， among them so-called macular atrophy. Paradoxically， “macular”atrophy is actually papular. A third， and last， type of “cutaneous”atrophy involves the subcutancous fat， where pronounced loss of adipocytes results in a clini-cal appearance of one or more gullies. Stereotypical examples are the end stage of the panniculitis of discoid lupus erythematosus， known also as lupus profundus， lipodystrophy， and pancreatic panniculitis.

【159】In sum， atrophic lichen planus and atrophic discoid lupus erythema-tosus soretimes may be difficult to distinguish from one another， clinically and histopathologically. If attention is paid to the criteria listed on the first page of this chapter， histopathologic differentiation can be accomplished with facility in most instances.

【14】页码间删除-1:<u>### Differential Diagnosis</u>

【15】页码间删除-1:<u>#### Fibroadenoma, Cellular Fibroadenoma, Juvenile Fibroadenoma, and Benign Phyllodes Tumour</u>

【16】Fibroadenomas, especially those with areas of increased stromal cellularity, can be difficult to distinguish from the benign phyllodes tumour. The juvenile fibroadenoma, which often has increased stromal cellularity, may also pose difficulty in delineation from benign phyllodes tumour. Table 3.2 shows the key diagnostic characteristics of these tumours.

【17】A conservative approach is recommended for young patients in cases with features that are intermediate between cellular fibroadenoma and benign phyllodes tumour. The WHO 2012 working group recommends categorising such cases as benign fibroepithelial neoplasms to avoid unnecessary overtreatment 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u>. This approach is supported by a recent consensus review 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>, although it was cautioned that the term should be used sparingly.

【23】页码间删除-1:<u>#### Benign, Borderline, and Malignant Phyllodes Tumours</u>

【24】Grade assignment in phyllodes tumours follows the assessment of stromal features of atypia, hypercellularity, overgrowth and mitoses, and the nature of the tumour borders. Table 3.3 shows a guide to phyllodes tumour grading. While the grading appears straightforward, with sharp dividing lines, it is in fact a continuum, and there is substantial overlap in histologic characteristics between grades.

【29】#### Malignant Phyllodes Tumour with Sarcomatous Stromal Overgrowth, Spindle Cell Metaplastic Carcinoma, and Primary Breast Sarcoma

【30】Stromal overgrowth of a malignant phyllodes tumour can resemble a spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma  or primary breast sarcoma , particularly when the typical phyllodal fronded architecture is effaced. Apart from diligent sampling of these tumours to locate the characteristic leaf-like pattern of phyllodes tumour or conventional carcinoma component of spindle cell carcinoma, firm diagnoses usually require immunohistochemistry. The presence of diffuse p63 and keratin staining of spindle cells indicates a metaplastic carcinoma. It is important to note, however, that phyllodes tumours may manifest focal keratin staining of stromal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>, and p63 reactivity has recently been described in stromal cells of malignant phyllodes tumours 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Conversely, some metaplastic carcinomas may disclose heterogeneity in keratin positivity. More than one block may sometimes need to be submitted for immunohistochemical interrogation. Selection of tumour blocks containing areas with more cohesive epithelioid-like cells may be more promising in yielding positive results on keratin immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis of primary breast sarcoma is one of exclusion, after phyllodes tumour and metaplastic carcinoma have been ruled out. Table 3.4 shows features that may help distinguish these tumours.

【38】人名段删除-1:<u>#### Phyllodes Tumour and Periductal Stromal Tumour</u>

【39】Previously referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma, the WHO classification of breast tumours in 2012 revised the terminology to a more “neutral” term, periductal stromal “tumour”, avoiding the connotation of malignancy with “sarcoma”, as the biological behaviour of this rarely diagnosed lesion remains uncertain. Instead of the presence of well-formed stromal fronds capped by benign epithelium, the periductal stromal tumour consists of hypercellular collections of spindle cells present around pre-existing ducts and terminal ductal lobular units . Some of these tumours progress to conventional phyllodes tumours, and they are therefore currently classified under the rubric of phyllodal neoplasms.

It is non-circumscribed, consisting of a spindle cell proliferation localised around open tubules. Progression to classic phyllodes tumour has been documented, suggesting that it may be part of the same spectrum of disease. ( b ) Periductal stromal tumour. Stromal cells in the peri-epithelial region display accentuation of cellularity with moderate nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic activity. Such tumours with cytologic anaplasia and increased mitoses may be referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma. It is recommended that the diagnoses of periductal stromal tumour, or periductal stromal sarcoma when malignant histologic features are present, be qualified as belonging to the spectrum of phyllodes tumours</u>

【41】页码间删除-1:<u>### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations</u>

【42】Benign phyllodes tumours can recur locally, while malignant tumours are at higher risk of local recurrence and can metastasise. Borderline tumours tend to also locally recur and may rarely metastasise. Recurrence rates for benign, borderline, and malignant phyllodes tumours are 10 %–17 %, 20 %–25 %, and 23 %–27 %, respectively. Malignant tumours may metastasise and cause death in about 22 % of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>.

【43】Prognostication based on grading has challenges. Each microscopic parameter has several tiers of assessment, resulting in a significant number of permutations that confound accuracy and precision. While grading at extreme ends of the spectrum of phyllodes tumours is reliable, tumours in between are subject to interobserver variability due to challenges in applying the specified histologic criteria. A nomogram based on weighted parameters (AMOS criteria—stromal atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, surgical margins) attempts to circumvent the difficulties of conventional grading to allow individualised risk categorisation for patients diagnosed with phyllodes tumours  通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 – 13 \]</u>.

【45】The main therapy for phyllodes tumours is surgical excision. Although there is an approach for complete excision with negative margins for phyllodes tumours of all grades, there is some evidence to suggest that benign tumours that have been enucleated without ensuring negative margins may be expectantly followed, with complete excision if there is recurrence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>. 【15】页码间删除-1:<u>#### Fibroadenoma, Cellular Fibroadenoma, Juvenile Fibroadenoma, and Benign Phyllodes Tumour</u>

【16】Fibroadenomas, especially those with areas of increased stromal cellularity, can be difficult to distinguish from the benign phyllodes tumour. The juvenile fibroadenoma, which often has increased stromal cellularity, may also pose difficulty in delineation from benign phyllodes tumour. Table 3.2 shows the key diagnostic characteristics of these tumours.

【17】A conservative approach is recommended for young patients in cases with features that are intermediate between cellular fibroadenoma and benign phyllodes tumour. The WHO 2012 working group recommends categorising such cases as benign fibroepithelial neoplasms to avoid unnecessary overtreatment 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u>. This approach is supported by a recent consensus review 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>, although it was cautioned that the term should be used sparingly.

【23】页码间删除-1:<u>#### Benign, Borderline, and Malignant Phyllodes Tumours</u>

【24】Grade assignment in phyllodes tumours follows the assessment of stromal features of atypia, hypercellularity, overgrowth and mitoses, and the nature of the tumour borders. Table 3.3 shows a guide to phyllodes tumour grading. While the grading appears straightforward, with sharp dividing lines, it is in fact a continuum, and there is substantial overlap in histologic characteristics between grades.

【26】页码间删除-1:<u>Comparison of histologic features of benign, borderline, and malignant phyllodes tumours</u>

| Histologic feature | Benign phyllodes tumour | Borderline phyllodes tumour | Malignant phyllodes tumour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stromal cellularity | Mild | Moderate | Marked |
| Distribution of stromal hypercellularity | Variable | Variable | Diffuse |
| Stromal atypia | None to mild | Mild to moderate | Marked |
| Stromal mitoses | 0–4 mitoses/10 HPF | 5–9 mitoses/10 HPF | ≥10 mitoses/10 HPF |
| Stromal overgrowth | Absent | Absent, very focal if present | Often present |
| Tumour borders | Pushing and rounded | Pushing and rounded, may be permeative | Permeative |
| Malignant heterologous elements | Absent | Absent | May be present |

【28】页码间删除-1:<u>HPF high-power fields</u>

【29】#### Malignant Phyllodes Tumour with Sarcomatous Stromal Overgrowth, Spindle Cell Metaplastic Carcinoma, and Primary Breast Sarcoma

【30】Stromal overgrowth of a malignant phyllodes tumour can resemble a spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma  or primary breast sarcoma , particularly when the typical phyllodal fronded architecture is effaced. Apart from diligent sampling of these tumours to locate the characteristic leaf-like pattern of phyllodes tumour or conventional carcinoma component of spindle cell carcinoma, firm diagnoses usually require immunohistochemistry. The presence of diffuse p63 and keratin staining of spindle cells indicates a metaplastic carcinoma. It is important to note, however, that phyllodes tumours may manifest focal keratin staining of stromal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>, and p63 reactivity has recently been described in stromal cells of malignant phyllodes tumours 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Conversely, some metaplastic carcinomas may disclose heterogeneity in keratin positivity. More than one block may sometimes need to be submitted for immunohistochemical interrogation. Selection of tumour blocks containing areas with more cohesive epithelioid-like cells may be more promising in yielding positive results on keratin immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis of primary breast sarcoma is one of exclusion, after phyllodes tumour and metaplastic carcinoma have been ruled out. Table 3.4 shows features that may help distinguish these tumours.

【38】人名段删除-1:<u>#### Phyllodes Tumour and Periductal Stromal Tumour</u>

【39】Previously referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma, the WHO classification of breast tumours in 2012 revised the terminology to a more “neutral” term, periductal stromal “tumour”, avoiding the connotation of malignancy with “sarcoma”, as the biological behaviour of this rarely diagnosed lesion remains uncertain. Instead of the presence of well-formed stromal fronds capped by benign epithelium, the periductal stromal tumour consists of hypercellular collections of spindle cells present around pre-existing ducts and terminal ductal lobular units . Some of these tumours progress to conventional phyllodes tumours, and they are therefore currently classified under the rubric of phyllodal neoplasms.

Stromal cells in the peri-epithelial region display accentuation of cellularity with moderate nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic activity. Such tumours with cytologic anaplasia and increased mitoses may be referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma. It is recommended that the diagnoses of periductal stromal tumour, or periductal stromal sarcoma when malignant histologic features are present, be qualified as belonging to the spectrum of phyllodes tumours</u>

【41】页码间删除-1:<u>### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations</u>

【42】Benign phyllodes tumours can recur locally, while malignant tumours are at higher risk of local recurrence and can metastasise. Borderline tumours tend to also locally recur and may rarely metastasise. Recurrence rates for benign, borderline, and malignant phyllodes tumours are 10 %–17 %, 20 %–25 %, and 23 %–27 %, respectively. Malignant tumours may metastasise and cause death in about 22 % of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>.

【43】Prognostication based on grading has challenges. Each microscopic parameter has several tiers of assessment, resulting in a significant number of permutations that confound accuracy and precision. While grading at extreme ends of the spectrum of phyllodes tumours is reliable, tumours in between are subject to interobserver variability due to challenges in applying the specified histologic criteria. A nomogram based on weighted parameters (AMOS criteria—stromal atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, surgical margins) attempts to circumvent the difficulties of conventional grading to allow individualised risk categorisation for patients diagnosed with phyllodes tumours  通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 – 13 \]</u>.

【29】#### Malignant Phyllodes Tumour with Sarcomatous Stromal Overgrowth, Spindle Cell Metaplastic Carcinoma, and Primary Breast Sarcoma

【30】Stromal overgrowth of a malignant phyllodes tumour can resemble a spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma  or primary breast sarcoma , particularly when the typical phyllodal fronded architecture is effaced. Apart from diligent sampling of these tumours to locate the characteristic leaf-like pattern of phyllodes tumour or conventional carcinoma component of spindle cell carcinoma, firm diagnoses usually require immunohistochemistry. The presence of diffuse p63 and keratin staining of spindle cells indicates a metaplastic carcinoma. It is important to note, however, that phyllodes tumours may manifest focal keratin staining of stromal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>, and p63 reactivity has recently been described in stromal cells of malignant phyllodes tumours 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Conversely, some metaplastic carcinomas may disclose heterogeneity in keratin positivity. More than one block may sometimes need to be submitted for immunohistochemical interrogation. Selection of tumour blocks containing areas with more cohesive epithelioid-like cells may be more promising in yielding positive results on keratin immunohistochemistry. 【39】Previously referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma, the WHO classification of breast tumours in 2012 revised the terminology to a more “neutral” term, periductal stromal “tumour”, avoiding the connotation of malignancy with “sarcoma”, as the biological behaviour of this rarely diagnosed lesion remains uncertain. 【41】页码间删除-1:<u>### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations</u>

【42】Benign phyllodes tumours can recur locally, while malignant tumours are at higher risk of local recurrence and can metastasise. Borderline tumours tend to also locally recur and may rarely metastasise. Recurrence rates for benign, borderline, and malignant phyllodes tumours are 10 %–17 %, 20 %–25 %, and 23 %–27 %, respectively. Malignant tumours may metastasise and cause death in about 22 % of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>.

【43】Prognostication based on grading has challenges. Each microscopic parameter has several tiers of assessment, resulting in a significant number of permutations that confound accuracy and precision. While grading at extreme ends of the spectrum of phyllodes tumours is reliable, tumours in between are subject to interobserver variability due to challenges in applying the specified histologic criteria. A nomogram based on weighted parameters (AMOS criteria—stromal atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, surgical margins) attempts to circumvent the difficulties of conventional grading to allow individualised risk categorisation for patients diagnosed with phyllodes tumours  通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 – 13 \]</u>.

Although there is an approach for complete excision with negative margins for phyllodes tumours of all grades, there is some evidence to suggest that benign tumours that have been enucleated without ensuring negative margins may be expectantly followed, with complete excision if there is recurrence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>. 【42】Benign phyllodes tumours can recur locally, while malignant tumours are at higher risk of local recurrence and can metastasise. 【29】#### Malignant Phyllodes Tumour with Sarcomatous Stromal Overgrowth, Spindle Cell Metaplastic Carcinoma, and Primary Breast Sarcoma

【30】Stromal overgrowth of a malignant phyllodes tumour can resemble a spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma  or primary breast sarcoma , particularly when the typical phyllodal fronded architecture is effaced. Apart from diligent sampling of these tumours to locate the characteristic leaf-like pattern of phyllodes tumour or conventional carcinoma component of spindle cell carcinoma, firm diagnoses usually require immunohistochemistry. The presence of diffuse p63 and keratin staining of spindle cells indicates a metaplastic carcinoma. It is important to note, however, that phyllodes tumours may manifest focal keratin staining of stromal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>, and p63 reactivity has recently been described in stromal cells of malignant phyllodes tumours 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Conversely, some metaplastic carcinomas may disclose heterogeneity in keratin positivity. More than one block may sometimes need to be submitted for immunohistochemical interrogation. Selection of tumour blocks containing areas with more cohesive epithelioid-like cells may be more promising in yielding positive results on keratin immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis of primary breast sarcoma is one of exclusion, after phyllodes tumour and metaplastic carcinoma have been ruled out. Table 3.4 shows features that may help distinguish these tumours.

【29】#### Malignant Phyllodes Tumour with Sarcomatous Stromal Overgrowth, Spindle Cell Metaplastic Carcinoma, and Primary Breast Sarcoma

【30】Stromal overgrowth of a malignant phyllodes tumour can resemble a spindle cell metaplastic carcinoma  or primary breast sarcoma , particularly when the typical phyllodal fronded architecture is effaced. Apart from diligent sampling of these tumours to locate the characteristic leaf-like pattern of phyllodes tumour or conventional carcinoma component of spindle cell carcinoma, firm diagnoses usually require immunohistochemistry. The presence of diffuse p63 and keratin staining of spindle cells indicates a metaplastic carcinoma. It is important to note, however, that phyllodes tumours may manifest focal keratin staining of stromal cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>, and p63 reactivity has recently been described in stromal cells of malignant phyllodes tumours 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>. Conversely, some metaplastic carcinomas may disclose heterogeneity in keratin positivity. More than one block may sometimes need to be submitted for immunohistochemical interrogation. Selection of tumour blocks containing areas with more cohesive epithelioid-like cells may be more promising in yielding positive results on keratin immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis of primary breast sarcoma is one of exclusion, after phyllodes tumour and metaplastic carcinoma have been ruled out. Table 3.4 shows features that may help distinguish these tumours.

【39】Previously referred to as periductal stromal sarcoma, the WHO classification of breast tumours in 2012 revised the terminology to a more “neutral” term, periductal stromal “tumour”, avoiding the connotation of malignancy with “sarcoma”, as the biological behaviour of this rarely diagnosed lesion remains uncertain. Instead of the presence of well-formed stromal fronds capped by benign epithelium, the periductal stromal tumour consists of hypercellular collections of spindle cells present around pre-existing ducts and terminal ductal lobular units . Some of these tumours progress to conventional phyllodes tumours, and they are therefore currently classified under the rubric of phyllodal neoplasms.

【42】Benign phyllodes tumours can recur locally, while malignant tumours are at higher risk of local recurrence and can metastasise. Borderline tumours tend to also locally recur and may rarely metastasise. Recurrence rates for benign, borderline, and malignant phyllodes tumours are 10 %–17 %, 20 %–25 %, and 23 %–27 %, respectively. Malignant tumours may metastasise and cause death in about 22 % of patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>.

【43】Prognostication based on grading has challenges. Each microscopic parameter has several tiers of assessment, resulting in a significant number of permutations that confound accuracy and precision. While grading at extreme ends of the spectrum of phyllodes tumours is reliable, tumours in between are subject to interobserver variability due to challenges in applying the specified histologic criteria. A nomogram based on weighted parameters (AMOS criteria—stromal atypia, mitoses, overgrowth, surgical margins) attempts to circumvent the difficulties of conventional grading to allow individualised risk categorisation for patients diagnosed with phyllodes tumours  通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 – 13 \]</u>.

Although there is an approach for complete excision with negative margins for phyllodes tumours of all grades, there is some evidence to suggest that benign tumours that have been enucleated without ensuring negative margins may be expectantly followed, with complete excision if there is recurrence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>.
