There is no definite answer， which of the existing memory tests might be the most sensitive and specific ones to look for mild cognitive impairment due to neurodegeneration in middle-aged patients. The ADNI group decided for the Auditory Verbal Learning Test and the story recall (logical memory test) of the Wechsler Memory scale and nothing is wrong with this decision. We use the California Verbal Memory Test (CVLT) and story recall from the Wechsler Memory Test. Story recall is an everyday based memory task and therefore helpful to analyze how far the patient can understand and reproduce verbal information being told to him or her. The CVLT assesses word list learning as the CERAD-NAB. However， not only 10 but 16 words are presented. The CVLT has five learn-ing trials， a short delay free and cued recall test， but also provides informa-tion about long-term delayed free and cued recall (20 minutes delay) and the recognition performance. The higher number of words and the delay allows for detecting mild or even subtle impairments. Moreover， the recognition test incorporates different foils and provokes the production of false positives. Additionally， as a further tests of visuospatial memory， we use paired associate learning for picture drawings at different place to assess middle-aged patients(refer Chapter 2： Alzheimer’s Disease： Neuropathology， Neuropsychological**

【1】Differential Diagnosis and Treatment， on Alzheimer’s disease， why one should use this task in patients with preclinical AD) and we assess the ability to remem-ber a pathway through an imagery town map.

【2】**Although there are population norms for the TMT-A and TMT-B for young- and middle-aged patients， the test is relatively easy for this groups of persons. We therefore use PC-based attention testing to assess such patients. One should look for the ability to divide attention between different sensory sources 删除2:<u>(hearing and seeing targets)</u> and for selective responding. We use the Testbatterie zur Aufmerksamkeitsprifung (TAP) 删除1:<u>(Zimmermann， 1992)</u>， which provides subtests for divided and selective attention. In the divided attention task， a square built up by 4 × 4 points is shown. Small crosses cover seven or eight of the points. During the task these crosses jump irregu-larly to the different points and sometimes four of them are grouped like a small square (covering four adjacent points of the large square). The task is to press the button as soon as four crosses form a such square. At the same time participants hear high and low tones. They also must press the button as soon as two same tones are presented directly in a sequence. The duration of the task is between 4 and 5 minutes. The selective attention task is a variant of the Simon paradigm： the participant must press the left or the right button as soon as an arrow appears pointing in this direction. The arrows appear very shortly on the left and the right side of the screen， thus sometimes pro-ducing a conflict between the side where they are presented and the side where they point to. Accordingly， the test probes selective visuospatial atten-tion and response inhibition.**

【3】**Experienced deficits in attention are state marker for depression， and a lack of self-conscience in one’s own cognitive performance due to depressive mood can motivate the patients to attend a neuropsychological assessment. Subtle deficits in the divided attention have been demonstrated in patients suffering from depression and they seem not to recover even after remission from the mood disorder 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Reppermund et al.， 2007； Reppermund， Ising， Lucae， & Zihl， 2009)</u></u>.**

The copying task of the CERAD-NAB is much too easy for mild impair-ments in visuoconstructive functions. Therefore we use the Block design test|删除0换行|of the Wechsler Intelligence Examination in middle-aged patients. On the other hand， the block design test is hypersensitive for visuospatial perfor-mance and an impairment in this task should only be taken as indication to reproduce the deficit with additional tasks 删除2:<u>(e.g.， copying the Rey-Osterrieth complex figure)</u> and with dorsal visuospatial subtests from the Visual Object and Perception Battery 删除2:<u>(compare the Chapter 3： The Alphasynucleinopathies：Parkinson’s Disease， Lewy Body Dementia， and Multisystem Atrophy， on alpha synucleinopathy on the meaning of these tests：for differential diagnosis)</u>.**

【5】**1.6 Structured and efficient testing presupposes a structured and efficient anamnesis**

**The specific strategy of testing patients for a differential diagnosis should be based on a preliminary idea/suspicion of the patient’s disease (whereby this hypothesis should be reformulated if test results are discrepant). The anam-nesis provides the necessary information to formulate a first hypothesis for the testing strategy(删除2:<u>(Chapter 8：： A Short Guideline forthe Neuropsychological Differential Diagnosis of the Dementias， provides a guideline which information should be looked for after having formulated a first hypothesis for the diagnosis)</u>. For many patients， one will have to go back to the anamnesis more than once or patients and their relatives must be given questionnaires to validate the etiological hypothesis. An anamnesis should start with patients providing a description of their problems (by them-selves). It is important to ask relatives not to intervene during this phase and to wait with comments and additional information until the anamnesis of the patient is finished. After the spontaneous delineation of the problems， that is， the reasons for attending the neuropsychological assessment， the anamnesis should primarily focus on the functions of the autonomous nervous system. This includes problems with swallowing and speaking (hoarseness)， pro-blems with vertigo， incontinence and constipation， erectile dysfunctions， and any sleep issues (duration， depth， and motor unrest such as speaking during sleep， and restless legs). Disorders of the autonomous nervous system， in situations where they cannot be explained by additional diseases， are fre-quently anindicationforrtypicalOTatypical1Parkinson's disease. Incontinence might be a symptom of normal pressure hydrocephalus. Finally|删除0换行|regularly sleeping 10 or more hours a daycan be aa sign of ongoing neurodegeneration.**

【7】**The anamnesis should then focus on walking impairments， experienced falls， and postural instability as well as the use of the hands， handwriting， and any existing tremor. Resting tremor， frequent falls， problems with pos-tural balance， and limited handwriting abilities are frequent problems in idio-pathic and atypical Parkinson’s disease. The third major topic of the anamnesis concerns the senses， that is， deficits in seeing， hearing， smelling， and taste. Hypoacusis (partial loss of hearing ability) is a common problem in elderly individuals which leads to social isolation and may have detrimen-tal effects on cognition. Therefore advising the patient to use hearing aids the whole day might be helpful. Olfactory deficits may be the first signs of a beginning Parkinson’s disease. Furthermore the patient should be asked about his or her appetite as well as possible weight loss since weight loss is common in patientsVwith dementia. In this case， weight lossis usually accompanied by some loss of appetite or of having a regular meal. A signifi-cant weight loss (>8 kg in less than half a year) without any explanation(e.g.， another disease， voluntary reduction of caloric intake) should be han-dled as a warning signal for a possible cancer or tumor growth.**

【8】**The next step of the anamnesis should focus on the cognitive functions of memory， working memory， attention， and language. Patients with subjective memory impairments should always be asked whether they have problems with orientation in new environments (e.g.， when they are on vacation). The anamnesis should also try to determine whether the subjective memory impairment concerns episodic memory (Can you remember things that you heard yesterday?) or working memory (Do you (only) forget what your intention is when you move into the next room?). Working memory pro-blems are uncommon in Alzheimer’s disease； however， patients often con-fuse them with episodic memory problems. To gain a better impression of the problem， one may also ask whether the patients usually remember the forgotten events through recognition， that is， after receiving some cues about the event by relatives or friends. Intact recognition but high forgetfulness biases the diagnostic hypothesis away from AD.**

【9】**Attentional performance should be assessed by differentiating between distractibility and tiredness. Again， excessive tiredness1LsSunusual for Alzheimer’s disease. Falling asleep during the day may be caused by sleep problems (e.g.， sleep apnea) or by cardiovascular diseases. Both are often associated with cognitive problems. If patients stress that they tire quickly， one should also ask if they experience mental slowing when confronted with problems. Mental slowing is a typical problem in patients with white matter lesions (vascular dementia) as well as in patients with Parkinson’s disease.**

**The questions regarding language impairments concern understanding， word finding problems， and reduced drive for verbal communication. It is important to inquire about comprehension and word finding problems|删除0换行|separately and to make sure that the patients report their verbal understand-ing abilities independent of hearing problems. If the patient reports word finding problems，oneshould examine (as with memory impairments) whether this impairment started suddenly， if it is slowly increasing or if it is constant. Another important question is whether it concerns the speaking or the access of the words. Moreover， it is important to look for paraphasia dur-ing the interaction with the patient. Paraphasia may concern the use of a wrong， but semantically related word or producing phonological similar but deviating words. It is important to note which of these possibilities are pres-ent. Another aspect of language is how the patient’s speech sounds： are there any signs of dysarthric speech or reduction in the force of the voice? If the patients are answering only in short sentences， one should also ask if they have lost interest in or reduced their amount of verbal interactions.**

【11】**The last topic of the anamnesis regarding subjectively experienced changes concerns mood. Questioning patients about mood changes should cover aspects such as depressed or euphoric mood， loss of drive， social with-drawal， increased irritability， anxiety and fearfulness， and being driven by unrest. Feeling more dependent on others is typical for patients with AD， whereas social withdrawal and increased irritability in the presence of stran-gers might be an indication of the behavioral variant of frontotemporal dementia. On the other hand， increased short-term irritability and affect labil-ity are symptoms often associated with vascular dementia. If the patient tries to encourage a relative to answer the questions during the anamnesis， the development of the patient’s interpersonal dependency， for example， a recent aversion of being home alone， should be examined.**

【12】**The last part of the anamnesis concerns the medical history. The patient should be asked about any drugs or medications he or she is taking. The meaning of the question has also been introduced above. It is also important to ask if they have already experienced any neurological， psychiatric or psy-chological disorder， or disease during their life. This question should be broadened to include the medical history of the patient’s family as well. There are some kinds of dementia that have a strong genetic component(e.g.， behavioral frontotemporal lobe dementia， early onset Alzheimer’s dis-ease). Finally， whether the patient has been assessed by cranial Computer Tomography or Magnet Resonance Imaging should be established and the results should be requested.**

**After having finished the anamnesis with the patients， the relatives should be asked whether the patient’s answers fit their impressions or whether there are differences. After discussing potential differences between the patients report and that of the relatives， one should explicitly ask whether the patients suffer from motor unrest during night-time dreaming 删除2:<u>(more specifically， whether there are any signs of a“REM sleep behavior disorder”， compare Chapter 3： The Alphasynucleinopathies： Parkinson’s Disease， Lewy Body Dementia， and Multisystem Atrophy， for this disorder)</u>， how long they sleep|删除0换行|during the day， whether there is a change in appetite and how the relatives rate the memory performance. Another important topic concerns the rela-tive’s impression of the patient’s mood and behavior. If there are signs of increased irritability and disinhibition， whether the patient is only aggressive at home or whether the patient is also aggressive and/or show aberrant behavior towards strangers should be determined. Relatives should also fill out questionnaires regarding the instrumental abilities of daily living， the neuropsychiatric inventory and whether the patient moves and speaks during sleep as well as a questionnaire concerning REM sleep behavior disorder. These questionnaires will be discussed later.**

【14】**1.7Summary： Prospect of neuropsychological testing of dementia**

【15】**As worldwide life expectancy raises， the upcoming decades will see a global increase in the number of patients with dementia. This will be accompanied by an enormous medical and psychosocial challenge for the patients， their relatives， and society. The diagnosis of dementia is a syndrome diagnosis and should therefore be based on accepted criteria (e.g.， the ICD-10). The syndrome of dementia can be caused by several diseases which must be dif-ferentiated. Only an etiological classification (e.g.， which is listed in ICD-10) permits a well-founded statement about disease progress and necessary treat-ment. Dementia is a clinical， descriptive diagnosis； it does not necessarily imply a prognostic statement and even if the cause is progressive neurode-generative the long-term course may vary considerably between patients.**

**Effective treatment for dementia relies on precise and early diagnosis because in later stages the neurodegenerative process already caused irrevers-ible atrophy. During later phases of dementia， delaying its progression will be the most important concern. There are currently no specific or clear-cut biomarkers for many types of dementia. Therefore the differential diagnosis relies on the clinical investigation of the patients and on the combination of different information to arrive at the most appropriate diagnosis (“probable”in the case of a combined positive functional and somatic validation and“possible”in the case of only the functional impairments coinciding with the diagnosis). Neuropsychological testing is one method that can assist the dif-ferential diagnosis of dementia at the earliest clinical period of the disease. While screening tests like the MMSE help in determining the severity of the dementia， they do not provide information for a differential diagnosis， or do they detect the first signs of cognitive decline. Moreover， most of the screen-ing tests do not rely heavily enough on age-， gender-， and education-based test norms. Because these variables influence the results of screening tests， these tests do not convey reliable information. Rather， they provide only an estimation of the disease’s progression. Such a rating is important to judge the probable handicaps of the patient in everyday life and to assist the|删除0换行|decision-making process regarding， for example， driving or nursing homes. Neuropsychological testing in patients with suspected dementia therefore has two purposes： predicting the ability to live independently and to offer infor-mation about the possible cause of the impairment (supporting a specific dif-ferential diagnosis). Hopefully in the near future， there will be a third purpose of neuropsychological testing： to inform patients about the best func-tional treatment as well as its optimal level of difficulty 删除2:<u>(the scarce literature concerning neuropsychological rehabilitation in the specific dementias will be discussed at the end of the following chapters)</u>.**

【17】With respect to the purpose of differential diagnosis， Table 1.14 provides an overview of a set of core tests that may be used for a first impression of the cognitive problems. These core tests should be complemented by further tests depending on the etiological hypothesis based on this assessment.

【18】**The CERAD-NAB is a standardized test battery that is based on the results of more than 1100 control subjects 删除1:<u>(Schmid et al.， 2014)</u> and there-fore the use of the CERAD-NAB as a core set of tests is recommended. In theory， a performance below an absolute cut-off score should be indicative of the specific neurodegenerative disease the patient is suffering from. Unfortunately， there seems to be no absolute cut-off scores for any subtest of the CERAD-NAB concerning differential diagnosing.**

【19】**The statement of a possible diagnosis depends on the formulation of assumptions regarding the kind of disease that might be present. Such assumptions depend on the anamnesis， which should encompass questions concerning cognitive deficits as well as autonomous functioning， walking， control of the hands， mood， and previous relevant diseases of the patient and their relatives. Together with the results of the CERAD-NAB and the other tests from the core set， it should be possible to define specific impairment patterns that help to develop a hypothesis for the differential diagnosis. This**

【20】**TABLE 1.14 A proposal for neuropsychological core tests set.**

【21】**hypothesis has to be tested through the assessment of other more specific tests that are sensitive for the specific etiologies of the different types of dementia. Therefore a neuropsychological differential diagnosis must be based on a combination of standard tests and a flexible integration of more specific ones. In the following chapters， we will analyze which additional tests best assist the differential diagnosis of a variety of different dementias.**

【22】**The test core test set defined earlier should be used in patients older than60 years. In younger patients， especially in those that are well-functioning the set of tests might be too easy and therefore not sensitive enough for sub-tle impairments. Consider Section 1.5.6 for a replacement of some of the tests from the core set by others testing younger patients.**

If the patient tries to encourage a relative to answer the questions during the anamnesis， the development of the patient’s interpersonal dependency， for example， a recent aversion of being home alone， should be examined.**

【12】**The last part of the anamnesis concerns the medical history. The patient should be asked about any drugs or medications he or she is taking. The meaning of the question has also been introduced above. It is also important to ask if they have already experienced any neurological， psychiatric or psy-chological disorder， or disease during their life. This question should be broadened to include the medical history of the patient’s family as well. There are some kinds of dementia that have a strong genetic component(e.g.， behavioral frontotemporal lobe dementia， early onset Alzheimer’s dis-ease). Finally， whether the patient has been assessed by cranial Computer Tomography or Magnet Resonance Imaging should be established and the results should be requested.**

**After having finished the anamnesis with the patients， the relatives should be asked whether the patient’s answers fit their impressions or whether there are differences. After discussing potential differences between the patients report and that of the relatives， one should explicitly ask whether the patients suffer from motor unrest during night-time dreaming 删除2:<u>(more specifically， whether there are any signs of a“REM sleep behavior disorder”， compare Chapter 3： The Alphasynucleinopathies： Parkinson’s Disease， Lewy Body Dementia， and Multisystem Atrophy， for this disorder)</u>， how long they sleep|删除0换行|during the day， whether there is a change in appetite and how the relatives rate the memory performance. Another important topic concerns the rela-tive’s impression of the patient’s mood and behavior. If there are signs of increased irritability and disinhibition， whether the patient is only aggressive at home or whether the patient is also aggressive and/or show aberrant behavior towards strangers should be determined. Relatives should also fill out questionnaires regarding the instrumental abilities of daily living， the neuropsychiatric inventory and whether the patient moves and speaks during sleep as well as a questionnaire concerning REM sleep behavior disorder. These questionnaires will be discussed later.**

【14】**1.7Summary： Prospect of neuropsychological testing of dementia**

【15】**As worldwide life expectancy raises， the upcoming decades will see a global increase in the number of patients with dementia. This will be accompanied by an enormous medical and psychosocial challenge for the patients， their relatives， and society. The diagnosis of dementia is a syndrome diagnosis and should therefore be based on accepted criteria (e.g.， the ICD-10). The syndrome of dementia can be caused by several diseases which must be dif-ferentiated. Only an etiological classification (e.g.， which is listed in ICD-10) permits a well-founded statement about disease progress and necessary treat-ment. Dementia is a clinical， descriptive diagnosis； it does not necessarily imply a prognostic statement and even if the cause is progressive neurode-generative the long-term course may vary considerably between patients.**

**Effective treatment for dementia relies on precise and early diagnosis because in later stages the neurodegenerative process already caused irrevers-ible atrophy. During later phases of dementia， delaying its progression will be the most important concern. There are currently no specific or clear-cut biomarkers for many types of dementia. Therefore the differential diagnosis relies on the clinical investigation of the patients and on the combination of different information to arrive at the most appropriate diagnosis (“probable”in the case of a combined positive functional and somatic validation and“possible”in the case of only the functional impairments coinciding with the diagnosis). Neuropsychological testing is one method that can assist the dif-ferential diagnosis of dementia at the earliest clinical period of the disease. While screening tests like the MMSE help in determining the severity of the dementia， they do not provide information for a differential diagnosis， or do they detect the first signs of cognitive decline. Moreover， most of the screen-ing tests do not rely heavily enough on age-， gender-， and education-based test norms. Because these variables influence the results of screening tests， these tests do not convey reliable information. Rather， they provide only an estimation of the disease’s progression. Such a rating is important to judge the probable handicaps of the patient in everyday life and to assist the|删除0换行|decision-making process regarding， for example， driving or nursing homes. Neuropsychological testing in patients with suspected dementia therefore has two purposes： predicting the ability to live independently and to offer infor-mation about the possible cause of the impairment (supporting a specific dif-ferential diagnosis). Hopefully in the near future， there will be a third purpose of neuropsychological testing： to inform patients about the best func-tional treatment as well as its optimal level of difficulty 删除2:<u>(the scarce literature concerning neuropsychological rehabilitation in the specific dementias will be discussed at the end of the following chapters)</u>.**

【17】With respect to the purpose of differential diagnosis， Table 1.14 provides an overview of a set of core tests that may be used for a first impression of the cognitive problems. These core tests should be complemented by further tests depending on the etiological hypothesis based on this assessment.

【18】**The CERAD-NAB is a standardized test battery that is based on the results of more than 1100 control subjects 删除1:<u>(Schmid et al.， 2014)</u> and there-fore the use of the CERAD-NAB as a core set of tests is recommended. In theory， a performance below an absolute cut-off score should be indicative of the specific neurodegenerative disease the patient is suffering from. Unfortunately， there seems to be no absolute cut-off scores for any subtest of the CERAD-NAB concerning differential diagnosing.**

【19】**The statement of a possible diagnosis depends on the formulation of assumptions regarding the kind of disease that might be present. Such assumptions depend on the anamnesis， which should encompass questions concerning cognitive deficits as well as autonomous functioning， walking， control of the hands， mood， and previous relevant diseases of the patient and their relatives. Together with the results of the CERAD-NAB and the other tests from the core set， it should be possible to define specific impairment patterns that help to develop a hypothesis for the differential diagnosis. This**

Therefore a neuropsychological differential diagnosis must be based on a combination of standard tests and a flexible integration of more specific ones. In the following chapters， we will analyze which additional tests best assist the differential diagnosis of a variety of different dementias.**

【22】**The test core test set defined earlier should be used in patients older than60 years. In younger patients， especially in those that are well-functioning the set of tests might be too easy and therefore not sensitive enough for sub-tle impairments. Consider Section 1.5.6 for a replacement of some of the tests from the core set by others testing younger patients.**

MAL-PDT is unique in not only demonstrating a high efficacy in the treatment of superficial BCC; it has also been shown to be effective in the treatment of nodular BCC 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 33 \]</u>. Vismodegib, an oral Hedgehog pathway inhibitor, has also been shown to be an important option in the treatment of BCCs. However, the side effects of oral vismodegib, including muscle spasms, hair loss, altered taste sensation, weight loss, fatigue, nausea, decreased appetite, and diarrhea, may not be well tolerated in some patients 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 34 , 35 \]</u>. 【1】While great care is taken to treat BCC’s, prophylactic therapy may be used to prevent growth of new cancers. Given these patients’ high risk for continually developing BCCs, therapy to prevent them can save disfiguring treatments. Acitretin has been shown to reduce the size of clinically apparent skin cancers and may been used as chemoprevention 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 37 \]</u>. While the efficacy of acitretin has been described for squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), the drug may be used for patients with BCNS. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are also used as chemoprevention for SCCs. Oral celecoxib has been shown to be effective in suppression BCCs in both mice and humans with PTCH1 gene mutations 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 38 \]</u>.

【2】For the detection of odontogenic keratocysts, annual dental panoramic X-rays are recommended beginning at the age of eight 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 27 \]</u>. These cysts are typically removed by wide excision/enucleation with curettage but have a high rate of recurrence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 23 , 39 \]</u>. There is some evidence that oral vismodegib is also an important treatment option for keratocysts; however, more studies are needed in patients with BCNS 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 40 \]</u>.

【3】Notably in pediatric patients, surveillance for the development of medulloblastoma and cardiac fibroma is important. An annual cranial MRI is recommended until 8 years of age for the detection of a medulloblastoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 25 \]</u>. For the treatment of a medulloblastoma, radiation therapy should be avoided because it causes multiple BCCs to develop in the field of radiation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 28 \]</u>. To monitor for the presence of a cardiac fibroma, an echocardiogram should be completed in the first year of life. Asymptomatic patients with a cardiac fibroma should be closely followed by a pediatric cardiologist 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 25 \]</u>.

【4】30.6 Conclusion
---------------

【5】Gorlin syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition characterized by countless number of basal cell carcinomas, in combination with various other findings such as odontogenic (jaw) keratocysts and palmar and/or palmar pits, and medulloblastoma. Treatment requires a multidisciplinary approach to monitor the various organ systems involved. Dermatologists play a crucial role not only in treating skin cancers but also in preventing the onset of new malignancies.

【54】Abstract

【55】Muir-Torre syndrome (MTS) is a rare, autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by sebaceous neoplasms, keratoacanthomas, and visceral malignancies 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1, 2\]</u>. MTS is a phenotypic subset of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC) caused by mutations in mismatch repair genes associated with microsatellite instability 通用删除6(英):<u>\[3\]</u>. Due to the increased risk in developing visceral malignancies, it is important that the proper diagnosis to be made as early as possible and family members be evaluated for MTS and its associated cancers.

【56】31.1 Introduction
-----------------

【57】Muir-Torre syndrome (MTS) is a rare, autosomal dominant genodermatosis characterized by sebaceous neoplasms, keratoacanthomas, and visceral malignancies 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 , 2 \]</u>. MTS is a phenotypic subset of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC) caused by mutations in mismatch repair genes associated with microsatellite instability 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>. Due to the increased risk in developing visceral malignancies, it is important that the proper diagnosis to be made as early as possible and family members be evaluated for MTS and its associated cancers.

【58】MTS was first described separately by Muir 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 \]</u> and Torre 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u> in 1967 and 1968, respectively. Muir first reported a patient with a sebaceous adenoma, multiple keratoacanthomas of the face, and multiple carcinomas of the gastrointestinal tract 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 4 \]</u>. Torre described a case of multiple sebaceous neoplasms in a patient with a history of two gastrointestinal malignancies 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 5 \]</u>. The combined name of the syndrome was created in 1982 when Fahmy et al. reported 20 cases with a similar constellation of findings 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 6 \]</u>.

【59】31.2 Background
---------------

【60】MTS is inherited as an autosomal dominant disorder with variable penetrance and expressivity 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>. The syndrome has a slight male predilection, with a male to female ratio of 3:2 and a mean age of 53 (ranging from the 30s to 80s) at the time of diagnosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 7 , 8 \]</u>. A 2004 study reported that more than 200 cases of MTS have been described in the literature since 1982 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 \]</u>. There is limited data on an ethnic or ancestral predisposition to MTS; however, the majority of cases are reported in Caucasian patients residing in the developed world 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 2 \]</u>. MTS is observed in 28 % of families and 9 % of individuals with HNPCC 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 9 \]</u>. The two disorders share similar genetic mechanisms—both are caused by mutations in mismatch repair genes, which produce enzymes involved in maintaining accurate DNA replication in cells 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 10 \]</u>.

【61】MTS is caused by heterozygous germline mutations in one of the following mismatch repair genes: MutS homolog 2 (MSH2), MutL homolog 1 (MLH1), or MutS homolog 6 (MSH6). The mismatch repair mechanism prevents errors in the short, repeat sequences of DNA, called microsatellites. Ninety percent of mutations in MTS occur in MSH2 on chromosome 2 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 11 , 12 \]</u>. Mismatch repair deficiency results from an inherited germline mutation combined with a somatic loss-of-function mutation in the contralateral wild-type allele. Ensuing errors in DNA replication at multiple loci begin to accumulate and are termed microsatellite instability (MSI), which promote tumor formation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 \]</u>.

【62】In HNPCC, approximately 75 % of germline mutations are seen in either MSH2 or MLH1, with the remainder of mutations in MSH6 and postmeiotic segregation increased 2 (PMS2) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 3 , 9 \]</u>. Mutations in MSH2 disrupt the MSH2-MSH6 heterodimer, ultimately causing a lack of expression of the MSH6 protein in both MTS and HNPCC 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 14 \]</u>.

【63】31.3 Clinical Presentation
--------------------------

【64】A diagnosis of MTS is made by the presence of at least one sebaceous gland neoplasm and at least one visceral malignancy, in the absence of any known predisposing factors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 15 \]</u>. While sebaceous adenomas are the most common sebaceous neoplasms found in MTS (68 %), sebaceous carcinomas (30 %), sebaceous epitheliomas (sebaceoma), keratoacanthomas with sebaceous differentiation (seboacanthoma), or basal cell carcinomas with sebaceous differentiation are included in the diagnostic criteria (sebaceous hyperplasia and nevus sebaceous of Jadassohn are excluded) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 13 \]</u>. Alternatively, when no sebaceous tumor is present, a patient can be diagnosed with MTS based on a personal history of multiple keratoacanthomas and visceral malignancies in the setting of a family history of MTS 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 1 , 10 , 16 \]</u>.

【63】人名段删除-1:<u>结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The Case Presentation**</u></u>

【64】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The spoken case presentation is a concise summary of the history and physical examination. Unlike the written ver-sion in a patient’s chart， the oral presentation is dynamic and ranges from a brief summary given by phone to a consultant to a more formal presentation to a large medical audience at an academic session. Succinctness and organization are espe-cially important， as the presenter has neither the luxury of omitting important details nor time for repetition. Brevity is of paramount importance； simply reading from a chart defeats the purpose of the exercise. Highlighted in this chapter are the essential components of the presentation： the chief com-plaint， the history of present illness (HPI)， the past medical history， the family and social history， the review of systems， and finally， the physical examination findings.</u>

【65】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The chief complaint should be as directed and short as possible， articulating the principal subject under consideration. Invariably， there is one overriding problem in the majority of patients， and a listener is helped enormously by its identifica-tion immediately， allowing focus. Indeed， from the first words of a presentation， a listener is formulating possible diagnoses. A lengthy chief complaint including details of past history serves only to confuse and lengthens the presentation-a car-dinal sin. The patient’s own words need be mentioned only if they illuminate the problem under consideration. The source is always assumed to be the patient， and its content accurate； if considered otherwise by the presenter， this qualification must be made clear. The patient is best identified as a man or woman， which are more respectful designations than male or female. Mentioning the patient’s occupation is often helpful medically and certainly socially， because a listener is likely to examine the patient shortly after the presentation.</u>

【66】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The HPI is the most important part of the exercise. If the problem is not understood at the conclusion of a properly pre-sented HPI， it is unlikely to be understood after extensive fur-ther evaluation. Instead of calendar dates， the duration of time prior to the episode of care should be specified. Calendar dates require a listener to remember the current date and subtract backwards to determine the duration of a problem， an unnec-essary distraction.**</u>

【67】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The initial step in organizing the HPI is to identify the logical parts of the present illness. For example， beginning the HPI with a chronic history of hypercholesterolemia is sensi-ble in a middle-aged man with chest pain. Thereafter， events should be given chronologically， up to the present moment.</u>

【68】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Many presentations are confusing because they include recen information first， followed by previous but relevant data Instead， the HPI should be related like a story， with a begin-ning and an end. Again， the value to a listener is significant.</u>

【69】结尾批量删除-1:<u>What about the inclusion of pertinent negative historical information in the HPI? Presenting negative data is unneces-sary when positives tell the whole story. However， negative data become extremely important in narrowing the differen-tial diagnosis when the positive information leaves the listener uncertain. For example， a 27-year-old woman with erushing substernal chest pain that radiates to both arms and is associ-ated with a sense of impending doom sparks the interest of the listener； the differential diagnosis includes psychiatric. cardiovascular， gastrointestinal， and drug-induced causes. In this case， presenting the absence of symptoms referable to those symptoms helps the listener focus his or her differential diagnosis.</u>

【70】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The past medical history， although a crucial componen of the patient’s written record， adds little to the presentation If a historical fact is deemed relevant， it likely belongs in the HPI， and some past history may be eliminated entirely in the interest of time. The same is true for the family history； a lengthy pedigree often serves no function， and if important family history is best consigned to the HPI.</u>

【71】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Presenting the social history is always important and is a humanizing endeavor as well. Statements such as “the social history was noncontributory” diminish the practice of medi-cine by rendering patients pathophysiologic specimens rather than human beings. In addition， such knowledge may facili-tate the doctor-patient interaction. Although medications and habits are often included at this point， such items may be more relevant in the HPI.</u>

【72】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The review of systems should be as brief as possible containing only those symptoms felt to be significant enough to merit further investigation. Including numerous positive responses by well-meaning patients only dilutes the signif-cance of truly important symptoms.</u>

【73】结尾批量删除-1:<u>It is of utmost importance that in the spoken presentatior information not be repeated. The presenter decides where a fact best belongs， and its repetition will only consume time.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>Although the physical examination is beyond the scope of this book， a few suggestions are in order. It is best delivered in simple declarative sentences. Qualifiers such as remarkable and unremarkable， although widespread in medical parlance，|删除0换行|are cliches that do not assist the listener. A complete examina-tion can be presented in less than 1 minute， and a brief men-tion of each system tells the listener that they all have been examined. For instance，“the chest was clear” is an entirely appropriate elucidation of the pulmonary examination in a patient whose symptoms do not suggest lung disease. All positive findings， expected or not， are given； whereas negative data focus on signs logically expected by a listener.“There were no spider angiomata" in the patient with liver disease tells the listener that the examiner sought them. Announcing the system being presented (for example， “chest-he had no wheezes， rales， or rhonchi") is unnecessary because the lis-tener should know what part of the body is being described.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Although laboratory or other diagnostic tests， problem lists， and the assessment are also not the focus of this book，|删除0换行|a few points are pertinent. Specific laboratory data presented depend on the setting， such as a hospital or clinic， and the nature of the patient’s symptoms or clinical problem. Some listeners prefer that the presentation be concluded with a brief case synthesis， but a lengthy assessment and plan are bette placed in the written record. Once again， the issue is time， and it is well known that the captive audience attention span rarely exceeds 7 minutes.</u>

【76】结尾批量删除-1:<u>In summary， the best oral presentation resembles a narra tive， given chronologically and delivered in language similai to routine conversation. The ability to articulate a crisp， clear presentation requires practice and skill. It is a dying art， bu not one that cannot be rekindled.</u>

【63】人名段删除-1:<u>结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The Case Presentation**</u></u>

【64】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The spoken case presentation is a concise summary of the history and physical examination. Unlike the written ver-sion in a patient’s chart， the oral presentation is dynamic and ranges from a brief summary given by phone to a consultant to a more formal presentation to a large medical audience at an academic session. Succinctness and organization are espe-cially important， as the presenter has neither the luxury of omitting important details nor time for repetition. Brevity is of paramount importance； simply reading from a chart defeats the purpose of the exercise. Highlighted in this chapter are the essential components of the presentation： the chief com-plaint， the history of present illness (HPI)， the past medical history， the family and social history， the review of systems， and finally， the physical examination findings.</u>

【65】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The chief complaint should be as directed and short as possible， articulating the principal subject under consideration. Invariably， there is one overriding problem in the majority of patients， and a listener is helped enormously by its identifica-tion immediately， allowing focus. Indeed， from the first words of a presentation， a listener is formulating possible diagnoses. A lengthy chief complaint including details of past history serves only to confuse and lengthens the presentation-a car-dinal sin. The patient’s own words need be mentioned only if they illuminate the problem under consideration. The source is always assumed to be the patient， and its content accurate； if considered otherwise by the presenter， this qualification must be made clear. The patient is best identified as a man or woman， which are more respectful designations than male or female. Mentioning the patient’s occupation is often helpful medically and certainly socially， because a listener is likely to examine the patient shortly after the presentation.</u>

【66】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The HPI is the most important part of the exercise. If the problem is not understood at the conclusion of a properly pre-sented HPI， it is unlikely to be understood after extensive fur-ther evaluation. Instead of calendar dates， the duration of time prior to the episode of care should be specified. Calendar dates require a listener to remember the current date and subtract backwards to determine the duration of a problem， an unnec-essary distraction.**</u>

【67】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The initial step in organizing the HPI is to identify the logical parts of the present illness. For example， beginning the HPI with a chronic history of hypercholesterolemia is sensi-ble in a middle-aged man with chest pain. Thereafter， events should be given chronologically， up to the present moment.</u>

【68】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Many presentations are confusing because they include recen information first， followed by previous but relevant data Instead， the HPI should be related like a story， with a begin-ning and an end. Again， the value to a listener is significant.</u>

【69】结尾批量删除-1:<u>What about the inclusion of pertinent negative historical information in the HPI? Presenting negative data is unneces-sary when positives tell the whole story. However， negative data become extremely important in narrowing the differen-tial diagnosis when the positive information leaves the listener uncertain. For example， a 27-year-old woman with erushing substernal chest pain that radiates to both arms and is associ-ated with a sense of impending doom sparks the interest of the listener； the differential diagnosis includes psychiatric. cardiovascular， gastrointestinal， and drug-induced causes. In this case， presenting the absence of symptoms referable to those symptoms helps the listener focus his or her differential diagnosis.</u>

【70】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The past medical history， although a crucial componen of the patient’s written record， adds little to the presentation If a historical fact is deemed relevant， it likely belongs in the HPI， and some past history may be eliminated entirely in the interest of time. The same is true for the family history； a lengthy pedigree often serves no function， and if important family history is best consigned to the HPI.</u>

【71】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Presenting the social history is always important and is a humanizing endeavor as well. Statements such as “the social history was noncontributory” diminish the practice of medi-cine by rendering patients pathophysiologic specimens rather than human beings. In addition， such knowledge may facili-tate the doctor-patient interaction. Although medications and habits are often included at this point， such items may be more relevant in the HPI.</u>

【72】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The review of systems should be as brief as possible containing only those symptoms felt to be significant enough to merit further investigation. Including numerous positive responses by well-meaning patients only dilutes the signif-cance of truly important symptoms.</u>

【73】结尾批量删除-1:<u>It is of utmost importance that in the spoken presentatior information not be repeated. The presenter decides where a fact best belongs， and its repetition will only consume time.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>Although the physical examination is beyond the scope of this book， a few suggestions are in order. It is best delivered in simple declarative sentences. Qualifiers such as remarkable and unremarkable， although widespread in medical parlance，|删除0换行|are cliches that do not assist the listener. A complete examina-tion can be presented in less than 1 minute， and a brief men-tion of each system tells the listener that they all have been examined. For instance，“the chest was clear” is an entirely appropriate elucidation of the pulmonary examination in a patient whose symptoms do not suggest lung disease. All positive findings， expected or not， are given； whereas negative data focus on signs logically expected by a listener.“There were no spider angiomata" in the patient with liver disease tells the listener that the examiner sought them. Announcing the system being presented (for example， “chest-he had no wheezes， rales， or rhonchi") is unnecessary because the lis-tener should know what part of the body is being described.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Although laboratory or other diagnostic tests， problem lists， and the assessment are also not the focus of this book，|删除0换行|a few points are pertinent. Specific laboratory data presented depend on the setting， such as a hospital or clinic， and the nature of the patient’s symptoms or clinical problem. Some listeners prefer that the presentation be concluded with a brief case synthesis， but a lengthy assessment and plan are bette placed in the written record. Once again， the issue is time， and it is well known that the captive audience attention span rarely exceeds 7 minutes.</u>

【76】结尾批量删除-1:<u>In summary， the best oral presentation resembles a narra tive， given chronologically and delivered in language similai to routine conversation. The ability to articulate a crisp， clear presentation requires practice and skill. It is a dying art， bu not one that cannot be rekindled.</u>

Skipping over the question would miss important clinical information， and demanding an answer would alienate the patient and prevent further discussion.**</u>

【63】人名段删除-1:<u>结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The Case Presentation**</u></u>

【64】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The spoken case presentation is a concise summary of the history and physical examination. Unlike the written ver-sion in a patient’s chart， the oral presentation is dynamic and ranges from a brief summary given by phone to a consultant to a more formal presentation to a large medical audience at an academic session. Succinctness and organization are espe-cially important， as the presenter has neither the luxury of omitting important details nor time for repetition. Brevity is of paramount importance； simply reading from a chart defeats the purpose of the exercise. Highlighted in this chapter are the essential components of the presentation： the chief com-plaint， the history of present illness (HPI)， the past medical history， the family and social history， the review of systems， and finally， the physical examination findings.</u>

【65】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The chief complaint should be as directed and short as possible， articulating the principal subject under consideration. Invariably， there is one overriding problem in the majority of patients， and a listener is helped enormously by its identifica-tion immediately， allowing focus. Indeed， from the first words of a presentation， a listener is formulating possible diagnoses. A lengthy chief complaint including details of past history serves only to confuse and lengthens the presentation-a car-dinal sin. The patient’s own words need be mentioned only if they illuminate the problem under consideration. The source is always assumed to be the patient， and its content accurate； if considered otherwise by the presenter， this qualification must be made clear. The patient is best identified as a man or woman， which are more respectful designations than male or female. Mentioning the patient’s occupation is often helpful medically and certainly socially， because a listener is likely to examine the patient shortly after the presentation.</u>

【66】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The HPI is the most important part of the exercise. If the problem is not understood at the conclusion of a properly pre-sented HPI， it is unlikely to be understood after extensive fur-ther evaluation. Instead of calendar dates， the duration of time prior to the episode of care should be specified. Calendar dates require a listener to remember the current date and subtract backwards to determine the duration of a problem， an unnec-essary distraction.**</u>

【67】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The initial step in organizing the HPI is to identify the logical parts of the present illness. For example， beginning the HPI with a chronic history of hypercholesterolemia is sensi-ble in a middle-aged man with chest pain. Thereafter， events should be given chronologically， up to the present moment.</u>

【68】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Many presentations are confusing because they include recen information first， followed by previous but relevant data Instead， the HPI should be related like a story， with a begin-ning and an end. Again， the value to a listener is significant.</u>

【69】结尾批量删除-1:<u>What about the inclusion of pertinent negative historical information in the HPI? Presenting negative data is unneces-sary when positives tell the whole story. However， negative data become extremely important in narrowing the differen-tial diagnosis when the positive information leaves the listener uncertain. For example， a 27-year-old woman with erushing substernal chest pain that radiates to both arms and is associ-ated with a sense of impending doom sparks the interest of the listener； the differential diagnosis includes psychiatric. cardiovascular， gastrointestinal， and drug-induced causes. In this case， presenting the absence of symptoms referable to those symptoms helps the listener focus his or her differential diagnosis.</u>

【70】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The past medical history， although a crucial componen of the patient’s written record， adds little to the presentation If a historical fact is deemed relevant， it likely belongs in the HPI， and some past history may be eliminated entirely in the interest of time. The same is true for the family history； a lengthy pedigree often serves no function， and if important family history is best consigned to the HPI.</u>

【71】结尾批量删除-1:<u>Presenting the social history is always important and is a humanizing endeavor as well. Statements such as “the social history was noncontributory” diminish the practice of medi-cine by rendering patients pathophysiologic specimens rather than human beings. In addition， such knowledge may facili-tate the doctor-patient interaction. Although medications and habits are often included at this point， such items may be more relevant in the HPI.</u>

【72】结尾批量删除-1:<u>The review of systems should be as brief as possible containing only those symptoms felt to be significant enough to merit further investigation. Including numerous positive responses by well-meaning patients only dilutes the signif-cance of truly important symptoms.</u>

【73】结尾批量删除-1:<u>It is of utmost importance that in the spoken presentatior information not be repeated. The presenter decides where a fact best belongs， and its repetition will only consume time.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>Although the physical examination is beyond the scope of this book， a few suggestions are in order. It is best delivered in simple declarative sentences. Qualifiers such as remarkable and unremarkable， although widespread in medical parlance，|删除0换行|are cliches that do not assist the listener. A complete examina-tion can be presented in less than 1 minute， and a brief men-tion of each system tells the listener that they all have been examined. For instance，“the chest was clear” is an entirely appropriate elucidation of the pulmonary examination in a patient whose symptoms do not suggest lung disease. All positive findings， expected or not， are given； whereas negative data focus on signs logically expected by a listener.“There were no spider angiomata" in the patient with liver disease tells the listener that the examiner sought them. Announcing the system being presented (for example， “chest-he had no wheezes， rales， or rhonchi") is unnecessary because the lis-tener should know what part of the body is being described.</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Although laboratory or other diagnostic tests， problem lists， and the assessment are also not the focus of this book，|删除0换行|a few points are pertinent. Specific laboratory data presented depend on the setting， such as a hospital or clinic， and the nature of the patient’s symptoms or clinical problem. Some listeners prefer that the presentation be concluded with a brief case synthesis， but a lengthy assessment and plan are bette placed in the written record. Once again， the issue is time， and it is well known that the captive audience attention span rarely exceeds 7 minutes.</u>

【76】结尾批量删除-1:<u>In summary， the best oral presentation resembles a narra tive， given chronologically and delivered in language similai to routine conversation. The ability to articulate a crisp， clear presentation requires practice and skill. It is a dying art， bu not one that cannot be rekindled.</u>

【7】ANTHOGRANULOMAS _2_ andreticulohistiocytic granulomas share several histopathologic features， namely， relative circum-scription by collarettes of adnexal epithelium， dense， diffuse， predominantly histiocytic infiltrates， mononucleated and multinucleated histiocytic giant cells， and resolution with fibrosis. These similarities not only pose problems in histopathologic differential diagnosis， but they prompt reflection about the possibility that the two seemingly different conditions actually might be related closely or even the same disease.

【8】**Clinically， xanthogranulomas are papules or nodules with a yellow， orange， or tan hue. The color results from abundant lipid within histiocytes that comprise the lesion. The condition is better termed xanthogranuloma than nevoxanthoendothelioma， the former designation， which implies in-correctly that it is a nevus partly related to blood vessels.**

【9】**Although xanthogranulomas may occur at any age， they are more com-mon in infants and young children. In youngsters， they tend to be numer-ous， to favor the face， and to involve organs besides the skin， such as an eye and the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts. Hemorrhage from xan-thogranuloma into the anterior chamber of an iris may lead to permanent blindness. The skin lesions of juvenile xanthogranuloma tend to resolve in months without treatment. The clinical differential diagnosis of many le-sions of juvenile xanthogranuloma is nodular lesions of urticaria pigmen-tosa. Morphologically， they may be indistinguishable， but the lesions consti-tuted of mast cells urticate when they are rubbed， a phenomenon known as Darier’s sign. A solitary lesion of juvenile xanthogranuloma may be confused clinically with a Spitz’s nevus. Each may be an orange， smooth-surfaced papule. In contrast to the juvenile form， xanthogranulomas in adults almost always are solitary， do not involve organs other than the skin， and generally do not resolve without treatment. No abnormalities of serum lipids are found in either children or adults who bear xanthogranulomas.**

【10】**One histopathologic presentation of a solitary nodule of xan-thogranuloma in adults may be misinterpreted as a malignant neoplasm because it is characterized by a dense diffuse infiltrate of cells that extends throughout the reticular dermis and sometimes far into the subcutaneous fat. Some of the cells may have atypical nuclei and many of the nuclei are in mitosis. A clue to the true xanthogranulomatous nature of such an infiltrate is found， sometimes with difficulty， in the form of slightly foamy cells situ-ated often at the periphery of a lesion.**

**Reticulohistiocytic granuloma may present itself as a single lesion or as widespread ones(multicentric reticulohistiocytosis). _·_ Bothformsof|删除0换行|reticulohistiocytic granuloma occur entirely in adults， and they exhibit simi-lar histopathologic findings. Persons with multicentric reticulohistiocytosis are reputed to have an increased incidence of internal malignancies， espe-cially of carcinomas.**

【12】A solitary reticulohistiocytic granuloma typically is a dome-shaped nodule positioned on a face or scalp. Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis also consists of dome-shaped nodules， and they tend to affect the face and hands. Polyarthritis of variable severity is a common accompaniment of the widespread form of reticulohistiocylic granuloma (interestingly named lipoid dermatoarthritis). Sections of biopsy specimens from the involved joints show the same kind of infiltrate as that contained in skin lesions.

【13】The material that gives cytoplasm of reticulohistiocytic granuloma a ground glass”appearance is PAS-positive and diastase-resistant， an indica-tion that it is a neutral mucosubstance， probably a glycolipid.

【14】**Lesions of histiocytosis X are differentiated by conventional microscopy from those of xanthogranulomas and reticulohistiocytic granuloma by their cells with large kidney-shaped nuclei and， by electron microscopy， by their many Langerhaniss’’ granules within abundant cytoplasm of cells that house reniform nuclei.**

【15】**Touton giant cells are not specific for xanthogranulomas. They may be seen in other xanthomas and， commonly， in the histiocytic stage of evolving dermatofibromas. Furthermore， Touton cells are not a sine qua non for diagnosis of xanthogranuloma； foamy histiocytes (no matter how slightly vascuolated) are. Evolving xanthogranulomas may have no Touton cells.**

【16】**In sum， one reason the list of differentiating findings at the outset of this chapter is so short is that， in reality， reticulohistiocytic granuloma may be a xanthogranuloma. Features such as “ground glass cytoplasm”and“Touton giant cells，"reputed to be differentiating， in actuality， may be irrel- _evant._**

【7】ANTHOGRANULOMAS _2_ andreticulohistiocytic granulomas share several histopathologic features， namely， relative circum-scription by collarettes of adnexal epithelium， dense， diffuse， predominantly histiocytic infiltrates， mononucleated and multinucleated histiocytic giant cells， and resolution with fibrosis. These similarities not only pose problems in histopathologic differential diagnosis， but they prompt reflection about the possibility that the two seemingly different conditions actually might be related closely or even the same disease.

【8】**Clinically， xanthogranulomas are papules or nodules with a yellow， orange， or tan hue. The color results from abundant lipid within histiocytes that comprise the lesion. The condition is better termed xanthogranuloma than nevoxanthoendothelioma， the former designation， which implies in-correctly that it is a nevus partly related to blood vessels.**

【9】**Although xanthogranulomas may occur at any age， they are more com-mon in infants and young children. In youngsters， they tend to be numer-ous， to favor the face， and to involve organs besides the skin， such as an eye and the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts. Hemorrhage from xan-thogranuloma into the anterior chamber of an iris may lead to permanent blindness. The skin lesions of juvenile xanthogranuloma tend to resolve in months without treatment. The clinical differential diagnosis of many le-sions of juvenile xanthogranuloma is nodular lesions of urticaria pigmen-tosa. Morphologically， they may be indistinguishable， but the lesions consti-tuted of mast cells urticate when they are rubbed， a phenomenon known as Darier’s sign. A solitary lesion of juvenile xanthogranuloma may be confused clinically with a Spitz’s nevus. Each may be an orange， smooth-surfaced papule. In contrast to the juvenile form， xanthogranulomas in adults almost always are solitary， do not involve organs other than the skin， and generally do not resolve without treatment. No abnormalities of serum lipids are found in either children or adults who bear xanthogranulomas.**

【10】**One histopathologic presentation of a solitary nodule of xan-thogranuloma in adults may be misinterpreted as a malignant neoplasm because it is characterized by a dense diffuse infiltrate of cells that extends throughout the reticular dermis and sometimes far into the subcutaneous fat. Some of the cells may have atypical nuclei and many of the nuclei are in mitosis. A clue to the true xanthogranulomatous nature of such an infiltrate is found， sometimes with difficulty， in the form of slightly foamy cells situ-ated often at the periphery of a lesion.**

Persons with multicentric reticulohistiocytosis are reputed to have an increased incidence of internal malignancies， espe-cially of carcinomas.**

Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis also consists of dome-shaped nodules， and they tend to affect the face and hands. Polyarthritis of variable severity is a common accompaniment of the widespread form of reticulohistiocylic granuloma (interestingly named lipoid dermatoarthritis). Sections of biopsy specimens from the involved joints show the same kind of infiltrate as that contained in skin lesions.

【14】**Lesions of histiocytosis X are differentiated by conventional microscopy from those of xanthogranulomas and reticulohistiocytic granuloma by their cells with large kidney-shaped nuclei and， by electron microscopy， by their many Langerhaniss’’ granules within abundant cytoplasm of cells that house reniform nuclei.**

【61】ERMATOFIBROMA and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans are lesions comprised of dense diffuse infiltrates of mostly oval-shaped cells that tend to occupy at least much of the thickness of the dermis. Their nuclei are not atypical as a rule， and mitotic figures are few or absent. Despite the histopathologic features in common， dermatofibroma and der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans are confused with one another mostly be-cause their names sound so much alike and because general pathologists persist in designating dermatofibroma a tumor， i.e.， a neoplasm， rather than the inflammatory process that it actually is.

【62】Clinically， dermatofibromas appear as firm， brown， hairless papules and nodules on the extremities， especially the lower ones. They arise second-ary to trauma， often in the form of puncture wounds and arthropod (espe-cially mosquito) bites， but sometimes secondary to ruptured follicles or follicular cysts. Therefore， the term dermatofibrosis describes the lesion more aptly， conveying that it is a type of fibrosing dermatitis， rather than a neoplasm of fibrocytes.

【63】Many synonyms have been given to dermatofibroma， depending upon clinical and histopathologic nuances and the stage in the pathologic process at which it was sampled by biopsy. Nodulus cutaneous expresses the nodu-larity seen clinically. Fibroma durum describes the hardness of some le-sions. During the relatively early granulation tissue phase of its develop-ment， blood vessels are prominent， thus earning the appellation sclerosing mei 1 vessels are hemangioma. Later， secondary to extravasation of erythrocytes， histiocytes ingest hemosiderin and lipid， and therefore the term histiocytoma is em-ployed. When both histiocytes and fibrocytes are numerous， the lesion sometimes is called a fibrous histiocytoma. To very old lesions in which fibrocytes are decreased in number and bundles of collagen have a homoge-neous appearance， the name subepidermal nodular fibrosis (sclerosis) has been applied. Irrespective of histopathologic variation， dermatofibromas behave like a fibrosing inflammatory process， i.e.， they regress slowly in time， leaving a macular hypopigmented center and hyperpigmented rim as residuum.

By contrast， dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans begins clinically as a skin-colored， slightly yellowish or pink macule or patch that， in time， be-comes an indurated plaque upon which firm papules， nodules， and tumors arise eventually. The lesion occurs predominantly on the trunk and proximal portions of the extremities， but may appear on other sites such as the face. Even though dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is slow-growing， it may extend deep into the subcutaneous fat and beyond it into skeletal muscle|删除0换行|and fascia， but metastases rarely occur and then hardly ever beyond re-gional lymph nodes.

【65】The exact nosologic status of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is not yet established with certainty. Some authors contend that it is a fibrocytic neoplasm， whereas others argue that it is a neural one. The presence of melanocytes within some lesions of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， the fibrillary bundles of collagen， the S-shaped and wavy nuclei， and the abun-dance often of acid mucosubstances indicate that it may be a neoplasm of perineural fibrocytes.

【66】**he limited usefulness of the terms “benign”and“malignant”in the description of cutaneous neoplasms is well illustrated in the case of der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans. Is the neoplasm benign or malignant? If by malignant one meanshavingthe potential for metastasis， thender-matofibrosarcoma protuberans is malignant. But dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， like basal-cell carcinoma， metastasizes rarely， tending instead to persist at a local site following repeated attempts at extirpation of it. In fact， most lesions of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， like most basal-cell carcinomas， are not threatening to the lives of patients. Nonetheless， they should be removed completely during the first procedure that is designed to do that. In order to accomplish that desideratum it is necessary for a sur-geon to carry an excision considerably beyond what are thought clinically to be the lateral and deep margins of the neoplasm. If less than that is done， dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans doubtlessly willpersist at the local site because some neoplastic cells are left behind during the original procedure.“Wide and deep excision” has no value for primary cutaneous malignant melanoma； only enough skin to ensure that that malignant neoplasm has been removed completely is requisite. 【61】ERMATOFIBROMA and dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans are lesions comprised of dense diffuse infiltrates of mostly oval-shaped cells that tend to occupy at least much of the thickness of the dermis. Their nuclei are not atypical as a rule， and mitotic figures are few or absent. Despite the histopathologic features in common， dermatofibroma and der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans are confused with one another mostly be-cause their names sound so much alike and because general pathologists persist in designating dermatofibroma a tumor， i.e.， a neoplasm， rather than the inflammatory process that it actually is.

【62】Clinically， dermatofibromas appear as firm， brown， hairless papules and nodules on the extremities， especially the lower ones. They arise second-ary to trauma， often in the form of puncture wounds and arthropod (espe-cially mosquito) bites， but sometimes secondary to ruptured follicles or follicular cysts. Therefore， the term dermatofibrosis describes the lesion more aptly， conveying that it is a type of fibrosing dermatitis， rather than a neoplasm of fibrocytes.

【63】Many synonyms have been given to dermatofibroma， depending upon clinical and histopathologic nuances and the stage in the pathologic process at which it was sampled by biopsy. Nodulus cutaneous expresses the nodu-larity seen clinically. Fibroma durum describes the hardness of some le-sions. During the relatively early granulation tissue phase of its develop-ment， blood vessels are prominent， thus earning the appellation sclerosing mei 1 vessels are hemangioma. Later， secondary to extravasation of erythrocytes， histiocytes ingest hemosiderin and lipid， and therefore the term histiocytoma is em-ployed. When both histiocytes and fibrocytes are numerous， the lesion sometimes is called a fibrous histiocytoma. To very old lesions in which fibrocytes are decreased in number and bundles of collagen have a homoge-neous appearance， the name subepidermal nodular fibrosis (sclerosis) has been applied. Irrespective of histopathologic variation， dermatofibromas behave like a fibrosing inflammatory process， i.e.， they regress slowly in time， leaving a macular hypopigmented center and hyperpigmented rim as residuum.

By contrast， dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans begins clinically as a skin-colored， slightly yellowish or pink macule or patch that， in time， be-comes an indurated plaque upon which firm papules， nodules， and tumors arise eventually. The lesion occurs predominantly on the trunk and proximal portions of the extremities， but may appear on other sites such as the face. Even though dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is slow-growing， it may extend deep into the subcutaneous fat and beyond it into skeletal muscle|删除0换行|and fascia， but metastases rarely occur and then hardly ever beyond re-gional lymph nodes.

【65】The exact nosologic status of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is not yet established with certainty. Some authors contend that it is a fibrocytic neoplasm， whereas others argue that it is a neural one. The presence of melanocytes within some lesions of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， the fibrillary bundles of collagen， the S-shaped and wavy nuclei， and the abun-dance often of acid mucosubstances indicate that it may be a neoplasm of perineural fibrocytes.

【66】**he limited usefulness of the terms “benign”and“malignant”in the description of cutaneous neoplasms is well illustrated in the case of der-matofibrosarcoma protuberans. Is the neoplasm benign or malignant? If by malignant one meanshavingthe potential for metastasis， thender-matofibrosarcoma protuberans is malignant. But dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， like basal-cell carcinoma， metastasizes rarely， tending instead to persist at a local site following repeated attempts at extirpation of it. In fact， most lesions of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans， like most basal-cell carcinomas， are not threatening to the lives of patients. Nonetheless， they should be removed completely during the first procedure that is designed to do that. In order to accomplish that desideratum it is necessary for a sur-geon to carry an excision considerably beyond what are thought clinically to be the lateral and deep margins of the neoplasm. If less than that is done， dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans doubtlessly willpersist at the local site because some neoplastic cells are left behind during the original procedure.“Wide and deep excision” has no value for primary cutaneous malignant melanoma； only enough skin to ensure that that malignant neoplasm has been removed completely is requisite. In contrast， “wide and deep excision” _LS_ Inecessary for dermatofibrosarcomaprotuberans， angiosarcoma of the SCalp， and microcystic adnexal carcinoma， all of which are notorious for persistence at local sites as a consequence of insufficient margins of cxci-sion. Mohs' micrographic surgery is an alternative to generous excisions by scalpel for removal of these recalcitrant neoplasms.**

【90】**ICHEN amnyloidosis and colloid milium both re-sult from deposits of homogeneous material， but of different chemical na-tures， in the upper part of the dermis. In both， fibrocytes are affiliated closely with the deposits of homogeneous material. In fact， it is likely that fibrocytes are responsible for the formation of amyloid in lichen amyloidosis and colloid in colloid milium.**

【91】**Because of the highly characteristic histopathologic features just listed， specialized stains need not be performed routinely to differentiate between amyloid and colloid. When necessary for academic resolution of the issue， Congo red is the most reliable stain for differentiation because it is positive by dichroism for amyloid， and negative for colloid. Crystal violet stain for amyloid is prettier and more dramatic， but less reliable.**

【92】**The clinical lesion of lichen amnyloidosis consists of agminated， discrete， slightly raised， brownish-red translucent papules that often are keratotic. The condition is intensely pruritic and occurs most commonly on the ante-rior aspects of the legs， but in some instances may be widespread. Macular arnyloidosis， as the title implies， begins as flat lesions. In contrast to lichen amyloidosis， macular amyloidosis has a predilection for the interscapular region. The keratotic papules of lichen amyloidosis are consequent not only to progressive accumulations of amyloid in the papillary dermis， but to the effects of persistent rubbingas well. In short， superimposition of lichen simplex chronicus upon macular amyloidosis transforms that condition into lichen amyloidosis. The evidence for that is prominent compact orthokera-tosis and hypergranulosis in virtually all lesions of lichen amyloidosis， signs of persistent， prolonged rubbing. Macular amyloidosis that has not been rubbed， and therefore not thickened by lichen simplex chronicus， remains flat， as it is stereotypically in the interscapular region. A current hypothesis about how amyloid is formed in the upper portion of the dermis in lesions of macular amyloidosis and lichen amyloidosis holds that globules of amyloid derive from necrotic keratinocytes in the epidermis and when those apop-totic bodies are acted upon by fibrocytes， amyloid is the result.**

**Colloid milium consists of discrete， smooth， yellowish， translucent， waxy papules on sun-exposed areas， especially the malar eminences of the face and dorsa of the hands. Sometimes the papules of colloid milium are restricted to the left side of the face and the dorsa of the left hand in persons who spend much of their time driving cars in sunny climates， such as taxi drivers. At first glance， the smooth translucent papules of colloid milium may be misinterpreted as tense vesicles or as "juicy”edematous papules of polymorphous light eruption. Histopathologically， colloid is surrounded|删除0换行|always by copious amounts of solar elastosis， and both of them are stained bluish-gray by hematoxylin and eosin. These findings indicate that colloid and elastotic material are related closely to one another. Amyloid， by con-trast， is not connected to damage by sunlight.**

【94】**Whereas colloid in the skin is found only in colloid milium， amyloid is detected in a variety of circumstances other than in the macular andpapu-lar (lichenoid) forms. For example， amyloid is present around blood vessels in the skin and subcutaneous fat of patients with systemic amyloidosis， in large solitary nodules of nodular amyloidosis and， most commonly， as an incidental finding in a host of inflammatory， hamartomatous， and neoplas-tic conditionsin the skin， especially iinn sseebborrheic keratoses， tricho-epitheliomas， and basal-cellcarcinomas. These are conditions in which individual keratinocytes tend to undergo necrosis.**
