【7】ANTHOGRANULOMAS _2_ andreticulohistiocytic granulomas share several histopathologic features， namely， relative circum-scription by collarettes of adnexal epithelium， dense， diffuse， predominantly histiocytic infiltrates， mononucleated and multinucleated histiocytic giant cells， and resolution with fibrosis. These similarities not only pose problems in histopathologic differential diagnosis， but they prompt reflection about the possibility that the two seemingly different conditions actually might be related closely or even the same disease.

【8】**Clinically， xanthogranulomas are papules or nodules with a yellow， orange， or tan hue. The color results from abundant lipid within histiocytes that comprise the lesion. The condition is better termed xanthogranuloma than nevoxanthoendothelioma， the former designation， which implies in-correctly that it is a nevus partly related to blood vessels.**

【9】**Although xanthogranulomas may occur at any age， they are more com-mon in infants and young children. In youngsters， they tend to be numer-ous， to favor the face， and to involve organs besides the skin， such as an eye and the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts. Hemorrhage from xan-thogranuloma into the anterior chamber of an iris may lead to permanent blindness. The skin lesions of juvenile xanthogranuloma tend to resolve in months without treatment. The clinical differential diagnosis of many le-sions of juvenile xanthogranuloma is nodular lesions of urticaria pigmen-tosa. Morphologically， they may be indistinguishable， but the lesions consti-tuted of mast cells urticate when they are rubbed， a phenomenon known as Darier’s sign. A solitary lesion of juvenile xanthogranuloma may be confused clinically with a Spitz’s nevus. Each may be an orange， smooth-surfaced papule. In contrast to the juvenile form， xanthogranulomas in adults almost always are solitary， do not involve organs other than the skin， and generally do not resolve without treatment. No abnormalities of serum lipids are found in either children or adults who bear xanthogranulomas.**

【10】**One histopathologic presentation of a solitary nodule of xan-thogranuloma in adults may be misinterpreted as a malignant neoplasm because it is characterized by a dense diffuse infiltrate of cells that extends throughout the reticular dermis and sometimes far into the subcutaneous fat. Some of the cells may have atypical nuclei and many of the nuclei are in mitosis. A clue to the true xanthogranulomatous nature of such an infiltrate is found， sometimes with difficulty， in the form of slightly foamy cells situ-ated often at the periphery of a lesion.**

**Reticulohistiocytic granuloma may present itself as a single lesion or as widespread ones(multicentric reticulohistiocytosis). _·_ Bothformsof|删除0换行|reticulohistiocytic granuloma occur entirely in adults， and they exhibit simi-lar histopathologic findings. Persons with multicentric reticulohistiocytosis are reputed to have an increased incidence of internal malignancies， espe-cially of carcinomas.**

【12】A solitary reticulohistiocytic granuloma typically is a dome-shaped nodule positioned on a face or scalp. Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis also consists of dome-shaped nodules， and they tend to affect the face and hands. Polyarthritis of variable severity is a common accompaniment of the widespread form of reticulohistiocylic granuloma (interestingly named lipoid dermatoarthritis). Sections of biopsy specimens from the involved joints show the same kind of infiltrate as that contained in skin lesions.

【13】The material that gives cytoplasm of reticulohistiocytic granuloma a ground glass”appearance is PAS-positive and diastase-resistant， an indica-tion that it is a neutral mucosubstance， probably a glycolipid.

【14】**Lesions of histiocytosis X are differentiated by conventional microscopy from those of xanthogranulomas and reticulohistiocytic granuloma by their cells with large kidney-shaped nuclei and， by electron microscopy， by their many Langerhaniss’’ granules within abundant cytoplasm of cells that house reniform nuclei.**

【15】**Touton giant cells are not specific for xanthogranulomas. They may be seen in other xanthomas and， commonly， in the histiocytic stage of evolving dermatofibromas. Furthermore， Touton cells are not a sine qua non for diagnosis of xanthogranuloma； foamy histiocytes (no matter how slightly vascuolated) are. Evolving xanthogranulomas may have no Touton cells.**

【16】**In sum， one reason the list of differentiating findings at the outset of this chapter is so short is that， in reality， reticulohistiocytic granuloma may be a xanthogranuloma. 【90】**ICHEN amnyloidosis and colloid milium both re-sult from deposits of homogeneous material， but of different chemical na-tures， in the upper part of the dermis. In both， fibrocytes are affiliated closely with the deposits of homogeneous material. In fact， it is likely that fibrocytes are responsible for the formation of amyloid in lichen amyloidosis and colloid in colloid milium.**

【91】**Because of the highly characteristic histopathologic features just listed， specialized stains need not be performed routinely to differentiate between amyloid and colloid. When necessary for academic resolution of the issue， Congo red is the most reliable stain for differentiation because it is positive by dichroism for amyloid， and negative for colloid. Crystal violet stain for amyloid is prettier and more dramatic， but less reliable.**

【92】**The clinical lesion of lichen amnyloidosis consists of agminated， discrete， slightly raised， brownish-red translucent papules that often are keratotic. The condition is intensely pruritic and occurs most commonly on the ante-rior aspects of the legs， but in some instances may be widespread. Macular arnyloidosis， as the title implies， begins as flat lesions. In contrast to lichen amyloidosis， macular amyloidosis has a predilection for the interscapular region. The keratotic papules of lichen amyloidosis are consequent not only to progressive accumulations of amyloid in the papillary dermis， but to the effects of persistent rubbingas well. In short， superimposition of lichen simplex chronicus upon macular amyloidosis transforms that condition into lichen amyloidosis. The evidence for that is prominent compact orthokera-tosis and hypergranulosis in virtually all lesions of lichen amyloidosis， signs of persistent， prolonged rubbing. Macular amyloidosis that has not been rubbed， and therefore not thickened by lichen simplex chronicus， remains flat， as it is stereotypically in the interscapular region. A current hypothesis about how amyloid is formed in the upper portion of the dermis in lesions of macular amyloidosis and lichen amyloidosis holds that globules of amyloid derive from necrotic keratinocytes in the epidermis and when those apop-totic bodies are acted upon by fibrocytes， amyloid is the result.**

**Colloid milium consists of discrete， smooth， yellowish， translucent， waxy papules on sun-exposed areas， especially the malar eminences of the face and dorsa of the hands. Sometimes the papules of colloid milium are restricted to the left side of the face and the dorsa of the left hand in persons who spend much of their time driving cars in sunny climates， such as taxi drivers. At first glance， the smooth translucent papules of colloid milium may be misinterpreted as tense vesicles or as "juicy”edematous papules of polymorphous light eruption. Histopathologically， colloid is surrounded|删除0换行|always by copious amounts of solar elastosis， and both of them are stained bluish-gray by hematoxylin and eosin. These findings indicate that colloid and elastotic material are related closely to one another. Amyloid， by con-trast， is not connected to damage by sunlight.**

【94】**Whereas colloid in the skin is found only in colloid milium， amyloid is detected in a variety of circumstances other than in the macular andpapu-lar (lichenoid) forms. For example， amyloid is present around blood vessels in the skin and subcutaneous fat of patients with systemic amyloidosis， in large solitary nodules of nodular amyloidosis and， most commonly， as an incidental finding in a host of inflammatory， hamartomatous， and neoplas-tic conditionsin the skin， especially iinn sseebborrheic keratoses， tricho-epitheliomas， and basal-cellcarcinomas. These are conditions in which individual keratinocytes tend to undergo necrosis.**

【46】When the patient performs abduction maneuvers， it is important to palpate the scapula for a normal gleno-humeral to scapula ratio of movement. The ratio be-tween humeral and scapular motion is often quoted as2：1； however， this figure is an average. The ratio in the first30° is closer to somewhere between 4：1 and 7：1； from90° to 150° it is closer to 1：1.12，13 Thus， little movement occurs in the first 30°. Because the ratio changes with movement， it is often referred to as a rhythm. This rhythm changes with resistance.14 With no resistance， the ratio starts at 7.9：1 and changes to 2：1 as the arm is raised. Light loads applied to the shoulder through the arm re-sult in a rhythm ratio from 3：1 initially to 4.3：1 as the arm is raised. With heave loading， the rhythm ratio starts at 1.9：1， going to 4.5：1 as the arm is raised. 【162】**Definition of Diarrhea**

【163】**Diarrhea is a common manifestation of a number of gastrointestinal (GI) diseases. The definition is based on the frequency， volume， and consistency of stools. The patient’s perception of the stool and the components of a definition of diarrhea often are variable.**

【164】·Acute： lasting less than 14 days in duration

【165】**·Persistent： more than 14 days in duration**

【166】**·Chronic： more than 30 days in duration**

【167】Chronic diarrhea involves a decrease in stool consistency of more than 1 month duration.

【168】**_Etiology for Acute Diarrhea_**

【169】·VIRAL： most common； examples of viruses are norovirus， adenovirus， rotovirus

【170】·BACTERIAL： usually severe but self-limiting； examples of bacteria are Salmonella， Shigella， Staphylococcus _aureus， Clostridium difficile， Campylobacter_

【171】·PROTOZOAL： not usually identified as a cause of diarrhea in the developed world； examples of protozoa _are Giardia lamblia， Cryptosporidium， Entamoeba histolytica_

【172】**_Etiology for Chronic Diarrhea_**

【173】·IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME (IBS)： defined as a symptom complex of chronic lower abdominal pain； altered bowel habits are the primary characteristic of IBS

【174】·FUNCTIONAL DIARRHEA： defined as continuous or recurrent passage of loose (mushy) or watery stools with abdominal pain or discomfort

【175】**·INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE (IBD)： refers primarily to Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis； Crohn’s disease may involve the entire GI tract； ulcerative colitis is often defined as mild， moderate， or severe and often presents in a variable manner with diarrhea as its main symptom**

【176】·MICROSCOPIC COLITIS： seen as chronic watery (secretory) diarrhea without bleeding； usually occurs in middle-aged patients but can affect children

【177】·MALABSORPTION SYNDROME： is defined as impaired absorption of nutrients； it occurs as a result of congenital defects in the transport system， acquired defects， such as celiac disease， extensive surgical resection (gastric bypass)

【178】·CHOLECYSTECTOMY： diarrhea occurs in 5% to 12% of patients； it will resolve or improve over the course of weeks to months and is related to excessive bile acids entering the colon

【179】**·CHRONIC INFECTIONS： persistent bacterial and protozoal infections can be seen in patients with chronic diarrhea； specific risk factors should be assessed such as travel， HIV infection， use of antibiotics， and consumption of contaminated drinking water**

【49】Weight gain is an absolute increase in body weight. Weight gain is usually a consequence of accumulation of excess body fat， although processes such as edema and ascites can cause substantial weight gain. Weight gain is common and a significant public health concern. Regard-less of baseline weight， weight gain can lead to adverse health consequences and to the development of obesity， a major cause of morbidity and the second leading cause of preventable deaths in the United States. Over the last 2decades， the prevalence of obesity has risen dramatically；

Most weight gain is primary weight gain， resulting from excess body fat accumulation due to physiologic or behavioral changes that result in an imbalance between energy intake and expenditure. The natural history of weight change depends on several factors. Weight gain is highest between the ages of 24and 34 years； after age 55， adults tend to lose weight. Weight|删除0换行|gain is also higher among women than men. African American women between 25 and 45 years have slightly higher average weight gain than Caucasians possibly due to differences in socioeconomic status. Furthermore， weight gain can result from a change in the physiology such as during pregnancy of menopause. It can also occur when a cigarette smoker stops smoking because nicotine is a mild stimulant and appetite suppressant.

Weight gain uncommonly results from secondary causes such as endocrine disorders， genetic syndromes， or medication side effects. Although the prevalence is not well established， secondary weight gain is important because it can be reversed if the underlying cause is addressed. However， secondary causes frequently coexist with primary obesity， so treatment for a specific secondary cause may not entirely reverse weight back to the normal level. Medication side effects are probably the|删除0换行|most common secondary cause. Common offenders include glucocorticoids， anticonvulsants， antipsychotics， antidepres-sants， contraceptives， and diabetic medications. Endocrine disorders causing obesity include hyperinsulinemia， hypercorti-solism， hypothyroidism， polycystic ovary syndrome， and hypo-gonadism. Obesity is also a component of several rare genetic syndromes， including Prader-Willi syndrome， Laurence-Moon syndrome， Cohen syndrome， and Biemond syndrome.

【48】**GETTING STARTED WITH THE HISTORY**

【49】·LLet patients give the history in their own words by say-ing， for example， “Tell me about the diarrhea.”AAvoid interrupting. AAssess for related symptoms， beginning with open-ended questions， such as “Are you having any other symptoms?”

【50】·TThe most important first step in taking the history is to determine duration. The goal is to differentiate between acute and chronic diarrhea， because the respective differ-ential diagnoses differ substantially. Keep in mind that chronic diarrhea will initially present as acute diarrhea that does not resolve over time.

【51】**In acute diarrhea， the initial focus is to determine whether the patient is volume depleted.**

【52】**Identify alarm features for both acute and chronic diarrhea.**

【54】**IDENTIFYING ALARM SYMPTOMS**

【55】Most episodes of acute diarrhea will be self-limited. The astute clinician should look for signs of volume depletion such as thirst， fatigue， or dizziness that may warrant intrave-nous fluid resuscitation and/or hospitalization. Also look for alarm features in order to identify serious diagnoses.

【56】**In assessing chronic diarrhea， ask about alarm features and symptoms of organic illness that would prompt further evaluation**

【57】**Serious Diagnoses**

【58】The main goal is to distinguish functional (ie， IBS) and self-limited (ie， gastroenteritis) causes of diarrhea from those due to organic etiologies. Alarm symptoms and features can help differentiate between the two groups. Serious diagnoses include neoplasm， IBD (Crohn’s disease and ulcerative coli-tis)， infection， intermittent bowel obstruction， systemic dis-ease， and malabsorption.

【40】**INTRODUCTION**

Diarrhea accounts for up to 28 million office visits and 1.8million hospital admissions in the United States each year， with up to 200 million total cases per year. The yearly inci-dence in adult patients has been reported to be 3% to 63% per year， depending on the referral source. In the United States，|删除0换行|several billion dollars are spent annually on medical care and lost productivity due to diarrhea. Although a strict definition of diarrhea includes stool frequency and stool weight， many patients use the term when they experience increased stool liquidity. This chapter aims to clarify some key components of the history when interviewing a patient with diarrhea.

| **KEYTERMS**  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **Acute diarrhea**  | **Diarrhea lasting<2 weeks.**  |
| **Chronic diarrhea**  | **Diarrhea lasting at least 4 weeks.**  |
| **Diarrhea**  | **Increased frequency of stools (> 3 per day) with increased stool weight (> 200 g/d).**  |
|  | **However， patients may use the term"diarrhea"to describeincreased liquidity. In one**  |
|  | **series of patients referred to a gastrointestinal (Gl) clinic for diarrhea， only 40% of patients**  |
|  | **actually had output>200 g/d.**  |
| **Dysentery**  | **The passage of bloody stools.**  |
| **Irritable bowel**  | **A functional disorder characterized by the Rome Ill criteria， which include"Recurrent**  |

【48】**GETTING STARTED WITH THE HISTORY**

【49】·LLet patients give the history in their own words by say-ing， for example， “Tell me about the diarrhea.”AAvoid interrupting. AAssess for related symptoms， beginning with open-ended questions， such as “Are you having any other symptoms?”

【50】·TThe most important first step in taking the history is to determine duration. The goal is to differentiate between acute and chronic diarrhea， because the respective differ-ential diagnoses differ substantially. Keep in mind that chronic diarrhea will initially present as acute diarrhea that does not resolve over time.

【51】**In acute diarrhea， the initial focus is to determine whether the patient is volume depleted.**

【52】**Identify alarm features for both acute and chronic diarrhea.**

【53】_·C_ Consider comorbidities， accompanying symptoms， and precipitating factors.

【54】**IDENTIFYING ALARM SYMPTOMS**

【55】Most episodes of acute diarrhea will be self-limited. The astute clinician should look for signs of volume depletion such as thirst， fatigue， or dizziness that may warrant intrave-nous fluid resuscitation and/or hospitalization. Also look for alarm features in order to identify serious diagnoses.

【56】**In assessing chronic diarrhea， ask about alarm features and symptoms of organic illness that would prompt further evaluation**

【57】**Serious Diagnoses**

【58】The main goal is to distinguish functional (ie， IBS) and self-limited (ie， gastroenteritis) causes of diarrhea from those due to organic etiologies. Alarm symptoms and features can help differentiate between the two groups. Serious diagnoses include neoplasm， IBD (Crohn’s disease and ulcerative coli-tis)， infection， intermittent bowel obstruction， systemic dis-ease， and malabsorption.

【38】Because pleomorphic fibrosarcoma and MFH appears very similar， the differential diagnosis may be extremely difficult (196，202，216). 【4】Rarely， fibrosarcoma can arise in a periosteal loca-tion (periosteal fibrosarcoma). However， some investi-gators postulate that these lesions represent primary soft tissue tumors abutting the bone and invading the underlying periosteum (185).

【5】**_Clinical Presentation_**

【6】Fibrosarcoma and MFH usually occur in the third to sixth decades of life and represent about 5% and 2%， respectively， of all malignant bone tumors (213，236). Their sites of predilection are the femur， humerus， tibia， and pelvic bones (197，210，246) . The most common clinical symptoms are pain and localized swelling， ranging in duration from a few weeks to several months (199). In about 23% of reported cases， a pathologic fracture leads to incidental detection of the tumor<mark> (213，235)</mark>.

【7】**_Imaging_**

Radiographically， both lesions are marked either by an osteolytic area of destruction surrounded by a wide zone of transition or by a moth-eaten or permeative type of bone destruction (204). There is little or no reactive sclerosis， and usually no periosteal reaction (189) . The lesions are often eccentrically lo-cated， close to or within the articular end of the bone. Pathologic fractures are not uncommon. A soft tissue mass is frequently present (198). These lesions may re-semble giant cell tumor of bone or telangiectatic os-|删除0换行|teosarcoma， and they may be mistaken for metastatic carcinoma because of the age group in which they usu-ally occur. Some authorities believe that an almost pathognomonic sign of fibrosarcoma is its tendency to allow the preservation of small sequestrum-like frag ments of cortical bone and spongy trabeculae， which canbe demonstrated on conventional radiographs or CT e PX-x-amination. On scintigraphy， both lesions typically ex-hibit an area of increased uptake (186，217)， often around the periphery of the tumor (17).

【9】On CT examination， both fibrosarcoma and MFH show a predominant density similar to that of normal muscle (207，232) and exhibit the nonspecific tissue at-tenuation values of Hounsfield units encountered in most nonmineralized tissues. Hypodense areas reflect ar-eas of necrosis within tumor. MRI is useful to outline the intraosseous and extraosseous extension of these tu-mors， but there are no characteristic MRI findings for either one (181，186，207，229) . Some investiga-tors found the signal characteristics comparable to those of other lytic bone tumors (230，239). Signal intensity is intermediate to low on Tl-weighted images and high on T2 weighting， frequently heterogeneous and varying with the degree of necrosis and hemorrhage within the tumor (17). Peripheral enhancement was noted after in-travenous injection of Gd-DTPA (218).

【1】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Recently， Goldstein， Levin， Goldman， Clark， and Altonen (2001) compared the neuropsychological test performance of 18 elderly with MHI to test scores of 17 elderly with moderate CHI and 14 community-residing elderly controls. Patients were followed prospectively， over the two months following their trauma (an average follow-up of about one month). The moderate CHI group performed consistently more poorly than mild CHI and controls， who essentially did not differ from one another on the neuropsychological measuires (only 1 of 10 scores was significant，p<.05). Both the mild and moderate CHI groups reported significantly more affective distress， anxiety and somatic concern than did the control groups. The researchers concluded that their results extended the findings of prior investigations in young adults by demon-strating a relatively good cognitive outcome in elderly persons following a single uncomplicated MHI， despite continuing subjective complaints.**</u>

【2】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Some have contended that the inability to find objective evidence for persistent effects of MHI relates to inadequate characterization of ini-tial severity， and/or to insensitive measures of outcome. As I have argued in another paper 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 1999)</u>， any attempt at improving assess-ment of initial trauma severity or outcome should show statistical advan-tages over current methodologies， in particular， in relation to dose effects. In other words， any proposed improvement in assessment of severity， such as the procedure for estimating g force proposed by Varney and Varney (1995)， should show negative correlations with GCS and neuropsychological test scores， and positive correlations with dura-tion of post-traumatic amnesia. Data published by Culotta， Sementilli， Gerold， and Watts (1996) demonstrated greater need for neurosurgical intervention and more frequent intracranial lesions in persons with GCS of 13 and 14， vs. GCS of 15. Although these data show the benefits of grading severity of MHI relative to acute injury characteristics， Culotta and colleagues did not study long-term neuropsychological out-come for these different levels of GCS.**</u>

【3】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Novel neurodiagnostic procedures such as quantitative EEG (QEEG)， SPECT， or PET have been suggested as outcome measures 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Holman &Devous， 1992； Tebano et al.， 1988)</u></u>. These novel procedures should show stronger associations with depth and duration of coma and with duration of PTA than are obtained with neuropsychological measures of outcome删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Larrabee， 1999； Ricker & Zafonte， 2000)</u></u>. To date， various professional groups have advised aguinst the use of QEEG， PET， and SPECT in MHI， due in large part to the poor specificity of these procedures 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(i.e.， high false positive error rates； American Academy of Neurology 1989， 1996， 1997； Society of Nuclear Medicine Brain Imaging Council， 1996)</u></u>.**</u>

【4】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**NON-NEUROLOGICAL INTURY VARIABLES RELATED TO PERSISTENT SYMPTOMATIC COMPLAINT AND TO NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TEST PERFORMANCE**</u>

【5】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**In addition to being sensitive to neurological dysfunction， neuropsycho-logical tests are also affected by a variety of psychiatric disorders， in par ticular disorders such as depression that affect attention and effortful processing 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Cohen， 1993； Cohen， Weingartner Smallberg， Pickar， &Murphy， 1982)</u></u>. Indeed， several diagnostic categories in the DSM-IV are characterized by accompanying cognitive symptoms， including schizophrenia， mood disorders， anxiety disorders， and in particular， post-traumatic stress disorder 删除1:<u>(American Psychiatric Association，1994)</u>. These psychiatric conditions must be included in any differen-tial diagnosis of MHI.**</u>

【6】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Developmental disorders and substance abuse can also affect sympto-matic complaints and neuropsychological performance， I have described a case of MHI， diagnosed by another psychologist as having left hemi-sphere brain damage， due to reduced verbal memory， lower Verbal IQ relative to Performance IQ， and reduced right hand motor functions. This other psychologist was unaware of a history of verbal learning dis-ability， verified through school records， and did not consider either the effects of peripheral injuries to the right upper extremity or the neuro-logically atypical pattern of poorer gross relative to fine motor skills删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Greiffenstein， Baker， & Gola， 1996； Larrabee， 1990)</u></u>. Hence， learning disability and attention deficit disorder are important differential diag-nostic considerations in any MHi case.**</u>

【7】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Substance abuse， in particular alcohol abuse， is a significant differen~tial diagnostic consideration， particularly given the known association of alcohol use with motor vehicle accidents. As previously reviewed， alcohol use does not appear to adversely affect outcome in MHI删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(AIterman et al.， 1985； Dikmen et al.， 1993)</u></u>. Alcohol abuse， in and of itself， however， is certainly associated with neuropsychological deficits删除1:<u>(Parsons， Butters， & Nathan， 1987)</u>. In fact， data exist demonstrating that non-alcoholic progeny of alcoholic parents perform more poorly on neuropsychological testing than do non-alcoholic progeny of non-alcoholic parents .**</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**As discussed earlier in the analysis of the poor specificity of PCS， per-sistent symptomatic complaints following MHI can be viewed as a type of sornatoform disorder 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Mittenberg et al.， 1992；Mittenberg， Tremont， Zielinski， Fichera， & Rayls， 1996； Putnam & Millis， 1994)</u></u>. The high|删除0换行|baserates of syinptoms such as headache， forgetfulness， and irritability in non-head-injured subjects 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(cf. Lees-Haley & Brown， 1993； Mittenberg et al.， 1992)</u></u> and association of exacerbation of these symptoms with stress 删除1:<u>(cf. Gouvier et al.， 1992)</u> provide a basis for selective attentional bias and misattribution of symptoms to MHI 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Mittenberg et al.， 1992，1996； Putnam & Millis，1994)</u></u>. Thus， the patient who premorbidly exhib-ited tendencies toward excessive health concerns may focus excessively on common daily symptoms such as irritability and memory， become more anxious regarding these complaints， and experience heightened frequency of these “symp-toms，" fearing they are the result of their recent MHI. The problem is compounded if these individuals are informed by a variety of health care professionals that they have suffered traumatic brain injury. As Mittenberg and associates (1996) demonstrated， information on the natural history of MHI， ubiquitous nature of “symptoms”in everyday life， and cognitive-behavioral instructions for symptom re-attribution， can significantly diminish PCS by six months later.**</u>

【9】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Chronic pain and pharmacological treatment of pain are also related to changes in neuropsychological test performance 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Taylor， Cox， &Mailis， 1996； Uomoto & Esselman， 1993)</u></u>. Chronic pain complaints， in particular headache， neck/shoulder， and back pain， are significantly more frequent in MHI relative to moderate/severe HI； for example，95% of MHI in one series had pain complaints， in contrast to only 22%of moderate/severe HI with pain complaints (Uomoto & Esselman). Taylor and associates (1996) compared the information-processing per-formance of three groups of patients： (1) whiplash， (2) chronic pain without history of whiplash or head injury， and (3) moderate to severe HI. The whiplash and chronic pain samples were carefully matched on IQ， WMS-R Digit and Visual Span， pain severity ratings， and MMPI-2profiles. There were no group differences on either the PASAT or Auditory Consonant Trigrams procedures. Both the chronic pain and whiplash patients had higher pain ratings and MMPI-2 Depression scales than did the moderate/severe HI group， but did not differ from one another. These data not only clearly demonstrate the effects of pain on neuropsychological test performance， but also contradict the associ-ation between whiplash and MHI reported by some investigators删除1:<u>(Sweeney， 1992)</u>. Taylor and colleagues concluded that their results demonstrated poor specificity for detecting subtle effects of brain trall-ma， and their data did not support the theory of neuronal degeneration as the etiology of whiplash-related cognitive complaints.**</u>

【10】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**MALINGERING**</u>

【11】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Malingering is the intentional distortion of symptoms and/or behav-ior for external incentives such as obtaining monetary compensation or avoiding criminal prosecution 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(American Psychiatric Association，1994；Rogers， 1997)</u></u>. In the context of neuropsychological evaluation， malingering can occur as(1) false and/or exaggerated report of symptoms 删除1:<u>(Berry et al.， 1995)</u>，(2) intentionally poor performance on neuropsychological tests 删除1:<u>(Millis & Putnam， 1996)</u>， or (3) a combina tion of symptom exaggeration and intentional performance deficit删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 2000)</u>. Litigation and its effects on patient motivation and malingering are important considerations in the evaluation of any person manifesting persistent complaints following MHI. Binder and Rohling (1996) reported an effect size of .47 in a meta-analysis of the effects of financial incentive on recovery after closed head injury. The effect was particularly strong for MHI. Moreover， the effect size of .47 for head injury was quite similar to the effect size of .48between financial incentives and chronic pain 删除1:<u>(Rohling， Binder， &Langhinrischen-Rohling， 1995)</u>. It is noteworthy that both of these financial effect sizes are four times the general effect size for MHI， reported by Binder and associates (1997). Not surprisingly， baserates for malingering are significantly higher than the persistent MHI neu-ropsychological effect baserate of 5%， estimated by Binder’s group(1997). Binder and Kelly (1996)， using a PDRT cutoff of the bottom2% of a non-litigating brain injury group， found that up to 47% of a series of MHIs performed below this cutoff. Youngjohn， Burrows， and Erdal (1995) found that 48% of a consecutive series of MHIs showed evidence of motivational impairmenton a battery of tests for malin-gering. As noted earlier， Millis (1992) and Greiffenstein and col-leagues (1994) reported data consistent with malingering baserates of50% and 60%， respectively.**</u>

【12】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Exaggeration of Symptom Complaints**</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The MMPI/MMPI-2， 删除1:<u>(Butcher， Dahlstrom， Graham， Tellegen， &Kaemmer， 1989)</u> is the most frequently used personality test in forensic neuropsychology 删除1:<u>(Lees-Haley， Smith， Williams， & Dunx， 1995)</u>. The MMPI-2 provides for the assessment of the validity of a person’s sympto-matic response pattertt， via the standard validity scales， L， F， K， Back F， VRIN，and TRIN， and via scales developed subsequent to the publication|删除0换行|of the MMPI-2， such as F (p)， the Infrequency Psychopathology Scale删除1:<u>(Arbisi & Ben Porath， 1995)</u> and the Fake Bad Scale， FBS 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Lees-Haley，1992；Lees-Haley， English， & Glenn， 1991)</u></u>.**</u>

【14】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Two types of malingering and/or exaggeration of symnptomatic com-plaint can occur on the MMPI/MMPI-2： globally exaggerated psy-chopathology 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Berry et al.， 1995； Heaton， Smith， Lehman， & Vogt，1978)</u></u>， and specific exaggeration of cognitive and somatic complaints 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Larrabee，1998；Lees-Haley， 1992； Lees-Haleyet al.，1991)</u></u>. In globally exaggerated psychopathology， the traditional MMPI/MMPI-2 scales such as F and its derivatives， Back-F and F(p) are elevated 删除1:<u>(Berry et al. 1995； Heaton et al.，1978)</u>. The second type of malingering， exaggeration of somatic symp-toms， is more specific to personal injury than crmninal settings， and is not as sensitive to F-scale derived validity measures as it is to the Lees-Haley FBS 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Boone & Lu， 2000； Larrabee， 1998；Millis， Putnam， & Adams，1995； Slick， Hopp，Strauss， & Spellacy，1996)</u></u>.**</u>

【15】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**I have observed 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 1998)</u> that somatic symptom complaints such as pain， paresthesias， and malaise were common in neuropsycho~logical settings and associated with items on MMPI/MMPI-2 scales 1and 3. Yet there was only one F scale item on either of these two clinical scales. I found that F was not sensitive to the presence of somatic symp-tomn exaggeration on scales I and 3 in groups of litigants with objective test evidence for cognitive malingering， despite elevations on scales 1and 3 that exceeded mean elevations for a variety of published studies of chronic pain patients 删除1:<u>(cf. Keller & Butcher， 1991)</u>， moderate to sevcre head injury， and non-injured simulators 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(including subjects from Berryetal.，1995 and Heaton et al.， 1978)</u></u>. By contrast， FBS was sensitive to the presence of somatic malingering， with 11 of 12 malingerers seor-ing at or above the cutoff scores of 24 for men， and 26 for women 删除1:<u>(cf. Lees-Haley，1992)</u>.**</u>

结尾批量删除-1:<u>**My data were quite similar to data published by Suhr， Tranel， Wefel， and Barrash (1997)， contrasting the MMPI-2 profiles of MHI probable malingerers with a variety of different patient samples， including those with severe head injury， depression， or somatization. The Larralce(1998) and Suhr and associates (1997) data are also quite similar to data reported by Millis and colleagues (1995) in a group of MHl patients selected for the presence of poor motivation， defined as less than chance performance on one or both aspects of the Warrington Recognition Memory Tesl， with the exception that the Millis group's subiects had significant elevations on the F scale. Despite this difference， the authors found the FBS to be a more efficient diagnostic discrimina-tor than F. Furthermore， the Larrabee (1998) somatic malingerers had|删除0换行|the greatest mean elevation on MMPI-2 Scale 3 (93.8) compared to the Millis (86.7) and the Suhr groups (81.4)， despite having the lowest F(63.5 vs. 67.6 for Suhr et al， and vs. 89.7 for Millis et al.). Recently， Boone and Lu (2000) have reported significant elevations on MMPI-2Scales 1 (T83.5) and 3 (T89.2) in litigants claiming brain dysfunction who demonstrated evidence of a motivated performance deficit， and I have also reported significant elevations on MMPI-2 Scale I (T82) and Scale 3 (T82.4) in litigants claiming brain dysfunction who failed the PDRT 删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 2003)</u>，**</u>

【17】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Figure 7.1 contrasts the average sample-size-weighted MMPI-2 proba-ble malingerer profile for the Boone and Lu (2000)， Larrabee 删除1:<u>(1998，2003)</u>， Millis and colleagues (1995)， and Suhr and colleagues (1997) investigations (pooled n= 101)， with MMPI-2 profiles for chronic pain删除2:<u>(Keller & Butcher， 1991； pooled n， males and females =502)</u>； and depression 删除2:<u>(Suhr et al.， 1997， n=30)</u>. Figure 7.2 contrasts the probable malingerer profile with MMPI-2 profiles for non-litigating severe head injury subjects 删除2:<u>(Millis et al.， 1995a； Suhr et al.， 1997； Youngjohn， Davis，& Wolf， 1997； pooled n=47)</u>， multiple sclerosis 删除2:<u>(Connor， Ogden， Walker， Cullum， & Frohman， 1998； Nelson & Do， 1998； pooled n=66)</u>， and spinal cord injury 删除2:<u>(Rodevich & Wanlass， 1995； n=42)</u>. Inspection of Figures 7.1 and 7.2 demonstrates greater elevations on scales 1， 2， 3，7， and 8 for the probable malingerers relative to all other clinical groups， including subjects with a relatively higher psychological contri-bution to symptomatic complaint (chronic pain， depression)， and sub-jects with a relatively higher physiological and neurological contribution to symptomatic complaint (spinal cord injury， multiple sclerosis， and non-litigating severe head traumna).**</u>

【18】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**In two separate investigations， Millis et al. (1995)， and Larrabee(1998) found that scale 3 was the best MMPI-2 clinical scale discrimina-tor， contrasting probable malingerers with a variety of different clinical groups. Consequently， the scale 3 mean scores for the probable malin-gerers (M=84.4， SD=12.4) were contrasted with those from multiple sclerosis (M=71.4， SD=11.6)， spinal cord injury (M=60.8， SD=10.8)， non-litigating severe head injury (M= 60.4， SD= 12.3)， depression(M=72.4， SD=15.9)， and chronic pain (M=75.4，SD=13.2).The prob-able malingerers had significantly greater scale 3 than all other groups， at p<.0005， one-tail. Effect sizes (based on g， the pooled SD for probable malingerers and other clinical samples)， were all large， with g= 1.08 (vs. multiple sclerosis)， g=1.97 {vs. spinal cord injury)，g=1.94 (vs. non-litigating severe head injury)，g=.90 (vs.depression)，and g=.69 (vs. chronic pain).**</u>

【24】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**intentionally Poor Performance on Cognitive Tests**</u>

【25】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Procedures for identifying cognitive malingering (i.e.， poor effort on neuropsychological tests)， can be grouped in three descriptive categories删除1:<u>(Larrabee， 2000)</u>： (1) relatively simple tests performed well by neuro-logically impaired patients， (2) pattern analysis， and (3) forced-choice symptom validity procedures. A multiple-component assessment of malingering employing measures from each category is more sensitive in detecting reduced effort， and is recommended in evaluating MHI lit-igants 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Larrabee， 2000； Youngjohn et al.， 1995)</u></u>.**</u>

【26】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**The Rey 15-Itern Test 删除1:<u>(Lezak， 1995)</u> is a good example of a relatively simple test performed well by neurologically impaired patients. This procedure， developed by the French psychologist， Rey， requires the sub-ject to draw， from memory， 15 items； however， the items are easily grouped (e.g.， identical sequences of Arabic and Roman numerals， identical alphabet sequences in upper and lower case)， so that even patients suffering significant brain dysfunction can perform well. 【2】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Some have contended that the inability to find objective evidence for persistent effects of MHI relates to inadequate characterization of ini-tial severity， and/or to insensitive measures of outcome. Data published by Culotta， Sementilli， Gerold， and Watts (1996) demonstrated greater need for neurosurgical intervention and more frequent intracranial lesions in persons with GCS of 13 and 14， vs. GCS of 15. Although these data show the benefits of grading severity of MHI relative to acute injury characteristics， Culotta and colleagues did not study long-term neuropsychological out-come for these different levels of GCS.**</u>

【3】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**Novel neurodiagnostic procedures such as quantitative EEG (QEEG)， SPECT， or PET have been suggested as outcome measures 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Holman &Devous， 1992； Tebano et al.， 1988)</u></u>. 【5】结尾批量删除-1:<u>**In addition to being sensitive to neurological dysfunction， neuropsycho-logical tests are also affected by a variety of psychiatric disorders， in par ticular disorders such as depression that affect attention and effortful processing 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Cohen， 1993； Cohen， Weingartner Smallberg， Pickar， &Murphy， 1982)</u></u>. 【63】**Despite the several features that Kaposi's sarcoma have in common with a hemangioma on a leg of a young person， the two conditions may be differentiated from one another with near-certainty if heed is paid to the following facts： the hemangioma consists mostly of discrete blood vessels with round or oval shapes lined by plump endothelial cells that often pro-trude into lumina and those vessels often involve the papillary dermis but not the immediate vicinity of pre-existing venules， whereas the vessels in patch and plaque lesions of Kaposi's sarcoma are not discrete but are ar-ranged in clusters， do not have smooth borders， but are jagged， are lined by thin endothelial cells that hardly protrude into lumina， and tend to follow pre-existing vascular plexuses within the reticular dermis. The papillary dermis nearly always is spared in patches and plaques of Kaposi’s sarcoma. Thrombi occur from time to time within hemangiomas， but hardly ever in Kaposi's sarcoma. 【1】**One might ask how such errors could possibly make their way into pub-lication and the assessment process， especially given the literature on ensuring the accuracy of translations and the profound effects ofeduca-tion on cognitive test performance. The fact is， there may be a number of reasons neuropsychologists who are in all other respects adequately qualified fail to address such important issues. These include ignorance and poor judgment， and seem to be accompanied by a conspicuous absence of accurate self-appraisal with regard to the impact that these factors have on one's decision making.**

【2】**Regarding language， ignorance manifests in predictable ways that include a lack of knowledge about what fluency really is， a lack of aware-ness about one's own level of fluency in a second language， and a more general cultural ignorance or ethnocentrism. After eighteen years of exposure to Spanish-language neuropsychological materials， raw data and reports， as well as the opportunity to review a significant number of articles for publication， it is the belief of this author that with regard to the concept of fluency， two separate groups of individuals may possess inadequate self-assessment skills.**

【3】**The first group consists of native speakers of English of any ethnic origin who may have studied Spanish either in high school or college， or who have taken brief intensive Spanish-language courses in a Spanish-speaking country. Acquiring native fluency in any second lan-guage is an arduous task， particularly for an adult. The approaches to language study described above do not provide the time and intensity of training sufficient to acquire the competence of a native Spanish speak-er. Individuals with this level of language education are unlikely to pos-SesSthe sophistication necessary for adequate iest construction， translation， or assessment.**

【4】**The fact is that monolingual English speakers generally demionstrate a very poor understanding of the concept of fluency. Individuals with marginal knowledge of a second language routinely assess themselves as fluent. In fact， they are notorious for underestimating the point along the language proficiency continuum at which an individual can begin to be described as fluent. When the idea of fluency is poorly understood， so too is the realization that different levels of language proficiency are necessary to function in different settings. 【1】# PART II: TREATMENT OF PHONOLOGICAL DISORDERS/CHAPTER 8: A procedure for classification of speech disorders/The purpose of assessment

【2】The purpose of assessment
=========================

【3】The type and extent of the assessment depends upon its purpose. For example, a clinician may carry out a particular (broad-ranging) set of assessments if the report is to be used to set up an individual education plan for a child. In contrast, screening all children in a preschool would lend itself to brief assessments, where difficulties were identified for further investigation in another session. Assessment for planning an episode of intervention might be specific to a child’s area of difficulty. Decisions regarding assessment format are also dependent upon a clinician’s resources and the nature of individual children: their age, intellectual ability, behavioural characteristics and problems mooted in the referral letter. For example, one child referred was reported to be ‘resistant’ to assessment. The first session consequently avoided the use of formal assessments. In this chapter we focus on the assessment of a child referred for the first time with a suspected speech disorder.

【4】A question was posed in Chapter 1: ‘How should speech-disordered children be classified?’ The literature reviewed identified approaches to classifying speech disorders that make relevant contributions to the process of differential diagnosis and clinical management: age of onset, severity, causal and maintenance factors, description of linguistic symptomatology and deficits in the speech-processing chain. The description of the behavioural characteristics of the disorder, especially the linguistic symptomatology, seems essential for clinical decisions concerning the linguistic unit that will be the focus of therapy, and the therapeutic approach used. This chapter proposes procedures for the classification of speech disorders that allows management decisions to be made. Its specific aim is to provide a means of identifying subgroups of phonological disorder.

【5】When a child presents with mispronunciations of words that are associated with unintelligibility and caregivers and/or the client are concerned, the initial role of the clinician is to assess the child’s communication function . Standardized assessment will provide evidence concerning the child’s function in comparison to peers and determine whether there is a communication disability that needs intervention. Khan (2002) argues that clinicians, who have limited time resources, need to obtain a standardized score, to provide feedback to parents and justify clinical decisions. An assessment of different aspects of communication (articulation, phonology, receptive and expressive language) allows understanding of the extent of the disability. Bleile (2002) recommends assessing other aspects of communication, rather than focusing on articulation or phonology, because a speech difficulty may indicate a larger developmental problem. Non-verbal cognitive testing, hearing and oro-motor assessment provide information about current causal and maintenance factors of the speech disorder. Case history information provides additional information and allows the level of concern to be evaluated. Such broad-ranging assessment affords a basis for further investigation (e.g. referral to other professionals) and will influence the following clinical management decisions.

【6】# PART II: TREATMENT OF PHONOLOGICAL DISORDERS/CHAPTER 8: A procedure for classification of speech disorders/Is intervention indicated?

【7】Is intervention indicated?
==========================

Chapter 7 provides a general discussion of the issues relevant to deciding whether intervention is indicated. The decision is not solely based on the presence of speech errors. Justification for the decision to offer therapy targeting speech needs to include evidence that:|删除换行|the articulation and/or phonological system differs from those of the client’s peers;
*   speech is impaired relative to other aspects of communication or non-verbal ability;
*   there is potential for change;
*   there is caretaker or client concern about speech difficulties;
*   the service delivery option chosen is appropriate for the family context.

【9】All five points should be considered in deciding whether intervention is indicated.

【10】Standardized testing is essential since a child with normal developmental speech errors, if seen, would be taking up resources needed by a child whose speech errors reflected delay or disorder. Speech errors may be part of a more pervasive communication or developmental problem, indicating the need for broad-based assessment. A child with little or no potential for change (e.g. a child whose language is in line with all other aspects of their development or a child with a lisp who has no current concern) consume resources that may be better expended on a child with a more specific communication difficulty about which there is concern. Service delivery must be discussed with parents to ensure the best use of resources. Parents may not be able to attend a clinic regularly due to other commitments or may not feel the service offered (e.g. group therapy) is worth the time and expense of attending.

【11】The decision concerning whether intervention is indicated implicitly involves each child’s prioritization for therapy. The need for services can dramatically exceed resources. To maximize their effectiveness, clinicians need to distinguish between speech-disordered children to provide clients with time-effective therapy by using a variety of therapeutic strategies and service delivery models. While the particular policy of a speech and language pathology service may limit prioritization options, general policies should include the potential for varying the wait between assessment and the commencement of therapy.

【12】# PART II: TREATMENT OF PHONOLOGICAL DISORDERS/CHAPTER 8: A procedure for classification of speech disorders/What is the initial diagnosis?

【13】What is the initial diagnosis?
==============================

【14】Diagnosis must be based on data, raising the problem of what type of data should be collected. The major decision concerns the type of speech sample: standardized test vs. spontaneous speech. Miccio 删除2:<u>(2002, p. 224)</u> emphasizes the need for a spontaneous speech sample because standardized tests that depend upon single word picture-naming fail to ‘provide adequate information on the systematic nature of the child’s phonology or how it is used in connected speech’. Miccio (2002) also notes that most standardized tests that report the number of errors do not examine the type of errors made (whether typical or atypical of normal development) or whether the child’s errors are consistent 删除1:<u>(cf. DEAP, Dodd et al. 2002)</u>. She also notes that all standardized assessments are culturally biased to some degree. In contrast, Khan (2002) argues for the need for standardized assessments as the basis for clinical decisions. Some children are so unintelligible that it is necessary for the clinician to know the target words in order to be able to describe their system, resulting in Sentence Imitation Tasks to examine continuous speech . The size of the sample depends on the purpose of the assessment, the type of disorder and the clinician’s time for collecting and analysing the sample.

【15】Description and quantification of data
--------------------------------------

【16】There are a number of different ways that speech samples can be analysed. Some measures are standardized so that a child can be compared against their peers. Severity of the speech disorder can be calculated by counting the number of errors and assigning a severity category 删除1:<u>(Shriberg et al. 1997)</u>. Intelligibility can be rated 删除1:<u>删除2:<u>(Fudala and Reynolds, 2000; Ingram and Ingram, 2001)</u></u>. The different methodologies are derived from linguistic theories about phonology that have different clinical implications. Nevertheless, their purpose is descriptive – they are ways of concisely and accurately characterizing children’s errors. Four common approaches are summarized.

【17】### _1\. Linear phonologies_

【18】Linear phonologies, derived from generative phonology 删除1:<u>(Chomsky and Halle, 1968)</u>, describe errors that occur in acquisition 删除1:<u>(Smith, 1973)</u> and disorder 删除1:<u>(Compton, 1970)</u> in terms of ‘rules’. The rule specifies the conditions (phonetic context) that elicit a specific error 删除1:<u>(Dinnsen and O’Connor, 2001)</u>. For example, children acquiring their phonological system typically realize word-initial fricative sounds as stops at the same place of articulation so that /v/ is realized as /b/ in \[baen\] for van, and /s/ is realized as /t/ in \[toup\] for soap. This error pattern is commonly known as ‘stopping’. There is evidence that rules must be applied in a particular order. For example, Smith’s (1973) case pronounced puzzle as \[p  dзl\] (velars are realized as alveolars – ‘fronting’) but puddle as \[p   зl\] (alveolars are realized as velars before syllabic /l/). The first rule must, then, be applied after the second, otherwise puzzle would be realized as \[pugel\]. Dinnsen and O’Connor’s (2001) criticism of linear models is that rules are assumed to be independent of one another 删除1:<u>(cf. Smith, 1973)</u>, whereas optimality theory allows implicational relationships that can inform what error patterns should be targets of therapy to maximize generalization. Bernhardt and Holdgrafer (2001) criticize linear phonological descriptions because they focus on segments (phonemes) as opposed to larger linguistic units that include stress, intonation and tone.

【19】### _2\. Non-linear phonologies_

【20】Non-linear phonologies use a hierarchical framework of tiers, where effects may be either top-down or bottom-up 删除1:<u>(Bernhardt and Holdgrafer, 2001)</u>. Different non-linear theories propose differing levels of tiers . Bernhardt and Gilbert (1992) propose a prosodic tier that governs syllable stress, a skeletal tier that governs timing and syllable shape (e.g. CV vs. CVC) and a segmental tier that governs phoneme production. In turn, the segmental tier consists of a series of hierarchically arranged nodes that specify which phoneme will be produced in terms of distinctive feature oppositions (e.g. the root node determines consonantal vs. vowel production; the laryngeal node governs voicing; the place node determines place of articulation: labial, coronal or dorsal). Thus a word’s pronunciation is represented by a tree diagram .

【21】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 8.1** Non-linear phonology tree diagram 删除1:<u>(Bernhardt and Gilbert, 1992)</u>.</u>

【22】Bernhardt and Holdgrafer (2001) argue that non-linear theory allows a more economic description of error patterns, and can include the influence of other factors (e.g. stress). One example given is children’s deletion of the first syllable of bisyllabic words where the first syllable is unstressed (\[lun\] for balloon). Linear descriptions, however, do include stress as an influencing factor by stating rules such as _unstressed initial syllables delete_ . Non-linear analysis is useful for describing error patterns that are characterized by influence from the prosodic tier, although tree hierarchies seem unnecessarily cumbersome for most error patterns.

【23】### _3\. Sonority_

【24】Sonority is important for some non-linear descriptions of phonology. In acoustic phonetics, the loudness of a segment, in comparison to other segments of the same pitch, stress and duration, is known as ‘sonority’ 删除1:<u>(Crystal, 1991)</u>. For example, /s/ is ‘louder’ than /sh/. The sonority principle, ‘that the sonority profile of a legitimate syllable must rise continuously to a peak and fall continuously after the peak’ 删除2:<u>(Radford et al. 1999, p. 90)</u>, has been used to explain phonotactic constraints (e.g. /spr/ is legal but /sbr/ is not). Children’s developmental phonotactic constraints (in word-final nasal plus plosive clusters, nasals delete so that count is \[ko  t\]) have also been explained using the sonority principle 删除1:<u>(Radford et al. 1999)</u>. However, neither of the examples given by Radford et al. (1999) is convincing. For example, many children delete the plosive word finally, and retain the nasal (e.g. \[hæn\] for hand).

【25】### _4\. Optimality theory_

【26】Optimality theory proposes a set of universal constraints that apply to all phonologies – developing and mature versions of all languages 删除1:<u>(Barlow, 2001)</u>. Differences in phonological systems arise through varying ranking orders of constraints. There are two types of constraints: faithfulness constraints that require words to be produced to match those heard and markedness constraints that require words produced to be simplified in structure. ‘Marked’ properties of a language include those that are perceptually or productively difficult or occur less frequently crosslinguistically. There is, then, a conflict between the two sets of constraints. Barlow (2001) states that every word spoken violates constraints: if a child says \[sip\] for sleep, then markedness constraints are not violated because the word has a CVC form, but a faithfulness constraint is violated because the cluster /sl/ is simplified to \[s\]. According to optimality theory, the acquisition of phonology requires children to learn the ranking of constraints appropriate for their language environment – that is which constraints may be legally violated. Children initially seem to favour markedness constraints over faithfulness constraints. Barlow (2001) notes that optimality theory can account for the variable production of two versions of any word (by hypothesizing that two constraints have the same ranking). One difficulty, however, is that in some cases, a lower-ranked constraint overrides a higher-ranked constraint 删除1:<u>(Barlow, 2002)</u>. This caveat makes the task of ranking error patterns problematic.

【27】It is unclear whether different linguistic approaches to the description of errors lead to different clinical management decisions. For example, Dinnsen and O’Connor’s (2001) review indicates that optimality theory requires the identification of error patterns in terms of descriptive statements that are similar in form to those associated with linear phonology. The arguments for and against particular linguistic theories seem to be primarily related to linguistic principles, despite claims concerning target selection in therapy. The procedure for the classification of speech disorders now described is largely derived from linear phonology. This choice was made for the following reasons: the linear approach is already widely used clinically, the error pattern statements are economical and, if precise, allow easy prediction of how words not in a sample will be pronounced, there is normative data available on error patterns and the procedure provides data allowing a choice of therapy targets.

Screening of oro-motor function using a standardized assessment 删除1:<u>(e.g. DEAP, Dodd et al. 2002)</u> will allow a decision about whether a more in-depth assessment of oro-motor function is warranted 删除2:<u>(e.g. VIMPAC, Hayden and Square, 1999, referral to ENT)</u>. However, Lof 删除2:<u>(2002, pp. 255–6)</u> note that there is clear evidence that ‘oro-motor exercises do not bring about changes in speech-sound productions’. More-subtle oro-motor difficulties reflected by ‘undifferentiated lingual gestures’ 删除1:<u>(Gibbon and Scobbie, 1997)</u> may also be important. They argue that some children, whose substitution errors are thought to be linguistically based, are actually making covert contrasts between the target and error sounds, reflecting a speech-motor constraint that can be detected and treated using electro-palatography. While Gibbon and Scobbie’s (1997) research implies that motor constraints may be more important than is generally assumed, such constraints cannot account for a variety of error types (e.g. sound and syllable deletions, inconsistent substitutions, syllable constraints, e.g. initial syllables are always marked by /h/).

【37】The fact that a child can articulate a phone in one syllable position does not necessarily imply that the phone will always be produced correctly in others, or in clusters. Specific clusters are not listed separately in the chart, since their reduction is noted under phonological error patterns. 【22】**ALS Variants**

【23】**Bulbar Presentation**

【24】**A. General considerations：**

【25】1\. Growing evidence that ALS is a multisystem degener-ation

【26】**B. Clinical features：**

【27】**1\. Most common in post menopausal women**

【28】**2\. Poor prognosis； in past death occurred in approxi-mately one year**

【29】**3\. Possibly up to 25% of ALS patients present with this onser**

【30】4.Spread to the lower cervical upper thoracic myotomes； later to lumbosacral muscles

【31】**5\. Rarely， it remains bulbar**

【32】**Primary Lateral Sclerosis**

【33】**A. General considerations：**

【34】**1\. Does not involve the lower motor neuron**

【35】**B. Clinical features：**

【36】1\. Age of onset is usually between 50 and 55 years

【37】**2\. Progresses very slowly**

【38】**3\. May start as spastic paraparesis**

【39】**4\. Severe generalized spasticity， bilateral Hoffman and Babinski signs**

【40】**5\. Pseudobulbar palsy**

【41】**6\. Cognitive impairment is common； overt dementia is rare**

【42】**Progressive Muscular Atrophy**

【43】**A. General considerations：**

【44】**1\. Rarest variant of ALS**

【45】**2\. Occurs in approximately 2.5% of patients**

【46】**B. Clinical features：**

【47】**1\. Slowly progressive with better outcome than in classic disease**

【48】**2\. A pure lower motor neuron disease**

【49】**3\. Differential is between this and lower motor onset of SMA**

【51】**A. General considerations：**

【52】**1\. Relatively symmetric proximal and distal wasting of the upper extremities**

【53】**2\. Hyperactive reflexes in both upper and lower extremi-ties**

【54】**3\. Corticospinal tract dysfunction with Babinski signs**

【56】**A. General considerations：**

【57】**1\. Rare； possibly 5% of patients**

【58】**B. Clinical features：**

【59】**1\. Corticospinal and lower motor neuron involvement of one side**

【61】**A. General considerations：**

【62】**1\. Approximately 5-10% of ALS patients**

【64】**1) Apparent single founder for these patients(D90A mutation)**

【65】2) Tunisian families with 2q33-35 mutations

【78】**2\. Greater involvement of Clarke’s columns**

【79】**Guam Parkinsonian ALS Dementia Complex**

【80】**A. General considerations：**

【81】**1\. Endemic areas for this clinical complex are： Western Pacific， Kii peninsula of Japan； West New Guinea**

【82】**2\. No gene has been identified**

【83】**3\. Excitotoxic cell death from B-N-methylamine BMAA， derived from the cycad nut is not causative**

【84】**4\. ALS form of the complex has declined**

【85】**B. Clinical features：**

【86】**1\. Parkinsonism presents primarily as akinetic rigid vari-ety**

【87】**2\. Dystonia is prominent (“Lubag)； particularly of the mouth**

【88】3\. ALS in combination with Parkinsonian features； pa-tients may have severe dementia

【89】**Differential Diagnosis of ALS**

【90】**Since ALS and its variants may strike all levels of the neuraxis the differential diagnosis is extremely wide. In reality， the di-agnosis is restricted， as there are few illnesses that strike the upper and lower motor neurons simultaneously.**

【91】**The clinician must not miss the illnesses that simulate ALS but are treatable. The most common of these is cervi-cal spondylosis. This is primarily a disease of the motion seg-ments of the spinal segments and occurs in both cervical and lumbar areas concomitantly. It is asymmetrical， biceps jerks are lost， knee jerks are increased ankle reflexes may be asym-metrically decreased. If the ventral roots are severely con-stricted in the cervical canal fasciculations are noted in the upper extremities. It does not involve the cranial nerves， the neck is in a forward flexed posture and cannot be moved to lateral， anterior and posterior planes. The hands are usually spared， whereas in ALS the first dorsal interosseous is often affected very early. Mentation is normal. The problem arises when the patient has both diseases. Cervical spondylosis does not affect paraspinal muscles. MRI of the cervical spine and back corroborate the diagnosis.**

【92】**The pure motor autoimmune neuropathies may simulate the lower motor form of ALS. The causative antibodies are GMI， MAG， and Gdlb. Serum protein electrophoresis and immune focused electrophoresis often demonstrates an IgM peak (particularly for MAG). Most importantly EMG identi-fies a conduction block. Wasting is not nearly as prominent as in progressive muscular atrophy (which is most often proxi-mal).**

【93】**Hexosaminidase A deficiency is extremely rare and has prominent psychiatric and cerebellar features.**

【94】**There still is controversy over the link between lymphoma and leukemia with ALS. Clearly， there is a strong association between many malignancies and destruction of various parts of the neuraxis (anti-Hu， anti-Yo， anti-Ri， anti-Ma and anti-anti TA). A careful evaluation of the bone marrow is in order if there is a suspicion of a lymphoproliferative disorder.**

**Hyperparathyroidism， hyperthyroidism， benign fascicula-tions， and hyperexcitable syndromes all may produce wide spread fasciculation. A fasciculation must be accompanied by wasting and weakness to be significant. Neurogenic cramps induced by exercise， if in the lower extremity are most often|删除0换行|due to dise or spondylitic disease in the lumbar roots partic-ularly S1. This rarely occurs in the upper extremity. Neuro-genic cramps of the upper extremity suggest the cramp fas-ciculation syndrome or motor neuron disease. The differenti-ation can easily be made by EMG. Acid maltase deficiency may give exercise induced cramps with muscle weakness.**

【96】**There is some evidence that anterior horn cell disease may occur in anterior hom cells formerly affected by a polio virus infection. The post polio syndrome is painful and most prob-ably represents accelerated cell death in those anterior homn cells that had compensated for the death of their neighbors.**

**Monomelic ALS seems to affect all muscles of the affected extremity rather than particular muscles of the hand which oc-curs in ALS (benediction sign of 4th and 5th finger or the lat-|删除0换行|eral hand). There are frequently EMG findings in unaffected muscles in ALS.

【98】**Amyotrophy of extremities occurs with multiple system atrophies. The most severe is spinocerebellar atrophy (SCA3) or Machado-Joseph disease. The amyotrophy is never the dominant component of these syndromes.**

【99】**Kennedy’s disease， a bulbar neuronopathy， is X-linked and distinguished by facial fasciculations， genetics and gyneco-mastia. The CK is usually high and there are diminished SNAPs.**

【100】**The late onset spinal muscular atrophies may overlap with ALS. They usually have symmetric proximal weakness and some are distal with pes cavus.**

【102】**Section IV**

【103】**SPINAL CORD DISEASE**

【104】删除7:<u>This page intentionally left blank</u>

【105】**Spinal Cord Disease**

【106】**The spinal cord is frequently involved in specific patterns and at characteristic levels that is extremely helpful in differen-tial diagnosis. The lamination of both the dorsal column and the spinal thalamic tracts is such that the patient's symptoms may not reflect the true level of involvement. This is partic-ularly true with sensory levels. Pain afferents enter the cord and are distributed approximately two segments above and below their level of entry by Lissauer’s tract. Propriospinal fibers connect adjacent spinal dermatomes. The corticospinal tract is arranged so that the fibers innervating the legs are lat-eral to those of the arm. Bladder fibers are between arm and leg fibers. The spinothalamic fibers are laminated such that sacral fibers are most lateral and leg， trunk and arm fibers are medial and cross at their level of entry. Thus a lateral cord lesion at cervical levels will affect the contralateral sacral and leg sensory fibers prior to arm fibers.**

【107】**The clinical and neuropathological division of the cord is into three spaces： (1) epidural； (2) intraparenchymal and；(3) intradural and extramedullary. Processes that compress the spinal cord cause ataxia， a sensory level， then bilateral motor weakness below the level of the lesion and bladder in-volvement. If epidural processes are acute， such as metastasis， intradural hematoma or fracture， there will be spinal shock. If this supervenes all sensation， motor function， bowel， and bladder control and reflexes will be lost below the level of the lesion. Long standing intraparenchymal spinal cord disease causes spasticity below the level of the lesion with a neuro-genic bladder. There is a segmental sensory loss with nor-mal sensation above and below the lesions. Occasionally， re-flexes will be increased above the level of the lesion (Schiff-Sherrington reflex). This is due to disinhibition of excitatory ascending fibers. Cystic intraparenchymal lesions and tumors often cause minimal bladder dysfunction. Epidural compres-sion affects bowel， bladder and then ability to walk， rarely ataxia present initially. Predominantly as the dorsal and ven-tral spinocerebellar tracts are in the periphery of the cord and they both subserve cerebellar functions of the legs. The pa-tient is ataxic prior to becoming paralyzed. The cuneocere-bellar tract conveys proprioception from the upper extremities and is located at cervical levels C1-C4. Propioceptive loss has to be sought by the examiner， although there is frequently a lateral drift of the ipsilateral extremities.**

**Intradural extramedullary lesions are few and comprise meningiomas， neurofibromas， dropped metastasis and en-larged nerve roots from congenital hereditary motor sensory neuropathies. If a neurofibroma or meningioma occurs in the thoracic or cervical area there is often concomitant root and|删除0换行|spinal cord compression. In the lumbar area， roots are in-volved as the spinal cord ends at T12-L1 (conus medullaris).**

【109】**Differential diagnosis of spinal cord pathology depends on location and pattemn of involvement as well as the course of the process.**

【110】**Specific Patterns of Involvement**

【111】**1\. Transverse (in fact these are usually longitudinal)**

【112】**2\. Longitudinal hemisection (Brown-Sequard syndrome)**

【113】**3\. Epidural compression**

【114】**4\. Intramedullary (usually inflammatory or tumor and cause a longitudinal lesion on MRI)**

【115】**The specific diagnostic radiographic features for these pat-tems are：**

【116】参考段删除-1:<u>**1\. Transverse myelitis involves more than one segment and expands the spinal cord. If involvement is more ventral a viral etiology is expected. Dorsal column involvement suggest Sjogren’s， B12 deficiency， Tabes dorsalis or tox-ins.**</u>

【117】**2\. Brown-Sequard： This is a longitudinal division of the cord. The patient suffers ipsilateral proprioceptive， touch and vibratory loss in association with contralateral pain and temperature deficits. There is ipsilateral paralysis be-low the lesion. The usual etiology is trauma (knife or bul-let) or X-RT therapy in which individual sulcal arteries are involved.**

【118】**3.IIntramedullary：The cord is swollen over several segments in an ovoid pattern. Central or asymmetric cysts suggest a syrinx. A post traumatic syrinx occurs above the level of the lesion. Tumors that are associated with intramedullary syrinxes are cystic astrocytomas 删除2:<u>(frequently an enhancing nodule is seen)</u>， hemangioblastomas as well as astrocy-tomas that occur in the wall of syrinxes.**

**4\. Epidural compression： A saw-toothed or paint brush pat-tern on myelography is seen with epidural processes.Bony destruction suggests metastatic disease. This is often only at one segment. Dise involvement， with gadolinium en-hancement， denotes infection. The anterior and posterior ligament often enhance with gadolinium with infection. Lymphomas often start in the epidural fat. Epidural com-pression is noted with extra medullary hematopiesis， as well as by fat in patients on steroids. Dural AVMs are epidural and are most common dorsal in the thoracic seg-ments of the cord. Meningitis of all forms may be dorsal and invades the spinal parenchyma through draining veins or exit foramina. Sarcoid often invades the dura at cervical and thoracic levels. Processes that thicken the spinal dura itself are lymphoma， tuberculosis， cryptococcus； rheuma-toid arthritis and idiopathic pachymeningitis which si-multaneously affect intracranial dura. Carcinomatosis of the meninges characteristically thickens the dura and is seen in the sulci of the cerebellum and cortex. Angio-plastic endotheliosis may affect cerebral blood vessels and|删除0换行|those of the dura. Amyloid may greatly thicken the dura of intracranial and spinal compartments and occasionally forms mass lesions.**

【120】**Intradural Extramedullary Lesions**

【121】**The most common of these are Schwannomas that form“dumbbell tumors."The neuronal exit foramina are expanded and the tumor is seen to compress the spinal cord. Myelog-raphy reveals a“cap" sign. Neurofibromas grow through the nerve root， as opposed to Schwannomas which can be sepa-rated from the nerve root. Plexiform neurofibromas may in-volve multiple nerve roots and are characteristic of neurofi-bromatosis type I (chromosome 17). Hereditary motor sen-sory neuropathy particularly Dejerine-Sottas disease (HSMN Ill) greatly enlarge nerve roots and may compress the cord. Meningiomas characteristically are found in the intradural ex-tramedullary space of the thoracic cord in women and are ex-tremely rare in men. A free fragment of a disc may migrate in this space for several cord segments， while arachnoid cysts may fill， in a ball valve fashion， and compress the spinal cord intermittently. Prior to MRI this process was often misdiag-nosed as multiple sclerosis. Medulloblastomas， spinal cord， metastases and leukemia frequently seed the spinal cord in the intradural extramedullary space. Spontaneous， traumatic and anticoagulation induced subdural hematomas of the spinal cord also occur here.**

【122】**Locations**

【123】**The area of the spinal cord invol ved is a major clue in the dif-ferential diagnosis. The examination is quite specific for each entity. A forward flexed neck with limitation of movement to the lateral planes suggests cervical spondylosis. Degener-ative changes in the spine occur at movement segments such as C5-C6， C4-5， while C8-T1 is not affected. All patients above 40 years of age get some degree of cervical spondylo-sis. The exam will often demonstrate an inverted radial or in-verted supinator reflex， increased knee jerks， as well as inabil-ity to tandem walk due to lateral pressure on the dorsal and ventral spinocerebellar tracts. A short neck suggests Turner’s syndrome， platybasia， Chiari malformation or abnormalities of C1-C2， basilar invagination or Klippel Feil syndromes. There are five ossification centers of C2. and anomalies and fractures occur in these areas. A long neck is suggestive of the“droopy shoulder syndrome”and brachial plexus traction in-juries， but may also be associated with homocystinuria， Mar-fan’s or Ehlers Danlos syndrome. Lhermitte’s sign is most often associated with demyelinating disease， but also occurs with any lesion that irritates the dorsal columns.**

**Characteristic pathology involving the cervical cord in-cludes HIV infection and B12 myelopathy (both give a vac-uolar myelopathy) Sjogren’s syndrome， as well as， spondy-losis， dise disease， stenosis， and demyelinating disease. This|删除0换行|is very frequently associated with a dropped sensory level to T4-T6 due to lamination of the sensory systems of the spinal cord. A level here invariably draws an MRI at this level， but most often pathology will be at cervical levels. Hirayama’s disease， abnormal movement of the cervical spinal cord with consequent pathology at C8-T1， and calcification of the pos-terior longitudinal ligament with cord compression is com-mon in Asian patients. Syrinxes and cavernous hemangiomas are common parenchymal lesions although demyelinating in-flammatory lesions are by far the most common. Rarely sar-coid presents with both inflammatory and dural lesions at this level. A ventral AVM of the anterior spinal artery， the “Foix Alajouanine syndrome" lesion， can be found from cervical to thoracic areas.**

【125】**Thoracic Spinal Cord**

【126】**Inflammatory lesions at this level are usually demyelinating， but sarcoid may thicken the dura here as well as inflame the cord. Dural AVMs， if spinal， are most common in the dorsal cord. Disc disease is rare， but protrusions here are very dan-gerous， as the spinal canal is tight (12-24 mm) and the cord is easily compressed. Diabetes， a syrinx and amyloid may de-stroy propioceptive and pain fibers which produce a“Charcot joint". This is more common at the shoulder joint， particularly for a syrinx. Metastatic disease with a pathologic fracture and meningioma in women are characteristic. Osteoporosis with anterior vertebral body fracture are most common in elderly women at this level. Ganglioneuromas and chordoma， We-ing's sarcoma are rare tumors of the thoracic cord. An astro-cytoma may grow a long distance and destroy anterior horn cells of the thoracic spine asymmetrically giving rise to a“C”form of scoliosis. An “S” shaped scoliosis is congenital (with compensatory curves) and is often asymptomatic. Diastem-atomyelia， a fibrous band that splits the spinal cord， and redu-plication of the cord (two spinal cords with their own dural cover) are rare congenital anomalies. A devastating infection of the thoracic spinal cord is herpes type 6， which leads to necrosis with minimal recovery. West Nile virus， as well as polio， may severely affect this part of the cord， but not to the same degree. Axonal necrosis of the cervical cord with op-tic neuritis (Devic’s) disease is more common in the cervical cord， but dose occur in the thoracic cord as well.**

【127】**The many forms of hereditary spastic paraparesis affect the thoracic cord severely. In uncomplicated variants， only the spinal cord is affected while complicated variants are also as-sociated with optic， cerebellar， cortical and peripheral nerve deficits.**

【128】**Lumbar**
